members.name: Ronda Talley
members.note: The 1973 Talisman's Kappa Delta chapter page records that Talley was voted a representative to the Associated Student Government Congress, and names her Lambda Chi Alpha's outstanding Crescent Girl for 1972 and a Who's Who selection in the 1972 edition. A profile in the same volume calls her the student representative from the College of Education to the Associated Students.
profile: Ronda Talley sat in the Associated Students Congress in 1972-73 as the student representative from the College of Education. The 1973 Talisman recorded that she had been voted a representative to the Congress and named to the 1972 edition of Who's Who in American Colleges and Universities, one of two Kappa Delta members tapped that year.

The same yearbook recorded her other campus work: membership of Kappa Delta, the Student National Education Association and Lambda Chi Alpha's Crescent Club, which named her its 1972 Outstanding Crescent Girl. She was also one of the student contributors listed on the 1973 Talisman staff page.

The yearbook's own pages spell the name two ways: Ronda in the Kappa Delta and Who's Who sections and in the name index, Rhonda in the Crescent Club caption and the Talisman staff list. The archive keeps the spelling its source used and flags the difference rather than settling it.

leaders.name: Steven Yater
leaders.note: Confirmed by the Herald's own 16 April 1974 retrospective, 'Presidency Ends for Steve Yater; One Major Program Started,' which places his presidency closing out at the end of the 1973-74 year, matching the plaque term.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Steve Yater led the Associated Student Government through 1973-74. Early in his term he publicly commended the Board of Regents in the Herald, weeks after the board had increased ASG's budget allotment.

Yater's win was reported in the Herald's 13 April 1973 election returns; the same issue profiled him as making a good impression in his first contact with Congress and stressing a calm approach to the office. Carter Pence's companion article covered new officers being installed at a Congress party the same week, though the archive index does not yet name who besides Yater took office.
In April 1974, stung by election-season criticism, President Yater defended his administration in a letter to the Herald.
His final weeks in office stayed argumentative: the Herald of April 30 carried dueling letters under the heading 'Linda Jones vs. Steven Yater' as the student regent race closed out the year.

The Herald's own retrospective on his term, by Al Cross, ran 16 April 1974 under the headline 'Presidency Ends for Steve Yater; One Major Program Started' - the archive does not yet hold the article's text, only its headline crediting his administration with a single major accomplishment.

events.title: Yater wins the presidency; new officers installed
events.body: The Herald reported Steve Yater's win in the spring election under 'Associated Student Government Election Returns,' profiling him as making a good impression in his first Congress contact and stressing a calm approach. The same issue covered new officers being installed at a Congress party.

events.title: Gregory McKinney sworn in as WKU's first African American student regent
events.body: Seven years before Julius Price became the first Black gubernatorial appointee to the board in 1981. The student seat integrated the Board of Regents first.

events.title: Regents raise the ASG allotment
events.body: The Herald opened the year reporting a budget bulge: the Board of Regents voted to increase the Associated Student Government allotment. A companion piece introduced freshmen to ASG under the headline 'Every College Has One.'

events.title: Free University continues, smaller
events.body: ASG's Free University of no-cost, no-credit evening courses continued for another year, though with fewer courses than before.

events.title: Housing survey urges dorm improvements
events.body: An ASG housing survey urged improvement in dormitory conditions, part of a fall agenda that also included a committee on part-time student opportunities and a push for paper recycling.

events.title: A congressman resigns in protest
events.body: ASG representative Reginald Glass resigned his post in protest, the Herald reported, an early sign of strain inside the congress.

events.title: Sam Ervin booked for April
events.body: ASG contracted Senator Sam Ervin, chairman of the Senate Watergate committee, to speak at Western on April 2. The same issue reported ASG acting to revamp its committees.

events.title: Spending limit stays
events.body: ASG voted to retain its campaign spending limit rather than loosen the cap on campaign outlays.

events.title: Consolo and Henry win the election
events.body: Jeff Consolo and Steve Henry won the spring ASG election, in a cycle whose primary the Herald said showed Greek influence. Henry resigned his post over the student discount program after the results.

events.title: Five file for the student regent seat
events.body: Five students filed for the student seat on the Board of Regents ahead of the spring vote, the position that carried a place at the board table.

events.title: Herald retrospective closes out Yater's presidency
events.body: Al Cross wrote the Herald's retrospective on Steve Yater's term, headlined 'Presidency Ends for Steve Yater; One Major Program Started.' The same issue reported the regent post election set for the following week.

events.title: An $11,000 budget increase pays for the concert and lecture year
events.body: The Board of Regents approved an $11,000 increase in the student affairs budget allocated to ASG in place of a proposed head fee rise. President Steve Yater said the increase was better than a higher head fee because it took no additional money from students' pockets, and the Talisman credited it with paying for the Doobie Brothers, Seals and Crofts and the mini-concerts.

events.title: Street dance and Ginger open the year at the amphitheatre
events.body: ASG began the year with the traditional street dance during registration week, then followed a few days later with the rock band Ginger in a mini-concert at the outdoor amphitheatre. It was the first outdoor performance at the fine arts amphitheatre and the first of the year's mini-concert series.

events.title: Stringbean headlines the second Bluegrass Festival
events.body: The second Bluegrass Festival was held on 6 September 1973 with the Hee Haw star Stringbean and other Nashville acts. The Herald reported five days later that a country-western 'git-together' had replaced the bluegrass festival.

events.title: Ethos plays the second mini-concert
events.body: The electronic-rock group Ethos from Fort Wayne, Indiana, played ASG's second mini-concert on 13 October 1973 in Van Meter Auditorium. Guitarist Bill Sharpe told the boogie-oriented audience that most of the boogies would have to be in their noses; the band was warmly received and returned in the spring as an off-campus support act.

events.title: Homecoming rock and roll revival: Jerry Lee Lewis cancels and Chuck Berry never shows
events.body: ASG's first attempt at a major concert, a 1950s Rock and Roll Revival for Homecoming, collapsed twice. Jerry Lee Lewis was first booked and cancelled over management problems, Chuck Berry was signed in his place and then took an unscheduled holiday in Las Vegas and ignored the date, leaving Gary U.S. Bonds to headline with the Crystals, Freddie Cannon and Lloyd Price. Ron Beck warned the crowd before the show and offered refunds to anyone who left within fifteen minutes, and he and ASG were still trying to recover the refund money from producer Richard Nader months later.

events.title: Red Snapper plays the ASG Homecoming dance
events.body: The Homecoming dance sponsored by ASG ran from 8pm to midnight after the game against Morehead, with music by Red Snapper. Homecoming 1973 took its theme from the movies and drew a crowd of 19,500 to the game in the rain.

events.title: A student takes the concert complaints to Congress
events.body: Tony Agee, a junior from Albany, brought his and his friends' grievances before the ASG Congress at the meeting of 29 October 1973. He charged that ASG had misrepresented facts, used false advertising and put incompetent people in charge of booking; president Steve Yater blamed the producer of the Homecoming revival.

events.title: Amnesty is the least successful mini-concert of the series
events.body: The soul-blues-jazz combo Amnesty played a mini-concert in Van Meter. The Talisman said much of the crowd enjoyed it but that it was the least successful show of the mini-concert series.

events.title: The Doobie Brothers play to 6,000
events.body: The Doobie Brothers played Diddle Arena on 4 December 1973 before a crowd of 6,000. The group had originally been booked for October and was postponed over a recording commitment; the Herald called the show average but the Talisman said it pleased most of the crowd.

events.title: Seals and Crofts play the first free concert in more than a year
events.body: Seals and Crofts opened the spring semester on Saturday 19 January 1974 before what the 1974 Talisman called one of the largest crowds ever to see a show in Diddle Arena. The Talisman called it in some ways the best campus concert in more than a year and the first free concert since the autumn of 1972, scheduling and money having prevented one since.

events.title: The Free University shuts down after two semesters
events.body: The Herald reported that the Free U had shut down after two semesters. Coordinator Glenn Jackson blamed a lack of student interest and the difficulty of finding people to teach the classes, which had covered knitting, photography, yoga and other subjects.

events.title: ASG considers ending the legal loan fund
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG might end its legal loan fund. The Legal Rights Committee had been working towards a bail-bond fund for arrested students and had taken up drug expulsions, the refusal to show X-rated films in the student center and the 'Fly' censorship case.

events.title: Raymond McNally lectures on Dracula
events.body: ASG brought Dr Raymond McNally of Boston College, co-author of 'In Search of Dracula', to lecture on vampirism before a large audience in the Garrett Conference Center Ballroom. He traced the legend to a fifteenth century Romanian prince and showed clips from vampire films.

events.title: Harry Chapin opens the major-mini concert series
events.body: ASG scheduled the folk singer and balladeer Harry Chapin for two shows in Van Meter on 3 March 1974. Activities vice president Tom LaCivita called it the first example of his new concept of major-mini concerts, in which medium-priced performers were brought in, sometimes free and sometimes as a pay event.

events.title: Herald calls the lecture series ASG's best effort to date
events.body: The Herald judged ASG's 1973-74 lecture series its best effort yet. The series had carried Senator Barry Goldwater, former attorney general Elliot Richardson and Senator Edmund Muskie, and ASG jointly sponsored the psychic Uri Geller with the University Lecture Series.

events.title: Marshall Tucker Band is upstaged by Freddie King
events.body: ASG brought the Marshall Tucker Band to Diddle Arena on Monday 8 April 1974, with Freddie King leading in. The Talisman said King, brought back for encores by a screaming crowd, was the biggest crowd pleaser, while Diddle's acoustics destroyed much of Marshall Tucker's set and the disappointed crowd began drifting towards the doors halfway through.

events.title: Kool and the Gang announced to close the year
events.body: The Herald previewed boogie and bluegrass coming to campus, and the Talisman recorded that the soul show band Kool and the Gang was scheduled to close out ASG's year alongside a festival set for 27 April. Neither source confirms that either event took place.

events.title: Student-Faculty Interaction seminars
events.body: ASG set up a series of informative seminars under a Student-Faculty Interaction Program, run with the undergraduate advisement office. The programmes were informal meetings between students and department representatives to discuss possible majors, aimed at students who had not decided.

events.title: Steve Henry resigns the discount post
events.body: The Herald reported that Steve Henry had resigned his ASG discount post. Henry was elected ASG president a year later and ran on a platform of entertainment and student services.

events.title: Edmund Muskie calls for Nixon's impeachment in an ASG lecture
events.body: ASG sponsored the lecture Senator Edmund Muskie of Maine gave at Western on 11 December 1973, on the restoration of confidence in government. Muskie called for the impeachment of President Nixon, saying he had decided on the night of the Saturday Massacre that impeachment was the only way the issue should be raised. He cited a Harris poll in which 19 per cent of Americans said they had confidence in the executive branch. The 1974 Talisman lists Muskie with Barry Goldwater and Elliot Richardson among the lectures ASG sponsored that year.

src.label: 1974 Talisman, pp. 52-55 (Lectures); date from College Heights Herald 53:26, 4 Dec 1973

events.title: Sam Ervin analyses Watergate
events.body: Senator Sam Ervin, chairman of the Senate Watergate committee, spoke at Western on 2 April 1974 under a contract ASG had signed in February. The Herald reported the lecture on 5 April, and in the same issue judged ASG's 1973-74 lecture series its best effort to date.

src2.label: College Heights Herald 53:39, 15 Feb 1974

events.title: Reginald Glass asks for minority representation
events.body: Jerry Elam reported in the Herald of 9 October 1973 that Reginald Glass, the ASG representative from the Graduate College, had asked for better representation for minority groups in student government and on the Academic Council. The 1974 Talisman recorded that Glass said the lack of Black and foreign students in these groups harmed both the minorities and the University, and that he resigned his Congress seat in protest.

src.label: Herald 53:12, 9 Oct 1973; 1974 Talisman, Associated Student Government, p. 61

events.title: Glenn Jackson introduces the reorganization bill
events.body: Carl Clayworth reported in the Herald of 25 January 1974 that administrative vice president Glenn Jackson had introduced a bill to reorganize ASG. The 1974 Talisman recorded that the change folded ASG's programmes into student affairs and academic affairs, each under an area chairman, keeping the Activities, Rules and Elections, and Legislative Research Committees, after Jackson said the old system's many specific committees left ideas that fit no area and caused new committees to be constantly formed, with projects placed by the president subject to Congress approval.

events.title: Amendment issues on the autumn ballot
events.body: The Herald reported that amendment issues highlighted the autumn balloting. The archive does not hold the article's text, so what the amendments proposed and whether they carried are not established.

executive.name: Glenn Jackson
executive.note: Jackson was administrative vice president in 1973-74 and the yearbook's spokesman for the reorganization bill that abolished ASG's committee system and folded all programs into two areas, student affairs and academic affairs. He said the old system was too rigid and that ideas often fitted no committee, leaving some with nothing to do and others with too much. He also co-ordinated the free university, and cited lack of interest and difficulty finding teachers as its main problem. The Herald reported the same reorganization push in its own coverage that October and January, when Jackson introduced an interaction proposal and then a bill to reorganize ASG.
profile: Glenn Jackson was elected administrative vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1973-74, serving under president Steve Yater alongside activities vice president Tom LaCivita, treasurer Lee Goodpaster and secretary Pam Stewart.

Jackson was the executive branch's public spokesman for a reorganization of ASG's committee system, which the Herald reported him introducing in the Congress that October and again as formal legislation in January 1974. The 1974 Talisman quotes him saying the old, more numerous committee structure was too rigid, that ideas often fitted no existing committee, and that the result left some committees with nothing to do and others overloaded; the reorganization folded ASG's programs into two broader areas, student affairs and academic affairs. Jackson also coordinated ASG's free university program that year, begun the previous spring, and said afterward that a lack of student interest and difficulty finding people to teach the non-credit courses were its main problems.

executive.name: Lee Goodpaster
executive.note: Goodpaster was ASG treasurer in 1973-74 and appears in the same officer list and meeting caption. The yearbook mentions her separately in its elections and homecoming coverage. The same volume's Who's Who feature profiles her as an accounting major who was a member of Alpha Xi Delta sorority and an Alpha Tau Omega Little Sister; the 1975 Talisman further records that she received Alpha Xi Delta's Frances C. Bloker Pledge Trainer Award at the sorority's national convention in Chicago.
profile: Lee Goodpaster served as treasurer of the Associated Student Government for 1973-74 under president Steve Yater, one of the five-member executive branch shown in the year's officer photograph and meeting caption alongside Yater, Tom LaCivita, Glenn Jackson and Pam Stewart.

The 1974 Talisman's Who's Who feature profiles Goodpaster separately: an accounting major, she was a member of Alpha Xi Delta sorority and an Alpha Tau Omega Little Sister. The following year's Talisman records that she received Alpha Xi Delta's Frances C. Bloker Pledge Trainer Award at the sorority's national convention in Chicago.

src.label: 1974 Talisman, Associated Student Government, p. 56, and Who's Who, p. 95

executive.name: Pam Stewart
executive.note: Stewart was ASG secretary in 1973-74. She appears in the section's officer list and in a caption of officers conducting a meeting with Yater, LaCivita, Jackson and Goodpaster.
profile: Pam Stewart served as secretary of the Associated Student Government for 1973-74 under president Steve Yater. The 1974 Talisman lists her in the year's executive officer roll and pictures her in a meeting caption alongside Yater, activities vice president Tom LaCivita, administrative vice president Glenn Jackson and treasurer Lee Goodpaster.

executive.name: Thomas LaCivita
executive.note: LaCivita was activities vice president in 1973-74 and again in 1974-75, making him one of the few officers to serve two consecutive years in this decade. The 1974 volume says he was elected in one of the most controversial elections in the school's history and carries a Herald reviewer's criticism of the concert programme; the 1975 volume has President Jeff Consolo crediting him with a more diversified entertainment series on a $42,000 budget. The 1974 Talisman traces the friction behind that review to a dispute between LaCivita and Ron Beck, assistant dean of student affairs: LaCivita said Beck put too little creativity into the entertainment program and did not keep up with the music scene, while Beck said cost, student appeal and any encouragement of drug use were what shaped which acts were booked, adding that he would not book a group he had not heard of; the two reconciled enough during the year to run a program that turned a profit after a slow start.
profile: Thomas LaCivita was elected activities vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1973-74 in what the 1974 Talisman calls one of the most controversial elections in the school's history, serving under president Steve Yater alongside administrative vice president Glenn Jackson, treasurer Lee Goodpaster and secretary Pam Stewart. He was re-elected to the post for 1974-75, one of the few ASG officers of the decade to serve two consecutive years; that second term is recorded under his 1974-75 entry.

Early in his first year LaCivita clashed publicly with Ron Beck, the assistant dean of student affairs who administered concert bookings through ASG. LaCivita charged that Beck put too little creativity into the entertainment program, did not weigh LaCivita's opinions, and did not keep up with the music scene; he also argued that concerts should be advertised beyond Bowling Green to draw more ticket revenue. Beck, who at first declined to respond to the specific charges, said cost, student appeal and any tendency of an act to encourage drug use were what determined which acts were booked, telling the Herald's reviewer, 'If I haven't heard of a group, they won't go on this campus.' The dispute eased as the year went on, and the two ran an entertainment program that turned a profit after a rocky start.

officers.name: Robert Deboe
officers.note: The 1974 Talisman names Deboe, in its Alpha Phi Alpha page, as a member of the Judicial Council and as elected to Who's Who. A Robert Deboe had been approved to the Rules and Elections Committee at Congress's first meeting of 31 August 1972, reported in the Herald of 1 September 1972; the volumes do not say the two are the same man.
profile: Robert Deboe, a brother of Alpha Phi Alpha fraternity, served on Associated Student Government's Judicial Council in 1973-74. The 1974 Talisman's fraternity page named him among the chapter's outstanding brothers, reporting he had been elected to Who's Who Among Students in American Universities and Colleges; the same volume's Zeta Phi Beta sorority page separately records him as that chapter's "Mr. Omega Delta" that year, an honor unconnected to Alpha Phi Alpha.

A Robert Deboe had been approved to Congress's Rules and Elections Committee at its first meeting of the year, 31 August 1972, as the Herald reported the following day; the archive has not confirmed this is the same man rather than a returning member from the prior Congress.

members.name: Melody Edwards
members.seat: representative in the Associated Student Government and on the Academic Council
members.note: Her Who's Who entry in the 1974 Talisman names her an agriculture club member and a representative in the Associated Student Government and on the Academic Council. The entry does not date the term; it is placed here because it appears in the 1974 volume.
profile: Melody Edwards, an agriculture major, was recorded by the 1974 Talisman as a representative in the Associated Student Government and on the Academic Council, and was named to Who's Who. The same entry has her holding that involvement was worth having so long as it stayed moderate.

Her other recorded campus work was in her field: she belonged to the Agriculture Club, whose Halloween carnival in 1972 the yearbook credited her with supplying its Great Pumpkin, and to the Agricultural Education Club. Her Who's Who entry argued that agriculture was changing fast and had room for men and women alike.

members.name: Debbie Filburn
members.note: The Kappa Delta chapter page names members who distinguished themselves on campus, including 'Debbie Filburn, serving as representative-at-large on the ASG Congress' — a direct, dated statement of the seat, not merely a general mention. The volume's index separately lists a distinct person, Donna Marie Filburn, confirming the two should not be merged.
profile: Debbie Filburn sat in the Associated Student Government Congress as a representative-at-large in 1973-74; the 1974 Talisman named her among the Kappa Delta members who had distinguished themselves on campus, in that office. She had been a student contributor to the 1973 Talisman the year before.

The 1975 Talisman recorded that two sisters, Donna and Debbie Filburn, were both in the Associated Student Government. They are two people, and the archive records them separately: Donna Filburn sat in the 1974-75 Congress and was Panhellenic Council president.

members.seat: ASG representative from the Graduate College

His prior 1971-72 Associated Students vice-presidency is not sourced to this citation.

members.name: Steve Henry
members.note: The Sophomores section says active class members included seven sophomores who were members of the ASG congress, and names Steve Henry as class president in text and in a photo caption of Henry and Jeff Wampler checking notes before an ASG meeting.

members.name: Michael Inman
members.note: Named as junior class president, coordinating class activities (including a Homecoming float and spring dance) with vice-president Deborah Locke.
profile: Michael Inman moved up from sophomore class vice-president to junior class president for 1973-74, with Deborah Locke as vice-president. The 1974 Talisman recorded the pair coordinating the class's activities, which included a Fiddler on the Roof float in the Homecoming parade and a spring dance. He was also a junior ROTC student, photographed by the yearbook helping to ease traffic and assist visiting families as students converged on campus at the start of the year.

In April 1974 the Herald ran the contest for the student seat on the Board of Regents over four issues. The issue of 19 April, whose lead reported that five students had filed for the seat, printed a letter under his name headlined "Inman Announces". The archive has not been able to read the letter and cannot say what he announced or whether he was one of the five.

members.name: John Donofrio, Jr.
members.note: Named as coordinating freshman class projects with vice-president Christy Kay Vogt, under the heading 'Donofrio and Vogt lead freshman class.'
profile: John Donofrio, Jr. was elected freshman class president for 1973-74, with Christy Kay Vogt as vice-president. The 1974 Talisman headed its account of the class "Donofrio and Vogt lead freshman class" and recorded their first major project as a Homecoming float on the theme of Camelot, with Marcia Heckman as the class's queen candidate and a concert-dance planned for the spring. The pair were photographed in the Helm library.
His vice-president that year went on to be administrative vice president of the Associated Student Government in 1975-76 and its president in 1976-77, under the name Christy Vogt.

members.name: Deborah Locke
members.note: Named in the junior class pages and caption as vice-president; the Kappa Delta chapter page separately lists 'Debbie Locke, as vice-president of the junior class' among members who distinguished themselves on campus.
profile: Deborah Locke was elected junior class vice-president for 1973-74, serving with president Michael Inman; the 1974 Talisman recorded the two coordinating the class's Homecoming float and a planned spring dance, and named her among the Kappa Delta members who had distinguished themselves on campus.

members.name: Hamp Moore
members.note: Named with Carl Stoltzfus in the senior class pages and photograph caption as senior class vice-president; the same section notes he was elected vice-president of the Southeast Regional Inter-Fraternity Conference that year.
profile: Hamp Moore was elected senior class vice-president for 1973-74 under president Carl Stoltzfus. The 1974 Talisman recorded the two supervising the class's Homecoming activities, including its Gone with the Wind float, and listed Moore among the seniors receiving outside honours that year as vice-president of the Southeast Regional Inter-Fraternity Conference. He was a member of Sigma Alpha Epsilon and appears in the yearbook at that fraternity's signing of its scroll before the run to Middle Tennessee, alongside university president Dero Downing.

He appears to have been a candidate in the April 1974 election for the student seat on the Board of Regents. The Herald printed letters endorsing him in two of the four issues that covered the race — from Bruce Merrick on 19 April, the issue whose lead reported that five students had filed, and from Gail Getchell on 23 April, the issue in which the candidates listed their qualifications — alongside parallel endorsements of Hank Miles. No source the archive has read names the field outright, and the seat went to Greg McKinney, whom the Herald of 26 April reported vying for the post with Sid Stevens.

The Sigma Phi Epsilon chapter page separately says he was senior class president, chairman of the Rules and Election Committee of the ASG, Talisman Greek editor, and a member of the University Academic Complaint Committee and of Who's Who.

profile: Jeff Wampler was elected sophomore class vice-president for 1973-74, serving under president Steve Henry. The 1974 Talisman recorded that seven sophomores sat in the Associated Student Government Congress that year, and photographed the two class officers checking notes before an Associated Student Government meeting; the class's executive committee had tentatively planned a free dance for the spring. The 1976 volume gives him as a pre-med major from Jeffersontown.
