leaders.name: Gregory McKinney
leaders.note: Student regent, not president. Sworn in 19 June 1974 as WKU's first African American student regent.

sources.label: WKU Timeline: Gregory McKinney (Western Alumnus, 19 Jun 1974)

profile: Gregory McKinney came to campus prominence as a speaker: in March 1974 the Herald reported him winning top honors in competition.

That spring McKinney ran for the student seat on the Board of Regents against Sid Stevens, the two candidates' final appeals running side by side in the Herald as an editorial called the race a clear choice for voters.
McKinney won the seat and was sworn in on June 19, 1974, becoming WKU's first African American student regent.

Midway through the fall 1974 semester, Herald writer Al Cross profiled the new regent under the headline 'Greg McKinney Feels Regents Can Aid Western's Progress,' as McKinney settled into his seat on the Board of Regents.
As the academic year closed, the Herald reported 'Student Regent Greg McKinney Calls Year Rewarding,' in the same issue that covered the regents approving a record budget and academic proposals.

After his term as student regent, McKinney stayed on at WKU as a graduate assistant in Student Affairs. The university's own file on him, opened in 1983, holds correspondence between McKinney and President Donald Zacharias and a paper he wrote titled "Student Affairs: An Analysis" - the record of a former student regent moving into the administration whose board he had once sat on.

leaders.name: Jeffrey Consolo
leaders.note: ASG president. The Herald of 1974 reports 'Jeff Consolo Tabs Eight for Congress' - a president making appointments to the Associated Student Congress.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Jeff Consolo won the Associated Student Government presidency in the March 1974 election on a ticket with Steve Henry, in a cycle whose primary the Herald said showed Greek influence.
Taking office, Consolo told the Herald he hoped for increased student involvement during his term.

Consolo's term closed on April 15, 1975, when new ASG officers were installed at the day's meeting after a spring in which his congress had simplified election procedures and wound down its concert program.
Jeffrey Paul Consolo, of Mansfield, Ohio, served as the ninth president of WKU's Associated Student Government for the 1974-75 term, according to the SGA's own roster of former presidents.
Early in the fall 1974 semester, Consolo appointed eight students to seats in the ASG congress, reported by Jim Reynolds under the headline 'Jeff Consolo Tabs Eight for Congress.'

In early April 1975, as the polls prepared to open to elect his successor, the Herald ran 'Jeff Consolo Notes Progress in His Term' alongside items crediting ASG moves with cutting bookstore prices, gaining parking board input and folding the Volunteer Bureau into the organization.

events.title: Regents extend visitation as the year opens
events.body: The Herald's opening issue reported the Board of Regents extending dormitory visitation and approving a $29.8 million budget at the board's first session of the year.

events.title: Voting procedures simplified for the spring election
events.body: ASG passed a motion simplifying voting procedures for the spring election, and the ASG treasurer took to the Herald's letters column the same day.

events.title: New officers installed; concert plans dropped
events.body: New Associated Student Government officers were installed at the day's meeting, as the outgoing congress abandoned plans for a final concert of the semester and the editorial page pronounced incoming president Steve Henry's entertainment plan inadequate.

events.title: Keffer wins freshman vote; Consolo names eight to congress
events.body: The Herald reported that Jay Keffer won the freshman election for the top freshman post. In the same issue, ASG president Jeff Consolo tabbed eight students for seats in the ASG congress, and the Academic Council heard a proposal for more student votes.

events.title: Protesters urge ASG revamping
events.body: Protesters urged a revamping of the Associated Student Government. The same issue carried Janet Steen's report that ASG ecology projects were non-existent.

events.title: ASG schedules Kiss and initiates concert hour
events.body: ASG scheduled the rock band Kiss and initiated a concert hour, part of its role booking campus entertainment that fall. The concert program later became a major source of financial trouble for the organization.

events.title: Budget troubles threaten ASG entertainment role
events.body: The Herald reported that financial difficulties might force ASG to drop its entertainment duties, and the ASG congress heard the treasurer's budget explanation. Columnists Dave Allen and Craig Griffith examined the organization's budget problems in the same issue.

events.title: Quorum failures halt ASG twice in one week
events.body: ASG action was halted twice during the week by a lack of quorum. A Herald editorial said the confusion in ASG signaled a need for change.

events.title: Primary canceled; constitutional change approved
events.body: The primary election for Associated Student Government was canceled, and the student government approved a constitutional change. A letter writer in the same issue criticized the Herald's coverage of ASG.

events.title: Steve Henry elected to lead ASG
events.body: Following the spring election, the Herald reported that incoming president Steve Henry would give activities priority in Associated Student Government. The organization also prepared to name its top member, and the paper noted that Greeks continued to dominate the campus political scene.

events.title: Rain drives the Bluegrass Festival indoors
events.body: ASG sponsored a Bluegrass Festival on 28 August 1974, headlined by Lester Flatt and the Clinch Mountain Clan, who described their music as folk music with overdrive. Scheduled as an outdoor festival in the amphitheatre, it had to be moved into Van Meter Auditorium because of rain.

events.title: A $42,000 entertainment budget, $27,000 of it for two free concerts
events.body: ASG operated on a budget of $42,000 for all forms of entertainment in 1974-75. It set aside $27,000 for two free concerts and $15,000 for mini-concerts, dances and other acts, with major concerts financed by their own gate receipts.
events.money: $42,000 entertainment budget; $27,000 for two free concerts, $15,000 for mini-concerts and dances

events.title: Students picket the Doc Severinsen Homecoming concert
events.body: Doc Severinsen played the Homecoming concert on 11 October 1974 with Today's Children and the Now Generation Brass, before roughly 3,000 people, a substantial majority of them alumni. About thirty students picketed the doors; Severinsen complimented the audience for braving the picket lines and said he respected the demonstrators' right to exercise an American privilege.

events.title: Protest produces a coalition for change in concert booking
events.body: The Herald reported that the protest at the Severinsen concert had prompted a coalition seeking change in concert booking. The Student Action Committee that resulted argued that Ron Beck did not have the time the booking job needed and sought power for the activities vice president to negotiate with acts; Kentucky law prevented a student from controlling the funds, so the role stayed advisory, and the committee later folded into ASG's Student Activities Committee.

events.title: Barefoot Jerry costs ASG almost $1,500
events.body: The Nashville group Barefoot Jerry entertained a small crowd in Van Meter with a set that ranged across rock, country, blues and jazz and ended in a standing ovation. Activities vice president Tom LaCivita said ASG lost almost $1,500 on it; the Talisman, which does not date the show, called it one of the finer shows of its size at Western.

events.title: Al Stewart's mini-concert dies with his US tour
events.body: ASG booked Al Stewart for a mini-concert on 3 November 1974, but his United States tour was cancelled over immigration law. Tom LaCivita booked Kiss in his place, in an effort to ease the pressure students had put on ASG over its choice of acts.

events.title: America plays free and pushes ASG further into debt
events.body: ASG presented America as the first free concert of the school year on 7 November 1974, with Chad Stewart of Chad and Jeremy opening. Cracked speakers and feedback marred the sound, but lighters brought the band back for 'A Horse with No Name'; the Talisman recorded that ASG went into steadily increasing debt by presenting America free.

events.title: ASG establishes a service area
events.body: Jim Reynolds reported in the Herald that ASG had established a service area. The reorganisation of that year had put ASG's work into two areas, student affairs and academic affairs, with projects assigned to one or the other.

events.title: Kiss plays Van Meter and Ron Beck swears off the genre
events.body: Kiss played to a capacity crowd in Van Meter Auditorium on 7 December 1974, with smoke bombs, fire-eating, whiteface and leather bat wings, and Gene Simmons simulating vomiting and dripping stage blood over the front row. Ron Beck said afterwards that he would never again take part in booking this kind of act for Western because the show had no educational value for students.

events.title: War and the Charlie Daniels Band open warfare in Diddle
events.body: ASG's first major spring concert put War and the Charlie Daniels Band in Diddle Arena on 3 March 1975. Students called the Charlie Daniels set the best they had had in years and matches and lighters brought him back for 'Orange Blossom Special', but attendance was very low.

events.title: Bookstore prices cut and a part-time athletic discount approved
events.body: The Herald reported in the same issue that an ASG move had cut bookstore prices, that a part-time athletic discount had been approved and that the Volunteer Bureau had been made part of ASG. ASG had proposed raising the part-time incidental fee so part-time students could enter athletic events on the same footing as full-time students.

events.title: A better and cheaper student discount card
events.body: ASG changed the student discount card for what the Talisman described as a far better and cheaper one. The change was listed among the accomplishments of the Consolo administration alongside the new academic complaint system.

events.title: Pure Prairie League: sound ruins the first show, the second is far better
events.body: Associated Student Government billed Pure Prairie League, and the group played two shows in Van Meter on 31 January 1975. Sound problems ruined most of the first act at 7:30, and the bassist, printed in the Talisman as Mike Rieley, asked the 9:30 audience whether anyone had seen the first show. He said it was the group's first experience with the sound crew the university had contracted. The problems were solved before the second show, which the 1975 Talisman rated far better.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Entertainment; announced in College Heights Herald 50:31, 24 Jan 1975

events.title: ASG books its fall entertainment fare
events.body: The Herald reported on 30 August 1974 that Associated Student Government had booked its entertainment programme for the fall semester. The 1975 Talisman set out the season that followed: an ASG bluegrass festival on 28 August, moved indoors to Van Meter Auditorium by rain and headlined by Lester Flatt and the Clinch Mountain Clan; Doc Severinsen at Homecoming on 11 October, picketed by about 30 students; and America free on 7 November. ASG had booked Al Stewart for a 3 November mini-concert, but his United States tour was cancelled over immigration law and activities vice-president Tom LaCivita booked Kiss in his place.

events.title: ASG broke even on the Bar-Kays mini-concert
events.body: The Herald of 25 October 1974 billed the Bar-Kays for a mini-concert that night. The 1975 Talisman records that ASG presented the seven-member group, the backing band on Isaac Hayes's 'Hot Buttered Soul' and 'Shaft' albums, as one of its major mini-concerts of the year, and that ASG broke even on the concert.

events.title: ASG took over the Student Volunteer Bureau and the tutorial programme
events.body: The Student Volunteer Bureau, which placed students in community volunteer work, weakened when founder Rodney Berry could not secure administrators or funds. Berry approached ASG president Jeff Consolo about folding it into ASG, and the Talisman recorded the merger passing at the last meeting of the fall semester by better than 80 per cent, with the tutorial programme consolidated into ASG at the same time. The Herald of 21 January 1975 reported that ASG had agreed to administer the bureau and had rescued it.

src2.label: 1975 Talisman, Associated Student Government

events.title: ASG seeks more student votes on the Academic Council
events.body: Scott Johnston reported in the Herald of 20 September 1974 that ASG was seeking more votes on the Academic Council. The 1975 Talisman quoted president Jeff Consolo saying ASG had drawn up a resolution for the Council's Rules Committee asking for three more student votes and voting status for its three executive officers, since students without a declared major were not represented through a college; the Council then had two representatives from each of seven colleges, half of them voting, for a total of 40 votes.

src.label: Herald 50:7, 20 Sep 1974; 1975 Talisman, Associated Student Government, p. 112

events.title: A bill seeks a financial report from ASG
events.body: Jim Reynolds reported a bill seeking an ASG financial report. In February 1975 the Herald reported that ASG funds were dwindling and that Congress had heard the treasurer's explanation of the budget.

events.title: ASG votes to study its own effectiveness
events.body: Betsy Leake reported that ASG would study its own effectiveness. Four days later the paper reported that a report showed ASG funds were dwindling, and on 7 February that financial difficulties might force the organisation to drop its entertainment duties.

events.title: An ASG resolution becomes University policy through the Regents
events.body: The academic complaint system became University policy when the Board of Regents approved it in January 1975, four months after ASG passed a resolution asking that the complaint system be accelerated. A second ASG resolution, asking that incompletes not be counted in the computation of grade point averages, also reached the regents and was approved. The day of the January approval is not given in the source.

events.title: A Congress member counts the empty seats
events.body: In a letter printed in the Herald of 4 October 1974, Congress member Marc Levy wrote that he had hoped the year's meetings would differ from the previous year's invisible congress. The 1975 Talisman quoted the letter, recording that a roll call at the meeting of 1 October 1974 showed a good number of people missing and that three of the four committee reports were delivered by president Jeff Consolo because of absences.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Associated Student Government, p. 113, quoting the College Heights Herald of 4 Oct 1974

events.title: Hall hearing boards die
events.body: The Herald of 11 February 1975 reported, in a story by Neil Budde, that the residence hall hearing board system had ended. The archive does not hold the article's text, so what replaced the boards is not established.

executive.name: Paul Nation
executive.note: Nation was administrative vice president of ASG in 1974-75. President Jeff Consolo, listing the officers he worked with, named Nation first and said they had all done a good job; the 1975 Talisman's Greek pages also record him as administrative vice-president. The archive had no administrative vice president recorded for this year.
profile: Paul Nation was administrative vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1974-75 under President Jeff Consolo. The 1975 Talisman's Greek pages record him in the post, and at the close of the year Consolo, crediting each of his officers by name, named Nation first and said all four officers had done a good job.

executive.name: Ricky Johnson
executive.note: Johnson was ASG treasurer in 1974-75. The caption shows him discussing the signing of War and the Charlie Daniels Band with activities vice president Tom LaCivita. A Rickie Johnson appears on the ASG Congress attendance roll printed in the 1976 Talisman, so he may have stayed in Congress the following year; the spelling differs between the two volumes and is not settled.
profile: Ricky Johnson was treasurer of the Associated Student Government for 1974-75. A photograph caption in the 1975 Talisman shows him with activities vice president Tom LaCivita discussing the signing of the rock band War and the Charlie Daniels Band for a Western concert. A Rickie Johnson appears on the ASG Congress attendance roll the 1976 Talisman printed, so he may have stayed active in Congress after his term as treasurer ended, though the spelling differs between the two volumes and the identification is not certain.

executive.name: Cindy Kirkpatrick
executive.note: Kirkpatrick was ASG secretary in 1974-75, shown checking meeting notes while Consolo conferred with Panhellenic Council president Donna Filburn. She also appears in the 1974 Talisman talking with LaCivita and Vice President for Academic Affairs Dr. John Minton.
profile: Cindy Kirkpatrick was secretary of the Associated Student Government for 1974-75. The 1975 Talisman photographs her checking meeting notes as President Jeff Consolo conferred with Panhellenic Council president Donna Filburn. The 1974 Talisman, covering the year before her term as secretary, already shows her in conversation with activities vice president Tom LaCivita and Vice President for Academic Affairs Dr. John Minton, suggesting she was involved with ASG before she took office.

executive.name: Thomas LaCivita
executive.note: LaCivita held the activities vice presidency for a second consecutive year in 1974-75; the archive records his 1973-74 term separately, where his profile is written. He ran unopposed for re-election. He chaired the ASG Activities Committee, worked to a $42,000 entertainment budget of which $27,000 went to two free concerts, and after protests over the poorly attended Doc Severinsen Homecoming concert absorbed the newly formed Student Action Committee into his committee, saying the added personnel would give him more people to back him up. Bookings were settled between him and Ron Beck, assistant dean of student affairs, with whom LaCivita had publicly clashed over concert booking the previous year.
profile: Thomas LaCivita, elected unopposed to a second consecutive term as activities vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1974-75, chaired the ASG Activities Committee on a roughly $42,000 entertainment budget, of which $27,000 went toward two free concerts. His full account, including the 1973-74 dispute with assistant dean of student affairs Ron Beck over concert booking, is recorded under his first term the year before.

After students picketed the poorly received Doc Severinsen Homecoming concert on 11 October 1974, a newly formed Student Action Committee pressed to give LaCivita more say in negotiating with prospective acts; he absorbed the committee into his own rather than cede ground, though Kentucky law kept the activities vice president's role advisory, since a student could not control university funds outright. When a booked Al Stewart mini-concert fell through after Stewart's United States tour was cancelled under immigration law, LaCivita booked the New York hard rock group Kiss to replace him. President Jeff Consolo credited LaCivita afterward with running a more diversified entertainment series that year.

executive.name: Stan McDivitt
executive.note: McDivitt was elected to the Associated Student Government Congress, the 1975 Talisman's Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter pages record, alongside fraternity brother Steve Henry, who went on to be ASG president in 1975-76. This entry lists him as ASG's student affairs chairperson for 1974-75; the archive has not found a source confirming when or how he came into that post. The Herald issue of 7 February 1975 previously cited for it (digitalcommons.wku.edu/dlsc_ua_records/5048) does not name him in its index, and the earlier account of an appointment at the Congress meeting of 4 February 1975 has been withdrawn as unsourced.
profile: Stan McDivitt was elected to the Associated Student Government Congress, the 1975 Talisman's Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter pages record, alongside fraternity brother Steve Henry, who went on to be ASG president in 1975-76.

officers.name: Marc Levy
officers.note: Levy was an ASG Congress member in 1974-75 and again in 1975-76. In a letter to the College Heights Herald he wrote that he had hoped the year's meetings would differ from the previous year's invisible congress, and reported a good number absent from the 1 October 1974 meeting, at which three of four committee reports were given by the president himself. In 1975-76 he brought charges against ASG treasurer David Payne over spending before budget approval, appeared twice before the Judicial Council, and lost, the council ruling in Payne's favour.
profile: Marc Levy served as an ASG Congress member in 1974-75 and again in 1975-76, and was one of the Herald's most frequent student critics through both years, writing letters attacking Associated Student Government, the Herald itself, the Academic Council and the ASG constitution in issue after issue.

In a letter printed in the Herald of 4 October 1974, Levy wrote that he had hoped the year's meetings would differ from what he called the previous year's "invisible congress." He reported that a roll call at the meeting of 1 October 1974 showed a good number of members missing, and that three of the four committee reports were delivered by president Jeff Consolo himself rather than by the committee chairs.

In the fall of 1975 Levy brought a complaint against ASG treasurer David Payne over spending ahead of budget approval. The Judicial Council heard the case and cleared Payne of fund misuse, reported in the Herald's 21 November 1975 issue (51:25) under the headline "Judicial Council Clears David Payne of Fund Misuse"; the same issue separately reported Levy had been picked "top legislator" at a recent intercollegiate meeting, without the archive confirming which one.

src2.label: Herald 51:25, 21 Nov 1975

officers.name: Vern Pulman
officers.note: Consolo appointed Pulman representative-at-large in February 1975, filling one of the two places left vacant by Christy Vogt's resignation from Congress.
profile: ASG president Jeffrey Consolo appointed Vern Pulman a representative-at-large in February 1975, filling one of two Congress seats left vacant by Christy Vogt's resignation. The Herald reported the appointment in the same issue that covered the treasurer's budget presentation to Congress. The archive has found no further record of Pulman's time in the seat.

src.label: Herald 50:35, 7 Feb 1975, 'ASG congress hears treasurer's budget explanation'

officers.name: Beverly Davenport
officers.note: The 1975 Talisman records Davenport as representative-at-large on the ASG congress. In February 1975 she was one of two students appointed to the University Complaint Committee, alongside Suzanne Held and Ray Biggerstaff, an assistant professor in the health and safety department.
profile: Beverly Davenport, an Alpha Delta Pi sorority member, served as an ASG Congress representative-at-large in 1974-75, per the 1975 Talisman. In February 1975 the Herald reported she was one of two students appointed to the university's Complaint Committee, alongside fellow student Suzanne Held and assistant professor Ray Biggerstaff of the health and safety department.
No further record of her ASG term survives in this archive.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Alpha Delta Pi; Herald 50:35, 7 Feb 1975

officers.name: Christy Vogt
officers.note: Vogt sat in the ASG Congress in 1974-75 and resigned from it on 28 January 1975. The Herald reported that both the student affairs chairpersonship and a representative-at-large seat were vacated by her resignation and were filled the following week by presidential appointment. She returned the next year as administrative vice president, and the archive already records that term.

src.label: Herald 50:35, 7 Feb 1975, 'ASG congress hears treasurer's budget explanation'

members.name: Jo Ann Ballance
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Ballance as a sophomore class officer who held a seat on the student government, and quotes her arguing that an office amounting to building a float was not worth having and that two people could not represent a whole class. She favoured a student government made up only of representatives from the individual colleges.

members.name: Rodney Berry
members.seat: representative for the College of Business and Public Affairs
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Berry founding the Student Volunteer Bureau, which weakened for want of funds and administrators, and then approaching ASG president Jeff Consolo about folding it into ASG; the merger passed at the last meeting of the autumn semester by better than 80 per cent. A Lambda Chi Alpha chapter page in the same volume records him as having set up the bureau and served on student government.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Associated Student Government section; Greeks (Lambda Chi Alpha)

members.name: Thomas A. Blair
members.note: A Lambda Chi Alpha chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records Blair as serving on student government alongside Rodney Berry and Frank Medaris, and the senior directory gives his home as Bellbrook, Ohio. The volume confirms ASG membership but does not say which seat he held.

members.name: Paul Calico
members.note: A Sigma Nu chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records Calico as a representative-at-large to the student government.

members.name: Deborah DeJarnette
members.note: An Alpha Xi Delta chapter page in the 1975 Talisman names DeJarnette, Mary Pat Swift, Jennifer Rapp and Debbie Johnson as representatives for the Associated Student Government. The page confirms ASG membership but does not say which seat she held.

members.name: John Draheim
members.note: The 1975 Talisman pictures Draheim and Jo Ann Ballance, the sophomore class officers, comparing notes at an ASG meeting, under a caption saying that holding seats in the student government, rather than leading the class, was the main function of class officers.

members.name: Donna Filburn
members.note: A Kappa Delta chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records the sisters Donna and Debbie Filburn as both serving in the Associated Student Government, and Donna as Panhellenic president. A separate caption in the same volume names her Panhellenic Council president, conferring with ASG president Jeff Consolo.

src.label: 1975 Talisman, Greeks (Kappa Delta); Associated Student Government section

members.name: Gail Getchell
members.seat: representative for the College of Applied Arts and Health
members.note: Her Who's Who entry in the 1975 Talisman records the Lexington senior as a representative-at-large and a representative for the College of Applied Arts and Health in ASG, and as having served a term as president of the Panhellenic Council. The entry does not date the Panhellenic term.

members.name: Greg Goatley
members.note: His Who's Who entry in the 1975 Talisman names him a member of the Associated Student Government, along with chairman of the College Republicans, vice-chairman of the Kentucky College Republican Federation and campus coordinator for Marlow Cook's Senate campaign. He was a senior in 1974-75 and does not appear in the April 1974 returns; the entry summarises his career and does not date the term.

members.name: Tom Hayes
members.note: Ran on making the dorms more like home. The first of his reforms, passed by ASG in November 1974, provided a method by which residents could obtain change for vending machines, which resident assistants had not been allowed to give out. He suggested increasing the number of class officers while restricting voting rights to the president and vice-president.

members.name: Steve Henry
members.seat: elected member of the Associated Student Government
members.note: A Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records Henry and Stan McDivitt as elected members of the Associated Student Government. He was elected ASG president the following spring and served in 1975-76.

members.name: Larry Hooks
members.note: A Sigma Nu chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records Hooks as a representative for Ogden College.

members.name: Mike Inman
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Inman as senior class president with Pam Stewart as vice president, the only two to turn up at the class meeting called to organise Homecoming, and quotes him saying he ran for class office because it was the easiest way to get a seat in the student government. He proposed a bill to abolish class offices and create congress representatives for each class instead; ASG president Jeff Consolo opposed it.
profile: Mike Inman completed three consecutive years in the Associated Student Government Congress by way of class office, elected senior class president for 1974-75 with Pam Stewart as vice-president. The 1975 Talisman recorded that only the two of them attended the meeting called to organise the class's Homecoming contribution, for a class of 1,865, and that they rented the Harrodsburg Heritage mobile history unit rather than build a float.

The yearbook printed his own account of why he sought class office: he said it was the easiest route to a seat in the student government. He held the office itself to be of little consequence, since seniors had little class unity by then, and proposed a bill to abolish class officers and create congress representatives for each class instead. Student government president Jeff Consolo opposed the bill. Inman allowed that class officers carried slightly more standing than representatives-at-large, but argued there should be no distinction among members.

He was elected to Who's Who and was president of the Omicron Delta Kappa National Leadership Society. He was a member of the Scabbard and Blade military honour corps, and the same page records him as second runner-up for a national scholarship award the yearbook prints as Mayer-Raebum. Asked to name his chief accomplishment from a list that included the presidencies of his junior and senior classes, the vice-presidency of his sophomore class and a series of military science awards, he chose his involvement in ROTC, and said his campus activities had taught him more than his classes.

src2.label: 1975 Talisman, Who's Who, p. 95

src3.label: 1975 Talisman, Organizations (Scabbard and Blade), pp. 314-315

members.name: Debbie Johnson
members.note: An Alpha Xi Delta chapter page in the 1975 Talisman names Johnson among the sorority's representatives for the Associated Student Government. The same page separately lists a D. J. Johnson among the members, so the two names should not be treated as one person without a source that links them.

members.name: Jay Keffer
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Keffer and Tom Hayes as holding the only two freshman seats in the student government, and says both held that including class officers in the student government was essential.

members.name: Karen McNally
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records McNally as junior class vice president and quotes her saying students took no interest in class activities and that nobody came when class meetings were called. She argued that ASG needed more representatives-at-large.

members.name: Frank Mendaris
members.note: A Lambda Chi Alpha chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records him serving on student government with Rodney Berry and Tom Blair, spelling the surname Medaris, which matches the senior directory's Frank C. Medaris, Jr. The page confirms ASG membership but does not say which seat he held.

members.name: Hank Miles
members.note: The 1975 Talisman pictures Miles with Evie Shrewsbury, both graduate students, considering a programme issue at an ASG meeting, under a passage on college representatives conferring at meetings.

members.name: David Payne
members.note: An Alpha Kappa Psi chapter page in the 1975 Talisman records Payne, Andrew Carter and Don Colombero as serving on the Associated Student Government. The page does not say which seat he held. He was elected ASG treasurer the following spring and served in 1975-76 and again in 1976-77.

members.name: Jennifer Rapp
members.note: An Alpha Xi Delta chapter page in the 1975 Talisman names Rapp among the sorority's representatives for the Associated Student Government. She does not appear in the April 1974 returns, so any seat was filled later in the year; no second source has been found.

members.name: Evie Shrewsbury
members.note: The 1975 Talisman pictures Shrewsbury with Hank Miles, both graduate students, considering a programme issue at an ASG meeting, under a passage on college representatives conferring at meetings.

members.name: Pam Stewart
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Stewart as senior class vice president alongside president Mike Inman, the only two to turn up at the class meeting called to organise Homecoming. The 1974 Talisman separately records her as secretary of the Associated Student Government the year before.

members.name: Mary Pat Swift
members.note: An Alpha Xi Delta chapter page in the 1975 Talisman names Swift among the sorority's representatives for the Associated Student Government. The page does not say which seat she held.

members.name: Jeff Wampler
members.note: The 1975 Talisman records Wampler as junior class president with Karen McNally as vice president, says their main function was to attend meetings of the Associated Student Government, and reports both saying there was really no need for class officers.
profile: Jeff Wampler was elected junior class president for 1974-75, moving up from the sophomore class vice-presidency, with Karen McNally as his vice-president. The 1975 Talisman recorded that their main function as officers was to attend meetings of the Associated Student Government.

The same account recorded both officers saying there was really no need for class officers, even though they had worked hard to get elected. McNally said students took no interest in class activities and that nobody turned up when meetings were called; she offered no remedy beyond adding more representatives-at-large to the Associated Student Government. The judgement matched that of the senior class president the same year, Mike Inman, who put a bill to abolish class officers altogether.

The 1976 Talisman, covering his senior year, named him one of four Sigma Alpha Epsilon members elected to Who's Who, and printed his view that students and the administration both had to move toward each other before student apathy about elections and concerts would lift.

src2.label: 1976 Talisman, Greeks (Sigma Alpha Epsilon), p. 322

src3.label: 1976 Talisman, Student opinion, p. 88

leaders.name: Steve Henry
leaders.note: Likely the Steve Henry who later served as Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky (1995-2003). Wikipedia's biography of Stephen L. Henry (b. 8 Oct 1953) states he was elected WKU Student Body President "in his second attempt, after losing a close election the preceding year to Jeff Costello," and served on the WKU Board of Regents as a Kentucky resident while president - matching this record's own Herald sourcing almost exactly: Jeffrey Consolo (not "Costello", likely a Wikipedia transcription of the same name) won the presidency in spring 1974, and the Herald's 30 Apr 1976 wrap-up of Henry's term specifically describes him balancing the dual jobs of student regent and ASG president. The match in name, university, era, and this specific narrative beat is treated as verification, but the identification rests on a secondary source (Wikipedia), not a WKU archive document that states it outright - flagged here rather than treated as fully closed.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Steve Henry appeared in ASG coverage as early as September 1972, when the Herald reported his view that the Associated Student Government had lost respect.
Henry won the spring 1974 election on a ticket with Jeff Consolo, and resigned his post running the student discount program after the victory.

As president in 1975-76 Henry moved in November to change ASG's concert proposal after a money-losing fall season, while a student group urged support for his energy awareness plan. At year's end the Herald summed up his tenure with a piece on how the role had required balancing the twin jobs of student regent and ASG president, which he held at the same time.

A Wikipedia biography of Stephen L. Henry, later the 52nd Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky (1995-2003), describes an orthopedic surgeon and WKU alumnus who was elected Student Body President on his second attempt after an earlier loss, and who sat on the WKU Board of Regents as president - a career arc that lines up point for point with this record's own Herald sourcing, though no WKU archive document has yet been found that states the identification directly.

events.title: ASG suggests a campus bank
events.body: ASG suggested creating a campus bank for students, one of the new administration's early service proposals.

events.title: Budget approved amid concert debate
events.body: The ASG budget won approval as concerts were discussed, two weeks after the money-losing season opener had put the program under scrutiny.

events.title: Fund misuse charges aired
events.body: Charges of ASG fund misuse were heard in the same week the congress voted to create an activities committee and a letter writer attacked the organization.

events.title: A budget remedy and a book exchange
events.body: The Herald weighed whether a new ASG budget offered a remedy, and reported a spring semester book exchange to be co-sponsored by ASG and Veterans on Campus. President Steve Henry moved to change the concert proposal the same week.

events.title: Petition drive seeks support
events.body: ASG sought student support with a petition and prepared to hear appeals over its concert policy as the fall semester closed.

events.title: Election season and an acquittal
events.body: During the spring election season ASG acquitted congress member Gerard Faulk in an internal proceeding, and the Herald polled voters on the races.

events.title: Final meeting approves a budget
events.body: The congress approved a tentative budget at the final ASG meeting of the year, and the Herald assessed how Steve Henry's year had required balancing his twin jobs as student regent and ASG president.

events.title: Faulk impeachment hearings open as campaign begins
events.body: The Associated Student Government began impeachment hearings against congress member Gerard Faulk the same week candidates for the spring election, including Christy Vogt, were set to speak to students. An editorial the same issue held up Associated Student Government's troubles as a cautionary example for the university's newly forming Faculty Senate.

events.title: Christy Vogt wins the ASG presidency
events.body: The Herald reported Christy Vogt's win in the Associated Student Government presidential election under the headline "Christy Vogt Wins Election," with Vogt's own "Winner Says Thanks" running in the same issue. The paper reported the result the same week Gerard Faulk was acquitted in his impeachment case.

events.title: Bruce Smith and Christy Vogt survive the primary, 527 ballots cast
events.body: The Herald reported the Associated Student Government presidential primary under the headline "Bruce Smith, Christy Vogt Survive as 527 Cast Ballots," the two advancing to the 9 April runoff that Vogt went on to win.

events.title: Herald supplement recaps a year of ASG wins
events.body: A special supplement to the Herald, paid for and written by the Associated Student Government, summed up the outgoing Henry administration's year: women's hours abolished with ASG's backing, better intramural facilities credited to ASG resolutions, a new ASG discount card program, a second campus site for cashing checks, and a Veterans on Campus book exchange. The supplement also printed the year's roster of congress members and its bills and resolutions, and carried Christy Vogt's own piece on laundry facility improvement.

events.title: Regents add $16,000 to the entertainment budget and buy a second free concert
events.body: The Board of Regents passed a $16,000 increase in the ASG entertainment budget in August 1975. President Steve Henry said the increase allowed a second free concert and that he had never known one year to have two free concerts, much less two in a semester.
events.money: $16,000 increase in the ASG entertainment budget

events.title: Gove, Alex Harvey and Bottom and Company welcome students back
events.body: Two free concerts opened the fall semester to welcome students back, featuring Gove, Alex Harvey and Bottom and Company at the fine arts centre outdoor theatre. Harvey picked a dulcimer with a feather during his set.

events.title: ASG sponsors LAMB, a messianic music duo
events.body: On 11 September 1975 ASG sponsored LAMB, a duo specialising in messianic music, in Van Meter Auditorium. The Talisman noted the concert was well attended, perhaps because many students had writing assignments for MC 272 classes that required it.

events.title: Loggins and Messina open the season and lose $7,000
events.body: Kenny Loggins and Jim Messina played the first major concert of the year in Diddle Arena on Wednesday 17 September 1975, with the Amazing Rhythm Aces also on the bill. The crowd of 4,300 was too small and ASG lost about $7,000; activities vice president Rick Kelley blamed a lack of student body support. The Herald carried the loss two days later, and the argument over concert money it opened ran through the fall.

src2.label: Herald 51:7, 19 Sep 1975

events.title: Jules Bergman speaks on '2000 A.D. - The Way it Will Be'
events.body: ABC science editor Jules Bergman came to campus on 23 September 1975 for the first guest of the University Lecture Series, which the Talisman notes was also sponsored by ASG. Poor weather hurt the crowd; Bergman said man was adaptable enough to fly to the moon six times but could not endure much longer what he had created for himself on earth.

events.title: Doug Kershaw takes three encores in Homecoming week
events.body: ASG brought the Cajun fiddler Doug Kershaw for the Thursday night of Homecoming week, 30 October 1975. About 700 people saw him jump into the crowd to lead 'Jambalaya' and land in the lap of a startled coed in the fourth row; he took three encores and closed with 'Louisiana Man'.

events.title: Pat Paulsen returns for a free 'Lecture in Humor'
events.body: Pat Paulsen entertained a Diddle Arena crowd on Homecoming eve, 31 October 1975, at a free show sponsored by ASG. Presenting 'A Lecture in Humor', he traced the history of comedy from prehistoric times to the future and said he had found out you cannot speak your mind and expect to get elected.

events.title: Oliver and Jerico Harp play free to a sparse crowd
events.body: A sparse crowd attended the Oliver and Jerico Harp concert on Wednesday 3 December 1975. The Talisman described it as a freebie to students.

events.title: ASG and Veterans on Campus run a book exchange against the bookstore
events.body: To give students an alternative to the College Heights Bookstore, ASG co-sponsored a book exchange with Veterans on Campus from 12 to 26 January 1976. Administrative vice president Christy Vogt said the two groups had covered expenses by 21 January through the sale of over 600 books, with ASG and VOC making 25 cents on each book sold.
events.money: over 600 books sold; 25 cents profit per book

events.title: A second campus check-cashing facility opens after an ASG survey
events.body: An ASG survey at fall registration found that the most significant desire of students was a new check-cashing facility. A second campus check-cashing point opened in the customer service area of the bookstore on 26 January 1976 for nine hours a week, after the original proposal for a full-service campus bank branch was judged impractical by area bankers.

events.title: George Allen lectures on success and ambition
events.body: George Allen, head coach of the Washington Redskins, spoke in the Garrett Conference Center on 12 February 1976 in one of the spring ASG-sponsored lectures. He showed a film, answered questions on professional football and advised those facing a tight job market that the last thing to talk about when looking for a job is money.

events.title: Chris Miller of National Lampoon draws 1,100 and a rebuke from the dean
events.body: Chris Miller of National Lampoon drew about 1,100 people to the Garrett Conference Center on 24 February 1976 with a lecture titled 'Toe Sucking in Albania, or An Evening of Erotic Laughter'. Three days later the Herald reported that dean of student affairs Charles Keown had criticised ASG's taste in sponsoring the lecture.

events.title: George Wallace is fought over in committee and never appears
events.body: President Steve Henry reported a 99 per cent chance of getting George Wallace, then seeking the Democratic presidential nomination, to speak in April 1976. A subcommittee of ASG's Student Activities Committee voted 4-2 with one abstention on 6 February to strike Wallace from the list of lecturers on the grounds that the arrangements had been made improperly, ASG Congress overruled the resolution, and by 13 February the Herald reported the lecture was uncertain; no appearance is recorded.

events.title: Truman Capote lectures off the cuff
events.body: Truman Capote lectured on 21 April 1976. The Herald's account two days later reported that off-the-cuff remarks were the highlight.

events.title: ASG plans an activities grand finale
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG was planning an activities grand finale to end the year. The fortnight that followed carried the Truman Capote lecture, two teacher forums and the free James Taylor concert.

events.title: ASG to sponsor two teacher forums
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG would sponsor two teacher forums. They came at the end of a year in which ASG had also pushed through the academic complaint system.

events.title: ASG's own supplement counts the discount cards and the book exchange
events.body: In the Student Insight supplement it paid for and wrote itself, ASG set out its services for the year: the discount cards it sponsored, the book exchange run with Veterans on Campus which it called a success, and its work on laundry facilities and intramural facilities. Christy Vogt wrote the piece on laundry improvements and Elaine Boeckman the piece on the abolition of women's hours.

events.title: Laundry improvements take effect
events.body: From 15 April 1976 the university installed more washers and dryers, an air-conditioned study area and a laundry pick-up service, with dry cleaning by a local firm in the proposal. Steve Henry said he hoped the facilities, which ASG had proposed the previous October, would be long-lasting.

events.title: ASG sets up a Student Activities Committee to choose the acts
events.body: After a semester of argument over who should decide what came to campus, ASG adopted a Student Activities Committee to bring more student opinion into the booking and publicising of concerts and lecturers. Seventeen members were chosen from 63 applicants and divided into three sub-committees: seven for concerts with three alternates, and five each for lectures and publicity with two alternates apiece. Activities vice-president Rick Kelley said the committee was formed to widen student say over booking and publicity. The dispute behind it lingered from the ASG meeting of 2 December 1975 and sharpened when assistant dean of student affairs Ron Beck argued that any programme the university presented ought to have educational value; students wrote to the Herald against him. The yearbook gives no date for the committee's adoption, only that it was in place in time to help bring the free Spinners and Wet Willie concert of 30 January 1976.

src.label: 1976 Talisman, Concerts, Lectures and student activities

events.title: Linda Ronstadt's Homecoming concert nets ASG $4,300
events.body: Linda Ronstadt played the Homecoming concert in Diddle Arena on Saturday 1 November 1975, opening with "Colorado", with Goose Creek Symphony before her and Andrew Gold as her backup group. The 1976 Talisman put the crowd at about 6,500 and the profit to ASG at $4,300, and reported that activities vice-president Rick Kelley and ASG president Steve Henry rated it among the most successful concerts in years - successful enough, the yearbook said, to guarantee a free Spinners and Wet Willie concert for students on 30 January. The yearbook is not consistent on the crowd: its concerts section gives 6,500 and its Homecoming section 6,300.
events.money: netted $4,300 for ASG; attendance about 6,500, though the same yearbook's opening section gives 6,300

events.title: James Taylor plays a free concert to close the year
events.body: The Herald of 20 April 1976 billed James Taylor for a free concert that Friday, and the issue of 23 April told readers the performance would be that night. The next issue, 27 April, carried Tip Shanklin's review under the headline "Evening with James Taylor Well Spent", so the concert took place. The 1976 Talisman listed James Taylor among the year's concerts but, before the event, recorded only that he was scheduled to give a free concert in April.

events.title: ASG sponsored Natalie Cole in Van Meter
events.body: The Herald reported on 9 December 1975 that Associated Student Government would sponsor a concert by the jazz vocalist Natalie Cole. The 1976 Talisman records that Cole, daughter of the late Nat King Cole, performed in Van Meter Auditorium on 10 December to an estimated crowd of 325, singing 'This Will Be', 'Killing Me Softly With His Song', 'Honky Tonk Women' and 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life'.

src.label: 1976 Talisman, Concerts; announced in College Heights Herald 51:29, 9 Dec 1975

events.title: Charles Berlitz opens the ASG lecture series on the Bermuda Triangle
events.body: Charles Berlitz, author of The Bermuda Triangle, opened the Associated Student Government lecture series in Van Meter Auditorium on 9 September 1975. The Herald carried the advance notice that morning; the 1976 Talisman reported a standing-room-only audience and recorded that Berlitz said more than 100 planes and ships and 1,000 people had vanished in the region since 1945, and that he ran through theories from heavy magnetisation to alien beings.

src2.label: 1976 Talisman, p. 52

events.title: The Spinners and Wet Willie drew 7,500 to a free concert
events.body: The Spinners and Wet Willie played free to students on 30 January 1976 before a crowd of 7,500, the second straight major ASG promotion to make money. It was the first concert the new Student Activities Committee helped bring about. The Spinners worked impressions of the Ink Spots, the Mills Brothers, Tom Jones, the Miracles and Elvis Presley into the set, donned wigs for the Supremes, and came back for two encores.

src2.label: 1976 Talisman, Concerts and student activities

events.title: Constitutional abuses alleged against Rick Kelley
events.body: Jay Wethington and Roger Harris reported in the Herald of 3 October 1975 that constitutional abuses had been alleged against Rick Kelley, ASG's activities vice president. The archive does not hold the article's text, so what was alleged and whether it was resolved are not established.

events.title: Judicial Council chairman Gerard Faulk faces impeachment action
events.body: The Herald of 19 March 1976 reported, in a story by Alfina Mami, that Judicial Council chairman Gerard Faulk faced a move to impeach him. The archive does not hold the article's text, so who brought the action, on what grounds, and how Congress responded are not established from this source.

executive.name: Christy Vogt
executive.note: Vogt was ASG administrative vice president in 1975-76. She ran the book exchange ASG co-sponsored with Veterans on Campus from 12 to 26 January 1976, reporting that the two groups had covered expenses by 21 January on sales of over 600 books at a margin of 25 cents a book. She said the executive officers were closer than in any past administration she had witnessed.
profile: Before she became administrative vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1975-76, Christy Vogt had already spent two years working her way up through ASG. A Talisman profile of Vogt recorded that she came to Western from Angela Merici High School in Louisville, where she had served four years on student council and been both its vice president and president; as a Western freshman she ran for and won freshman vice president, then as a sophomore was elected an ASG representative-at-large before President Jeff Consolo appointed her student affairs chairman. She ran for administrative vice president with about a week left before the spring 1975 election and won.

In office, Vogt ran the book exchange ASG co-sponsored with Veterans on Campus from 12 to 26 January 1976, reporting that the two groups had covered their expenses by 21 January on sales of more than 600 books at a margin of 25 cents a book. She said the year's executive officers were closer than in any administration she had witnessed, crediting President Steve Henry for not minding which officer brought him ideas directly. She told the Talisman there was a 90 percent chance she would run for the ASG presidency in 1976-77; she did, and won. Her term as president is recorded separately, under 1976-77.

executive.name: David Payne
executive.note: Payne was ASG treasurer in 1975-76. Congress member Marc Levy brought charges against him for spending before budget approval had been given, and Levy appeared twice before the Judicial Council. Payne argued the constitution provided for such spending and the council ruled in his favour. Note for the editor: years.json separately carries a David Payne who succeeded Marcel Bush as ASG president in January 1982, filed under 1981-82 (not 1982-83) with year_confidence "corrected" - Board of Regents minutes of 30 January 1982 already confirm that identification, so he is not simply an unresolved name. Whether the 1981-82 president is the same person as this 1970s ASG treasurer is not established by any source found so far, and this archive should not merge them without one that links them.
profile: David Payne was treasurer of the Associated Student Government for 1975-76, a job he described to the 1976 Talisman as "simple record keeping": reviewing the past year's records, planning a budget, getting it approved, vouching for payments, advising the ASG president on finances and preparing an expenditure report each semester. Congress member Marc Levy brought charges against him that year for spending before budget approval had been given, and appeared twice before the Judicial Council to press the case; Payne argued the ASG constitution provided for such spending, and the council ruled in his favour.

Note for the editor: years.json separately carries a David Payne who succeeded Marcel Bush as ASG president in January 1982, filed under 1981-82 (not 1982-83) with year_confidence "corrected" - Board of Regents minutes of 30 January 1982 already confirm that identification, so he is not simply an unresolved name. This Payne was re-elected treasurer for a second term in 1976-77, recorded there. Whether the 1981-82 president is the same person as this 1970s ASG treasurer is not established by any source found so far, and this archive should not merge them without one that links them.

executive.name: Nancy Wilk
executive.note: Wilk was ASG secretary in 1975-76 and kept the attendance roll the yearbook printed in full, effective 6 April 1976. She explained the rule: a warning after four absences and automatic removal from Congress after two more. The printed roll names some fifty Congress members and marks Mitchell Deep as resigned.
profile: Nancy Wilk was secretary of the Associated Student Government for 1975-76 and kept the attendance roll the 1976 Talisman printed in full, effective 6 April 1976. She explained the rule to the yearbook: a member received a warning after four absences and was automatically removed from Congress after two more. The printed roll named roughly fifty Congress members and marked Mitchell Deep as resigned.

executive.name: Rick Kelley
executive.note: Kelley was ASG activities vice president in 1975-76. He introduced a bill in October creating a student activities committee, whose members were chosen in December from open applications and which ran three subcommittees for concerts, lectures and special events and publicity. The volume credits the year's concerts with turning a profit of around $4,300 for ASG. His surname is printed both Kelley and Kelly in the same volume; the spelling is not settled.
profile: Rick Kelley was activities vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1975-76, the first of two consecutive terms in the office. In October he introduced a bill creating a student activities committee; members were chosen in December from open applications, and the committee ran three subcommittees covering concerts, lectures, and special events and publicity, meant to bring more student input into the entertainment program after controversy over past concert bookings. The 1976 Talisman credits the Homecoming concert by Linda Ronstadt, on 1 November 1975, with a $4,300 profit for ASG, calling it a tremendous financial success that kept ASG in the black; an earlier concert that September by Kenny Loggins and Jim Messina, by contrast, lost about $7,000 to poor attendance. His surname is printed both Kelley and Kelly in the same volume; the spelling is not settled.

officers.name: Gerard Faulk
officers.note: Six congressmen moved on 16 March 1976 to impeach Faulk over his handling of two cases sent to the Judicial Council, one on Tom Blair's allegation that President Steve Henry had obstructed an advisory intramurals committee and one on Marc Levy's misuse-of-funds charge against treasurer David Payne. Congress acquitted him on 6 April 1976. The Herald reported his was a two-year term that would run into the 1976-77 session.
profile: Gerard Faulk, an elementary education major, chaired ASG's Judicial Council beginning in 1975-76, a post the Herald reported carried a two-year term running into the 1976-77 session. Six members of Congress moved to impeach him on 16 March 1976 over his handling of two cases before the council: Tom Blair's allegation that president Steve Henry had obstructed an advisory intramurals committee, and Marc Levy's charge that treasurer David Payne had misused funds. Congress held hearings, postponed a vote once, and acquitted Faulk on 6 April 1976. No later report of a successor has been found in this archive.

officers.name: Jane Anne Coverdale
officers.note: ASG's own Student Insight supplement credited Coverdale and her committee with contracting 29 local discounts by the end of December 1975; the 1976 discount cards were then mailed to all Western students.
profile: Jane Anne Coverdale chaired Associated Student Government's Student Discount Service committee in 1975-76. ASG's own Student Insight supplement to the Herald, published 27 April 1976, credited Coverdale and her committee with contracting 29 local business discounts by the end of December 1975; the 1976 discount cards drawing on that work were then mailed to every Western student.

The 1976 Talisman's Kappa Delta sorority page separately named Coverdale among the chapter's outstanding members as an Associated Student Government representative and noted she had been elected to Who's Who Among Students in American Universities and Colleges that year.

src.label: Student Insight, supplement to the Herald, 27 Apr 1976

officers.name: Susan Hurley
officers.note: Hurley co-chaired the housing committee that visited the campus laundry, surveyed students and drafted the laundry resolution Congress passed and sent to the university committee President Dero Downing had appointed.
profile: Susan Hurley co-chaired Associated Student Government's housing committee in 1975-76. ASG's Student Insight supplement to the Herald, 27 April 1976, credited the committee she co-chaired with visiting the campus laundry, surveying students on its condition, and drafting the resulting laundry resolution, which Congress passed and forwarded to the university committee President Dero Downing had appointed to study the issue.
The 1976 Talisman's Chi Omega sorority page separately listed Hurley among the chapter members serving as an Associated Student Government representative that year.

officers.name: Scott Taylor
officers.note: Taylor co-chaired the housing committee with Susan Hurley on the laundry resolution. He is separately listed in the same supplement's Congress roster as a representative-at-large.
profile: Taylor, a member of the Pi Kappa Alpha fraternity, served in 1975-76 as an Associated Student Government representative-at-large and co-chaired the housing committee with Susan Hurley on the laundry resolution. The 1976 Talisman independently describes him as a Pike "representative to the Associated Student Government."
Congress's own attendance roster for the year lists him among the members tracked for meetings missed.
