documents.title: ASG minutes, 24 April 1979
documents.summary: The outgoing 1978-79 Congress's final meeting, with 34 members present. Four resolutions passed, the new constitution was reported ratified, and the incoming officers for 1979-80 were sworn in, with Jamie Hargrove taking the gavel as the new president.
documents.extract: The new officers for 1979-80 were officially sworn in.

leaders.name: James Hargrove
leaders.note: The plaque reads "James Hargroave". The Herald called him Jamie Hargrove throughout 1979-80, and SGA's own roster of former presidents, archived in September 2001, lists "James Earl Hargrove, Milton" and stars him as a student regent. Two independent sources against the plaque's spelling, so this site follows them. Surname spelling on the plaque is HARGROAVE. The Herald, in a 30 August 1979 profile calling him ASG Head at the start of the year, spells the name 'Jamie Hargrove.' Flagging the discrepancy rather than silently correcting the plaque spelling, per project rule.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Hargrove, a Milton junior, won the ASG presidency in the 17 April 1979 general election, defeating David Young 1,087-535 on a turnout of 1,725 votes. The same day's balloting elected the rest of his executive slate: Steve Fuller administrative vice president, Dean Bates activities vice president, Betty Thompson secretary and Terri Craig treasurer. All five were sworn in at the outgoing Congress's 24 April meeting, where Congress waived its rules so that Hargrove's first act as president, a resolution asking that Helm-Cravens Library stay open longer, could pass unanimously the same night. By August 30, 1979, at the start of the school year, the Herald profiled him - spelled 'Jamie Hargrove' in the byline - under the headline that he believed students were interested.

Beyond the executive roster now on record, the archive does not yet show in detail what Hargrove's administration passed or fought over during 1979-80, beyond the record's general sweep of the year. Further Herald issues from the fall and spring semester have not yet been checked.

events.title: 830 students vote in the ASG primary; the Herald runs a defence of not voting
events.body: The Associated Student Government's spring primary drew 830 voters and put the open-house policy on the ballot. The same issue carried a piece justifying student apathy in ASG voting - the paper had moved from scolding non-voters to explaining them. This primary elected the officers who took office for 1979-80; it was previously misfiled under 1978-79.

events.title: Donald Zacharias sworn in as WKU's sixth president
events.body: Zacharias, previously executive assistant to the chancellor of the University of Texas system, took office as WKU's sixth president at the opening of the academic year; he was formally installed the following spring.

events.title: ASG head Jamie Hargrove profiled at year's start
events.body: The Herald profiled the Associated Student Government head under the headline that he believed students were interested, in the same issue that introduced the new president's wife, Tommie Zacharias, to campus.

events.title: ASG weighs expanding hall representation
events.body: The Associated Student Government considered expanding residence hall representation in its congress, in the same issue reporting the Board of Regents set to consider a two-year budget request.

events.title: Resolution 79-10 seeks staff for scholarship administration
events.body: The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 79-10, urging the university to assign staff to administer academic scholarships.

events.title: Hargrove opens the year saying students are interested
events.body: Associated Student Government head Jamie Hargrove told the Herald he believed students were interested in their government as the year opened. A week later ASG heard its 1979-80 budget and discussed changing its delegate policy.

events.title: Seats bill passes after revision under pressure
events.body: A bill on Associated Student Government seats passed after being revised under pressure, expanding on earlier talk of broader residence hall representation. The Herald called the representation bill a small step in the right direction.

events.title: ASG rejects move to close Diddle Hall
events.body: The Associated Student Government rejected a move to close Diddle Hall dormitory. The vote came amid a fall of housing debates that later included a push to make Keen Hall a coed dorm.

events.title: ASG proposes an activity fee for part-time students
events.body: ASG proposed a part-time student activity fee. The proposal came as the Board of Regents weighed budget requests for the coming biennium.

events.title: ASG considers moving its spring elections
events.body: The Associated Student Government considered changing the date of its spring elections. The discussion took place against campus anger over a proposed tuition increase.

events.title: Fuller and Irons win the presidential primary
events.body: Steve Fuller and Tim Irons emerged as victors in the ASG presidential primary, from a field of three that also included David Rue. Candidates had been certified earlier in the month.

events.title: Steve Fuller elected ASG president
events.body: Steve Fuller, Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to the top Associated Student Government jobs. The Herald wrote that persistence had paid off in Fuller's campaign, while runner-up Tim Irons looked to the future after losing.

events.title: New ASG officers and members sworn in
events.body: The new Associated Student Government officers and members were sworn in. ASG and the Interhall Council were also conducting student polls as the year closed.

events.title: ASG replaces concerts with opinion polls and a radio phone-in
events.body: Stripped of entertainment, ASG spent the year on student opinion polls, a phone-in programme on the campus station WKYU where President Jamie Hargrove answered questions, and expanded publicity for its own elections. Hargrove said the transfer of activities to the University Center Board had cost ASG between $60,000 and $70,000 of budget but no real power. Poll committee chairman Kevin Kinne said the university administration was showing a lot of support for the polls.
events.money: $60,000 to $70,000 of activities budget lost to the Center Board

events.title: ASG asks the bookstore to break even on books
events.body: ASG introduced a bill asking the College Heights Bookstore to adopt a break-even policy on book sales, arguing that the store had a monopoly on textbooks and that the College Heights Foundation which runs it is a non-profit organisation. Congress was to vote on it the following week. At the same meeting congress formed an ad hoc committee on university food services.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 55, No. 34, 31 January 1980

events.title: ASG asked the state to seat a student on the higher education council
events.body: Resolution 79-6, dated 25 September 1979, called for a student representative to be included on the Kentucky Council on Higher Education. It is the earliest dated piece of legislation held for the 1979-80 session in SGA's own archive, and it set the tone of a year in which the organisation, stripped of its entertainment budget, turned to academic and state-level questions.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-6, Student on Council of Higher Education

events.title: ASG announced it would run student opinion polls
events.body: The Herald of 4 October 1979 carried a notice that Associated Student Government opinion polls were planned. This is the announcement, not a report of any poll: it proves what was set up, not what came back. The polls became the signature project of Jamie Hargrove's term, run by a committee under Kevin Kinne, and by the following September the Herald was reporting the first results.

events.title: ASG proposed cutting special benefits for athletes
events.body: Ken Morris reported that an ASG proposal would reduce special benefits for athletes. The same issue carried the report by Morris and Tim Fish that favouritism had been alleged in the plans for the Homecoming dance, and news that Western had been denied construction funds.

events.title: The Homecoming edition ran a history of student government
events.body: Tom Beshear wrote a feature for the Homecoming edition under the line that student government had grown as the university expanded. It ran in an issue given over to campus history, alongside pieces on Hugh Poland, on how the Second World War left Western with few men, on the naming of the Herald and the Talisman, and on the old Fort Bridge.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Homecoming edition, 25 October 1979

events.title: A $250 grant to a fraternity drew charges of favouritism
events.body: Low attendance at the Saturday night Homecoming dance left the sponsoring fraternity, Sigma Chi, out of pocket, and the University Center Board gave the group $250. The Talisman reported that the payment prompted allegations of favouritism because ASG president Jamie Hargrove sat on the centre board and was a former Sigma Chi president. The Herald had already reported on 18 October that favouritism was alleged in the plans for the dance. The yearbook records the allegation only: it names no complainant, reports no finding, and no resolution of the matter appears in the digitised index.

events.title: A resignation was clarified in the Herald
events.body: Lisa Hunn wrote to the Herald under the heading that a resignation from the Associated Student Government had been clarified. The digitised index records the letter and its subject but names nobody, so who resigned and why is not established here.

events.title: A library book drop for Downing University Center
events.body: Resolution 79-12, dated 13 November 1979, asked for a library book drop to be installed in the Downing University Center so students would not have to walk to the library to return books. It was one of four resolutions filed that night, with the scholarship staffing resolution 79-10 and the part-time activity fee resolution 79-11. ASG asked again two years later, in Resolution 81-4 of September 1981.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-12, Book Drop in Downing University Center

events.title: ASG asked for an ice skating rink
events.body: Resolution 79-13, dated 13 November 1979, asked the university to build a skating rink. SGA's archive holds the document and describes it in a single line, and the Herald of 7 February 1980 carried an item on an ice skating rink. Nothing in the record says the rink was ever built.

events.title: ASG asked that Keen Hall be made a coed dorm
events.body: Karen Owen reported that ASG wanted Keen Hall turned into a coed dormitory. The request is Resolution 79-9, dated 30 October 1979 in SGA's own archive under the title Keen Hall Conversion. It came in the same autumn in which the congress refused to back closing Diddle Hall, and coed housing did not reach the Board of Regents until February 1984.

events.title: Hargrove said ASG had laid foundations
events.body: Michele Wood reported Jamie Hargrove's assessment at the halfway point of his term, that the Associated Student Government had laid foundations. The same issue reported that open house hours had been increased to 31 a week, the policy question ASG had spent the autumn surveying other universities about.

events.title: ASG backed the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act
events.body: Resolution 79-16, dated 5 February 1980 and filed under the name Ultra Extension Support, put ASG behind the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act. Michele Wood reported ASG's support for the tenants' rights bill in the Herald of 7 February, in an issue that also carried a letter from Marion Tabor crediting ASG for its survey work. Off-campus housing stayed on the agenda into the next session, when Resolution 80-34 set out the duties of ASG's off-campus representatives in landlord and tenant disputes.

events.title: ASG moved to create a vice president for public affairs
events.body: Resolution 79-18, dated 26 February 1980, supported amending the ASG constitution to add a vice president of public affairs. It failed within a fortnight: on 13 March Michele Wood reported that the proposal for a new congress position had been rejected. The office was still unsettled the following autumn, when Resolution 80-14 of 21 October 1980 carried the same title again.

src.label: SGA Resolution 79-18, Public Affairs Vice President

events.title: A bill would have changed the activities officer's duties
events.body: Michele Wood reported a bill to change the duties of the ASG activities officer, and two days later the Herald reported the activities office ready for change. The office was the last remnant of the entertainment function the Board of Regents had moved to the University Center Board the previous spring, taking between $60,000 and $70,000 of ASG's budget with it.

events.title: The student seat on the state council was refused
events.body: Michele Wood reported that a student seat on the Council on Higher Education had been denied. It was the answer to Resolution 79-6, which ASG had passed on 25 September 1979 asking for exactly that. The same issue reported that few tickets remained for the NCAA tournament.

events.title: ASG wrote rules for campaign spending, and for withdrawals
events.body: Resolution 79-22, dated 8 April 1980, dealt with campaign budgets for ASG elections, and the same night's Resolution 79-23 addressed withdrawal periods and deficiency reports. The spending cap became a live argument the following year, when the congress voted in September 1981 to raise it.

events.title: ASG proposed a longer period for dropping classes
events.body: Michele Wood reported that ASG had proposed lengthening the time students had to drop a class. It ran in the same issue that named Steve Fuller, David Rue and Tim Irons as the three candidates for the presidency.

events.title: The Herald called the centre board seat a burden on ASG
events.body: The Herald's editorial page argued that the University Center Board position was a burden for the Associated Student Government, and Roland Gibbons drew a cartoon of the centre board against ASG in the same issue. ASG had lost campus entertainment to the centre board the previous spring but its president still sat on it, which was what had made the Homecoming dance grant so awkward.

events.title: ASG printed a candidate pamphlet for the spring election
events.body: After the primary, ASG distributed pamphlets carrying a photograph of each executive office candidate and a short statement written by the candidate on their qualifications and plans. President Jamie Hargrove said ASG was moving away from leaving publicity to the candidates and treating turnout as its own responsibility. Rules and elections committee chairman Tim Irons said voters had stayed away in the past because ASG had not told them where the voting tables were or how to use them. The Talisman does not give the exact date the pamphlets went out; the primary was on 17 April and the general election on 24 April.

events.title: Hargrove went to the White House to meet President Carter
events.body: ASG president Jamie Hargrove was invited, with about 250 other student leaders, to the White House to discuss foreign and domestic issues with President Jimmy Carter. Hargrove told the Talisman that draft registration and energy policy were the main subjects of his meetings with Carter and some of his senior advisers, and that the purpose of the meeting was to explain why the administration was taking the actions it was taking. The yearbook does not give the date of the visit.

events.title: ASG surveyed 28 universities on open house hours
events.body: ASG surveyed 28 institutions comparable to Western and found that Western's open house policy gave the fewest visitation hours per semester of any of them. The Herald reported the finding on 27 September 1979 under the line that Western came last in a 28-college housing poll. ASG also published the results of the previous spring's open house referendum, which showed a majority of students surveyed wanted weekly open houses. The policy finally adopted came from the student affairs office rather than from ASG.

events.title: The first resolution against room inspections
events.body: Resolution 80-1, dated 6 May 1980, was a resolution to stop room inspections. It opens the fight that dominated the next academic year, in which ASG twice voted down bills to abolish the inspections, the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union took the question towards a federal court, and the congress instead approved stricter rules for entering rooms.

src.label: SGA Resolution 80-1, Permission for Room Inspection

events.title: New ASG officers sworn in; Hargrove's first resolution passed
events.body: At its 24 April 1979 meeting, ASG's outgoing 1978-79 Congress passed four housing and parking resolutions and then swore in the newly elected 1979-80 officers: president Jamie Hargrove, administrative vice president Steve Fuller, activities vice president Dean Bates, secretary Betty Thompson and treasurer Terri Craig. Congress then voted to waive its rules and passed unanimously the new administration's first resolution, written by Hargrove, asking that Helm-Cravens Library stay open longer.

committees.name: Student Opinion Poll Committee
committees.note: Chaired ASG's student opinion poll committee under President Jamie Hargrove; also quoted criticizing apathy in congress and expecting Hargrove's new congress appointments to improve it. The text never calls him a representative or seated congress member this year, only a committee chairman.

committees.name: Rules and Elections Committee
committees.note: Chaired ASG's rules and elections committee and was quoted on low voter awareness and turnout in that spring's ASG elections. The text does not state he held a congress seat.

senate.note: A constitutional amendment this year replaced the 24 representatives-at-large with 24 seats split three ways: eight on-campus, eight off-campus and eight general-representative. The Herald covered the change as it moved through Congress that September (see the 13 and 20 September 1979 events, above); the 1980 Talisman's year-end account, p. 274, is the only source found naming the new three-way split itself. No roster of who held the new seats has been located.

executive.name: Steve Fuller
executive.note: A Bowling Green junior, elected 17 April 1979, defeating Tom Jecker, a Louisville senior, 973-574. At the 24 April swearing-in he urged Congress members to think about which committees they wanted to serve on.

src2.label: ASG Minutes, 24 Apr 1979

profile: Fuller was elected Administrative Vice President on 17 April 1979, defeating Tom Jecker, a Louisville senior, 973 votes to 574, the same election that sent Jamie Hargrove to the presidency. At the Congress's 24 April 1979 swearing-in he urged the incoming members to think about which committees they wanted to serve on.
He was elected Associated Student Government president the following spring, taking office for 1980-81.

executive.name: Dean Bates
executive.note: A Fairport, N.Y., junior, elected 17 April 1979, defeating Ben Bratcher, a Louisville senior, 785-761 - the closest of the four executive-office races. At the 24 April swearing-in he announced that applications were open for the University Center Board.
profile: Dean Bates, a junior from Fairport, N.Y., was elected Activities Vice President of Associated Student Government on 17 April 1979, defeating Ben Bratcher of Louisville 785-761, the closest of the year's four executive races. At the 24 April swearing-in he told Congress applications were open for seats on the University Center Board, the body the Board of Regents had handed control of campus entertainment three weeks earlier.

In February 1980 the Herald carried a piece under his byline headlined "Coffee House a Success." The 1980 Talisman's senior class listing records him as an environmental engineering technology major from Fairport, N.Y., confirming the hometown given in the election coverage.

executive.note: A Bowling Green junior, elected 17 April 1979, defeating Lynn Driver, a Goodlettsville, Tenn., sophomore, 1,052-517. She signed the minutes of the 24 April 1979 swearing-in meeting as secretary.
profile: Betty Thompson, a junior from Bowling Green, was elected Secretary of Associated Student Government on 17 April 1979, defeating Lynn Driver of Goodlettsville, Tenn., 1,052-517. She signed the minutes of the 24 April 1979 swearing-in meeting in that office.

executive.name: Terri Craig
executive.note: A St. Joseph, Ill., junior, elected 17 April 1979, defeating Darell Pierce, a Louisville junior, 937-623. At the 24 April swearing-in she moved to waive ASG's rules so Hargrove's first resolution could be voted on immediately, and told Congress she would be drafting the new budget.
profile: Terri Craig, a junior from St. Joseph, Ill., was elected Treasurer of Associated Student Government on 17 April 1979, defeating Darell Pierce of Louisville 937-623. Weeks earlier, the Herald had reported that she and Steve Thornton were elected to the Executive Council of the Student Government Association of Kentucky, a statewide body, ahead of her own ASG win. At the 24 April 1979 swearing-in she moved to waive ASG's rules so that newly sworn-in president James Hargrove's first resolution could be voted on immediately, and told Congress she would be drafting the year's budget.

leaders.name: Steven Fuller
leaders.note: Herald bylines consistently call him "Steve Fuller"; the plaque and this site list "Steven Fuller" - spelling unverified.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Steve Fuller entered the April 1980 Associated Student Government presidential race against David Rue and Tim Irons; the Herald covered ASG hopefuls debating the issues at an April 3 candidates' forum before reporting the three-way field on April 10.

Fuller won the presidency in the April 24 election, reported under the headline "Persistence Pays Off in Steve Fuller Campaign." Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to other top ASG offices the same day; Tim Irons's loss was covered separately.

Fuller's fall term was consumed by a running fight over dormitory room inspections. A September 4 inspection measure was voted down amid criticism of how the vote was conducted; a September 11 bill calling for a ban on bugs in the dorms drew a mocking editorial cartoon and an editorial calling the university's protective inspection policy unnecessary; and by November 13 the Herald reported ASG had nearly slept through its own vote before re-endorsing inspections, followed a week later by a bill proposing a stricter room-entry rule.

In office, ASG under Fuller also proposed a change to the organization's own title in October 1980 and asked the state to evaluate higher education funding in February 1981, as budget worries dominated the legislative session. His successor, Marcel Bush, was elected that April.

Fuller entered the Associated Student Government presidential race in the spring of 1980 as one of three candidates. Michele Wood's Herald report was headlined "3 Running for Associated Student Government President," naming Steve Fuller, David Rue and Tim Irons.

During the 1980-81 year the Associated Student Government pressed the state on the condition of higher education, with Robert Pillow reporting in February 1981 that the body had asked the state to conduct an evaluation. The request came as the campus argued over budget cuts, including cuts to athletics.

events.title: ASG proposes a title change
events.body: The Associated Student Government proposed a title change for the organization. The proposal surfaced in the same week campus activities were limited for the national election day.

events.title: Sturgeon and Bush win the ASG primary
events.body: David Sturgeon and Marcel Bush won the Associated Student Government primary, in a campaign the Herald said saw candidates playing big time politics. The same issue carried a resolution asking for a new ASG logo.

events.title: Bush defeats Sturgeon for the presidency
events.body: David Sturgeon was defeated in the Associated Student Government race, leaving Marcel Bush the winner after endorsements had split between the two. The congress also voted to keep the present ASG logo.

events.title: Close races prompt ASG recounts
events.body: Close races prompted recounts in the Associated Student Government election. The recounts came in the same week the Council on Higher Education approved a tuition increase.

events.title: ASG changes its mind on changing minds
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government changed its mind on changing minds, capping a contentious election month. The same issue covered a withdrawn regent selection and the board's study of reorganizing the university.

events.title: Three seek the ASG presidency
events.body: Steve Fuller, David Rue and Tim Irons entered the race for Associated Student Government president.

events.title: Fuller elected ASG president
events.body: Steve Fuller won the Associated Student Government presidency over David Rue and Tim Irons. Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to other top ASG offices the same day.

events.title: ASG hopefuls debate the issues; ASG weighs opposing a UCB change
events.body: Associated Student Government presidential hopefuls discussed the issues and courted votes at a candidates' forum ahead of the spring election. The same issue reported ASG considering opposition to a proposed change to the University Center Board's structure.

events.title: ASG room inspection measure defeated amid criticism
events.body: A proposed ASG measure on dormitory room inspections was voted down, in a session a separate Herald article criticized for how the vote was conducted. The defeat opened a fall-long fight over dorm inspection policy.

events.title: ASG bill targets pests in the dorms
events.body: ASG introduced a bill calling for a ban on bugs in residence halls; the Herald's editorial cartoon depicted a cockroach imperiled by the resolution. The paper's editorial page separately argued the university's protective inspection policy was unnecessary.

events.title: ASG re-endorses dorm inspections after nearly missing the vote
events.body: ASG voted to re-endorse dormitory room inspections, in a session the Herald reported the government had nearly slept through. The same issue covered ASG's sponsorship of an international film and dance series and an attorney's interest in a dorm inspection case.

events.title: ASG bill proposes a stricter room-entry rule
events.body: ASG introduced a bill proposing a stricter rule governing staff entry into student rooms, continuing the fall's running fight over dormitory inspections.

events.title: Resolution 80-32 asks for change machines in the dorms
events.body: ASG passed Resolution 80-32, requesting that change machines be installed in residence halls.

events.title: International Food Fest and fashion show
events.body: In the spring semester ASG followed International Week with an International Food Fest and fashion show. International students committee chairman Osama Sharif, a junior from Jerusalem, said attendance at the autumn programmes had been very good and that they were well put together. The Talisman called International Week the highlight of ASG's autumn semester.

events.title: ASG's car pool match-up
events.body: ASG ran a car pool match-up scheme jointly with the Barren River Area Development District and hoped to continue it. Almost 450 students took part across the two semesters. It was one of the few concrete services the organisation carried through in a year the Talisman headlined as a year of resolutions.

events.title: ASG's International Week
events.body: Associated Student Government sponsored International Week, which ran nightly from Monday 10 November 1980 and closed with a presentation on Brazil and Colombia on the Thursday evening. Two or three countries were featured each night through films, lectures, folk dances and slides given by students and faculty from those countries, and programme chairman Osama Sharif opened the week with a talk on Palestine and a Red Cross film on Palestinian children. The 1981 Talisman, which spells him Sharif and calls him international students committee chairman, credits the week to student government and the International Students Committee, places the nightly programmes in the university center, and lists nine countries: Switzerland, Palestine, Iceland, Malaysia, Colombia, Brazil, India, Pakistan and France.

src2.label: 1981 Talisman, "A year of resolutions", pp. 282-83

events.title: ASG asked the state to evaluate higher education
events.body: The Associated Student Government called on the state to carry out an evaluation of higher education. Robert Pillow reported the request in the Herald of 5 February 1981, an issue dominated by budget pressure across Kentucky's universities and by controversy over cuts to the athletic budget.

events.title: The ASG president also held the student regent seat
events.body: The 1980 Talisman's account of the Board of Regents records that ASG president Steve Fuller was also sworn in as student regent, in the same passage reporting the board's budget, two regent appointments and $66,000 of university money for renovating the president's home. The two offices were separated during the next session: after Marcel Bush resigned in January 1982 the seat went to a campus-wide election, and Sandra Norfleet won the runoff in February 1982.

events.title: Fuller opened the year wanting a stronger voice in policy
events.body: Diane Comer reported in the Herald's back-to-school issue that the Associated Student Government wanted a stronger voice in policy making. It was the opening statement of Steve Fuller's term, and within a fortnight the congress was in the middle of the room inspection fight that ran to Christmas.

events.title: ASG asked for longer check cashing hours
events.body: Resolution 80-6, dated 16 September 1980, requested extended hours for the university's check cashing service. It was filed the same night as Resolution 80-5 on open house visitor lists, at the start of a session whose legislation was dominated by residence hall questions.

events.title: A survey found students uninformed about ASG
events.body: Diane Comer reported the student opinion poll committee's first survey under the line that students were uninformed about the Associated Student Government. The Talisman gives the numbers: 29 per cent said they would recognise ASG president Steve Fuller, 31 per cent said they would recognise university centre director Ron Beck, and 28 per cent thought Beck was the ASG president. Seventy-four per cent said they would recognise university president Donald Zacharias. Committee chairman Kevin Kinne said he was disappointed so few could tell Fuller and Beck apart and more surprised that a quarter did not know Zacharias.

events.title: ASG objected to how residence hall budget cuts were shared out
events.body: Resolution 80-7, dated 18 September 1980, concerned what ASG called the inequity of the cuts made to residence hall budgets. Money was tight across the university that autumn, and the congress returned to the theme in April 1981 with Resolution 81-1, recording its dissatisfaction with budget cuts generally.

events.title: ASG made its own officers keep office hours
events.body: Resolution 80-9, dated 22 September 1980, required ASG officers to hold office hours and to report their availability. It is one of the few pieces of legislation from the session aimed at the organisation itself rather than at the university.

events.title: Dean Keown criticised a resolution and members walked out before the vote
events.body: Diane Comer reported that Charles Keown, the dean of student affairs, criticised an ASG resolution and that members left the meeting before the vote was taken. The same issue reported that advance registration would be extended to all students. Keown stayed a critic of ASG's internal changes and publicly questioned the organisation's constitutional revisions again in March 1983.

events.title: Low attendance at its own meetings disappointed the president
events.body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government's low attendance had disappointed president Steve Fuller. The same issue reported that students would grade faculty performance and carried a piece on how the room inspections left hall directors in the middle.

events.title: ASG refused to destroy the open house visitor list
events.body: Diane Comer reported that ASG rejected a bill to destroy the open house list. The congress had filed Resolution 80-5 on open house visitor lists three weeks earlier, and returned to visitor lists again in Resolution 80-30 the following March. The privacy of those lists sat alongside the room inspection fight as the year's running argument about what the university could record about students.

events.title: A joint resolution with Interhall Council on restroom stall doors
events.body: Resolution 80-10, dated 14 October 1980, was a joint resolution of the Interhall Council and ASG asking for stall doors to be installed in residence hall restrooms. Joint work with Interhall Council ran on through the decade, from this to the shared coed housing poll of September 1982.

events.title: ASG endorsed a rape prevention measure
events.body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government had endorsed a rape prevention measure. Ten days earlier the congress had filed Resolution 80-11 under the title Coed Security. The same issue reported that the dormitory inspections would be argued in court and carried an editorial saying inspections should stop until a ruling came.

events.title: ASG asked for the Downing grill to open on Sundays
events.body: Resolution 80-19, dated 18 November 1980, requested that the Downing University Center grill open on Sundays and holidays. It was filed the same night as Resolution 80-18 on advanced registration.

src.label: SGA Resolution 80-19, Downing University Center Grill & Cafeteria

events.title: The Herald said inactivity had improved ASG's image
events.body: The Herald's editorial page argued that the Associated Student Government's image was improved by inactivity, and ran a cartoon of an ASG clown in the same issue. A week later Marcel Bush, then a member and the following year's president, wrote in to defend the organisation.

events.title: ASG approved the stricter room entry rules
events.body: Diane Comer reported that the Associated Student Government had approved stricter rules for entering student rooms, a fortnight after the bill was introduced. The bill set out more standardised procedures for inspections and maintenance than the Hilltopics handbook gave, and was ASG's answer to a semester in which it had twice refused to call for the inspections to be abolished. The same issue carried a letter from member Lonnie Sears saying ASG wanted feedback.

events.title: ASG passed a resolution backing President Zacharias
events.body: The Herald reported an Associated Student Government resolution backing the university president, in an issue reporting Donald Zacharias meeting a state panel over money and a student sharing his budget worries. The paper reported on 10 February that students would sponsor a rally to back Zack, and on 12 February that about 200 people had gathered for it. The Herald's index does not say ASG organised the rally, only that it had passed the resolution.
events.money: about 200 at the rally two weeks later

events.title: ASG put off action on the open house bill
events.body: Robert Pillow reported that the Associated Student Government had postponed action on the open house bill. A week later he reported the congress conducting a survey of its own on inspections, and by 26 February committee absentees were delaying ASG action altogether.

events.title: ASG asked for video game machines in the residence halls
events.body: Resolution 80-28, dated 10 March 1981, requested that electronic video game machines be placed in residence halls. It belongs to a run of small quality-of-life measures that spring, alongside resolutions on ice machines, change machines and painting.

events.title: Only one polling place was opened for the ASG election
events.body: Robert Pillow reported that one poll would be open for the Associated Student Government elections. Five days later he reported four candidates getting a surprise, and the Herald's editorial page ran a piece saying few candidates would have to sweat out the result. After the vote Pillow wrote a column headed Who Cares, arguing the election would win no award for organisation.

events.title: Off-campus representatives given a role in landlord disputes
events.body: Resolution 80-34, dated 31 March 1981, set out the duties of ASG's off-campus housing representatives in landlord and tenant disputes. It followed the previous session's Resolution 79-16, which had put ASG behind the Uniform Landlord Tenant Reform Act.

events.title: The new administration was sworn in as the Herald counted the cost
events.body: The Herald reported the new Associated Student Government administration sworn in, alongside Robert Pillow's column headed Who Cares, which argued the election would not win an award for organisation, and a Bloss editorial cartoon on ASG. Marcel Bush had beaten David Sturgeon the week before, after recounts in the closest races.

events.title: ASG recorded its dissatisfaction with budget cuts
events.body: Resolution 81-1, dated 21 April 1981, expressed ASG's dissatisfaction with budget cuts. It was filed with Resolution 81-2 on traffic tickets in the last days of the session, and it opens the numbering of a session that spent much of the following autumn on the state's cuts to higher education.

events.title: ASG petitioned the governor over cuts to higher education
events.body: In the spring ASG circulated a petition asking state government to weigh the importance of higher education in Kentucky's future before making further cuts, and sent it to Governor John Y. Brown, finance secretary George Atkins and the Council on Higher Education. The petition argued that a quality education required financial support for faculty and facilities. President Steve Fuller said many students did not realise how serious the cuts were, and that they meant dismissing faculty. The Talisman dates the petition only to the spring.

executive.name: Mark Wilson
executive.note: Named 'Administrative Vice-President Mark Wilson' giving officer reports at every ASG meeting read from 7 October 1980 through 17 February 1981; also chaired the Legislative Research committee, one of two committee chairmanships the Congress approved by name at the year's first meeting. The 1981 Talisman calls him a Shelbyville junior and records him leading the opposition to M. A. Baker's resolution to abolish dormitory room inspections, arguing that individual freedoms sometimes had to be sacrificed for general public safety; ASG defeated the resolution 16-13 and a second attempt 24-9.
profile: Mark Wilson was elected to a top Associated Student Government office on 24 April 1980, reported alongside president-elect Steve Fuller and Activities Vice President-elect Greg Zoeller. ASG's own minutes name him Administrative Vice President giving officer reports in meetings read from 7 October 1980 through 17 February 1981, and record him chairing the Legislative Research committee, one of two committee chairmanships Congress approved by name at the year's first meeting.

The 1981 Talisman, which calls him a Shelbyville junior, records Wilson leading the opposition to a resolution by Michael Baker to abolish the dormitory room inspections, warning that if it passed, "individual rights of those living in dorms would be waived." Congress defeated Baker's resolution 16-13, and after the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union moved toward funding a suit over the inspections anyway, defeated a second attempt 24-9, with three abstentions.

executive.name: Mark Chesnut
executive.note: Named 'Treasurer Mark Chesnut' reporting ASG's account balances, 11 November 1980. Also named among the Congress members recorded absent on 17 February 1981, suggesting the treasurer sat in Congress ex officio.
profile: Mark Chesnut served as Associated Student Government Treasurer in 1980-81. He was named 'Treasurer Mark Chesnut' reporting the organization's account balances at the 11 November 1980 meeting, and was among the Congress members recorded absent on 17 February 1981, which suggests the treasurer sat in Congress ex officio.

executive.name: Marsha L. Sanner
executive.note: Signs the minutes of every ASG meeting read this year as secretary, with the signature line reading 'Marsha L. Sanner, ASG Secretary' on 2 Sept 1980; also chaired the Rules and Elections committee, the other of the two committee chairmanships Congress approved by name at the year's first meeting.
profile: Marsha L. Sanner signed the minutes of every Associated Student Government meeting read in 1980-81 as Secretary — the signature line reads 'Marsha L. Sanner, ASG Secretary' beginning 2 September 1980 — and chaired the Rules and Elections committee, the other of the two committee chairmanships Congress approved by name at the year's first meeting. The 1981 Talisman, which gives her full name as Marsha Lee Sanner and calls her a senior from Orchard Lake, Michigan, pictures her in that year's Associated Student Government group photograph alongside Wilson, Fuller and Zoeller.

executive.name: Greg Zoeller
executive.note: Named 'Activities Vice-President Greg Zoeller' giving officer reports at every ASG meeting read from 2 September 1980 through 31 March 1981.
profile: Greg Zoeller was elected to a top Associated Student Government office on 24 April 1980 alongside president-elect Steve Fuller and Administrative Vice President-elect Mark Wilson. ASG's minutes name him Activities Vice-President giving officer reports in meetings read from 2 September 1980 through 31 March 1981.

The 1981 Talisman quotes a 'concert chairman Greg Zoeller' — matching name, year and activities-related function, though this title sat with the University Center Board rather than ASG's Congress; the identification rests on the matching name and year, not on a source that states the two are the same person — on that year's concert season: Sunshine Promotions' cancellation of its concert contract with Western over the summer, and the three major shows the university put on, the Statler Brothers, Conway Twitty and John Prine. Zoeller called losing the exclusive promoter contract an advantage, since the university could now "do it with any promoter."
Near the end of his term, Zoeller wrote a Herald letter on 2 April 1981 headlined 'Marcel Bush Supported,' backing Bush, who had just won that week's ASG presidential primary, to succeed Fuller.

officers.name: Jeff Morris
officers.note: Appointed by President Fuller with the consent of Congress, 7 October 1980; moved floor motions the same meeting and reported on the Big Red costume under Old Business, 11 November 1980. Succeeded by Kevin Strader by 20 January 1981.
profile: Morris was appointed parliamentarian of the Associated Student Government by President Steve Fuller, with Congress's consent, at the meeting of 7 October 1980. He moved floor motions that same evening, and on 11 November 1980 he reported to Congress on the Big Red mascot costume under old business.
Kevin Strader had succeeded him as parliamentarian by the Congress meeting of 20 January 1981; the record does not say why the post changed hands.

officers.name: Kevin Strader
officers.note: Appointed by President Fuller with the consent of Congress, 20 January 1981, succeeding Jeff Morris; moved to dispense with the reading of the minutes the same meeting, and moved adjournment on 17 February and 31 March 1981.
profile: Strader was appointed parliamentarian of the Associated Student Government by President Steve Fuller, with Congress's consent, on 20 January 1981, succeeding Jeff Morris. He moved to dispense with the reading of the minutes at that meeting, and moved adjournment on 17 February and 31 March 1981.

The 1981 Talisman also profiles a Kevin Strader as president of the Interhall Council, the residence-hall student government, describing its purpose as making "residence halls a better place to live" and crediting the council with sponsoring that year's Parents' Day and Hall Olympics. The yearbook pictures a Kevin Strader in both the Associated Student Government and the Interhall Council group photographs, and its name index carries one person who could be either, entered as Strader, John Kevin. That is circumstantial, and the archive does not confirm that the parliamentarian and the council president were the same man.

officers.name: Paul J. Deom
officers.note: Wrote to the Herald in February 1982, identified in the article index as a former member of the Judicial Council, airing grievances after being replaced. The 1981 Talisman independently names Paul Deom, a junior from Boonville, Indiana, as an Associated Student Government member this year, and as the student who took the dormitory room inspection question to the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union after ASG defeated the resolution against the inspections.
profile: Deom, a junior from Boonville, Indiana, was an Associated Student Government member and Judicial Council representative in 1980-81 when he broke with ASG over the university's dormitory room-inspection policy. After Congress defeated a resolution against the inspections 16-13, he contacted the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union and asked it to investigate, and, working with campus KCLU chapter president Michael Taylor, joined the effort to build a broader Bowling Green chapter of the group drawing in non-student residents.

ASG did not follow him. After the KCLU took up the matter, Congress defeated a second resolution against the inspections and re-endorsed the university's policy; the 1981 Talisman's own account of the vote is inconsistent, giving the tally as both 24-9, with three abstentions, and separately as 29-4. Administrative vice president Mark Wilson argued in the debate that fire-safety checks should not be equated with search and seizure, and that if the resolution passed, dorm residents' rights would be waived.

By February 1982 Deom was no longer on the Judicial Council. The Herald's 4 February 1982 issue carried a letter from him, headlined "Former Judicial Council Member Irked," and two further letters followed in reply: M. A. Baker's "Paul Deom Honorable" on 9 February and Winston Stevenson's "Paul Deom Defended" on 18 February. The archive does not yet hold the text of any of the three, so what exactly was in dispute is not established beyond what the headlines record.
