leaders.name: Marcel Bush
leaders.note: The plaque reads "Marcell Bush" with two Ls. Herald bylines spell it Marcel throughout, and SGA's own roster of former presidents, archived in September 2001, lists "Marcel Bush, Lexington, 1981-82" with a footnote recording that he resigned in January 1982 and that administrative vice president David Payne filled the position. This site follows the sources. The roster stars Bush as a student regent and does not star Payne, which is why the Board seat went to a special election in February 1982 rather than passing with the presidency. Herald bylines consistently spell this "Marcel Bush" (one L); the plaque and this site list "Marcell Bush" - spelling unverified. Resigned the ASG presidency 14 January 1982; David Payne succeeded him for the balance of the term.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Marcel Bush won the Associated Student Government presidency in April 1981, defeating David Sturgeon after a campaign the Herald said saw candidates "playing big time politics." Close races elsewhere on the ballot prompted recounts.

In office that fall, ASG raised its own campaign spending limit and vetoed a plan to pay an education lobbyist, days after rallying publicly for higher education funding. Bush later listed the fall rally as one achievement of his term.

Bush resigned the presidency on or shortly before 14 January 1982, reported the same week as the retrospective on his term. David Payne succeeded him; Board of Regents minutes from 30 January 1982 name Payne the new SGA president.

leaders.name: David Payne
leaders.note: Plaque reads 1982; this site originally filed him under 1982-83. Board of Regents minutes (30 Jan 1982) and Herald coverage place him as SGA president succeeding Marcel Bush, who resigned 14 Jan 1982, filling the balance of the 1981-82 term. Margaret Ragan, elected president in April 1982, led the separate 1982-83 term - the two are not the same office-year. The Herald of 14 January 1982 photographed Payne, then Associated Student Government vice president, announcing the resignation of president and student regent Marcell Bush, whom he succeeded.

sources.label: WKU Board of Regents minutes, 30 Jan 1982
WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: David Payne first appears in the indexed record in February 1981 with a Herald letter titled 'Apathy Erased.' By October 1981, before he held the presidency, he was writing on the Associated Student Government's behalf, declaring that ASG was rallying for higher education as budget cuts loomed.

Payne became ASG's president after Marcel Bush resigned on 14 January 1982; Board of Regents minutes from the January 30 meeting name him the new SGA president. In early February the Herald reported that Payne wanted another adviser for ASG, and its editorial page attacked his judgment, while a report the next week said Payne considered certain resolutions misdirected.

Later that month, letter writers to the Herald argued that Payne had been made a victim in the affair; the indexed headline does not state what precipitated it. His name does not appear in the indexed headlines of the April 1982 election that chose Margaret Ragan for the 1982-83 term, nor in the 1982-83 issues examined - consistent with his presidency ending with Bush's original term.

leaders.name: Sandra Norfleet
leaders.note: Student regent, not president. The plaque reads 1982 and this site had filed her under 1982-83; the Herald puts the whole term inside 1981-82. Five students sought the seat in what the paper called the first campus-wide election for it, the vote of 9 February 1982 produced no majority, and Norfleet won the runoff on 16 February. On 15 April 1982 the Herald ran 'Student Regent's 2-month Term Nears End'. Who held the seat earlier in the year, before that first election, is not established in the archive.

sources.label: Herald 57:55, 15 Apr 1982 - Student Regent's 2-month Term Nears End

profile: No candidate won a majority on February 9, forcing a runoff, which Norfleet won on February 16. The Herald reported her election as student regent in its February 18 issue.

Her initial term was short: by mid-April 1982 the Herald noted that the student regent's 2-month term was nearing its end. She is listed among the 1982-83 student leaders, and in February 1983 the Herald's editorial page was still weighing the office, insisting the student regent must represent everyone.

Norfleet reached the student regent seat through a crowded contest. The Herald reported on 2 February 1982 that five students were seeking the student regent spot, and two days later Kevin Francke ran a piece in which the candidates set out their qualities.

Kevin Francke reported on 18 February 1982 that Sandra Norfleet had been elected student regent. The same issue carried his story on a group that would speak on the Associated Student Government's behalf.

Her time in the seat was short. By mid-April Francke was reporting that the student regent's two-month term was nearing its end, in an issue that also covered voided ASG election results and a joke resolution that nearly passed the congress.

events.title: Sandra Norfleet elected student regent
events.body: Reported by Kevin Francke. The same issue has a group set to speak on the Associated Student Government's behalf and Western's 1982 budget coming off hold.

events.title: ASG announces its goals for the year
events.body: The Associated Student Government announced its goals for the coming year. Within two weeks its executives were defending their actions in the Herald, whose editorial page complained that petty politics plagued the organization.

events.title: Campaign spending limit raised
events.body: ASG voted to increase its campaign spending limit. The change followed a week of debate over whether the cap should rise.

events.title: ASG vetoes plan to pay an education lobbyist
events.body: The Associated Student Government vetoed a plan to pay an education lobbyist. The vote came weeks after ASG had rallied publicly for higher education funding.

events.title: Five students seek the student regent seat
events.body: Five students sought the student regent spot in the first campus-wide election for the seat. The February 9 vote produced no majority, forcing a runoff the following week.

events.title: Ragan and Sargent survive the presidential primary
events.body: Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent survived the Associated Student Government presidential primary. The field had included Jack Smith, Kerrie Stewart and Jack Murphree, whose supporters filled the Herald's letters pages.

events.title: General election results voided
events.body: The student government election results were voided, a decision the Herald said disgusted the candidates. A repeat general election was scheduled for April 20.

events.title: Margaret Ragan wins the repeated election
events.body: Margaret Ragan won the ASG presidency in the repeated general election. The new officers were sworn in the following week.

events.title: ASG president Marcel Bush resigns
events.body: Associated Student Government president Marcel Bush resigned. The same issue reported him listing the fall's higher-education rally as one achievement of his term.

events.title: Board of Regents minutes name David Payne the new SGA president
events.body: Minutes of the WKU Board of Regents meeting identified David Payne as the new Student Government Association president, confirming his succession after Marcel Bush's resignation.

src.label: WKU Board of Regents minutes, 30 Jan 1982

events.title: Payne asks for a second ASG adviser
events.body: President David Payne said the Associated Student Government wanted another adviser. The Herald's editorial page criticized his judgment the same week.

events.title: Norfleet's short regent term nears its end
events.body: The Herald noted that the student regent's two-month term was already nearing its end, a reminder of how short a stopgap the office had been.

events.title: ASG and the University Center Board both ask for more money
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government and the University Center Board both wanted larger budgets and planned to submit requests. Two weeks later the paper ran a piece arguing that the Center Board outshone ASG.

events.title: The discount cards that never existed
events.body: ASG announced it would file complaints with the Better Business Bureaus of Georgia and Texas against University Press Inc. of Lewisville, Texas, and Atlanta, which had taken $275 from each of at least four Bowling Green merchants for ASG-endorsed student discount cards that were never produced. A man calling himself Louis F. Cordoba had told Gary Smith of the Bouquet Shoppe on the U.S. 31-W By-Pass that then-president Steve Fuller had recommended his shop as an advertiser, and Smith wrote a $275 cheque on 18 March. The cards were supposed to have been handed out at registration for the autumn.
events.money: $275 taken from each of at least four merchants

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 57, No. 5, 10 September 1981

events.title: 14,000 cards, a dead phone line and a returned letter
events.body: President Marcel Bush had spent three weeks trying to reach the company printing 14,000 ASG discount cards: the Texas number was disconnected, an answering service pushed her to an Atlanta number nobody answered, and a letter to the Texas address came back from the post office. On the day complaints were being filed, company representative Phil Bewley finally telephoned to say the cards had shipped from New York and that printing problems had caused the delay. The Herald noted that until two years earlier ASG had printed discount cards at its own expense as a free student service, charging merchants nothing, and had dropped it when costs became prohibitive.
events.money: 14,000 cards; merchants paid $275 for a listing

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 57, No. 10, 29 September 1981

events.title: Discount cards arrive, but do not go out
events.body: The ASG discount cards reached campus the day before the Herald's report of 1 October 1981. There were 14,000 of them and they offered students discounts at 21 listed merchants, valid until 1 September 1982. They were not handed out: Bush had been busy with other projects and passed the job to the communications committee, whose chairwoman, Laura Simms, was still working on a plan.

events.title: ASG appointed a council to settle its internal disputes
events.body: The Associated Student Government appointed a council to decide disputes inside the organization. The Herald report, by Kevin Francke, ran two weeks after his coverage of the resignation of ASG president Marcel Bush. The same issue reported that the regents bill, changing how the student regent was chosen, had passed the state House.

events.title: Bush opened his term saying students should understand ASG
events.body: Ellen Banahan's interview with the new president, Marcel Bush, ran in the second issue of the autumn under the line that he wanted students to understand the Associated Student Government. The same issue reported that campus police were offering a night escort service, a year before ASG and Interhall Council started a volunteer one of their own.

events.title: ASG submitted its budget
events.body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG had submitted its budget for the year. It ran in the same issue as her first report that the organisation could not find the student discount cards it had ordered, and in a week the Herald headlined as the beginning of budget pleas across the university.

events.title: ASG executives defended their actions, and a former president was honoured
events.body: Ellen Banahan reported that the ASG executives had defended their actions, in the same issue that reported the campaign spending limit might be raised and that Steve Thornton, the 1978 ASG president, had been honoured. The defence came five days before the Herald's editorial page complained that petty politics plagued the organisation.

events.title: ASG asked for a book drop away from the library
events.body: Resolution 81-4, dated 22 September 1981, requested a book drop in a central location away from the library, reviving a request ASG had first made in November 1979 for a drop in the Downing University Center. Resolution 81-3, on parking spaces, carries the same date.

events.title: ASG considered barring freshmen from bringing cars to campus
events.body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG was considering a plan to bar freshmen cars from campus. Parking ran through the session's legislation as well: Resolution 81-3 of 22 September dealt with parking spaces and Resolution 81-5 of 13 October with parking privileges.

events.title: ASG backed the budget protest as a petition reached the state council
events.body: Ellen Banahan reported that ASG supported the budget protest, in the same issue in which Wilma Norton reported a petition presented to the Council on Higher Education. Marcel Bush named the autumn's higher education rally as an achievement of his term when he resigned in January.

events.title: Bush appointed an ASG adviser
events.body: Tommy Newton reported that the ASG president had appointed an adviser. The question did not close with the appointment: after Bush resigned, his successor David Payne told the Herald in February that ASG wanted a second one.

events.title: A resolution on students' right to privacy
events.body: Resolution 81-6, dated 24 November 1981, concerned students' right to privacy, a year after the congress's long fight over dormitory room inspections and open house visitor lists. Resolution 81-9, on safety strips, carries the same date.

events.title: The discount cards left few happy
events.body: Kevin Francke's report on the student discount card scheme ran under the line that it had left few happy, and the same issue carried a second Francke piece reporting that many businesses were unhappy too. It closed a saga that had run since September: ASG could not find the cards, then found the printer's Texas telephone disconnected and its letter returned, then received 14,000 cards it did not hand out for weeks.

events.title: David Payne's appeal failed and a regent election was called
events.body: Kevin Francke reported that David Payne's appeal had failed and that an election for the student regent seat had been set. Payne had succeeded to the ASG presidency after Marcel Bush's resignation, and the Board of Regents minutes of 30 January 1982 name him as president. Under the previous arrangement the ASG president also sat as student regent, as Steve Fuller had. The seat instead went to a campus-wide vote and Sandra Norfleet won the runoff in February. The Herald index records the appeal and its failure but not the grounds on which it was made.

events.title: ASG heard two resolutions on state money and international students
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had heard two resolutions. Both are in SGA's own archive under the date 2 March 1982: Resolution 81-10 on the disbursement of state funds, and Resolution 81-11 asking that housing be provided for international students during the breaks when the dormitories close.

events.title: ASG asked for a grace week before finals
events.body: Resolution 81-12, dated 23 March 1982, requested a grace week between the last week of classes and finals week. It is the earliest of the calendar demands ASG returned to through the decade, which by 1985 included a fall mid-semester break and a week-long Thanksgiving.

events.title: The Herald argued a smaller ASG would be more effective
events.body: The Herald's editorial page argued that a smaller Associated Student Government would increase its effectiveness. It ran in the issue reporting Margaret Ragan's win in the repeated general election, and beside a letter applauding the University Center Board.

events.title: Marsupial Awards for ASG and the Herald, and a letter calling ASG a joke
events.body: Robert Carter's Marsupial Awards column handed prizes to both the Associated Student Government and the Herald, in the same issue that printed a letter from M. A. Baker headed that ASG was a joke. Baker had been the subject of a Herald feature in February 1981 describing him as fighting the system inside ASG. The pair closed a session that began with the paper complaining of petty politics and ended with the presidential election being run twice.

events.title: Judicial Council appointments draw criticism, and a replaced member writes in
events.body: The Herald of 4 February 1982 carried a Kevin Francke news story headlined "Judicial Appointments Criticized," about President David Payne's appointments to ASG's Judicial Council, alongside a letter from Paul Deom headlined "Former Judicial Council Member Irked" about his removal from the council. The archive's index preserves these headlines but not the articles' full text, so the specific grounds for the criticism and Deom's account of his removal are not confirmed here.

events.title: A joke resolution almost passes, and a Herald writer says ASG won't win an award
events.body: The Herald of 15 April 1982 - the same issue that reported the general election results voided - also carried a Kevin Francke story headlined that a joke resolution had almost passed ASG, and a piece by Robert Pillow headlined that ASG would not win an award for organization.

executive.name: Marcel Bush
executive.note: Resigned 14 Jan 1982.

executive.name: David Payne
executive.note: Succeeded Bush; named in Board of Regents minutes 30 Jan 1982.

src.label: WKU Board of Regents minutes, 30 Jan 1982

executive.name: Alesia Canafax
executive.note: Named Secretary in the minutes of 20 October 1981, announcing an opening for off-campus representatives and asking chairpersons for their committee rolls. Susan Albert filled in for her at the meeting of 9 February 1982.
profile: Alesia Canafax was named Secretary in the minutes of 20 October 1981, where she announced an opening for off-campus representatives and asked committee chairpersons for their rolls. She was absent from the 9 February 1982 meeting, where Susan Albert filled in for her and announced a new date for the ASG banquet.

executive.name: Laura Simms
executive.note: Named Public Affairs Vice-President in the minutes of 20 October 1981, reporting on the phone-a-thon and the week's campus events. The same year's minutes name her chairperson of the Communications Committee.
profile: Laura Simms was named Public Affairs Vice President in the minutes of 20 October 1981, where she reported on the phone-a-thon and that week's campus events. The year's minutes name her chairperson of the Communications Committee; the 20 October minutes themselves record no committee chairmanship for her, and the attribution rests on the meeting of 9 February 1982, at which another member reported for the committee in her place.

A Laura Simms wrote for the university's alumni magazine, Western Alumnus, in the two years after the term: a Fall 1982 article on the phone-a-thon, the same fundraiser she had reported on to Congress, and a Spring 1983 piece on the Elderhostel program for older adult students, co-bylined with Jim Bennett. The identification rests on the matching name and the matching subject, not on a source that states the two are the same person; it is recorded here as likely, not certain.

executive.name: Sandra Norfleet
executive.note: Separately elected office. The Herald puts the whole term inside 1981-82: no majority in the vote of 9 February 1982, a runoff won on 16 February, and the issue of 15 April 1982 reporting the two-month term nearing its end. This archive filed her under 1982-83 until August 2026.

members.name: Susan Albert
members.seat: Acting secretary, 9 February 1982 (Congress membership not established)
members.note: Recorded on 9 February 1982 as filling in for Secretary Alesia Canafax and announcing the new date for the ASG banquet. Sworn in as Secretary for the following year on 27 April 1982. Congress membership itself is not conclusively established by the minutes.

members.name: Doug Ball
members.note: Reported for the Student-Faculty Relations Committee at meetings from October 1981 through April 1982, on a student survey, a faculty reception, cable television in the dormitories and a grace-week proposal before the Faculty Senate. Nominated for Outstanding Congress Member on 20 April 1982.

members.name: Donna Bristow
members.note: Asked on 17 November 1981 whether ASG could hold an orientation for Congress members on what ASG is and does; moved the amendment to Article III of the revised constitution that was accepted on 7 December 1981; announced a Business College event on 16 February 1982; named in the absence list of 6 April 1982.

members.name: Jim Brumfield
members.note: Moved adjournment of the meetings of 20 October 1981 and 19 January 1982. On 23 March 1982 the chair called on him to move adjournment, the minutes say, to keep the tradition.

members.name: Chandy Christian
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 20 October 1981. Asked Congress members to attend the KSU Rally on 6 October 1981, and seconded the motion on 27 October 1981 that postponed Resolution 81-5 indefinitely.

members.name: Kelly Cook
members.seat: Congress member; University Center Board representative
members.note: Won the 6 April 1982 vote for University Center Board representative against Chris Groemling, filling the seat Susan Day had resigned. Sworn in as Treasurer for the following year on 27 April 1982.

members.name: Susan Day
members.seat: Congress member; University Center Board representative
members.note: Nominated for University Center Board representative on 27 October 1981 and named in the absence list of 16 February 1982. Her resignation from the University Center Board was reported on 6 April 1982, when a replacement was sought.

members.name: Tom Farmer
members.note: Suggested at the 9 February 1982 meeting that students receive a grade at mid-term, and named in the roll-call absence list of 6 April 1982.

members.name: Regina Haynes
members.seat: International Student Week announcement (Congress membership not established)
members.note: Announced the countries taking part in International Student Week at the 20 October 1981 meeting. This is the only mention found; Congress membership itself is not conclusively established by the minutes.

members.name: Sherry Howell
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 20 October 1981.

members.name: Greg Jennings
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 20 October 1981.

members.name: Jeff Link
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 13 October 1981.

members.name: Melody Murphy
members.note: Named on 13 October 1981 to head a committee investigating the possibility of a state student legislature in Kentucky. She reported on 17 November 1981 that a weekend meeting with representatives from Murray, the University of Tennessee and Georgetown had voted in favour of starting one, and President Bush congratulated her on the work. Named in the absence lists of 9 and 16 February 1982.

members.name: Diane Olson
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence lists of 13 October 1981, 19 January 1982 and 6 April 1982.

members.name: Polly Proctor
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence lists of 16 February and 13 April 1982.

members.name: Lonnie Sears
members.note: Reported for the Student Opinion Poll Committee through the year, circulating an internal poll of Congress members in November 1981 and a survey on ASG itself in February 1982. President Payne asked him on 9 February 1982 to help interpret the constitution and by-laws on where a resolution goes after it passes. Nominated for Outstanding Congress Member on 20 April 1982.

members.name: Mark Smith
members.note: Reported for the Communications Committee at the 9 February 1982 meeting, filling in for chairperson Laura Simms. This is the only mention found; Congress membership itself is not conclusively established by the minutes. Distinct from Kelly Smith (On-Campus chairperson) and Jack Smith (Administrative Vice President-elect), both of whom appear separately in these same minutes.

members.name: Kerrie Stewart
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 16 February 1982. Sworn in as Public Affairs Vice President for the following year on 27 April 1982.

members.name: Melinda Wood
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence lists of 7 December 1981 and 16 February 1982.

members.name: Bridget Wyatt
members.note: Named in the roll-call absence list of 20 October 1981, where the minutes spell the surname Wyatt.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 20 October 1981
documents.summary: A routine autumn meeting under President Marcel Bush, opening with a roll-call absence list that names four Congress members. Officer reports cover the Bluegrass Plan, a phone-a-thon and a week of campus events; Resolution 81-5 had its first reading.
documents.extract: The Absences were as follows: Chandy Christian; Greg Jennings; Sherry Howell; and Bridget Wyatt.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 17 November 1981
documents.summary: Committee reports on a student opinion poll, a faculty reception and the revising of the ASG constitution, which had its first reading at this meeting. Melody Murphy reported that a weekend meeting with other Kentucky institutions had voted in favour of founding a state student legislature, and President Bush congratulated her on the work.
documents.extract: The revised Constitution had its first reading.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 24 November 1981
documents.summary: The meeting at which ASG voted to withdraw from the Student Government Association of Kentucky rather than pay its fee. Margaret Ragan moved to pay and stay in; that motion died on the floor, and Doug Ball's motion to withdraw passed after long discussion. The scan is heavily degraded and much of the page is unreadable.
documents.extract: Doug Ball moved that we withdraw from SGAK.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 7 December 1981
documents.summary: Congress read Resolution 81-7, the revised constitution, for the third time and voted it through article by article. A grade-point-average requirement for candidates failed; requirements that the president have a semester's prior experience and the treasurer six hours of accounting passed, as did an increase in the judicial appeals window and an enlargement of a committee from one member to five.
documents.extract: Article II; section 2; part A1 - failed (Grade point average)

documents.title: ASG minutes, 19 January 1982
documents.summary: The first meeting after Marcel Bush left office, called to order by David Payne as president. Congress filled the resulting vacancy in the administrative vice presidency by secret ballot between Margaret Ragan and Doug Hill, after a dispute over whether the constitution or the handbook governed the procedure; Ragan won.
documents.extract: The new vice-president is Margaret Ragan.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 26 January 1982
documents.summary: President David Payne read Marcel Bush's letter of resignation to Congress and appealed for support and unity. Committee reports and a treasurer's balance follow. The scan is degraded in places.
documents.extract: President David Payne read a letter from Marcel Bush (resignation).

leaders.name: Margaret Ragan
leaders.note: Confirmed by her own byline in the Herald, 3 Feb 1983, plus the primary and election-night headlines in the same spring. SGA's own roster of former presidents, archived in September 2001, stars her as a student regent, so she held the Board seat as well as the presidency. An earlier reading here took the headline over her February 1983 piece, that the ASG presidency and the student regent position were separate, to mean she did not hold the seat. The headline will not carry that: the roster says she did, and the article body has not been read. SPELLING FLAG, not corrected: the 1983 Talisman's ASG group-photo caption (p. 232) prints her name "Margaret Regan," not "Ragan." Every other source cited here reads "Ragan"; left as printed elsewhere per the archive's flag-don't-fix rule.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Margaret Ragan survived the April 1982 Associated Student Government presidential primary along with Glenn Sargent, emerging from a five-way field. Endorsement letters for her ran in the Herald through both rounds of the election.
After the first general election was voided, Ragan won the presidency in the repeated election held April 20, 1982. She and the other new officers were sworn in before the month was out.

Midway through her term Ragan used the Herald's pages to explain that the ASG presidency and the student regent seat were now separate positions. Her spring saw a grade plan, a student shuttle vote, and a contested rewrite of the ASG constitution before Jack Smith was elected to succeed her.

Ragan's presidency came out of a disrupted spring. The Associated Student Government repeated its general election on 20 April 1982, after the Herald had reported the previous week that the first round's results were void.

She set out her agenda at the start of the fall term. Monica Dias reported in the Herald's second issue of the year that major ASG changes were envisioned by Margaret Ragan, and over the following months the congress took up a campus Wall of Fame, a joint coed housing poll with the Interhall Council, and a coed housing bill it approved in November.

Ragan also argued in print for keeping the two student offices distinct. In February 1983 the Herald carried her statement that the Associated Student Government and the student regent position were separate, in the same issue that reported the ASG shuttle service.

events.title: Norfleet wins the student regent runoff
events.body: No candidate won a majority in the February 9 student regent primary, forcing a runoff. Sandra Norfleet won the runoff on February 16.

events.title: Ragan and Sargent survive the ASG primary
events.body: Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent survived the Associated Student Government presidential primary, emerging from a five-way field.

events.title: Ragan wins the presidency in a repeated election
events.body: The first general election was voided, and Margaret Ragan won the Associated Student Government presidency in the repeated election held April 20. She and the other new officers were sworn in before the month was out.

events.title: ASG floats a shuttle service, and Ragan explains the split with the regent seat
events.body: The same issue that carried President Margaret Ragan's Herald piece explaining that the ASG presidency and student regent seat were now separate positions also reported ASG was considering a shuttle service, the proposal put to a student vote the following week.

events.title: Grade plan passes; students vote for a shuttle
events.body: ASG passed a grade plan, and 206 students voted for a campus shuttle service.

events.title: Constitution changes approved; filing opens
events.body: The Associated Student Government approved changes to its constitution, and ten students filed for offices ahead of the deadline. Dean Charles Keown publicly questioned the revisions the following week, as filings swelled to 68.

events.title: 500 vote in the ASG primary
events.body: About 500 students voted in the Associated Student Government primary. The Herald's letters pages carried a steady stream of endorsements for presidential candidate Jack Smith.

events.title: Jack Smith wins the ASG presidency
events.body: Jack Smith won the presidency of the Associated Student Government, and students voted for the ASG constitutional revisions on the same ballot. The Herald had dared students to vote at all in a sardonic election day editorial.

events.title: 24 elected to Senate
events.body: Twenty-four students were elected to the Associated Student Government Senate, the same issue reporting increased dormitory hours had been proposed.

events.title: ASG endorses a $15 athletic fee
events.body: The outgoing congress endorsed a $15 athletic fee. The vote came as the Board of Regents turned its focus to the budget.

events.title: ASG endorses William Natcher
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had backed William Natcher. The same issue previewed the ASG presidential primary set for the following Tuesday, and five days later the paper editorialized that endorsing was not wise for ASG.

events.title: Ragan opens the year promising major ASG changes
events.body: Monica Dias reported that major ASG changes were envisioned by Margaret Ragan. The story ran in the Herald's second issue of the fall semester and was the paper's first substantial account of her plans.

events.title: ASG considers a Wall of Fame
events.body: Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government was considering a Wall of Fame. A week later the Herald followed with a report that the wall looked promising.

events.title: ASG approves a coed housing bill
events.body: Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had approved a coed housing bill. The measure built through the fall: ASG and the Interhall Council polled students on coed housing in September, and ASG formally proposed it on 10 November.

events.title: ASG breaks from the student legislature
events.body: Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had broken from the student legislature. The break did not last, and by February 1984 the Herald was reporting that the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature might join ASG again.

events.title: No quorum, so ASG does not meet
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government failed to reach a quorum and did not meet. It was the first ASG item the paper carried after the winter break.

events.title: A volunteer student escort service
events.body: A student escort service jointly sponsored by Interhall Council, ASG and the university police began operating, walking women anywhere on campus from dark until midnight Sunday to Thursday on a single telephone number, with a vehicle in bad weather. Coordinator James Hunter said Western was the first university in the country with a completely volunteer, student-operated escort service, and that it had filled about 500 to 600 requests in its first year without a single incident. Public safety director Paul Bunch said requests for escorts had tripled after two students were raped the previous year.
events.money: 500 to 600 requests filled in the first year

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 58, No. 4, 2 September 1982

events.title: The student discount card came back with 17 merchants
events.body: The Herald's back-to-school issue reported that the student discount card carried 17 merchants. It succeeded the previous year's troubled card, which reached campus late, went undistributed for weeks and left students and businesses complaining by January. The card collapsed again the following autumn, when local merchants were left waiting for refunds.

src.label: College Heights Herald 58:1 Section A, 24 August 1982

events.title: ASG asked for transport for injured and disabled students
events.body: Resolution 82-1-F, dated 21 September 1982, requested special transportation from the Department of Public Safety for injured and handicapped students. It is the first numbered resolution of Margaret Ragan's session and the earliest transport proposal of a year that went on to put a campus shuttle service to a student vote.

src.label: SGA Resolution 82-1-F, Transportation for Injured or Handicapped

events.title: Jack Smith wrote in to applaud the escort service
events.body: Jack Smith wrote to the Herald applauding the student escort service, about eight weeks after the volunteer scheme run with Interhall Council and the university police began. The same issue reported that a concert by Alabama had packed Diddle Arena and that a small parade had ended the Homecoming weekend.

events.title: ASG supported the football proposal before the regents
events.body: Jamie Morton reported that ASG supported the football proposal the Board of Regents was to consider at its Saturday session, alongside the bookstore. The same issue reported ticket sales down $20,000 as 1982 attendance declined, carried a Herald editorial urging the regents to veto more football spending, and printed a letter calling concert apathy pathetic.

events.title: ASG proposed that athletic fees replace student game tickets
events.body: Resolution 82-8-S, dated 8 February 1983, proposed that students use their athletic fees to get into games rather than individual tickets being sold. It followed the previous session's Resolution 81-8, which had asked only that the ticket price be cut, and preceded the outgoing congress's endorsement of a $15 athletic fee in April.

src.label: SGA Resolution 82-8-S, Termination of Student Ticket Sales

events.title: ASG backed free admission to games
events.body: Jamie Morton reported that ASG supported the plan for free admission to athletic events, and a companion piece in the same issue reported that support for free game admission was growing. It was the public face of Resolution 82-8-S, filed nine days earlier.

events.title: ASG asked for a review of textbook policy at the bookstore
events.body: Resolution 82-9-S, dated 22 March 1983, requested a review of the College Heights Bookstore's new and used textbook policies. ASG had pressed the bookstore before, asking in January 1980 that it adopt a break-even policy on books, and the regents took the bookstore up themselves in January 1983.

events.title: Few women were using the escort service
events.body: Gary Elmore reported that few women were using the student escort service, in the same issue in which Jamie Morton reported ASG discussing its plans for the following year. The same issue reported the University Center Board satisfied with its concert series.

events.title: The new Congress reorganizes its committees and amends its by-laws
events.body: At its organizing meeting on 29 April 1982, the Congress elected under President Margaret Ragan reorganized its committee structure, amended its by-laws, and approved a slate of appointments to Congress seats.

events.title: Congress's constitutional revision has its first reading
events.body: At the meeting of 1 March 1983, Congress took up proposed changes to ASG's constitution.

events.title: The constitutional revision gets a second reading, clause by clause
events.body: At the meeting of 15 March 1983, Congress again took up the proposed changes to ASG's constitution, two days before the Herald reported the revision approved.

executive.name: Margaret Ragan
executive.note: Won a repeated general election 20 April 1982 after the first was voided; succeeded by Jack Smith in April 1983.

executive.name: Jack Smith
executive.note: Sworn in at the 29 April 1982 meeting, where he also went over how to write a resolution for the incoming Congress. The same minutes name him chairperson of both the Student Affairs Committee and the Legislative Research Committee.
profile: Jack Smith was serving as Administrative Vice President by the Congress meeting of 29 April 1982, where he went over how to write a resolution and its stages; the same minutes name him chairperson of both the Student Affairs Committee and the Legislative Research Committee.

A candidate also named Jack Smith ran in that spring's ASG presidential primary and was eliminated on 6 April 1982, and a Jack Smith went on to win the ASG presidency the following year, in April 1983 — already recorded elsewhere in this archive. No source found ties this Administrative Vice President directly to either the 1982 candidate or the 1983 president, and the archive does not merge them: this record is kept deliberately separate rather than assumed to be the same person.

executive.name: Kelly Cook
executive.note: Sworn in at the 29 April 1982 meeting, where as Treasurer he moved two amendments to the by-laws on Congress absences, both adopted. The same minutes name him chairperson of the Finance Committee.
profile: Before becoming Treasurer, Kelly Cook won a 6 April 1982 Congress vote for the University Center Board representative seat, defeating Chris Groemling to fill the vacancy Susan Day had resigned. He was serving as Treasurer by the 29 April 1982 meeting, where he moved two amendments to the by-laws on Congress member absences, both adopted — one defining how many absences trigger a show-cause hearing, the other on how a missed committee meeting counts toward that total; the same minutes name him chairperson of the Finance Committee.

executive.name: Susan Albert
executive.note: Sworn in at the 29 April 1982 meeting, where as Secretary she went over the chart for handling motions. The same minutes name her chairperson of the Rules and Elections Committee.
profile: Susan Albert filled in for Secretary Alesia Canafax at the 9 February 1982 meeting, where she announced a new, tentative date for the ASG banquet. During that spring's campaign season she wrote a Herald letter supporting Kerrie Stewart, one of the candidates for the ASG presidency who did not survive the primary that Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent came through. By the Congress meeting of 29 April 1982, at which Stewart was named chairperson of the Public Relations Committee, Albert herself was serving as Secretary, where she went over the chart for handling motions; the same minutes name her chairperson of the Rules and Elections Committee.

executive.name: Kerrie Stewart
executive.note: A LaCenter junior. Described ASG as a liaison between students and the administration, and said the ASG Congress proposed bills in weekly meetings that were then voted on by the administration once passed by Congress. The archive's 1981-82 Congress roll already anticipated this: it records her sworn in as Public Affairs Vice President for the following year on 27 April 1982.
profile: Kerrie Stewart stood in the Associated Student Government elections of spring 1982, a contest run twice after the first general election was voided. This archive's record of the presidential primary places her in the field that Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent came through, and her supporters filled the Herald's letters pages from 25 March to 20 April, the last of them, by Melody Murphy, backing Ragan and Stewart together. What office she was seeking by the repeated election of 20 April is not established here.

She was sworn in as Public Affairs Vice President for the following year on 27 April 1982, and at the Congress meeting of 29 April was named chairperson of the Public Relations Committee. A LaCenter junior, she described ASG as a liaison between students and the administration, and said its Congress proposed bills in weekly meetings which the administration then voted on once Congress had passed them. The 1983 Talisman's Associated Student Government portrait names her in the vice-presidential role. She also appears in a Phi Mu sorority composite in the WKU Archives' student organizations photograph collection.

The Herald marked her death the following year. The index of the issue of 23 August 1983 carries "Saying Goodbye to Kerrie Stewart is Especially Hard" as an obituary, and a remembrance by Jon Norris, "Kerrie Stewart Remembered," followed on 8 September 1983. Neither article was opened for this record, so nothing is said here of the circumstances.

documents.title: ASG minutes, 29 April 1982
documents.summary: The meeting that seated the incoming 1982-83 Congress under President Margaret Ragan. Congress approved a restructuring that folded the On-Campus, Off-Campus, Student Opinion Poll, Minority Affairs and International Students committees into a single Student Affairs Committee, renamed the Communications Committee to Public Relations, and dissolved the Complaints and Suggestions Committee. It then confirmed a full slate of representatives, who were sworn in, and approved the year's committee heads. Two by-law amendments on absences were also moved.
documents.extract: All of the representatives were approved by Congress.

leaders.name: Jack Smith
leaders.note: Two-year plate. Confirmed by name in Herald headlines across his whole term, from the April 1983 win through the April 1985 retrospective on his presidency ending.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Jack Smith first ran for the Associated Student Government presidency in spring 1982, drawing repeated endorsement letters in the Herald, and though Margaret Ragan won that race, Smith and Lonnie Sears took awards as the year closed. He returned as a candidate in March 1983, when 68 students filed for ASG positions and his supporters again filled the letters pages.

Smith won the presidency of the Associated Student Government in the April 12, 1983 election, in which students also approved constitutional revisions. His victory came after roughly 500 students had voted in the primary the week before.

His presidency was colorful and contentious: the fall brought a discount card controversy, letters accusing him of partying while committees waited and others defending him, and a December cartoon that he wrote in to protest. In April 1984 the Herald caught him impersonating a bunny as his ASG ran a low-turnout poll on beer and a campus pub.

Smith's plaque term runs two years, 1983-85, and the Herald's own account of his exit backs that up: its April 11, 1985 issue reported him ending his term as ASG president in an article headlined 'Jack Smith Ends Term as Associated Student Government President,' alongside a companion piece crediting his enthusiasm with reviving interest in the organization.

Smith's 1983 campaign drew an unusual run of supporting letters in the Herald. The issue of 7 April 1983 carried two, from Dorothy Metzmeler and Sarah Hein, following one from Tony Johnson the week before; the same issue reported that about 500 students had voted in the ASG primary.

Jamie Morton reported on 14 April 1983 that Jack Smith had won the presidency of the Associated Student Government. The same issue reported that students had also voted in favor of the ASG constitutional revisions worked out that spring.

His first term drew heavy comment. In December 1983 the Herald reported that ASG had voided its own procedures even as it saw growth in membership and took up fourteen proposals, and the same issue carried Stanley Reagan's letter headed "Jack Smith, Associated Student Government Thrown Away" along with another Lou Bloss cartoon on ASG. He filed for re-election in February 1984 and stayed in office through a second year, ending his term in April 1985.

events.title: Escort service returns; discount card floated
events.body: The Herald's opening issue reported that the student escort service would resume and that ASG might sponsor a discount card. Filing for freshman elections was set to begin September 19.

events.title: Discount card plan draws fire
events.body: ASG voted to study the discount card after the Herald editorialized that the organization should govern, not market cards. A week later the paper reported ASG would offer members a commission on card sales, prompting letters calling the plan cheap shots and old tricks.

events.title: ASG passes incomplete-grade deadline proposal
events.body: The Associated Student Government passed its proposal on the deadline for incomplete grades, after tabling it the week before. The grade issue had occupied ASG since September.

events.title: ASG voids its own procedures amid growth
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG voided its own procedures, while also noting growth in membership and a congress weighing 14 proposals. The editorial page mocked the body with a cartoon, and Jack Smith wrote in to say the cartoon aggravated him.

events.title: Student legislature may rejoin ASG
events.body: The Kentucky Student Legislature delegation was reported possibly rejoining the Associated Student Government. Letter writers sparred the same day over whether the ASG stereotype was deserved.

events.title: Top four ASG offices decided without runoffs
events.body: The top four Associated Student Government spots were decided, the Herald reported, as ASG emphasized representation. About 450 students had voted in the primary the week before.

events.title: ASG polls students on beer and a campus pub
events.body: ASG began a student poll on the beer and campus pub issue on general election day. The Herald's editorial page argued the economics of the campus pub plan were faulty.

events.title: Low turnout may force a beer poll revote
events.body: Low turnout threatened to spur a revote in the ASG beer poll. The same issue reported president Jack Smith impersonating a bunny for the season.

events.title: ASG election day: candidates court votes for the top offices
events.body: The Herald urged students to the polls for the Associated Student Government election. Beyond the presidential contest, candidates for ASG's other top offices - including Bob Shults, Laura McClellan, Traci Turner, Kim Binkley and Allan Kujala - each drew endorsement letters in the paper; the Herald index does not specify which office each sought.

events.title: Smith opens with a "year of action"
events.body: Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government was planning for a year of action. The story ran in the third issue of the fall semester, a week after the Herald first reported that ASG might sponsor a discount card.

events.title: ASG members to take a commission on discount cards
events.body: Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government would offer its members a commission on the discount cards. The same issue carried two critical columns aimed at ASG, Timi Flener's "Cheap Shots" and Connie Hoffman's "And Old Tricks."

events.title: ASG asks for cable television in dorm rooms
events.body: Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government wanted cable in dormitory rooms. The same issue ran a Lou Bloss editorial cartoon on an ASG penalty and a letter from Carl Davis disagreeing with an ASG proposal.

events.title: Budget falls short as the grade plan passes
events.body: Craig Dezern and Steve Paul reported that the ASG budget would not cover its planned projects. The same issue reported that ASG had approved its grade plan, the change to the grading scale that ran through most of the year.

events.title: ASG takes up a university day-care center
events.body: Barry Rose reported that a university day-care center would be studied by the Associated Student Government. It joined study hall research and cable television among the service questions ASG picked up that fall.

events.title: Vice president William Chandler quits
events.body: Victoria Malmer reported that Associated Student Government vice president William Chandler had quit. Within a week the Herald reported that three people had been nominated for ASG positions.

events.title: The top ASG officers file for re-election
events.body: Mark Edelen reported that the top Associated Student Government officers were seeking re-election. The same issue reported that legislators were upset with ASG and that students were being asked to gripe, and it carried further responses to the alcohol poll plan.

events.title: ASG prints the discount card itself
events.body: After an agreement collapsed with University Services Associates of St. Mary's, Missouri, ASG voted to print the student discount cards itself, and they were finally handed out in November through the Student Affairs and Public Relations committees working with Interhall Council. Nine businesses appeared on the card, among them the seven merchants who had paid company president George Wheaton for the original card and never got a refund. President Jack Smith said the businesses would have to recover their own money: "They got what they paid for. They got their discount card."
events.money: nine businesses on the card; seven merchants unrefunded

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 59, No. 23, 10 November 1983

events.title: Local merchants waited for refunds on the discount cards
events.body: Steve Paul reported that local merchants were waiting for refunds over the student discount cards. The card had been ASG's flagship service project of the autumn and had drawn a Herald editorial in September saying the organisation should govern rather than market cards. By November ASG had given up on the outside company and printed the cards itself.

events.title: An A-minus was floated for the grade plan
events.body: Steve Paul reported that an A-minus might be added to the Associated Student Government's grade plan, and the Herald's editorial page argued in the same issue that a new grade scale must include one. The plan had been approved five days earlier, and by 8 December a group had organised against it.

events.title: A group opposed the grade plan, and false proposals were said to risk impeachment
events.body: Steve Paul reported that a group had come out against ASG's grade plan, five weeks after the congress approved it. The same issue carried a second Paul piece reporting that writing false proposals could mean impeachment, in a semester in which the Herald had already reported ASG voiding its own procedures.

events.title: ASG urged to take up student rights
events.body: Barry Rose reported that ASG had been encouraged to look at student rights, and the Herald's editorial page argued in the same issue that the student rights policy needed re-examining. A week later Mark Edelen reported that ASG would examine rights. The issue also reported that a day-care centre was possible in the autumn, a project ASG had taken up in November.

events.title: ASG announced a poll on beer at athletic events
events.body: Mark Edelen reported that ASG would poll students on whether they wanted beer sold at games. This is the announcement of the poll, not its result. By 16 February the paper was reporting that an NCAA rule might prevent alcohol sales at ballgames and by 23 February that the NCAA and the Sun Belt would allow them. The poll itself went ahead on general election day in April, by then framed around beer and a campus pub, and low turnout threatened a revote.

events.title: ASG wanted evaluation changes but opposed achievement tests
events.body: Mark Edelen reported that the Associated Student Government wanted changes to faculty evaluation while opposing achievement tests. The same issue carried a Herald editorial arguing that linking the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature to ASG would be a mistake, and a letter from Vincent Lewis praising ASG. The legislature delayed its move the following week.

events.title: ASG, the centre board and Interhall Council found their duties overlapped
events.body: Mark Edelen reported that the Associated Student Government, the University Center Board and the Interhall Council overlapped in what they did. The ground had been divided between them five years earlier, when the regents moved campus entertainment and the money that paid for it from ASG to the centre board.

events.title: ASG forms a group to study the grade scale
events.body: The Herald reported that an Associated Student Government group would study the university's grade scale. In the same issue president Jack Smith wrote that ASG supported the paper's opinion on the question. ASG passed its incomplete-grade deadline proposal the following month.

leaders.name: Jack Smith
leaders.note: Two-year plate. Either re-elected or the plaque compresses two terms. Confirmed from inside the term: the Herald of 20 March 1984 reported the top four ASG posts decided, and coverage through 1984-85 names Smith as president in his second year.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Smith presided over a productive opening to the 1984-85 year. By the third week of September the Herald reported that four ASG proposals had been made reality, and the congress had begun studying a student book exchange, which became the signature project of his final year.
By mid-year the record was mixed. The book exchange venture appeared likely to take a summer pause, and the organization was weighing whether to fight cuts to education funding.

His term ended in April 1985. The Herald covered his exit with a news story headlined that Smith was ending his term as ASG president, an editorial crediting his enthusiasm with reviving interest in the organization, and an editorial cartoon. The SGA plaque records him on a two-year 1983-85 plate.

Jack Smith first won the presidency of the Associated Student Government in a race the College Heights Herald reported under the headline "Jack Smith Wins Presidency of Associated Student Government," in the paper's fifty-eighth volume. That win put him in the office he would go on to hold across more than one term.

Smith and the Herald did not always get along. One issue in the paper's fifty-ninth volume indexed an item headed "Jack Smith, Associated Student Government Thrown Away" together with a letter written by Smith himself under the title "Cartoon Aggravates," showing that he answered the paper's cartoonists in print rather than letting the criticism stand.

His time in office closed in April 1985, when Mack Humphreys wrote up Smith ending his term as Associated Student Government president. The Herald ran a second piece in the same issue crediting Smith's enthusiasm with reviving interest in ASG, and Kevin Knapp marked the departure with an editorial cartoon on Smith and the organisation.

events.title: Apathy as an editorial cartoon
events.body: 'Voter Apathy Can be Solved' ran alongside a cartoon on election apathy and a report that a 24-hour open house was under discussion.

events.title: Four proposals made reality in the third week of class
events.body: The Herald reported that four Associated Student Government proposals had already been carried out, and that the congress was beginning a study of a student book exchange. The exchange went on to become the running project of the year.

events.title: The grade scale proposal is denied
events.body: ASG's proposal for a new grade scale was denied, one week after the congress's early run of successes. It was the first setback of the fall reported in the Herald's coverage.

events.title: ASG wants less general education
events.body: The congress went on record wanting a reduction in general education requirements. It was an early instance of the body intervening in curriculum policy, three years before the fights over the General Education Task Force.

events.title: LaMont Jones drops out of a revote
events.body: LaMont Jones withdrew from an ASG revote, and the same issue carried an editorial cartoon on the organization. A disputed election requiring a revote marked the low point of the fall semester.

events.title: Education cuts loom and the book exchange stalls
events.body: ASG weighed a fight against state education cuts, while its book exchange venture looked likely to pause for the summer. Both stories ran in the same late-January issue.

events.title: Four file for congress president
events.body: A fourth candidate filed for ASG congress president and a debate was set, as the spring filing period opened. The same issue carried letters both applauding an ASG bill and requesting its support.

events.title: McKinney and Watkins take the primary
events.body: Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins rode their experience to victory in the ASG primary. The congress also passed a resolution on grade point averages the same week.

events.title: ASG candidates debated ahead of the spring election
events.body: Mack Humphreys covered a debate in which Associated Student Government candidates aired their views before the spring vote. The same issue of the Herald carried student letters backing Greg Elder, Chris Watkins and Mitchell McKinney, showing that the race to succeed Jack Smith was contested.

events.title: A reader disputed the Herald's editorial on ASG
events.body: The Herald printed a letter from Luis Dickson taking issue with an editorial the paper had run about Associated Student Government. The letter appeared in the middle of the spring campaign season.

events.title: An apathy editorial greets a 24-hour open house debate
events.body: The Herald ran an apathy editorial and cartoon aimed at student government alongside a report on debate over 24-hour open house policy in the dorms.

events.title: Dueling op-eds spar over forcing a bill
events.body: The Herald ran a pair of opposing opinion pieces, both headlined "Associated Student Government Shouldn't Force Bill," one by future ASG president Mitchell McKinney and the other by Jamie Morton.

events.title: ASG votes to study a book exchange
events.body: ASG voted to study the feasibility of a student book exchange and formed a committee to examine schemes at the universities of Louisville and Kentucky. Two models were discussed: a room where students sold and bought books at prices they set, and a cheaper list of students, telephone numbers, books for sale and asking prices. President Jack Smith said books were more expensive every year and students needed somewhere besides the College Heights Bookstore, adding, "I don't think there's anything wrong with a little competition."

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 60, No. 7, 20 September 1984

events.title: Book exchange ambassadors work the campus
events.body: ASG sent "ambassadors" out to campus organisations to explain the new book exchange and hand out registration cards, with public relations vice president John Holland promising to send a speaker "faster than Domino's pizza." Registration cards went into campus mailboxes on 5 December and had to be returned by 21 December, with an off-campus coupon printed in the Herald. The list of available books was to be compiled over Christmas and published as a tabloid of names, telephone numbers and titles when students returned in January.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 60, No. 24, 29 November 1984

events.title: The book exchanger's first edition
events.body: The tabloid book exchanger was distributed in the first week of the spring semester and students began telephoning each other to haggle over used textbooks. Committee co-chairmen John Holland and senior class president Danny Broderick, with President Jack Smith and administrative secretary Debra Stahl, keyed the entries into an IBM Personal Computer over the Christmas break on a program written for $25 by Bill Chestnut, a computer science graduate from Berea; Ginger Williams of the Franklin Favorite did the typesetting. Smith said the University of Kentucky had listed 700 books in its first exchange and Western had double that, and Broderick said ASG made no money from it: "This was a labor of love."
events.money: $25 paid for the computer program; about 1,400 books listed

events.title: ASG takes Big Brothers/Big Sisters children to a Lady Toppers game
events.body: Congress members each paired themselves with a child from Big Brothers/Big Sisters of Bowling Green for the women's last home basketball game, spending the evening counting heads, running trips to the bathroom and making enough noise to see the Lady Toppers past Cincinnati 122-72. Before the game the children ate snacks, made banners for the spirit contest and played pool and video games in the university center. The Herald reported that mothers in the crowd gave the student government members understanding looks.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 60, No. 43, 5 March 1985

events.title: Jack Smith ended his term as ASG president
events.body: The Herald of 11 April 1985 marked the end of Jack Smith's term as Associated Student Government president with a news story by Mack Humphreys. A companion editorial credited Smith's enthusiasm with reviving student interest in ASG, and Kevin Knapp drew an editorial cartoon on Smith and the organisation. Mitchell McKinney had been elected the new president the week before.

events.title: The Herald said dropping the campus pub was a good move
events.body: The Herald's editorial page said the Associated Student Government had made a good move by dropping the pub issue. It closed the alcohol question that had run through the previous spring's student poll, and the congress opened it again in November 1985.

events.title: ASG proposed a new required class
events.body: Chad Carlton reported that the Associated Student Government had proposed a new required class. It came in the same week the congress could point to four proposals already carried out, and eight days before its grade scale proposal was denied.

events.title: ASG asked for lot signs and safety railings
events.body: Victoria Malmer reported that the Associated Student Government had proposed parking lot signs and safety railings. The request followed a fall in the parking structure a week earlier, which the Herald had reported alongside safety director Paul Bunch's comment that the accident was unpreventable.

events.title: ASG moved to end the class attendance policy
events.body: Victoria Malmer reported that ASG wanted to end the university's class attendance policy, and the Herald's editorial page argued the same day that dealing with attendance ills could make things fairer. Kevin Knapp drew an editorial cartoon on excused absences in the same issue.

events.title: Vice President George Bush was announced to visit campus
events.body: The Herald of 25 October 1984 reported that Vice President George Bush would visit Western the following day, and its editorial page urged faculty to cancel classes for the visit. The digitised index carries the notice but no report of the visit itself, so nothing is recorded here about what happened on the day.

events.title: Few voted in the autumn ASG election
events.body: Victoria Malmer reported that few students had voted in the Associated Student Government election. A week later LaMont Jones dropped out of the revote and Kevin Knapp drew a cartoon on the organisation. Turnout was the theme of the whole year: by February the Herald was reporting that election apathy was hurting ASG.

events.title: Student government announced it would organise the book exchange
events.body: Victoria Malmer reported that student government was planning to organise the book exchange, and a companion item in the same issue described a programme to give students a choice of textbooks. By the end of November the Herald was reporting that ASG was promoting the exchange, and the first printed exchange list appeared at the start of the spring semester.

events.title: Two resolutions passed as the book exchange won its first praise
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had approved two resolutions, and printed a letter from Scott Vick applauding an ASG plan. Stan Reagan's column in the same issue argued that the book exchange would make money later but greater.

events.title: Apathy in the elections, and a summer for the book exchange
events.body: Mack Humphreys reported that election apathy was hurting the Associated Student Government. The same issue carried a short item that the book exchange was planned for the summer, a week after the paper had reported the venture might take a summer vacation instead.

events.title: Two resolutions pass, and a Book Exchanger chairman is appointed
events.body: At the meeting of 2 April 1985, Congress passed two resolutions and appointed a chairman for its Book Exchanger committee.

executive.name: Suzie Wilkins
executive.note: Reported to Congress on 18 September 1984 that 39 people had signed up and paid for Weekend in the Woods, discussed the budget, and told Congress the vouchers would be ready the following week.
profile: Suzie Wilkins served as Treasurer of the Associated Student Government in 1984-85. She reported to Congress on 18 September 1984 that 39 people had signed up and paid for the Weekend in the Woods retreat, discussed the year's budget, and told Congress the vouchers would be ready the following week. That January, while in office, she co-wrote a Herald letter to the editor with Ricki Richmond headlined 'Defends Greeks.'

executive.name: Connie Hoffmann
executive.note: Announced the vacancies on Congress week after week and, on 16 October 1984, the openings on the Judicial Council as well. She signed the minutes for the year.
profile: A Connie Hoffman — almost certainly the same person, given the continuity of interest — was writing about student government before she took office: a September 1983 Herald letter, 'And Old Tricks,' and, ahead of the spring 1984 ASG elections, an April 1984 letter defending a proposal from ASG's own Student Rights Committee (both bylined 'Hoffman' in the Herald's own index, one N; the ASG minutes and a later Herald letter about her spell it with two). The identification rests on the matching name and the continuous ASG involvement, not on a source that states the two are the same; it is recorded here as likely, not certain.
As Secretary in 1984-85 she announced the vacancies on Congress week after week and, on 16 October 1984, the openings on the Judicial Council as well; she signed the minutes for the year.

She sought further ASG office in the spring 1985 election: the Herald of 2 April 1985 carried a full slate of candidate-endorsement letters, one backing her ('Supports Connie Hoffmann'), alongside letters for Mitchell McKinney, Greg Elder, Loree Zimmerman, and Stan Reagan, plus a joint endorsement of Caroline Miller and Donna Holloway written by Elder himself. The Herald does not say which office any of the letters' subjects were seeking. Only McKinney's result is established elsewhere in this archive; it does not yet record who won the 1985-86 secretary, treasurer or vice-president races, so Hoffmann's absence from the recorded 1985-86 leadership does not establish that she lost — only that which office she sought, and how the race came out, is not yet established here.

executive.name: Julie Lippert
executive.note: Ran the class officers and the committee chairs. On 18 September 1984 she encouraged the class officers to meet and discuss ideas, and on 16 October she asked whether they had met with their committees and announced the committee chair dinner for 21 November 1984.
profile: Julie Lippert served as Administrative Vice-President of the Associated Student Government in 1984-85, running the class officers and the committee chairs. On 18 September 1984 she encouraged the class officers to meet and discuss ideas.

executive.name: John Holland
executive.note: Confirmed the speakers for the Weekend in the Woods retreat on 18 September 1984, and on 16 October announced the Talisman photograph date and raised the idea of a hayride.
profile: John Holland served as Public Relations Vice-President of the Associated Student Government in 1984-85, under President Jack Smith. He confirmed the speakers for that year's Weekend in the Woods retreat at Congress's 18 September 1984 meeting, and the following month announced the date for the Talisman yearbook's student-government photograph and raised the idea of a hayride.

Holland co-chaired the student book exchange, ASG's signature project of the year, alongside senior class president Danny Broderick. When the committee sent "ambassadors" out to campus organisations that November to explain the exchange and hand out registration cards, he promised, the Herald reported, to send a speaker "faster than Domino's pizza." Over the Christmas break he and Broderick, together with President Smith and administrative secretary Debra Stahl, keyed roughly 1,400 book listings into an IBM personal computer for the exchange's first printed edition, distributed when students returned for the spring semester.

officers.name: Mitchell McKinney
officers.note: Appointed Parliamentarian on 18 September 1984, the year before he was elected president. The minutes of that meeting write the name as Mitch McKinney. He also chaired the Student Affairs committee, and on 9 April 1985 commended his committee members for their year's work.
profile: McKinney was appointed Parliamentarian on 18 September 1984, a year before he was elected president; the minutes of that meeting record his name as Mitch McKinney. He also chaired the Student Affairs committee that year, and on 9 April 1985 commended its members for their work.

officers.name: Pat Franke
officers.note: Appointed Sergeant-at-Arms at the same meeting as the Parliamentarian, on 18 September 1984.
profile: Pat Franke was appointed Sergeant-at-Arms of the Associated Student Government Senate on 18 September 1984, the same meeting that named Mitchell McKinney parliamentarian. The archive has not turned up further coverage of their time in the post.
