members.note: Named absent at the roll call of the 4 September 1984 ASG meeting; she was elected secretary of Associated Student Government the following year, 1985-86.

documents.title: ASG meeting minutes, 4 September 1984
documents.summary: The first fall meeting of the year: roll call, officer reports on the Weekend in the Woods retreat, and the first reading of Bill 84-1-F.
documents.extract: Unexcused absences included: Jon Norris, Quinton Fawbush, Dorothy Metzmeier, Amy Deputy, Alexander Baird, William Beranek, Nancy Caudill, and Tara Wassom.

documents.title: ASG meeting minutes, 30 October 1984
documents.summary: Roll call, officer and committee reports, passage of Resolution 84-14-F by a vote of 17-4-1, and Mitchell McKinney chosen Congress member of the month.
documents.extract: Resolution 84-14-F passed with a vote of 17-4-1.

leaders.name: Mitchell McKinney
leaders.note: Named explicitly as SGA president in the outgoing congress's own commendation bill, Bill 86-13-S (3 Apr 1986), which settles the name.

sources.label: SGA Bill 86-13-S, Commendation of President, 3 Apr 1986
WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Before he was a candidate, McKinney wrote a Herald op-ed on 21 March 1985 headlined 'Associated Student Government Shouldn't Force Bill,' one of a pair of dueling pieces the paper ran on the same question - a sign he was already active in ASG's legislative debates a week before he entered the presidential race.

McKinney won the spring 1985 primary on a ticket with Chris Watkins on March 28, the Herald's headline saying the pair rode experience to their primary victory over a field that included candidate Stan Reagan. He was announced as the new Associated Student Government president in the Herald of April 4, in the same issue that reported an unnamed legislative group rejoining ASG. The record found so far does not confirm what office, if any, Watkins went on to hold.

In office, the congress abolished its own Finance Committee that September and, the following spring, wrote a Financial Advisory Council into the ASG bylaws in its place. The spring 1986 session was especially active: bills created major/minor college representative seats, revised the membership application process, asked Board of Regents members to attend an SGA meeting, sought chains for Pearce-Ford Tower windows, and pushed for a welcome sign at Normal Drive and University Boulevard.

In March 1986 McKinney pulled out of the race for a second term. The same issue carried a piece arguing that student government needed a strong leader, and the field he left behind grew to four candidates before Tim Todd won the presidency that April. The outgoing congress commended McKinney's work in Bill 86-13-S on April 3, and the WKU Board of Regents included a resolution honoring him, alongside outgoing president John D. Minton, at its meeting of August 8, 1986. A 1986 presidential proclamation he signed honoring English professor Thomas Jones survives in the SGA records.

events.title: McKinney and Watkins win the ASG primary
events.body: Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins won the Associated Student Government presidential primary over a field that included candidate Stan Reagan.

events.title: McKinney elected president; a legislative group rejoins ASG
events.body: Mitchell McKinney was elected Associated Student Government president. The same issue reported that an unnamed legislative group had rejoined ASG.

events.title: ASG abolishes its Finance Committee
events.body: The congress voted to abolish its own Finance Committee, a structural change later reversed in part when a Financial Advisory Council was written into the bylaws the following spring.

src.label: SGA Bill 85-1-F, Abolishment of Finance Committee

events.title: ASG orders its own student discount card
events.body: The congress passed legislation calling for ASG to produce its own student discount card, one of several consumer-service ideas the group pursued that fall.

src.label: SGA Bill 85-15-F, Production of Own Student Discount Card

events.title: A 20-vote margin and a GPA debate
events.body: About 20 votes separated the top two finishers in a fall ASG election, and the congress debated setting a grade-point average requirement for its own members. Both stories ran in the same late-October issue.

events.title: Alcohol on campus studied again
events.body: ASG returned to the question of alcohol on campus, an issue that had already produced a student poll and a campus pub debate in 1984. The congress opened a new study of the policy.

events.title: A shuttle to the mall
events.body: The congress discussed running a shuttle service from campus to the mall. It was one of several consumer-service ideas, alongside student discount cards, floated that fall.

events.title: Lighting proposal defeated
events.body: Student government defeated a campus lighting proposal in the last week of the fall semester. It was one of the few outright defeats of legislation reported that year.

events.title: Fall-break bill narrowly passes
events.body: A bill calling for a fall break narrowly passed ASG. The proposal drew an opposing editorial in the next issue calling the extra break impractical and not needed.

events.title: No day off for Martin Luther King Day
events.body: ASG rejected a proposal to dismiss classes for the Martin Luther King holiday, one week after passing the fall-break bill. The King holiday question returned to the congress the following year.

events.title: McKinney withdraws from re-election
events.body: Mitchell McKinney pulled out of the race for a second term as ASG president. The same issue carried a piece arguing that student government needed a strong leader.

events.title: Library hours proposals, and elections delayed a week
events.body: ASG proposals asked for more library hours, and the spring elections were pushed back a week. The same issue carried dueling letters on whether the organization was in trouble.

events.title: College representative seats created
events.body: The congress created major/minor college representative seats within its own membership.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-19-S, Voting of Representatives for Colleges

events.title: ASG revises its membership application
events.body: The congress adopted a revised application process for SGA membership.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-21-S, Adoption of New Application

events.title: ASG asks regents to attend a meeting
events.body: The congress asked that Board of Regents members attend and speak at one SGA meeting during their term.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-22-S, Attendance of Regents at Meetings

events.title: ASG seeks chains for Pearce-Ford Tower windows
events.body: The congress asked for chains to be placed on Pearce-Ford Tower windows so they could be opened.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-26-S, Placing of Chain on Windows

events.title: Financial Advisory Council written into the bylaws
events.body: The congress incorporated the Financial Advisory Council into the ASG bylaws, months after abolishing its own Finance Committee.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-3-S, Incorporation of Councils into By-Laws

events.title: Outgoing congress commends President McKinney
events.body: The outgoing congress passed a bill commending the work of SGA president Mitchell McKinney as his term ended.

events.title: Pranks and accusations mar the races
events.body: The Herald reported that pranks and accusations had marred the ASG races, and printed the election results in the same issue. Tim Todd emerged from the field as the new president.

events.title: ASG pushes for a campus welcome sign
events.body: The congress pushed for a welcome sign to be placed at the intersection of Normal Drive and University Boulevard.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-36-S, Placing of Welcome Sign on Campus

events.title: ASG commends outgoing President Minton
events.body: The congress passed a bill commending outgoing WKU president John D. Minton for his service to the university.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-39-S, Commendation of Dr. John D. Minton

events.title: The commonwealth attorney is asked to find the discount card printer
events.body: ASG's student discount cards finally went out in October after Phil Bewley of Parkland Publishers Inc. missed two August deadlines and the Warren County Commonwealth Attorney's Office was called in to find him. Bewley, reached by telephone in Nashville, said he believed President Mitchell McKinney had understood the cards would not be ready until 23 September, and blamed printer trouble. It was the second time in five years the same representative had left an ASG discount card in limbo.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 61, No. 13, 10 October 1985

events.title: ASG wins its division of November Nonsense
events.body: ASG was the only non-Greek group to enter November Nonsense, the variety show Chi Omega has staged since 1965, and took first place in the organisation division. Its skit followed an orange-faced, loud-mouthed "oompah" projected from 1965, when he was a star Western footballer, to 1985, when he became a potential candidate for the university presidency. Seven groups performed four-to-six minute skits on a "Back to the Future" theme, and the sorority raised about $800 for Hospice.

events.title: ASG hosts the state student government conference
events.body: ASG hosted the state Student Government Conference at Glasgow to promote involvement and the role of student government. President Mitchell McKinney and the organisation's roughly 100 members also joined the students, faculty and administrators who rallied in Frankfort in support of higher education in Kentucky. McKinney sat on the University Center Board and the Education Advisory Committee as well as the Board of Regents.

events.title: ASG asks for lights in 11 dark spots
events.body: After two women were assaulted within a fortnight in April, ASG passed a resolution on 10 April asking for more lighting in eleven places on campus. A Herald editorial on 15 April backed it, noting that a new lamppost cost between $500 and $750 and about $36.50 a year to run, "a small price to pay for safety." The same spring saw more women using the escort service and enrolling in the university's self-defence class.
events.money: $500 to $750 per lamppost; about $36.50 a year to run

events.title: ASG proposed cancelling classes for snow as needed
events.body: Bill 85-3-F, dated 8 October 1985, proposed that classes be cancelled because of snow as needed rather than on a fixed schedule. It is one of a run of small practical bills in Mitchell McKinney's term, filed a week after the bill creating the Financial Advisory Council.

events.title: ASG reconsidered child care as the Herald told it to represent students
events.body: Kim Parson reported that ASG was reconsidering child care, a question the congress had first taken up in November 1983. The same issue carried a Herald opinion piece saying ASG needed to start representing students and a Kevin Knapp editorial cartoon on the organisation, and reported that the field of candidates for the university presidency had been narrowed to about 20.

events.title: ASG pushed to merge the student ID and the SuperCard
events.body: Resolution 85-14-F, dated 3 December 1985, proposed creating a single card combining the student ID and the SuperCard. It followed Bill 85-12-F of 19 November, which asked that use of the SuperCard be extended across campus. The same night's Bill 85-15-F asked that ASG produce its own student discount card, after the outside printer's failures that autumn.

src.label: SGA Resolution 85-14-F, Student ID Card and SuperCard Merger

events.title: ASG joined the higher education rally in Frankfort
events.body: ASG joined students, faculty and administrators from Western at the state-wide rally for higher education held at the Frankfort Civic Center on 6 February 1986 and sponsored by Kentucky Advocates for Higher Education. Chartered buses left from in front of Downing University Center for the three-hour journey, carrying Spirit Masters, cheerleaders, pep bands, reporters, teachers and administrators, and the administration wrote to teachers asking them to excuse students who went. Every university in the state was represented, and Governor Martha Layne Collins and former North Carolina governor James Hunt spoke.

events.title: Greg Elder filed for the top job as the deadline neared
events.body: Jackie Hutcherson reported that the filing deadline was Friday and that administrative vice president Greg Elder had filed for the ASG presidency, two days after Mitchell McKinney withdrew from the race. The same issue carried a Herald opinion piece by Steve Reagan arguing that ASG had to develop goals and priorities, and letters from Meredith Gainer and Loree Zimmerman defending the organisation.

events.title: Few watched four candidates debate, and the Herald endorsed nobody
events.body: Jackie Hutcherson reported that few people watched the four candidates for the ASG presidency debate. The paper printed profiles of Greg Elder, Andy Hollifield, Terry Malone and Tim Todd and then declined to back any of them, running an editorial headed that no candidate stood out and endorsing a fictional Joe Ideal instead. The same issue reported ASG proposing that faculty return tests to students, the subject of Bill 86-15-S filed nine days earlier.

events.title: ASG asked for a campus map at Downing University Center
events.body: Bill 86-34-S, dated 8 April 1986, requested that a campus map be placed at the Downing University Center. It was one of ten bills the outgoing congress filed that night, among them Bill 86-35-S asking for a scholarship for students from Santo Domingo de los Colorados, Bowling Green's sister city, and Bill 86-37-S for bulletin boards in the Downing University Center lift.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-34-S, Placing of a Campus Map

events.title: Elder named the session's three achievements
events.body: Administrative vice president Greg Elder told the Talisman that ASG counted three bills as its main accomplishments of the year: having the English 101 pass/fail moved, reducing the hours a student needed to live in Poland Hall, and producing the book exchange programme. ASG was one of five organisations whose presidents met once a month over breakfast, a group the yearbook called the Big Five, with Interhall Council, Spirit Masters, the Interfraternity Council and the Panhellenic Council.

events.title: McKinney sat on the search that chose Kern Alexander
events.body: As student regent, ASG president Mitchell McKinney took an active part in Western's search for a president, which produced Kern Alexander after the board screened applicants, visited candidates on their own campuses and interviewed the finalists. McKinney also sat as a voting member of the University Center Board and the Education Advisory Committee, led a congress of about 100 members, and told the Talisman he intended to go on to graduate school and teach at university level.

events.title: A Financial Advisory Council replaces the Finance Committee
events.body: Two weeks after abolishing its Finance Committee, Congress considered Bill 85-2-F, which proposed forming a Financial Advisory Council with access to Congress's financial records.

src.label: SGA Bill 85-2-F, Formation of Financial Advisory Council

events.title: A bill proposes letting absent bill authors vote by proxy
events.body: Bill 86-8-S, considered by Congress in early 1986, proposed amending ASG's by-laws to allow voting by proxy.

events.title: By-laws amended on expelling representatives
events.body: Bill 86-31-S, filed 8 April 1986, proposed amending ASG's by-laws on the expulsion of representatives, tied to attendance at the Academic Council.

src.label: SGA Bill 86-31-S - Amendment of By-Laws for Expulsion of Representatives

executive.name: Mitchell McKinney
executive.note: Ran on a primary ticket with Chris Watkins in spring 1985; the record found so far does not confirm what office, if any, Watkins held afterward. Withdrew from re-election in March 1986 and was commended by the outgoing congress that April.

executive.name: Cindy Richards
executive.note: Named as the incoming Treasurer on 9 April 1985 and reported the ASG balance as $2,045.59 at the final meeting of the year on 15 April 1986.
profile: Cindy Richards, an accounting major from Cloverport, was named the Associated Student Government's incoming Treasurer at the 9 April 1985 meeting and served through 1985-86. At the year's final Congress meeting on 15 April 1986 she reported the organization's balance as $2,045.59. The 1986 Talisman's Associated Student Government page pictures her among that year's executive officers alongside Greg Elder, Tara Wassom and Loree Zimmerman.

executive.name: Tara Wassom
executive.note: Signed the minutes of 15 April 1986, at which she thanked the Student Affairs committee for addressing the banquet invitations.
profile: Tara Wassom, a public relations major from Fort Campbell, served as the Associated Student Government's Secretary in 1985-86 and signed the minutes of the year's final meeting, 15 April 1986, at which she thanked the Student Affairs committee for handling the banquet invitations.

executive.name: Greg Elder
executive.note: Named as the incoming Administrative Vice-President by the outgoing president on 9 April 1985. He was still in the office at the last meeting of the year, 15 April 1986, at which he had no report.
profile: Greg Elder, a Glasgow junior, was named the Associated Student Government's incoming Administrative Vice President by the outgoing president on 9 April 1985 and was still in the post at the year's final Congress meeting on 15 April 1986, though he gave no report that day. Describing ASG's work to the 1986 Talisman, Elder said the organization "take[s] students' wants and translate[s] them into action and results," and named moving English 101 to a pass/fail option, reducing the hours required to live in Poland Hall, and starting a book exchange program as the year's accomplishments.

Elder filed to run for ASG president in early March 1986. Mitchell McKinney's withdrawal from re-election left Elder and Tim Todd to contest an April runoff, which the Herald reported Todd winning. Elder ran again the next spring: the Herald's 9 April 1987 issue reported him and Todd through to a runoff it called a "deja vu primary," and the following week's issue reported Todd beating him in the re-run general election.

executive.name: Loree Zimmerman
executive.note: Also chaired the Public Relations committee. At the closing meeting of 15 April 1986 she thanked her committee, the Executive Council and the Congress members, and set out the schedule for the banquet and the organisation's anniversary activities.
profile: Loree Zimmerman, a senior from Providence, served as the Associated Student Government's Public Relations Vice President in 1985-86 and chaired its Public Relations committee. At the year's closing Congress meeting on 15 April 1986 she thanked her committee, the Executive Council and the Congress membership, and laid out the schedule for the year-end banquet and the organization's anniversary activities.

committees.name: Finance Committee
committees.note: Abolished by the congress in September 1985.

committees.name: Financial Advisory Council
committees.note: Written into the ASG bylaws in April 1986, replacing the abolished Finance Committee.

senate.note: Spring 1986 also created major/minor college representative seats (Bill 86-19-S) and revised the SGA membership application process (Bill 86-21-S).

officers.name: Donna Pack
officers.note: Called College Representatives to the meeting of 24 April 1986, which the minutes name only as AC, to discuss the new English policy.
profile: Donna Pack chaired the Academic Affairs Committee of Associated Student Government in 1985-86. At the Congress's meeting of 15 April 1986 she announced a meeting on 24 April — the minutes abbreviate it only as AC, and do not say which body it was — and asked college representatives to attend to discuss a new English policy; what was decided there is not recorded.
She is pictured with that year's other ASG officers and committee chairs in a group photograph in the 1986 Talisman.

officers.name: Caroline Miller
officers.note: Brought the spring session's closing block of legislation to Congress on 15 April 1986, recommending eight bills for approval including the establishment of KISL as a standing committee, the amendment of the by-laws and the campus welcome sign, and recommending against 86-30-S on retaining the faculty evaluation system.
profile: Caroline Miller chaired the Legislative Research Committee of Associated Student Government in 1985-86. At the Congress's closing meeting of 15 April 1986 she brought the spring session's last block of legislation to the floor, recommending approval of eight items, including making the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature delegation a standing ASG committee, amending ASG's by-laws, and placing a welcome sign on campus, while recommending against 86-30-S, which would have retained the existing faculty evaluation system. All of that night's legislation passed regardless: the eight recommended items were approved unanimously, by amendment, or viva voce, and Congress also passed 86-30-S unanimously, over Miller's committee's objection.

Miller was probably also the Caroline Miller who served as a delegate to the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature, the mock-legislature program ASG made a standing committee that spring. In the 1986 Talisman's account of campus political groups, the delegation's chairman, Lori Scott, named that Miller's election as the group's lieutenant governor one of the year's biggest accomplishments.

profile: Sean Peck chaired the Rules and Elections Committee of Associated Student Government in 1985-86, the year his committee ran that spring's Congress elections. At the 15 April 1986 closing meeting he congratulated the newly elected Congress members and thanked his committee for its work, and he seconded the motion to adjourn, made by Bill Schilling. A year earlier, before he held office, he had written to the Herald arguing that involvement in ASG was the answer to student apathy on campus.

The Herald of 27 March 1986 carried a piece from Peck himself, headlined "Thanks A Lot," addressed to Associated Student Government as his chairmanship closed. In the 1986 Talisman, a Sean Peck described as a Gilbertsville senior was quoted on the university's move to coed dormitory housing.

documents.title: ASG meeting minutes, 15 April 1986
documents.summary: The last surviving meeting of the year: roll call, officer and committee reports, and passage of a slate of resolutions including a commendation of Dr. John D. Minton.
documents.extract: Congratulated new Congress members, and wished them a successful year.

leaders.name: Timothy Todd
leaders.note: Two-year plate. A 1987 Herald piece reports a candidate shortage and mentions a Tim Todd race. Confirmed from inside the term by his own signed Herald column of 11 September 1986 explaining what ASG was and what it was for.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Todd reached the April 1986 runoff against Greg Elder after Mitchell McKinney's withdrawal left the presidential field open. The Herald reported the two-man race on 3 April, with the general election the following week.

Days after an election week the Herald described as marred by pranks and accusations, the paper identified Todd as the new ASG president in a sharply critical opinion piece headlined that he lacked knowledge of his own issues. Todd answered in print the following issue, criticizing the paper's reporting.
His first fall opened with an approved budget of $12,100, a plan to reach students by phone for their ideas and needs, and an ASG retreat featuring university president Kern Alexander.

Todd's first year leading Associated Student Government opened with ordinary organisational business. The Herald of 11 September 1986 reported that ASG approved a $12,100 budget, planned to telephone students to collect their ideas and needs, and scheduled a retreat that was to feature Kern Alexander.

By the end of the spring term the body was still working through routine legislation, tabling a phone bill after an amendment was raised, while a student government conference was set for that weekend. The same issue of 26 March 1987 covered the election for the following year, in which Todd stood again and Bill Fogle said he had entered the presidential race to help Todd rather than to win it.

events.title: Twenty years of amendments consolidated into one document
events.body: The constitution of the WKU Associated Students with amendments - the only surviving snapshot of how the 1966 framework had been patched over two decades. A Judicial Council roster for 1986-87 survives alongside it.

events.title: A minor change in voting
events.body: ASG sought a minor change in its voting procedures early in the fall term. It was the first structural tinkering of the Todd presidency.

events.title: Rules suspended, bills passed
events.body: The congress suspended its rules to pass a batch of bills in a single meeting. The rush came as the spring filing period for elections was opening.

events.title: Martin Luther King bill splits the congress
events.body: A Martin Luther King bill passed the congress with members split by the argument, a year after ASG had rejected dismissing classes for the holiday. The same issue reported that Tim Todd and Greg Elder would battle again for the presidency.

events.title: Attendance drops after the speeches
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG attendance fell off once campaign speeches had been heard. An accompanying piece warned voters that talk was cheap in the presidential race.

events.title: An amendment dies of low member turnout
events.body: A constitutional amendment was defeated because too few members turned up to vote on it. The failure came in the same week as the presidential election.

events.title: The Herald calls the race for Elder; the index calls it no contest
events.body: On election day the Herald endorsed challenger Greg Elder as the better choice to lead ASG, ran a letter calling the organization impotent, and headlined the race itself as no contest. The indexed issues that survive do not record the published result; the SGA plaque carries Todd through 1988 on a two-year plate.

events.title: ASG plans to phone students for their ideas
events.body: Associated Student Government announced that it would reach out to students by telephone to hear their ideas and needs. The plan was reported in the same 11 September 1986 issue that covered the year's budget.

events.title: ASG tables phone bill after amendment
events.body: Associated Student Government tabled a phone bill once an amendment to it was raised. The Herald reported the outcome in its issue of 26 March 1987.

events.title: Regents honor McKinney at term's end
events.body: The WKU Board of Regents included a resolution honoring outgoing ASG president Mitchell McKinney, alongside honors for Georgia Bates and outgoing WKU president John Minton, at its August meeting - held the same day Kern Alexander was named the university's new president.

events.title: ASG takes over the student discount card
events.body: Associated Student Government took production of the wallet-sized student discount card in house after the company contracted the previous year delayed distribution. The printer, John Bewley, had been indicted by a Warren County grand jury for theft of service over $100 for failing to pay ASG the $500 it was owed for distributing the cards, then paid and had the case dismissed. Administrative vice president Lori Scott said about 20 merchants had already bought advertising at $100 each and she hoped for 30 to 40, with the cards out by the first week of October.
events.money: $100 per merchant advertisement, about 20 sold; a $500 debt recovered from the previous printer

events.title: Weekend in the Woods, the fourth annual ASG leadership camp
events.body: ASG sponsored the fourth annual Weekend in the Woods, a leadership conference at Camp Decker about 13 miles from Bowling Green, and 45 students attended against accommodation for 75 at $30 a head covering meals and lodging. Members had begun lining up speakers and camp reservations the previous March; seminars covered leadership, goal setting, generating ideas and listening, and for the first time student leaders spoke alongside faculty. State senator-elect Nick Kafoglis lectured, and when President Kern Alexander could not make the closing session he invited every Weekender to breakfast at his home a week later. The yearbook does not date the weekend.

src.label: 1987 Talisman, 'Branching Out - Weekend in the Woods'

events.title: $10,000 for campus lights and a plan for a student hangout
events.body: The 1987 Talisman recorded ASG's two main projects of the year as more campus lighting and a student hangout in Downing University Center, both traced to President Kern Alexander's concern about student retention raised at a September breakfast with ASG members. ASG persuaded the administration to put up $10,000 for new lights. To stop students going home at weekends, members formed committees to arrange the music and the lighting for a place in the university center where students could dance without leaving campus.
events.money: $10,000 from the administration for new campus lighting

events.title: A recorded campus events phone line is put on hold
events.body: A proposal to start a telephone service playing recorded messages about campus events was tabled at the 3 February meeting until more research could be done. The equipment would have cost $500, with $60 for installation and a $17 monthly service charge, and author Bill Schilling said promotion would add $200 more. Public Information director Fred Hensley had not been consulted before the bill was introduced, and the sports information office already ran a line of its own.
events.money: $500 equipment, $60 installation, $17 a month, plus $200 promotion

events.title: ASG president shot in the members' assassination game
events.body: ASG members spent the autumn of 1986 playing an assassination game with squirt guns, sponsored by the congress's public relations committee. President Tim Todd was shot at about 8 p.m. on Thursday 2 October in his State Street apartment, wearing only a bathrobe. Kathryn Michelsen killed three other congress members the same night, including a sleeping Holger Velastegui, and three more on the Sunday, two of them in front of their girlfriends; she led the field until Gamaliel freshman Janet Dyer shot her between the eyes near the university center on the night of 8 October.

src.label: College Heights Herald 62:13, 9 Oct 1986 - Jessie, "Associated Student Government Members All Wet From Playing with Guns"

events.title: ASG prepared to host the second statewide student government conference
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG would host the second annual statewide student government conference from Friday 27 March through Sunday, at the American Plaza on Scottsville Road. President Tim Todd expected about 50 student leaders, against about 65 at the first conference, which ASG had also hosted, and put the cost of hosting at $400 to $500. Registration was $18 and the conference was open to all students. Saturday seminars covered leadership, communication and financial aid, with the Council on Higher Education flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington and sending its director, Gary S. Cox.

events.title: A $12,100 budget, a telephone outreach and a retreat with the university president
events.body: ASG approved an operating budget of $12,100. It also planned a telephone outreach effort to hear students' ideas and needs, and announced a retreat featuring university president Kern Alexander. The Herald carried all three items on 11 September 1986, in the second week of the fall semester.

events.title: International Day held three weeks of the congress's attention
events.body: International Day was ASG business through the autumn of 1986. The minutes of 14 October record it alongside events and discount cards, those of 21 October record it alongside elections and legislation, and those of 28 October record it with the Legislative Research Committee and the Student Action Committee. The minutes do not record how the day itself went.

events.title: Alphabet Day recurs across the year's minutes
events.body: Alphabet Day appears three times in the surviving 1986-87 minutes: on 23 September 1986 with elections, the retreat and committee appointments, on 24 February 1987 with the faculty reception and the high school leadership conference, and on 17 March 1987 with the spring conference and the lecture series. The minutes name it without describing it.

events.title: A joint hot dog supper with the University Center Board
events.body: On 3 October 1986 Tim Harper and David Rodriguez sent a joint invitation to the members of student government and of the University Center Board to a hot dog supper. The invitation survives in SGA's own records; the archive's description names the two men but gives them no offices.

src.label: SGA correspondence, Hot Dog Supper, 3 October 1986

events.title: A lecture series and a Young Democrats versus Young Republicans debate
events.body: The minutes of 25 November 1986 record a lecture series and a debate between the Young Democrats and the Young Republicans among the congress's business, together with legislation and a Kentucky student government association meeting at Western. The lecture series returns in the minutes of 17 March 1987, and debates again in those of 24 March 1987. What was scheduled is recorded; no account of either event survives in the minutes.

events.title: Lieutenant Governor Steve Beshear's visit comes before the congress
events.body: The minutes of 31 March 1987 record a visit by Lieutenant Governor Steve Beshear alongside the state student government meeting, other events and resolutions. This is a note of what was arranged; the minutes do not report the visit itself.

events.title: A faculty reception breakfast and the book exchange
events.body: The minutes of 17 February 1987 record a faculty reception breakfast and the book exchange among the congress's business, with legislation and the committee meeting schedule. The faculty reception returns in the minutes of 24 February 1987 alongside a high school leadership conference.

events.title: Todd went to Wisconsin to look at a campus hangout
events.body: The minutes of 18 November 1986 record ASG president Tim Todd's trip to Wisconsin about a campus hangout, alongside the Western-Notre Dame game and legislation. The hangout in Downing University Center was one of the two projects the 1987 Talisman named as ASG's main work that year, and the minutes of 24 March 1987 return to it.

events.title: ASG asked for the mandatory athletic fee to be abolished
events.body: Resolution 86-8-F, dated 14 October 1986, proposed ending the student athletic fee. The same meeting took Resolution 86-9-F, asking Campus Police to issue a warning rather than a ticket for a first offence.

src.label: Resolution 86-8-F, Abolishment of Mandatory Athletic Fee, 14 October 1986

events.title: Two academic resolutions on one night: the W and a reading day
events.body: On 18 November 1986 the congress took Resolution 86-14-F, asking that the W for a withdrawn course be removed from student transcripts, and Resolution 86-15-F, asking for a reading day before final exams. The study day request was still being made by successive congresses into the 1990s.

events.title: One member wrote most of the congress's bills
events.body: The Herald of 11 December 1986 reported that a single member of Associated Student Government, Bill Schilling, wrote most of the bills that came before the congress. Schilling was the author of the recorded campus events phone line proposal tabled that February, and he was at the centre of the impeachment attempt the following autumn.

events.title: The Herald's verdict on the year: conflicts and walkouts
events.body: Leigh Eagleston's piece in the Herald of 23 April 1987 summed up the ASG year under the headline that conflicts and walkouts had finished it off. It ran in the last issues of the spring term, after the amendment that died for want of members and the disputed presidential race.

events.title: Kern Alexander installed as Western's president
events.body: The minutes of 11 November 1986 record the installation of Kern Alexander as Western's president among the congress's business, with fall enrolment, the spring conference and the Western-Notre Dame game. Alexander had been named president that August; he resigned in the spring of 1988.

events.title: Athletic fee bill defeated; a top ASG race decided by eight votes
events.body: Associated Student Government defeated a bill that would have made the athletic fee optional. The same issue reported that a top ASG race had been decided by only eight votes.

events.title: Todd beats Elder in an election re-run
events.body: Leigh Eagleston reported that Tim Todd beat Greg Elder in a re-run of the Associated Student Government presidential election, two days after the Herald had indexed the first contest as no contest and endorsed Elder. The same issue carried a letter from Shannon Ragland asking that ASG's name be cleared. The archive previously recorded that the published result of the 1987 race did not survive; this settles it.

src.label: Herald 62:54, 16 Apr 1987, "Tim Todd Beats Greg Elder in Election Re-Run"

events.title: The Herald calls the congress paralyzed
events.body: Doug Gott wrote a piece headlined that Associated Student Government was paralyzed, in the last week of the spring term. It followed a fortnight of election re-run, walkouts and letters, and the surviving index preserves only the headline.

executive.name: Barbara Rush
executive.note: Presented the 1986-87 budget to Congress on 9 September 1986, which was accepted by acclamation.
profile: Barbara Rush, a senior from Louisville, served as the Associated Student Government's Treasurer in 1986-87 and presented the year's budget to Congress on 9 September 1986, which was accepted by acclamation. The 1987 Talisman pictured her taking notes as ASG treasurer during a lecture by state senator-elect Nick Kafoglis at the organization's Weekend in the Woods retreat that September.

executive.name: John Schocke
executive.note: Read the attendance policy to Congress at the first meeting of the year and kept the standing list of vacant seats, which in September 1986 stood at the Business, Ogden and Education college alternates and an on-campus representative. He signed the minutes as John C. Schocke.
profile: John Schocke served as the Associated Student Government's Secretary in 1986-87. At the first Congress meeting of the year he read the attendance policy to the body and kept the standing list of vacant seats, which by September 1986 covered alternate seats for the Business, Ogden and Education colleges and one on-campus representative; he signed the minutes as John C. Schocke.

executive.name: Lori Scott
executive.note: Set proposed goals for each of the standing committees at the first meeting of the year, and took charge of the student discount card, telling Congress it was being produced strictly by ASG and not by Key Line Guide.
profile: Lori Scott, of Princeton, chaired the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature committee for the Associated Student Government in 1985-86, reporting that spring's KISL session a success and being congratulated by Congress on being made KISL's Speaker Pro Tem. She moved up to Administrative Vice President the following year, 1986-87, setting proposed goals for each of ASG's standing committees at the first meeting of the year and taking charge of the student discount card, telling Congress it was being produced strictly by ASG rather than by the Key Line Guide.

executive.name: Daniel Rodriguez
executive.note: Distributed the new ASG brochures at the opening meeting of 2 September 1986 and announced the Weekend in the Woods leadership retreat at Camp Decker for 12 to 14 September 1986. He also chaired the Public Relations committee.
profile: Daniel Rodriguez, a senior from Barquisimeto, Venezuela, served as the Associated Student Government's Public Relations Vice President in 1986-87 and chaired its Public Relations committee. At the opening Congress meeting of 2 September 1986 he distributed the year's new ASG brochures and announced the Weekend in the Woods leadership retreat, held at Camp Decker 12-14 September 1986.

Rodriguez helped organize that retreat starting in March, lining up speakers and camp reservations, then promoting it with letters to freshmen, newspaper ads and brochures mailed to campus organizations. Rodriguez told the 1987 Talisman that the lower-than-expected turnout, 45 of a possible 75, actually helped attendees participate more. When the closing speaker, university president Kern Alexander, could not make the retreat, he invited the attendees to breakfast at his home the following week instead; Rodriguez called it "a great way to finish."

officers.name: Chris Millay
officers.note: Nominated from the floor and elected Parliamentarian on 2 September 1986. He was also vice-chair of the Legislative Research Committee that year.
profile: Chris Millay was nominated from the floor and elected Parliamentarian of Associated Student Government on 2 September 1986; the minutes note he also served as vice-chair of the Legislative Research Committee that year. Two weeks into his term, writing as Christopher Millay, he had a piece published in the Herald on the stereotyping of Christianity.

officers.name: Dwight Austin
officers.note: Elected Sergeant-at-Arms on 2 September 1986 from a field of four nominations, and appointed to the Judicial Council the following week. The minutes spell the surname both Austin and Austion.
profile: Dwight Austin was elected Sergeant-at-Arms of Associated Student Government on 2 September 1986, from a field of four nominees, and was appointed to the Judicial Council the following week. The minutes spell his surname both Austin and Austion. No further record of his time in office has been found in the sources searched so far.

officers.name: Dan Wooten
officers.note: Named chair when Congress confirmed the whole 1986-87 Judicial Council on 9 September 1986, the appointment having been held over from the first meeting of the year.
profile: Dan Wooten was named chair of the Judicial Council when Congress confirmed the full 1986-87 council on 9 September 1986, an appointment that had been held over from the year's first meeting. No further record of his time in the office has been found in the sources searched so far.

officers.name: Holger Velastegui
officers.note: Appointed chair on 2 September 1986 and encouraged freshmen to take part in that autumn's elections. In the previous year he had written the legislation asking for a scholarship for Bowling Green's sister city, Santo Domingo de los Colorados.
profile: Holger Velastegui, of Bowling Green, chaired the Rules and Elections Committee of Associated Student Government in 1986-87, appointed on 2 September 1986. The year before, he had worked on the legislation asking for a scholarship tied to Bowling Green's sister city, Santo Domingo de los Colorados, work the 1985-86 Student Affairs chairman publicly thanked him for; the minutes do not say which committee, if any, he served on at the time. As chairman himself he campaigned for turnout: the 2 September 1986 minutes record him encouraging freshmen to take part in that fall's elections, and the Herald carried a piece from him that October headlined "Freshmen, Vote Today." He also wrote to the Herald that October urging students to take part in a campus international event.

Velastegui had also written to the Herald that spring backing Daniel Rodriguez's campaign for ASG's public relations vice presidency, and a year later, in April 1987, Rodriguez returned the favor, writing publicly to back Velastegui in that spring's ASG elections; the record does not show what office he sought or whether he won. He appears with other ASG members in a 1986 Talisman group photograph.

profile: Jeff Key chaired the Student Affairs Committee of Associated Student Government in 1986-87, appointed on 2 September 1986. On 9 September he reminded all class vice-presidents that ASG's rules required them to serve on his committee. In February 1987 he co-wrote a Herald piece with fellow ASG officer Kim Summers on spring break options for students.

officers.name: Bill Fogle
officers.note: Appointed chair of Academic Affairs on 2 September 1986.
profile: Bill Fogle chaired the Associated Student Government's Academic Affairs Committee in 1986-87, appointed at Congress's 2 September 1986 meeting. He had written to the Herald in January 1986, before he joined the cabinet, under the headline "Student Apathy Criticized."

In spring 1987 Fogle entered the ASG presidential race himself. The Herald reported on 26 March that he had started his campaign to help fellow candidate Tim Todd rather than to win it, and on 7 April that he had ended his bid for the presidency; Todd went on to win a second term. Using the fuller name William Fogle, Fogle stayed visible in the organization's business afterward: the Herald of 10 December 1987 credited him with explaining Congress's actions in the affair around Administrative Vice President Bill Schilling, after Congress dropped an impeachment proceeding against Schilling and placed him under a watchdog committee instead.

profile: Kent Groemling chaired the Faculty Relations Committee of Associated Student Government in 1986-87, appointed on 2 September 1986, and also sat on that year's Judicial Council, confirmed by Congress the following week. He is pictured with other ASG officers and committee chairs in the 1986 Talisman the year before he took the chairmanship, and is probably the same Kent Groemling the 1987 Talisman elsewhere describes as being from Louisville.

Outside ASG that same fall, Groemling served on the University Center Board's special events committee, the year the Homecoming pep rally, Big Red's Roar, moved outdoors to Smith Stadium for the first time. He told the 1987 Talisman the change went over well apart from complaints about the cold, and that organizers expected to keep it outdoors.

profile: Chris LeNeave chaired the Student Rights Committee of Associated Student Government in 1986-87, appointed on 2 September 1986. Several months earlier, in April 1986, he had written to the Herald criticizing the paper's own staff.

The Christopher LeNeave listed in the 1987 Talisman's senior class directory as a Mayfield native studying biology is the same man. The yearbook's index carries a single Leneave, Christopher M., and refers him to the directory page and to the two pages carrying the Associated Student Government group photographs, in the first of which he is named in the second row beside William Schilling, with president Tim Todd in the back row. An earlier pass recorded the two as possibly distinct; the index entry closes the gap.

documents.title: ASG meeting minutes, 2 September 1986
documents.summary: The first fall meeting of the year: roll call, approval of the committee chairs and vice-chairs, and the floor elections of a Parliamentarian and a Sergeant-At-Arms.
documents.extract: Dwight Austin was elected Sergeant-At-Arms.

leaders.name: Timothy Todd
leaders.note: Two-year plate. A 1987 Herald piece reports a candidate shortage and mentions a Tim Todd race. Confirmed from inside the term: the Herald of 31 March 1988, reporting the ASG presidential primary, refers to Todd as the sitting president.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Todd sought a second term in spring 1987 in a rematch against Greg Elder, the man he had beaten the year before. The Herald reported the two would battle again in its 19 March issue.

On election day the Herald endorsed Elder as the better choice and indexed the race itself under the headline no contest. The vote was then re-run, and Todd won it: the paper carried the result on 16 April 1987. The SGA plaque lists him on a single 1986-88 plate, and no other president appears in the 1987-88 record.
The 1987-88 year under the two-year plate ended with the election of Scott Whitehouse on 7 April 1988, closing out the era of the Todd presidency.

Todd stood for a second term in the election held in March 1987. The Herald reported that Bill Fogle had entered the presidential race to help Todd rather than to win it, and the same issue recorded a shortage of candidates across the races and an appeal by a disqualified candidate.

His second year drew harder coverage. The Herald of 29 October 1987 reported that Associated Student Government was considering required course evaluations, and carried a separate article saying apathy was killing both ASG and the Residence Hall Association.

events.title: Not enough candidates to fill the ballot
events.body: ASG races faced a candidate shortage; one report notes a candidate entered a race to help a rival rather than to win. The same issue has ASG tabling a phone bill after amendment.

events.title: Dropping the intercollegiate legislature considered
events.body: ASG considered dropping its membership in the intercollegiate legislature, while the Herald warned that sharing an officer with Interhall Council could mean trouble for both groups. An editorial the following week argued the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature was worth keeping as a way to promote ideas.

events.title: Crosswalk resolution passes
events.body: The congress passed a resolution calling for a crosswalk. Campus safety items, including new screens for dormitory windows, filled much of the fall agenda.

events.title: Getting tough on absenteeism
events.body: ASG moved to get tough on absenteeism after a member lost his seat the week before. The Herald was simultaneously reporting that apathy was killing both ASG and the Residence Hall Association.

events.title: Constitutional amendments up for a vote
events.body: Constitutional amendments went before the body in November, in the same season the congress was pushing for required teacher evaluations. It was the third straight year of structural revision attempts.

events.title: ASG explains its empty seats
events.body: The organization publicly cited its reasons for the vacancies in its ranks, and four congress positions had been filled at a single meeting earlier that month. Days later an editorial told the body it needed better ideas, not gimmicks.

events.title: Ragland and Whitehouse win the primaries
events.body: Shannon Ragland and Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential primaries, narrowing a field of seven. The same issue reported passage of a proposal requesting a memorial area on campus.

events.title: Whitehouse elected; condom machines approved
events.body: Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential election, in an issue that also reported the congress approving condom machines for campus. The election coverage ran alongside editorials saying oversight and closed minds had marred the process.

events.title: Bruce Cambron calls for a new election
events.body: Bruce Cambron called for a new election a week after the results, following coverage of votes cast for a write-in candidate that ASG was told it could not ignore. The dispute carried into the following fall.

events.title: Disqualified candidate Ed Kenney appeals
events.body: Ed Kenney, disqualified as a candidate in the spring 1987 Associated Student Government election, appealed the ruling. The Herald reported the appeal on 26 March 1987 alongside the rest of its election coverage.

events.title: ASG considers required course evaluations
events.body: Associated Student Government took up a proposal to make course evaluations a requirement. The Herald reported the discussion in its issue of 29 October 1987.

events.title: Herald says apathy is killing ASG
events.body: The Herald ran an article arguing that apathy was killing both Associated Student Government and the Residence Hall Association. It appeared on 29 October 1987, part way through Todd's second term.

events.title: The Book Exchanger gets a third semester and a warning
events.body: ASG ran the Book Exchanger for a third semester, a free listing publication in which students advertised used textbooks to each other as an alternative to selling back to the bookstore. Cards went into student mailboxes on 11 November with a 20 November deadline, and about 60 students listed books each semester. Student Affairs chairman Victor Click said the project raised about $60 the previous fall and nothing in the spring against printing costs of about $653, that the year's budget allotted $750 to it, and that he would recommend dropping it if this run failed.
events.money: $750 budgeted; about $653 spent on printing the previous year; about $60 raised

events.title: The Angie Norcia Award is created for the yearly banquet
events.body: At the 9 February meeting student government created an award to present at its yearly banquet in May, named for Angie Norcia, an Owensboro senior who had died the previous summer of adult respiratory distress syndrome and Guillain-Barre syndrome and who had been active in student government for more than two years. President Tim Todd said it would be one of the highest honours given to a congress member, with recipients nominated and interviewed by a committee of members. It survived as the Mary Angela Norcia Memorial Award, still on the banquet nomination list in 1994.

events.title: ASG backs the Frankfort rally for higher education
events.body: ASG suspended its rules on 9 February to adopt the standard resolution urging Governor Wallace Wilkinson and the legislature to fund higher education, and presented it at the Frankfort rally on 16 February; Western's was the last of the eight state student governments to pass it. About 3,000 students, faculty and alumni marched up Capitol Avenue in what the Kentucky Advocates for Higher Education called the largest Frankfort demonstration since 1964. Western sent four free buses and 130 of the 161 people who signed up made the trip, joining a Western contingent of about 250, with cheerleaders handing out 250 red towels. A Herald editorial the same week said ASG had choked by passing only a form resolution while Murray State's government ran a write-a-thon that got more than 500 students to write the governor.

events.title: Bill Schilling lost his ASG seat when the hall association refused him leave
events.body: The Herald of 27 October 1987 reported that Bill Schilling was out after the Residence Hall Association denied him a leave of absence. The Herald had named Schilling the year before as the member who wrote most of the congress's bills. The same issue carried ASG's move to get tough on absenteeism. The report does not say which seat he lost, and the congress began an impeachment process against him three weeks later.

events.title: The congress began an impeachment process against Bill Schilling
events.body: Jill Duff reported in the Herald of 19 November 1987 that student government had begun an impeachment process against Bill Schilling. The proceeding did not go the distance: two issues later the Herald reported that the request for impeachment had been dropped.

events.title: The impeachment request was dropped
events.body: The Herald of 3 December 1987 reported that student government had dropped its request for impeachment. The following week's issue reported that Schilling was instead placed under the eye of a watchdog committee, carried a piece in which William Fogle explained the congress's actions, and ran three letters on it, including one defending the rescission and one from Van C. Hodge Jr. saying the issue was not closed.

events.title: A watchdog committee, and a page of letters about it
events.body: The Herald of 10 December 1987 reported that Bill Schilling was under the eye of a watchdog committee, and printed William Fogle's explanation of student government's actions beside letters from Hollie Hale defending the rescission, Kevin Hargrave calling an editorial an attack, and Van C. Hodge Jr. writing that the student government issue remained.

events.title: The Herald blamed diversity of opinion for the congress's conflicts
events.body: Dorren Klausnitzer's article in the Herald of 28 January 1988 attributed student government's conflicts to diversity. The same issue ran an editorial calling that a poor excuse. It appeared seven weeks after the Schilling watchdog committee and five weeks before the Herald reported that ASG's chief officers rarely kept their office hours.

events.title: Bill Schilling ran for president months after the impeachment attempt
events.body: The minutes of 1 March 1988 record Bill Schilling running for the presidency of student government, four months after the Herald reported him out following the Residence Hall Association's refusal of a leave of absence, and three months after the congress dropped its impeachment request. He was not among the two candidates the Herald reported surviving the primaries on 31 March.

events.title: A tuition rally and a flyer on the proposed budget freeze
events.body: The minutes of 1 March 1988 record a tuition rally, and the file preserves with them a flyer on the state budget and a proposed budget freeze for Western. It followed the Frankfort higher education rally that ASG had backed a fortnight earlier.

events.title: The six awards the congress gave at its banquet
events.body: A description of awards filed with the minutes of 15 March 1988 lists the six honours the congress presented: the Dero Downing Award, Outstanding Congress Member, Outstanding Committee Member, the Dean Charles A. Keown Award, the Kerrie Faye Stewart Memorial Award and the Mary Angela Norcia Award. The Norcia award had been created only the month before, in memory of a member who had died the previous summer.

src.label: ASG meeting minutes and description of awards, 15 March 1988

events.title: A campus ticket sales outlet proposed
events.body: Resolution 88-9-S, dated 12 April 1988, proposed a ticket sales outlet on campus and set out in detail what it called a Centritic Sales Office. It was one of the last pieces of business of Tim Todd's second term.

events.title: Weekend hours asked for Unicorn Pizza and the campus theatre
events.body: Resolution 88-10-S, dated 19 April 1988, asked that Unicorn Pizza be open at weekends. The same request came back through successive congresses: Resolution 89-2-F in October 1989 asked for the weekend hours to be expanded, and the administration granted them on a trial basis.

src.label: Resolution 88-10-S, Unicorn Pizza and Theater Open on Weekends, 19 April 1988

events.title: The Herald found the chief officers rarely kept office hours
events.body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported in the Herald of 3 March 1988 that Associated Student Government's chief officers rarely kept their office hours, and the same issue editorialised that published hours mean little if they are not kept. It ran nine days after the organisation had publicly explained its empty seats, and in the same season as the editorial telling it to find better ideas than gimmicks.

events.title: The Herald reported that Cambron had made false claims
events.body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported in the Herald of 26 April 1988 that Bruce Cambron, who a fortnight earlier had called for a new presidential election over the write-in votes, had made some false claims. Cambron took the complaint on regardless, raising it with university president Thomas Meredith the following October.

events.title: The filing deadline for congress seats is extended
events.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government filing deadline had been extended. It was the first of the year's several notices about seats that had not attracted candidates.

src.label: Herald 63:6, 15 Sep 1987, "Associated Student Government Filing Deadline Extended"

events.title: A member loses his seat
events.body: The Herald reported that Associated Student Government member Nick Hicks had lost his seat. Five days later the body moved to get tough on absenteeism.

src.label: Herald 63:17, 22 Oct 1987, "Associated Student Government Member Loses Seat – Nick Hicks"

events.title: Eighty-one students ratify the amendments
events.body: Eighty-one students voted to approve the constitutional amendments that had gone before the body two days earlier. The same issue reported that the congress had voted to withdraw its support from the Kentucky Intercollegiate Student Legislature, a membership it had been debating since September.

src.label: Herald 63:23, 12 Nov 1987, "81 Students Vote to Approve Student Government Association Amendments"

events.title: A class president quits mid-year
events.body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported that senior class president Greg Robertson had quit. It was the first of the vacancies the body would spend the spring explaining.

src.label: Herald 63:33, 21 Jan 1988, "Student Government Association Senior Class President Greg Robertson Quits"

events.title: Schilling asks for a leave of absence
events.body: Dorren Klausnitzer reported that Bill Schilling had asked the body for a leave of absence, twelve weeks after it dropped the impeachment request against him. The same issue carried an editorial telling the organisation it needed better ideas rather than gimmicks.

src.label: Herald 63:43, 25 Feb 1988, "Bill Schilling Asks for Leave of Absence"

events.title: An officer is reported arrested
events.body: The Herald reported the arrest of an Associated Student Government officer, printing the name as William Byron Shilling; earlier items in the same volume print the surname Schilling. The surviving index preserves only the headline: no charge is recorded, and no source found reports any outcome. The minutes of 1 March 1988 record that Schilling was running for the ASG presidency.

src.label: Herald 63:46, 17 Mar 1988, "Associated Student Government Officer Arrested"

events.title: Two of thirty-two congress positions contested
events.body: The Herald reported that only 2 of the 32 Associated Student Government positions on the spring ballot were contested. It is the only explicit seat count for Congress found in this period.

src.label: Herald 63:47, 22 Mar 1988, "2 of 32 Associated Student Government Positions Contested"

events.title: Congress tables a proposal against the university president
events.body: The body tabled a proposal directed against university president Kern Alexander. The same issue reported that the election was officially under way and that the congress would consider adding condom machines.

src.label: Herald 63:48, 24 Mar 1988, "Associated Student Government Tables Proposal Against Kern Alexander"

executive.name: Drew DeLozier
executive.note: Issued the monthly voucher summaries, and on 15 March 1988 reported to Congress that a bill for 1,000 copies had arrived unexplained from Kinko's.
profile: Drew DeLozier served as Treasurer of the Associated Student Government in 1987-88, under President Timothy Todd. He issued Congress's monthly voucher summaries through the year, and at the meeting of 15 March 1988 reported that a bill for 1,000 copies had arrived from Kinko's with no explanation of what the copies were for.

executive.name: Danielle Williamson
executive.note: Signed the minutes through the year, including those recording the opening of impeachment proceedings against the Administrative Vice-President. She kept the same short list of vacancies week after week: senior class vice-president, two off-campus representatives, and the Business and Potter college alternates.
profile: Danielle Williamson served as Secretary of the Associated Student Government in 1987-88, under President Timothy Todd. The Herald's coverage of the spring 1987 campaign that put that year's officers in place, in its issue of 14 April, carried a letter backing her under the headline "Danielle Williamson Best" — the same issue in which Kim Summers wrote in support of Todd's re-election as president.

As Secretary, Williamson signed Congress's minutes through the year, including those recording the opening of impeachment proceedings against Administrative Vice President Bill Schilling in November 1987. Week after week she read out the same short list of vacancies the body could not fill: the senior class vice-presidency, two off-campus representative seats, and the Business and Potter college alternate seats.

src2.label: Herald 62:53, 14 Apr 1987

executive.name: Bill Schilling
executive.note: Reported to Congress on the Bowling Green City Traffic Commission and on a rise of more than 20 per cent in campus crime, and handed down to Congress an official record from the Judicial Council to be implemented at the next election. Impeachment proceedings against him were opened on 17 November 1987; on 1 March 1988 he told Congress he had been cleared by the University, that he would run for the ASG presidency, and that he would take a leave of office until after the elections.
profile: Before he joined the cabinet, Bill Schilling was already the most prolific bill-writer in Congress: a Herald feature by Lisa Jessie on 11 December 1986 named him the one Associated Student Government member who wrote most of Congress's bills, the same season he chaired the Legislative Research Committee. He wrote to the Herald under his own name that year too — a column headlined "Associated Student Government Has New Ideas" in March 1986, a letter backing Tim Todd's first run for the presidency the following month, and a separate letter, "College Heights Herald Abuses Rights."

Schilling ran for the Interhall Council presidency in the spring 1987 elections; the Herald covered his signage under the headline "Candidate Using Big Red on Signs," and on 21 April 1987 reported that Delwin Cheek had defeated him for that council's presidency. He was then named Administrative Vice President of the Associated Student Government for 1987-88 under re-elected President Todd, and in that office reported to Congress on the Bowling Green City Traffic Commission and on a rise of more than 20 percent in campus crime, and handed down to Congress an official Judicial Council record to be implemented at the next election.

His term turned contentious that fall. The Herald reported on 27 October 1987 that he had lost his Congress seat after the Residence Hall Association refused him a leave of absence — the report did not say which seat — and three weeks later, on 19 November, Congress opened an impeachment process against him. The proceeding did not go the distance: the Herald reported on 3 December that the impeachment request had been dropped, and the following week's issue described Schilling placed under the eye of a new watchdog committee, alongside a page of reader letters divided between defending the outcome and, in one case from Van C. Hodge Jr., insisting the issue was not closed.

Schilling asked Congress for a leave of absence on 25 February 1988, and at the meeting of 1 March told the body he had been cleared by the university, that he would run for the ASG presidency, and that he would take leave from his office until after the election. A Herald item two and a half weeks later, on 17 March, reported the arrest of an Associated Student Government officer under the name William Byron Shilling; the surviving index preserves no charge. The Herald of 31 March 1988, the same issue that reported Shannon Ragland and Scott Whitehouse winning the presidential primary, carried the outcome: "Charge Against William Schilling Dismissed." He was not among the two candidates who survived that primary.

executive.name: Kim Summers
executive.note: Ran Weekend in the Woods in September 1987, introduced table tents and newsletters as publicity, and handed out the committee certificates in March 1988. She had been vice-chair of Faculty Relations the year before.
profile: A Kimberly Summers wrote twice to the Herald's letters pages in April 1986, over a year before Kim Summers's confirmed 1987-88 term in the ASG cabinet: "Appreciates Help – Associated Student Government" ran on 17 April, and "Commends Job Well Done – Associated Student Government" followed five days later. The identification rests on the matching name and the ASG subject matter, not on a source that states the two are the same; it is recorded here as likely, not certain. In April 1987 Kim Summers wrote in support of Tim Todd's re-election as president, in the same issue that carried Danielle Williamson's endorsement and coverage of Bill Schilling's Interhall Council campaign.

Summers served as Public Relations Vice-President of the Associated Student Government in 1987-88, under President Todd, after serving as vice-chair of the Faculty Relations Committee the year before. She ran that September's Weekend in the Woods retreat, introduced table tents and a newsletter as new publicity tools, and in March 1988 handed out the year's committee certificates.

officers.name: Rebecca Hack
officers.note: Accepted by Congress as chairman of Rules and Elections on 6 October 1987, while the committee was still running that autumn's freshman elections. The minutes of 22 September 1987 record the name as Becky Haaek and those of 6 October as Rebecca Hack; the spelling is unresolved.
profile: Rebecca Hack was accepted by Congress as chairman of the Rules and Elections Committee on 6 October 1987, while the committee was still running that autumn's freshman elections. ASG's own minutes are not consistent on her name: the 22 September 1987 minutes record a Becky Haaek and those of 6 October a Rebecca Hack, and no other source in the archive resolves which spelling is right. No further record of her term survives here.
