documents.title: ASG meeting minutes, 22 September 1987
documents.summary: The first fall meeting of the year: roll call, officer and committee reports, the swearing-in of Kenny Perry as Ogden College Representative, and passage of a resolution on the tuition increase.
documents.extract: Kenny Perry was sworn in as the Ogden College Representative.

leaders.name: Scott Whitehouse
leaders.note: ASG filed a formal reaction to the General Education Task Force proposal in 1988. Confirmed twice: the Herald of 7 April 1988 reported 'Whitehouse winner in presidential election', and coverage through the year names him as president.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Whitehouse won the March 1988 ASG presidential primary alongside Shannon Ragland, emerging from a field of seven candidates in a year when only two of 32 congress positions were contested.

He won the presidency on 7 April 1988, in an election the Herald's own editorial pages said had been marred by oversight and closed minds, and amid coverage of votes for a write-in candidate that the congress was told it could not ignore.

The disputed election shadowed his term into the fall: Bruce Cambron, who had demanded a new election in April, took his complaint to university president Thomas Meredith in October 1988, weeks after the congress banned future write-in campaigns. His year also produced ASG's formal written reaction to the General Education Task Force proposal.

Scott Whitehouse came through the Associated Student Government primaries in the spring of 1988. Dorren Klausnitzer reported that Whitehouse and Shannon Ragland were the winners, in an issue that also covered what a losing campaign cost candidates in money and in feeling.

By the middle of his year in office the Herald had settled on a running characterisation of him. Rebecca Fullen's feature called him the "Peddling President" who sold Associated Student Government to students, and the same issue reported that university president Thomas Meredith had come to speak to the organisation.

The following week the paper printed "Scott Whitehouse Selling Good Government" together with a John Chattin editorial cartoon drawing him as a salesman. The salesman image was the Herald's shorthand for a president whose main task was convincing students that student government mattered.

events.title: A formal reaction to the General Education Task Force
events.body: ASG filed a written response to a proposed overhaul of general education requirements - one of the earliest surviving examples of student government intervening in curriculum rather than campus life.

events.title: Write-in campaigns banned
events.body: ASG approved a ban on future write-in campaigns, five months after write-in votes had thrown its own presidential election into dispute. An editorial the next issue said the block showed ASG was not listening.

events.title: Freshman election turnout called pretty good
events.body: Turnout in the ASG freshman election was reported as "pretty good." The same issue said the organization was working to make the importance of voting register with students.

events.title: Cambron takes his election complaint to the president
events.body: Bruce Cambron, who had called for a new election in April, talked to university president Thomas Meredith about the ASG election. The spring's disputed result was still alive six months on.

events.title: Half the open slots filled; shelters for shuttle stops
events.body: ASG filled half of its open congress seats and sought shelters and seats for campus shuttle stops. The following week the Herald editorialized that ASG's efforts directly helped and served students.

events.title: The weeklong Thanksgiving break is dropped
events.body: ASG dropped its push for a weeklong Thanksgiving break, three weeks after voting to seek one. In the same issue, members rated their own organization as average.

events.title: More movie hours wanted
events.body: The congress asked for more movie hours on campus. It was one of the quality-of-life items that filled the spring agenda before election season.

events.title: Amos Gott edges Lynn Groemling
events.body: Amos Gott narrowly defeated Lynn Groemling in the ASG presidential race. The campaign season had drawn complaints from candidates about the brief primary and an editorial warning that name recognition should not decide the race.

events.title: The Herald profiled Whitehouse as ASG's salesman
events.body: Rebecca Fullen wrote a feature calling Scott Whitehouse the "Peddling President" who sold Associated Student Government to students. The piece framed his year in office around persuading a sceptical campus that the organisation was worth paying attention to.

events.title: President Thomas Meredith spoke to ASG
events.body: Diane Tsimekles reported that university president Thomas Meredith addressed an Associated Student Government meeting. The appearance put WKU's president directly in front of the student body's elected representatives.

events.title: A cartoon drew Whitehouse as a salesman
events.body: The Herald ran an article headlined "Scott Whitehouse Selling Good Government" in its 2 February issue. Alongside it, John Chattin drew an editorial cartoon casting Whitehouse as a salesman, returning to the image the paper had used the week before.

events.title: ASG sets up a Wednesday afternoon hotline
events.body: Student government set up a hotline for complaints and suggestions about the organisation. From Wednesday 26 October the ASG secretary was to answer the office line, 745-4354, from 1 to 4 p.m. every Wednesday, referring anything she could not answer to an executive officer. Public relations vice president Amos Gott said students could call at any time during the week but did not, and that with a set time people were more apt to call.

events.title: Mock presidential election with the College Republicans
events.body: ASG co-sponsored a mock presidential election with the College Republicans on Tuesday 25 October 1988, from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. in the university center, with student identification cards required to vote. Public relations vice president Amos Gott said before it that the aim was to see how Western felt as a community compared with Bowling Green and with the national response to the candidates. The Herald of 27 October reported that George Bush won the mock race.

src2.label: College Heights Herald 64:19, 27 Oct 1988

events.title: ASG recommended an extra study day before exams
events.body: Associated Student Government recommended adding an extra study day before exams to the university calendar. Diane Tsimekles reported the recommendation in the Herald's 16 February issue. The proposal followed January efforts to find a way to print teacher evaluations.

events.title: Vote America ran through the first month of the term
events.body: Vote America is in the minutes of 13, 20 and 27 September 1988, in a presidential election autumn. The 20 September meeting set it beside a lecture series, International Day, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association; the 27 September meeting set it beside committee service and Panhellenic activities. The drive ran before the mock presidential election ASG staged with the College Republicans in October.

events.title: A lecture series, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association
events.body: The minutes of 20 September 1988 record a lecture series, College Awareness Day and the Student Alumni Association among the congress's business, together with a meeting with the Council for Higher Education, a visit from the University of Louisville student government, International Day and constitutional amendments. The minutes name what was planned rather than what happened.

events.title: International Day again, with homecoming
events.body: International Day ran through the autumn of 1988 as it had in 1986: the minutes of 20 September, 11 October and 18 October all record it. The 11 October meeting took it alongside homecoming, the student alumni association and the member of the week awards.

events.title: Big Red's Roar and the bus stop shelters
events.body: The minutes of 25 October 1988 record Big Red's Roar, the mock election and bus stop shelters. Big Red's Roar returns in the minutes of 7 February 1989. The minutes place ASG in the event without saying what its part was.

events.title: A Christmas dance, a faculty reception and sponsored basketball games
events.body: The minutes of 28 November 1988 record a Christmas dance, a faculty reception and the sponsoring of basketball games, alongside the teacher evaluations work. The following week's minutes add a Christmas reception.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr Day recognised at Western
events.body: The minutes of 6 December 1988 record that the Martin Luther King Jr holiday was now recognised at Western. Student government had put a Martin Luther King bill through a divided congress in March 1987, a year after it had rejected dismissing classes for the holiday. The same meeting covered the Council for Higher Education, electronic mail, newsletters, a Christmas reception and the book exchange.

events.title: Campus Pride is Western Wide
events.body: The minutes of 17 January 1989 record a programme called Campus Pride is Western Wide, alongside the use of the hotline ASG had set up the previous October and a review of the autumn's legislation. The following week's minutes carry it as Campus Pride '89.

events.title: ASG Awareness Week
events.body: The minutes of 31 January and 7 February 1989 both record an ASG Awareness Week, set beside bus shelter construction, public relations, the General Education proposal and the State Student Government Conference. The organisation ran a comparable week under the name Anti-Apathy Week the following year.

events.title: An Oozeball tournament
events.body: The minutes of 28 February and 14 March 1989 both record an Oozeball tournament, the mud volleyball event. The Herald of 4 April 1989 carried a piece on Oozeball by Dresden Wall, in the same issue as a report that the presidential field would be shaved by two that day.

events.title: Two weekends built to keep students on campus
events.body: The minutes of 21 March 1989 record a Hell No, We Won't Go weekend, and those of 28 March 1989 a Stay and Play Weekend, alongside the ASG banquet and the shuttle shelter construction. Keeping students on campus at weekends had been the stated aim of the Downing University Center hangout project two years earlier.

events.title: A Senior Send-Off closed the year
events.body: The last surviving minutes of the spring, dated 4 April 1989, record a Senior Send-Off alongside open positions and the book exchange. It came a week after the minutes recording the ASG banquet and the installation of Thomas Meredith.

events.title: The secretary resigned in January
events.body: The minutes of 24 January 1989 record the resignation of Mickie Hennig as secretary, alongside shuttle stops and Campus Pride '89. The minutes record the resignation without giving a reason.

events.title: Bids taken for the shuttle shelters ASG had asked for
events.body: Having asked in Resolutions 88-2-F and 88-3-F of 1 November 1988 for shelters and benches at the Big Red shuttle stops, the congress followed the job through the spring. The minutes of 31 January 1989 record shelter construction, those of 7 February record shelter bids, and those of 21 February, 21 March and 28 March all return to the shelters.

events.title: A student athletic promotions committee proposed
events.body: Resolution 89-2-S, dated 14 February 1989, proposed creating a student athletic promotions committee to push attendance at athletic events up. The minutes of the following week, 21 February, record a basketball game among the congress's business.

events.title: A Sunday matinee at the campus theatre
events.body: Resolution 89-4-S, dated 21 February 1989, asked for a Sunday matinee to be added at the campus theatre. Two more resolutions carried the same date, 89-5-S asking that the library stay open until 10 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, and 89-6-S asking that men's intramural basketball and volleyball be played at weekends. The push for more film hours reached the Herald a week later.

events.title: More coed dorms and a later spring break
events.body: The Herald of 23 March 1989 reported that Associated Student Government wanted more coed dormitories and a later spring break. The two requests are in the legislation as Resolution 89-7-S of 20 March, moving spring break to the third week of March, and Resolution 89-8-S of 21 March, converting a residence hall without air conditioning to coed housing.

events.title: Thomas Meredith installed as Western's president
events.body: The minutes of 28 March 1989 record the installation of Thomas Meredith as Western's president among the congress's business, alongside the shuttle shelter construction, the ASG banquet and the Stay and Play Weekend. Meredith addressed an ASG meeting in January, and returned repeatedly over the following five years.

profile: Victor Click co-signed the same 2 April 1987 Herald letter with Hollie Hale endorsing Tim Todd for the Associated Student Government presidency. Todd won the race, in a re-run of the election the Herald reported on 16 April 1987.

By the fall of 1987 Click chaired the Associated Student Government's Student Affairs Committee, which ran the Book Exchanger — a free listing service through which students advertised used textbooks to each other instead of selling them back to the bookstore. Click told the Herald in November 1987 that the exchange had raised about $60 the previous fall and nothing that spring against roughly $653 in printing costs, against a $750 budget for the service, and said he would recommend dropping the project if that semester's run failed too.
Click continued in student government the following year as co-chair of the Student Affairs Committee, accepted by Congress on 13 September 1988 alongside chair Brad Cooper.

officers.name: Hollie Hale
officers.note: Accepted as chair of Student Rights on 13 September 1988; the committee worked on handicapped facilities and the ticket outlet issue that autumn. She was also the College Representatives' contact for Academic Council committee service.
profile: In the spring 1987 Associated Student Government election season, Hollie Hale and Victor Click co-signed a Herald letter endorsing Tim Todd for the presidency, printed in the paper's 2 April 1987 issue. The Herald's own editorial that month endorsed his opponent Greg Elder, but Todd won: the paper reported the result on 16 April 1987 under the headline "Tim Todd Beats Greg Elder in Election Re-Run," and Todd served as president through 1987-88.

That December, amid a controversy inside student government over member Bill Schilling — placed under a Congress watchdog committee after an earlier impeachment attempt against him — the Herald of 10 December 1987 carried a cluster of letters on the affair, among them one from Hale. The surviving index line for that issue runs the titles and the writers together, so which letter belongs to which correspondent is not established here; the titles indexed are an explanation of student government's actions, a letter calling an editorial an attack, a defence of the rescission and a piece on expanding to Glasgow, and the names indexed beside them are Hale, Kevin Hargrave, Van C. Hodge Jr. and Phillip Sellers.

The following year Congress accepted Hale as chair of the Student Rights Committee on 13 September 1988, with Elaine Burge joining as co-chair a week later. Her committee worked that autumn on handicapped-accessibility facilities and a dispute over the campus ticket outlet, and Hale also served as the college representatives' contact for the Academic Council committees.

leaders.name: Amos Gott
leaders.note: The best-documented pre-1992 presidency in the archive. Signed correspondence survives on extended library hours, the DUC flagpole, the stadium press box and a local pizza vendor dispute.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Gott was a visible member before he was president, signing Herald letters on ASG's behalf, including a January 1989 piece promoting Campus Pride '89 and an earlier letter urging readers to understand the organization.
He won the presidency in April 1989, edging Lynn Groemling in a race that had drawn candidate complaints about the brief primary.

His presidency ran on correspondence: resolutions went out over his signature as memoranda to named administrators and answers came back. In spring 1990 he wrote to six administrators under Resolution 90-6-S seeking changes to the final exam schedule, part of a surviving file that also covers extended library hours, the Downing University Center flagpole, mace sales at the bookstore, AIDS education and larger diplomas.

Gott was already writing on Associated Student Government's behalf before he led it, signing a January 1989 Herald piece promoting Campus Pride '89. That spring he ran for president, survived a primary that several candidates complained had been too brief, and then edged Lynn Groemling in the runoff to take the office for 1989-90.

He started early. The Herald's second issue of the fall reported that Gott had gotten a jump on the ASG semester, running alongside a piece urging students to participate. The fall that followed was busy and money was tight: the paper reported ASG's budget was tiny compared with other schools, the congress approved a new statewide board before admitting it could not afford the dues, and it spent the semester picking up and putting down a proposed Public Interest Research Group.

Gott opened the spring with a Herald letter asking students to become involved, and by February he was defending an Anti-Apathy Week in print after it drew criticism. The rest of his spring ran through the congress: opening Pearce-Ford Tower's windows, more parking on the lower end of campus, a revised WKU Glasgow constitution, and a vote to expand the congress so classes and student groups had more voice. He handed off to Michael Colvin in April 1990.

events.title: Extended library hours
events.body: Correspondence between President Amos Gott, Howard Bailey, Sally Ann Strickler and Michael Binder. Resolutions went out as letters to named administrators and answers came back.

events.title: The Downing University Center flagpole
events.body: One item in a working inventory of the job that year: the flagpole, the stadium press box, a dispute involving a local pizza vendor and a proposed budget for the Board of Student Body Presidents.

events.title: Gott gets a jump on the semester
events.body: The Herald reported that Amos Gott had gotten a jump on the ASG semester, opening his presidency before classes settled in. A companion piece urged students to participate in the organization.

events.title: A budget tiny compared to other schools
events.body: The Herald reported that ASG's budget was tiny compared to student governments at other schools. Two days later the congress approved joining a new board but admitted it could not afford the membership.

events.title: Resolution 89-3-F asks for AIDS education
events.body: Under Resolution 89-3-F, ASG corresponded with administrators requesting education on AIDS, HIV and sexually transmitted diseases. The letters survive in the SGA records alongside the year's other resolution correspondence on mace sales, larger diplomas and a food services committee.

events.title: Student government goes to Glasgow
events.body: Student government went to the WKU Glasgow campus, and the congress agreed to look again at a Public Interest Research Group. Both stories ran in the same mid-October issue.

events.title: PIRG sunk over its fee system
events.body: ASG voted down the proposed Public Interest Research Group, saying its fee system was the culprit. The decision ended a semester of on-and-off consideration of the group.

events.title: Congress votes to expand
events.body: ASG voted to expand its congress, a week after reporting it might add representatives. A follow-up story said classes and student groups would get more voice in the organization.

events.title: Withdrawals save an invalid primary
events.body: Candidates withdrew from the ASG races, saving a primary that would otherwise have been invalid; only two candidates were running for president. The Herald had already reported that interest in the organization might be lower, illustrated by a cartoon of student government in an empty room.

events.title: ASG joins the Board of Student Body Presidents
events.body: Associated Student Government joined the Board of Student Body Presidents, two weeks after approving the new board while saying it could not afford to join. The same issue reported that the congress had punted a decision on a Public Interest Research Group.

events.title: A push for weekend Unicorn pizza
events.body: The Herald reported that Associated Student Government wanted weekend service from the Unicorn pizza vendor. The dispute stayed in the paper: on 24 October the Herald ran an editorial cartoon showing ASG and the administration riding a unicorn.

events.title: Anti-Apathy Week on tap
events.body: The Herald reported that Associated Student Government had an Anti-Apathy Week coming up. The idea drew enough criticism that President Amos Gott wrote a defense of it in the paper a week later.

events.title: Open the windows in Pearce-Ford Tower
events.body: Associated Student Government said it wanted the windows in Pearce-Ford Tower opened. The Herald had reported two days earlier that the congress was set to vote on the resolution. The same issue carried Gott's defense of Anti-Apathy Week.

events.title: Michael Colvin wins, and a call to raise the activity fee
events.body: Michael Colvin aced the Associated Student Government election to succeed Amos Gott. The same issue reported that ASG wanted the student activity fee raised, a direct answer to the budget complaints that had run through the year.

events.title: Regents set the 1990-91 tuition and operating budget
events.body: WKU's Board of Regents met in special session and approved the university's 1990-91 operating budget, tuition rates, and personnel changes ahead of Colvin's term.

src.label: WKU Board of Regents, special meeting, 30 May 1990

events.title: A student government organised itself on the Glasgow campus
events.body: On 21 September 1989 the students of Western's Glasgow campus held an organisational meeting to settle a name, officers and elections for a student body of their own. A week later, on 28 September, the first executive council of the WKU-Glasgow Associated Student Government met, took homecoming and Christmas activities, drew up by-laws, and made a list of businesses to approach about homecoming. The Bowling Green congress had voted in August to include Glasgow representatives, and its minutes of 19 September record a Glasgow campus constitution.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow organisational meeting minutes, 21 September 1989

events.title: Glasgow's homecoming, Red and White Day and Women in Transition
events.body: The Glasgow student government's minutes of 6 October 1989 record homecoming events, elections, a Red and White Day, Women in Transition and Christmas activities. Its minutes of 13 October return to homecoming and fundraising, and those of 27 October add daycare and a book exchange. This is the founding programme of a student government that had existed for a fortnight.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow meeting minutes, 6 October 1989

events.title: Glasgow planned Christmas activities and a parade
events.body: The Glasgow student government's minutes of 10 November 1989 record Christmas activities, fundraising and a parade. Its minutes of 4 November and its report of 1 December are given over to the same preparations, the last surviving Glasgow record of the year.

src.label: Associated Student Body-Glasgow meeting minutes, 10 November 1989

events.title: Big Red Day for the mascot's tenth birthday
events.body: Resolution 89-9-F, dated 28 November 1989, made 2 December 1989 Big Red Day in honour of the mascot's tenth anniversary. The minutes of 14 November record Big Red's tenth birthday alongside the counselling centre and a leadership reception, and those of 28 November return to it with the tuition increase.

events.title: A Mitch McConnell lecture put on the congress's agenda
events.body: The minutes of 13 March 1990 record a Mitch McConnell lecture alongside a Drug Awareness and Health Enrichment Week and the coming elections. McConnell was then Kentucky's junior United States senator. The minutes record what was arranged; they do not report the lecture.

events.title: Gatewood Galbraith spoke on legalising drugs
events.body: The Herald of 22 March 1990 reported Gatewood Galbraith arguing for the legalisation of drugs, in a piece by Angie Jones. The minutes of 20 March 1990 record a Gatewood Galbraith lecture on the legalisation of drugs alongside elections and open positions.

events.title: Earth Day, Earth Week and a tree planting
events.body: Earth Day is in the minutes of 20 February 1990 with the telephone surveys and the elections, Earth Week in those of 27 February and 10 April, and a tree planting in those of 3 April. The 1990 Earth Day was its twentieth anniversary and the Herald reported on 24 April that its organisers hoped public interest would hold.

events.title: A reception for the regent, and Challenge of Change
events.body: The minutes of 16 January 1990 record a reception for the regent, a Challenge of Change programme, a Student Council Day and a student rights meeting. The regent's reception is in the minutes of 23 and 30 January as well, and Challenge of Change in those of 23 January.

events.title: A Valentine's dance and the organisational presidents roundtable
events.body: The minutes of 13 February 1990 record a Valentine's dance and the organisational presidents roundtable, with parking, awards and vacancies. The roundtable was put on a formal footing that autumn by Bill 90-2-F.

events.title: Alcohol Awareness Week
events.body: The minutes of 3 October 1989 record an Alcohol Awareness Week alongside the master plan committee, training sessions, the shuttle shelter, condoms and International Day. Alcohol came back before the congress on 7 November, when the minutes record petitions on alcohol and on twenty-four hour visitation.

events.title: Kentucky Higher Education Week and a professor of the year
events.body: The minutes of 10 October 1989 record Kentucky Higher Education Week, homecoming, and Luther Hughes as professor of the year. A leadership reception follows in the minutes of 14 November.

events.title: Unicorn Pizza's weekend hours were granted on trial
events.body: Correspondence dated 27 October 1989 replied to Resolution 89-2-F by expanding Unicorn Pizza's weekend hours on a trial basis. The congress had asked for the extension on 10 October, after the Herald reported the demand on 12 October and then drew ASG and the administration riding a unicorn. It is one of the year's few requests with a recorded answer.

src.label: SGA correspondence on Unicorn Pizza, 27 October 1989

events.title: A recorded information line asked for again
events.body: Resolution 90-2-S, dated 16 January 1990, asked for a recorded announcement telephone line. The congress had tabled the same idea in February 1987, when the equipment was costed at $500 with $60 for installation and $17 a month, and had set up a Wednesday afternoon hotline instead in October 1988.

events.title: A freshman orientation programme asked for
events.body: Resolution 90-1-S, dated 16 January 1990, asked for a freshman orientation programme. Correspondence answering it survives in the SGA records dated 24 January 1990.

events.title: New Rock 92 asked for on the university centre speakers
events.body: Resolution 90-8-S asked that WWHR, the student station then branded New Rock 92, be played over the Downing University Center speakers. The archive dates the resolution 6 January 1990.

events.title: ASG endorsed the fee rise that built the Preston Center
events.body: Resolution 90-18-S, dated 17 April 1990, approved the Board of Regents' increase in the student fee used to pay construction costs for the Preston Health and Activities Center. The regents set the 1990-91 budget and tuition six weeks later.
events.money: student construction fee increase approved by the regents

src.label: Resolution 90-18-S, Preston Health & Activities Center Construction Fees, 17 April 1990

events.title: A resolution on getting into the buildings
events.body: Resolution 90-17-S, dated 10 April 1990, asked for improvements to the accessibility of campus buildings. It was one of the last pieces of legislation of Amos Gott's term.

events.title: Two twenty-four hour visitation halls asked for
events.body: Resolution 90-13-S, dated 20 March 1990, asked for two residence halls with twenty-four hour coed visitation. The minutes of 24 October 1989 record twenty-four hour visitation among the congress's business, and those of 7 November record petitions on it and on alcohol.

events.title: A student food services committee, and a forum with it
events.body: Resolution 89-6-F, dated 31 October 1989, asked for a student advisory food services committee. The minutes of 24 October record a food service forum, and correspondence answering the resolution survives dated 9 November 1989. The same 31 October meeting produced Resolution 89-4-F on weekend library hours.

events.title: The year opened with Glasgow seats and a Judicial Board
events.body: The first minutes of the term, dated 29 August 1989, record Judicial Board candidates, an explanation of procedures, the inclusion of Glasgow representatives, committee organisational reports and the freshman elections. Three bylaw amendments followed on 5 September, on the president's board, on how legislation was to be written and submitted, and on the order of business.

executive.name: Eddie Smith
executive.note: Presented the budget summary at the first meeting of the year and told Congress the budget was an operational one; the 1989-90 budget was accepted the same night.
profile: Eddie Smith served as treasurer of the Associated Student Government for 1989-90. At the first meeting of the year, 29 August 1989, he presented the budget summary and told Congress it was an operational budget; Congress accepted the 1989-90 budget that same night.

executive.name: Julie Fleming
executive.note: Kept and read out the standing list of unfilled Congress seats week by week, and required proposed resolutions to reach her by Thursday or Friday of each week. She signed the minutes all year.
profile: Julie Fleming served as secretary of the Associated Student Government for 1989-90 and signed the minutes all year. She kept and read out, week by week, the standing list of unfilled Congress seats, and required proposed resolutions to reach her by Thursday or Friday of each week.

executive.name: Michael Colvin
executive.note: At the first meeting of the year he took Congress through the contents of the congressional notebook and how to write a resolution, set out the attendance policy, and discussed a resolution for a stop light at the corner of Regents and Normal. He was elected president for 1990-91.
profile: Michael Colvin served as administrative vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1989-90, under president Amos Gott. At the first Congress meeting of the year, 29 August 1989, he walked members through the congressional notebook and how to write a resolution, set out the attendance policy, and raised a resolution for a stop light at the corner of Regents Avenue and Normal Drive. He was elected president for 1990-91, succeeding Gott.

executive.name: Van Hodge
executive.note: Reported correspondence with other universities from the NACA conference and a meeting with the Herald in his first officer report, and ran a Promote ASG Night at South Hall that evening. In February 1990 he was working with President Gott on a Minority Handbook.
profile: Van Hodge served as public relations vice president of the Associated Student Government for 1989-90, the first of two consecutive terms in the office. In his first officer report he described correspondence made with other universities at a NACA conference and a meeting held with the Herald, and he ran a Promote ASG Night at South Hall that evening. By February 1990 he was working with President Amos Gott on a minority handbook. His second term, and his resignation from it, are recorded under 1990-91.

officers.name: Daryl Pepper
officers.note: Accepted by motion and sworn in at the first meeting of the year, 29 August 1989.
profile: Pepper was accepted by motion and sworn in as parliamentarian of the Associated Student Government at Congress's first meeting of the year, 29 August 1989, a meeting that also covered Judicial Board candidates, the inclusion of Glasgow campus representatives and freshman elections. The archive does not yet record anything further about his time in the post.

officers.office: Chairman of the Legislative Research Committee
officers.name: Daniel Duffy
officers.note: Approved as chairman by motion on 29 August 1989. His committee handled Resolution 89-01-F and looked at putting a course on sexually transmitted diseases and AIDS before the university.
profile: Duffy had been a rank-and-file Congress member the year before, named the contact for the Student Rights committee on 15 November 1988 and Congress Person of the Week twice, on 28 November 1988 and 31 January 1989. In the Herald of 9 February 1989 he wrote a letter headlined "Faulty Proposal," criticizing a proposed change to general education requirements, and he was nominated for a Congress award in two categories on 21 March 1989.

Congress approved him as chairman of the Legislative Research Committee on 29 August 1989. His committee handled Resolution 89-01-F and looked into bringing a course on sexually transmitted diseases and AIDS before the university. By 5 December 1989 Duffy had resigned from ASG; he recommended Greg Willoughby and Joe Rains as the committee's chairman and vice-chairman, and Congress formally accepted them that meeting.

officers.name: Bill Engle
officers.note: Approved as one of two chairmen of Student Affairs on 29 August 1989, alongside Brian Sewell.
profile: Engle joined Congress in 1988-89, accepted by floor motion as Business College alternate on 22 November 1988 and then as Business College representative on 28 November 1988; he reported for the Business College Academic Council on 17 January 1989. On 31 January 1989 Congress accepted him by floor motion as co-chair of the Student Affairs committee alongside Brian Sewell, and he was nominated for a Congress award on 21 March 1989.
He and Sewell continued as co-chairmen of Student Affairs into 1989-90, approved in that role at Congress's first meeting of the year, 29 August 1989.

officers.name: Brian Sewell
officers.note: Approved as one of two chairmen of Student Affairs on 29 August 1989, alongside Bill Engle.
profile: Sewell was named a Congress Person of the Week on 18 October 1988 and moved to an off-campus representative seat on 24 January 1989. On 31 January 1989 Congress accepted him by floor motion as co-chair of the Student Affairs committee alongside Bill Engle. In the Herald of 4 April 1989 he wrote a letter headlined "Loyalty, Leadership," backing Amos Gott's campaign for Associated Student Government president.
He and Engle continued as co-chairmen of Student Affairs into 1989-90, approved in that role at Congress's first meeting of the year, 29 August 1989.

officers.name: Dwight Adkins
officers.note: Approved as Student Rights chairman on 29 August 1989, the same night Congress accepted him as Junior Class Vice President. On 10 October 1989 his committee reported that it had gone over the university alcohol policy with the campus lawyer and had talked about more co-ed housing and 24-hour visitation; Adkins was recorded absent from that meeting.
profile: Dwight Adkins was sworn in as an Associated Student Government representative at-large on 6 September 1988, alongside Ron Hennig, and was accepted as co-chair of the Public Relations Committee two weeks later, on 20 September 1988.

The following year Congress approved Adkins as Student Rights chairman on 29 August 1989, the same meeting at which it accepted him as junior class vice president. His committee reported to Congress on 10 October 1989 that it had reviewed the university's alcohol policy with the campus lawyer and discussed expanding co-ed housing and 24-hour visitation; Adkins himself was recorded absent from that meeting. He resigned from the organization altogether at the 5 December 1989 meeting, citing schedule conflicts, and Congress replaced him as Student Rights chairman with Heather Falmlen.

Adkins ran for the Associated Student Government presidency the following spring: the Herald's coverage on 5 April 1990 named him and Michael Colvin as the field, and the paper ran further pieces backing his campaign over the following week. Colvin won the 19 April 1990 election and took office for 1990-91, not Adkins.

members.name: Dawn Bradley
members.seat: Congress member (later Secretary of Public Relations Committee)
members.note: Sworn in by President Gott, 3 October 1989 (no seat title recorded), with Kelly Elliot and Emily Morgan. Absent 21 November 1989, 27 February and 17 April 1990. Accepted by floor motion as Secretary of Public Relations, 30 January 1990.
profile: Dawn Bradley was sworn into ASG Congress on 3 October 1989, alongside Kelly Elliot and Emily Morgan, with no seat title recorded at the time. She was accepted by floor motion as Secretary of the Public Relations Committee on 30 January 1990. The minutes recorded her absent on 21 November 1989 and again on 27 February and 17 April 1990.

members.name: Justin Cook
members.note: Nominated unsuccessfully for University Center Board Representative, 29 August 1989 (lost to Hagan Rose). Accepted by floor motion as Off-Campus Representative and sworn in, 13 February 1990. Absent 3 April 1990.
profile: Justin Cook's first appearance in the record was a defeat: nominated for University Center Board Representative on 29 August 1989, he lost to Hagan Rose. He returned the following term, accepted by floor motion as Off-Campus Representative and sworn in on 13 February 1990, and was marked absent on 3 April 1990.

members.name: Ty Craig
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as Senior Class Vice-President and sworn in, 23 January 1990. No further mentions found, but the direct floor-motion seating-and-swearing-in is sufficient evidence on its own.

members.name: Roxana Crowe
members.seat: On-Campus Representative (later Student Affairs Committee Vice-Chair)
members.note: Accepted by floor motion (with Kristin Fryrear) as On-Campus Representative and sworn in, 7 November 1989 (recorded there as 'Roxane Crowe'). Accepted by floor motion as Student Affairs Vice-Chair, 30 January 1990. Nominated for the Kerrie Faye Stewart award, 3 April 1990.

members.name: Eric Elliot
members.seat: Congress member (seat not specified in the minutes)
members.note: On the absence roll 29 August 1989, before being sworn. Sworn in 12 September 1989, at which meeting he also spoke against a provision of Bill 89-02-F. Absent 14 November 1989, 6 and 20 February 1990. Distinct from 'Kelly Elliot' (sworn in separately 3 October 1989): the two names never co-occur, and each is tracked consistently and independently across a different span of the year, supporting but not conclusively proving these are two different people sharing a surname.
profile: Eric Elliot appeared on the Congress absence roll on 29 August 1989, before he had been sworn in. He was sworn in on 12 September 1989, and at that same meeting spoke against a provision of Bill 89-02-F. He was later marked absent on 14 November 1989 and on 6 and 20 February 1990. A second 'Elliot' -- Kelly Elliot, sworn in separately on 3 October 1989 -- appears in the same year's minutes; the two names never occur in the same meeting and each is tracked independently across a different span of the year, which supports, without proving outright, that they were two different people who happened to share a surname.

members.name: Kelly Elliot
members.seat: Congress member (seat not specified in the minutes)
members.note: Sworn in by President Gott, 3 October 1989 (no seat title recorded), together with Dawn Bradley and Emily Morgan. Absent 30 January, 27 March, 10 and 17 April 1990. Treated as distinct from 'Eric Elliot' per that entry's note.

members.name: Rob Evans
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as Co-Chair of Public Relations, 12 September 1989. Absent 24 October 1989, 13 February and 20 March 1990. Volunteered as ASG's representative to the Student Health Advisory Committee, 7 November 1989.

members.name: Heather Falmlen
members.seat: Sophomore Class President (formerly On-Campus Representative; later also Chairman of Student Rights)
members.note: Accepted by floor motion (with Darla Roof) as On-Campus Representative and sworn in, 29 August 1989; absent 10 October 1989. Chosen Sophomore Class President 24 October 1989, succeeding John Seiber (resigned 17 October). Accepted by floor motion as Chairman of Student Rights, 5 December 1989, succeeding Dwight Adkins (who resigned from ASG that meeting citing schedule conflicts). Absent 27 February 1990; nominated for the Kerrie Faye Stewart award, 3 April 1990.

members.name: Martha Ferreira
members.seat: Potter College Alternate (also separately accepted, a week later, as Junior Class Vice-President -- an unresolved conflict with Steve Mason's continued, unexplained presence in that same title afterward)
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as Potter College Alternate and sworn in, 23 January 1990. Absent 27 March 1990. A week later, 30 January 1990, a separate floor motion accepted Martha Ferreira as Junior Class Vice-President -- but Steve Mason continues on absence rolls afterward (1/30, 2/20, 3/27, 4/10, 4/17) with no title change noted, and the minutes give no explanation for the overlap. This is a genuine, unresolved contradiction in the source record.
profile: Martha Ferreira was accepted by floor motion as Potter College Alternate and sworn in on 23 January 1990; the minutes recorded her absent on 27 March 1990. A week later, on 30 January 1990, a separate floor motion accepted her as Junior Class Vice-President -- a title Steve Mason had held since September. Mason continued to appear on the absence rolls afterward with no title change noted, and the minutes never explained the overlap. The record leaves it unresolved for both of them.

members.name: Kristin Fryrear
members.note: Accepted by floor motion (with Roxana Crowe) as On-Campus Representative and sworn in, 7 November 1989 (recorded there as 'Kristin Fauser'). Absent under the 'Fryrear' spelling 6 and 27 February 1990. Named Outstanding Congress Member, 3 April 1990. The 'Fauser' spelling appears exactly once, at the swearing-in; 'Fryrear' recurs independently three more times afterward.
profile: Kristin Fryrear was accepted by floor motion, together with Roxana Crowe, as On-Campus Representative and sworn in on 7 November 1989; the minutes of that meeting rendered her name 'Kristin Fauser,' a spelling that appears nowhere else in the record. Under the 'Fryrear' spelling she was marked absent on 6 and 27 February 1990, and on 3 April 1990 she was named an Outstanding Congress Member.

members.name: Todd Gion
members.seat: Sergeant at Arms; later accepted by floor motion as a Representative, 10 April 1990 (exact seat title obscured by OCR damage)
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as Sergeant at Arms, 27 February 1990, apparently succeeding Hagan Rose. Accepted by floor motion and sworn in as a Representative, 10 April 1990 (recorded there as 'Todd Geon'). No link to the newly created Community College Representative seat is supported by the text: that seat was created by a constitutional amendment passed 27 March 1990, a separate and earlier meeting; the OCR around Gion's 10 April title is badly garbled and interleaved with an unrelated motion, so the seat there is left unspecified.
profile: Todd Gion was accepted by floor motion as Sergeant at Arms on 27 February 1990, apparently succeeding Hagan Rose in the post. He was accepted again by floor motion and sworn in as a Representative on 10 April 1990, where the minutes rendered his name 'Todd Geon'; OCR damage to that page leaves the exact seat he took unspecified, and nothing in the surviving text connects him to the Community College Representative seat the Senate had created by constitutional amendment two weeks earlier, on 27 March 1990.

members.name: Todd Johnson
members.note: Accepted by floor motion (with David Pittman) as Representative At-Large and sworn in, 29 August 1989. Absent 17 October 1989, 23 January and 27 March 1990.

members.name: Robin Kinman
members.seat: Congress member (seat not specified in the minutes)
members.note: On the absence roll 26 September, 3, 24 and 31 October 1989. Volunteered to be ASG's representative on the Student Health Insurance Committee, 17 October 1989. Resigned, reported in the 7 November 1989 minutes. This project's own 1988-89 records list a Secretary named Robin Kinman; nothing in these 1989-90 minutes ties this Congress-member activity to that executive office, and no source here confirms or refutes whether it is the same person -- that identity question is unresolved and is not implied by this entry.

members.name: Jeremy Lasley
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as On-Campus Representative and sworn in, 5 September 1989. On the absence roll repeatedly (verified 10/31, 1/23, 1/30, 2/6, 2/13, 3/20, 3/27).

members.name: Joe Leffert
members.note: Accepted 'by acclamation' as Education Representative, 12 September 1989 (recorded there as 'Joe Ledford'); the 19 September secretary's report still listed the seat as open, indicating the acclamation had not actually taken effect. Accepted again by floor motion and sworn in as College Education Representative, 26 September 1989. Resigned, reported in the 10 October 1989 minutes 'due to circumstances.'
profile: Joe Leffert's first term in Congress went wrong twice before it took. He was accepted 'by acclamation' as Education Representative on 12 September 1989, recorded in the minutes as 'Joe Ledford,' but the secretary's report the following week still listed the seat open, meaning the acclamation had not actually taken effect. He was accepted a second time, by floor motion, and sworn in as College of Education Representative on 26 September 1989. His resignation was reported at the 10 October 1989 meeting, 'due to circumstances' the minutes did not elaborate on.

members.name: Steve Mason
members.note: Accepted by floor motion as Junior Class Vice-President and sworn in, 5 September 1989, a week after Dwight Adkins had been accepted into the same title; Adkins stayed in ASG until he resigned on 5 December 1989, and the minutes never explain the overlap. On the absence roll repeatedly through the year (verified 9/19, 10/17, 10/31, 1/16, 1/30, 2/20, 3/27, 4/10, 4/17); named Committee-Member-of-the-Month, 27 February 1990. Unresolved conflict: the 30 January 1990 minutes separately record a floor motion accepting Martha Ferreira as 'Junior Class Vice-President' too, yet Mason continues on absence rolls afterward with no noted title change and the minutes never explain it.
profile: Steve Mason was accepted by floor motion as Junior Class Vice-President and sworn in on 5 September 1989, a week after Dwight Adkins had been accepted into the same title; Adkins stayed in ASG until he resigned on 5 December 1989, and the minutes never recorded him giving the post up. He appeared on the Congress absence roll repeatedly over the rest of the year -- 19 September, 17 and 31 October, 16 and 30 January, 20 February, 27 March, and 10 and 17 April -- and was named Committee-Member-of-the-Month on 27 February 1990. On 30 January 1990 -- the same night Mason himself was marked absent -- a separate floor motion accepted Martha Ferreira into that same Junior Class Vice-President title; the minutes never explained the overlap, and Mason kept appearing on the absence rolls afterward with no title change noted.

profile: Hagan Rose was elected University Center Board Representative on 29 August 1989, defeating Justin Cook's nomination for the same seat. He was accepted by floor motion as Sergeant at Arms on 3 October 1989, then accepted by floor motion into a third post, Off-Campus Representative, on 23 January 1990; Todd Gion was accepted as Sergeant at Arms the following month, on 27 February 1990. profile: Michael Colvin won the Associated Student Government presidential election in results the Herald reported on 19 April 1990 under the headline "Michael Colvin Aces Associated Student Government Election." The 1991 Talisman independently lists him as Associated Student Government President for 1990-91.
In office, the Herald reported ASG considering a four-day class week (7 February 1991) and covered concern inside the organization over a change affecting student insurance (15 January 1991).
The archive does not preserve further detail of how the term ended or what Colvin did afterward.

Colvin took office in August 1990, introduced by the Herald as a new leader who wanted to make ideas reality. He had been active in the organization at least since September 1989, when he signed a Herald piece soliciting help for ASG.

His spring 1991 agenda was the widest of the era: in a single February week ASG moved to cap tuition boosts, proposed overhauling the Detrex registration system, and planned lobbying to protect student financial aid.
Letters he signed under Resolution 91-7-S survive in the SGA records, pressing administrators Kemble Johnson and Debby Cherwak for improvements to Detrex Field.

Legislative records fill out the year beyond what the Herald's brief items captured. In fall 1990 the body introduced bills for a roundtable of student organization presidents (Bill #90-2-F) and for microwaves in the cafeterias (Bill #90-4-F). On 29 November 1990 it passed Resolution 90-10-F asking for a left-handed desk in every classroom, and killed Resolution 90-12-F, which had asked that absences tied to Iben Browning's widely publicized New Madrid Fault earthquake prediction be excused; no earthquake came. In the spring the Senate suspended and amended its own by-laws in a short cluster of bills, including Bill #91-6-S changing the procedure for overriding a presidential veto - a procedure tested weeks later when the emergency-kit resolution survived a veto on 14 March 1991. The spring term also produced a resolution asking the university to improve Detrex Field, the intramural field, and bills on joining the Hilltopper Athletic Foundation, recognizing presidential scholars in the Herald, and a book exchange board for Grise Hall.

profile: Falmlen won the Associated Student Government presidency in results the Herald reported on 11 April 1991 under the headline "Heather Falmlen Wins Amid Associated Student Government Election Protests." A Herald "Meet the Candidates" feature on 2 April had previewed four contenders for the race: Falmlen, Rob Evans, Van Hodge, and Dan Knowles. The same 11 April issue reported a rival group urging students to boycott the vote, an editorial calling the contest's "immature antics" a disappointment, and a published complaint that the Herald's own election coverage had been biased.

In office, her administration fought a running battle over the makeup of the Board of Regents. On 29 October 1991 the Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-6-F asking that Joe Iracane not be re-elected chair of the board; the Herald covered the vote the same day under "Associated Student Government Opposes Joseph Iracane." The board went ahead and re-elected him a week later, the university's own "On Campus" newsletter reported on 6 November. On 30 January 1992 the Herald reported the Associated Student Government was separately planning a committee aimed at student access to the regent, in the same issue that carried an editorial cartoon, "Ventriloquist's Dummy," targeting Falmlen. On 4 February 1992 the body passed Resolution 92-7-S, declaring its support for the WKU football program in spite of budget cuts; the Board of Regents voted that May to keep the program.

That fall the body passed Resolution 91-2-F, asking for a change to Big Red Shuttle bus fares, and held its regular fall senate elections in October, including a separate freshman senator election on 15 October.

The signature action of her term was procedural: on 7 April 1992 the Associated Students voted to rename itself the Student Government Association, a change students ratified in a referendum a week later, effective that autumn. WKU's own "On Campus" newsletter had confirmed on 22 May 1991, at the start of her term, that Falmlen held both the presidency and the student regent seat - the same dual role held by the presidents before and after her in this period. The archive does not preserve further detail of her regency or of what she did after her term.

Other legislative business that fall included Resolution 91-7-F, backing the renewal of President Thomas Meredith's contract by the Board of Regents; a bill funding a "President for a Day" fundraiser (Bill #91-09-F); a bill funding renovation of the ASG chambers (Bill #91-03-F); and a bill proposing a new organizational slogan (Bill #91-11-F), introduced the same season the body renamed itself from the Associated Students to the Student Government Association.

events.title: ASG resolves to support football despite budget cuts
events.body: The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 92-7-S, declaring its support for the WKU football program in spite of budget cuts. The resolution's own text argued the university had already awarded 67 football scholarships it would be contractually bound to honor even if the program were suspended, calling a suspension that still paid non-playing scholarship athletes an unnecessary expense. This entry corrects the resolution's date: an earlier record in this archive gave 4 February 1992, but the resolution itself is dated introduced 2 April 1992, shortly before the Board of Regents' 1 May vote to keep the program.

src.label: SGA Legislation, Resolution 92-7-S, "Support of Football Program"

events.title: Associated Students votes to become the Student Government Association
events.body: The body voted to rename itself on 7 April and students ratified the change in a referendum on 14 April. It took effect that autumn.

events.title: Board of Regents votes to keep football
events.body: The Board of Regents voted to keep the football program, following months of budget pressure that had prompted the ASG's February resolution of support.

src.label: Herald, 1 May 1992, "Board of Regents Votes to Keep Football"

events.title: Herald previews four ASG candidates
events.body: The Herald's "Meet the Candidates" feature previewed four contenders in the spring Associated Student Government elections: Heather Falmlen, Rob Evans, Van Hodge, and Dan Knowles. Falmlen went on to win the race.

events.title: ASG asks for a change in Big Red Shuttle fares
events.body: The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-2-F, sponsored by the Student Affairs committee, requesting a one-way fare option on the Big Red Shuttle for infrequent riders. The resolution's text called the existing $10 fee "outrageous and unfair" to students and faculty who did not ride the shuttle daily.

events.title: Fall ASG senate and freshman elections held
events.body: The Herald covered the Associated Student Government's fall elections on 10 October, and a separate freshman senator election on 15 October; the paper's abstracts do not preserve the results.

src.label: Herald 67:13, 10 Oct 1991, "Associated Student Government Elections Tuesday"

events.title: ASG introduces a bill for a student regent advisory committee
events.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #92-01-S, authored by Greg Butler, Mistianna Holcomb, Melony Jones and Melissa Maggard and sponsored by the Public Relations committee, proposing a Student Advisory Committee - made up of the class presidents, a representative from each college and the executive council as ex-officio members - to brief the student regent on Board of Regents agenda items and canvass student opinion before each meeting, two days before the Herald reported the plan.

src.label: SGA Legislation, Bill #92-01-S, "Development of Advisory Committee for Student Regent"

events.title: University newsletter confirms Falmlen holds both offices
events.body: WKU's own "On Campus" newsletter reported Heather Falmlen as both Student Regent and Associated Student Government President, a contemporaneous confirmation that the two offices - separately elected two decades earlier - were held by the same person entering her term.

src.label: On Campus 1:7, 22 May 1991, "Heather Falmlen is Student Regent, Associated Student Government President"

events.title: ASG asks that Iracane not be re-elected regents chair
events.body: The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-6-F, authored by Mark Miller and Eric McWilliams and sponsored by Mistianna Holcomb, asking that Joe Iracane not be re-elected chair of the Board of Regents. The resolution's text stated that Iracane, chairman for eight consecutive years, was under investigation by the FBI, the IRS and U.S. attorneys in Indiana and Kentucky over an alleged $6 million payment to Pyramid Mining Co. in return for contracts and a separate alleged $14,500 payment to the company for a consulting contract; it also accused him of overstepping into day-to-day university operations reserved for the president under the Board's bylaws. The resolution asked student regent Heather Falmlen to vote against him. No source found reports the investigation's outcome. The same day's Herald covered the vote under "Associated Student Government Opposes Joseph Iracane."

src.label: SGA Resolution 91-6-F, "Board of Regents Chair Term Limit"

events.title: Regents re-elect Iracane despite ASG's resolution
events.body: A week after the Associated Student Government asked the Board of Regents not to re-elect Joe Iracane as chair, the board did so anyway. The university's own newsletter reported the result under "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents."

src.label: On Campus 1:16, 6 Nov 1991, "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents"

events.body: The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-7-F, backing the renewal of President Thomas Meredith's contract by the Board of Regents.

events.title: ASG bill funds renovation of its own chambers
events.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-03-F, providing for the renovation of the ASG chambers.

events.title: ASG bill proposes changing its own slogan
events.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-11-F, proposing to change the organization's slogan, in the same fall that it voted to rename itself from the Associated Students to the Student Government Association.

events.title: Health tops the agenda; more money for the environment
events.body: Heather Falmlen opened the year with a student health issue at the top of her agenda, and ASG budgeted more money for environmental efforts. Both stories ran in the first week of the fall semester.

events.title: Fighting the city's noise ordinance
events.body: ASG resolved to fight Bowling Green's noise ordinance. It was the organization's most direct engagement with city government in years.

events.title: Officers go to the city's meeting
events.body: ASG officers attended a city meeting to press the noise ordinance fight, and the organization restarted its voter registration drive. A recycling resolution had its first reading the week before.

events.title: ASG asks the regents to elect a new leader
events.body: ASG urged the Board of Regents to elect a new leader in place of chairman Joseph Iracane, two days after the Herald reported the organization's opposition to him. It was a rare direct challenge to the university's governing board.

events.title: A mailing asks parents to back the health service
events.body: The Residence Hall Association and ASG sent a joint mailing asking parents to support the campus health service. It closed out the health-focused fall Falmlen had promised in August.

events.title: The primary is canceled
events.body: The ASG primary election was canceled, with too few candidates to require one, and a parking bill sat in committee the same week. The general election went ahead the following Tuesday.

events.title: Joe Rains wins big as 1,200 turn out
events.body: Joe Rains won the presidential election by a wide margin, with about 1,200 students casting votes. The same ballot carried the constitutional amendments students had voted on two days earlier, including the name change.

events.title: Rains takes office with a rename to carry out
events.body: The Herald reported that incoming president Joe Rains would oversee the change from the Associated Student Government to the Student Government Association, which students had ratified by referendum the week before. The new name took effect that fall, making Rains the first president to serve under it. Student reaction to the spring's parking bill was reported as varied in the same issue.

events.title: International Day, co-sponsored with the University Center Board
events.body: More than 800 high school students from around the state came to Western on Friday 25 October for the annual International Day, sponsored by the University Center Board, Associated Student Government, International Programs and Student Affairs. A bazaar on the third floor of Downing University Center sold handmade goods from other countries, including bracelets, ornaments, scarves and belts made by Indian tribes in Ecuador and African woodwork and silver and copper jewellery. Profits from the crafts went to Escuela Para Padres, a joint fundraising organisation working to prevent abuse of women and children; project coordinator Joan Martin said jewellery was the best seller.

events.title: Voter registration drive signs up nearly 1,000 students
events.body: ASG ran a voter registration drive for the 5 November 1991 election, led by vice president John Seiber, who with other congress members registered nearly 1,000 Western students. A full-page ASG advertisement in the Herald the following February listed the drive alongside fall break, campus recycling, organizational aid, new picnic tables, a new copier for the science library and the radio show as the year's work, with forums on the election, student concerns, the class presidents and a question and answer session with the regents.

events.title: A permanent voter registration booth at class registration
events.body: Bill 92-06-S, introduced on 24 March 1992 by Trent Lyda for the Legislative Research Committee, committed ASG to keeping a voter registration booth wherever class registration took place each fall and spring, to capitalise on the influx of unregistered eligible student voters. The committee was to coordinate the scheduling of students and organisations willing to staff it, and every ASG member was asked to work the booth for at least an hour during the registration period.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-06-S, Establishment of Permanent Voter Registration Program

events.title: A bill to set up a Coach for a Game fundraiser
events.body: Bill 92-03-S, written by Mistianna Holcomb and sponsored by the public relations committee, proposed a Coach for a Game programme alongside the President for a Day event ASG already sponsored in the fall. It would have made it mandatory for every ASG member to sell ten raffle tickets at 50 cents each, with the proceeds going to a philanthropic cause. The document carries no introduction, reading or voting dates, so the file does not show when or whether it passed.
events.money: raffle tickets 50 cents each, ten per member

executive.name: Joe Rains
executive.note: Presented the 1991-92 budget for acceptance at the first meeting on 3 September 1991, reported a running budget summary of $794.98 a fortnight later, and ran organizational aid, setting a 14 February 1992 application deadline with interviews from 17 to 28 February. He was elected president for 1992-93.
profile: Joe Rains served as treasurer of the Associated Student Government for 1991-92, under president Heather Falmlen. He presented the 1991-92 budget for acceptance at the first Congress meeting on 3 September 1991, reported a running budget summary of $794.98 a fortnight later, and ran the organizational aid process that year, setting a 14 February 1992 application deadline with interviews set for 17 to 28 February. He was elected president for 1992-93, running against Mistianna Holcomb in the April 1992 vote; the same election carried a referendum on renaming the Associated Student Government the Student Government Association, and the organization went by the new name from that year.

profile: Mistianna Holcomb served as ASG Public Relations Vice-President for 1991-92. She announced Western Pride Week for 9 to 14 September 1991, signed members up to work the primary and general elections, and reported to Congress on a coming meeting with Bowling Green mayor Sloan.
She sponsored Resolution 91-6-F, which asked that Joe Iracane not be re-elected chairman of the Board of Regents; the regents re-elected him anyway on 6 November 1991.
In April 1992 the Herald reported her standing against Joe Rains for the ASG presidency. Rains won with roughly 1,200 students voting.
