profile: Joe Rains was elected Associated Student Government president on 14 April 1992, a contested race the Herald's election-day issue covered with dueling opinion pieces: an editorial headlined "Associated Student Government Needs Joe Rains" ran alongside a cartoon depicting him as Darth Vader, and the paper carried separate profile pieces on candidates Mark Miller, Mistianna Holcomb and Melony Jones. The same ballot carried the referendum that renamed Associated Students as the Student Government Association; Rains took office that autumn as the first president to serve under the new name.

In office, Rains argued that SGA should support a campus student escort service (Herald, 10 December 1992) and took part in a rally at the state capitol in Frankfort urging the legislature to stop cuts to higher-education funding, for which the WKU University Senate commended him in Resolution R92.11.
The archive does not preserve further detail of how the term ended.

Rains ran for the presidency in April 1992 against Mistianna Holcomb, in the same election week that students voted on a referendum to rename the Associated Student Government as the Student Government Association. The Herald covered both races in a single issue, so his campaign and the rename were decided together.

On election day the Herald's opinion pages carried a letter headlined "Associated Student Government Needs Joe Rains" alongside a Patrick Richardson editorial cartoon depicting Rains as Darth Vader, a sign of how visible the race had become on campus.

The SGA's own list of presidents, published on its website in 2001, records Joe Rains of Nashville, Tennessee as the organization's 26th president, serving 1992-93, and marks him as having also served as student regent.

The digitised record of his year does not name him directly in any indexed description, but it carries one distinctive trace: the minutes for December 1, 1992 record plans for a call-in radio show the association titled 'Just Ask Joe,' alongside Project Western and President for a Day. The same year's minutes show a congress preoccupied with state budget cuts, tuition increases, student health insurance and repeated plans for a rally in Frankfort.

events.title: Joe Rains elected SGA president as the ASG-to-SGA renaming took effect
events.body: Rains won a contested Associated Student Government presidential election covered by the Herald under the headline "Associated Student Government Needs Joe Rains," alongside a rival editorial cartoon depicting him as Darth Vader and profile pieces on candidates Mark Miller, Mistianna Holcomb and Melony Jones. The same ballot carried the referendum renaming Associated Students as the Student Government Association.

events.title: Rains pushed SGA to back a student escort service
events.body: SGA president Joe Rains argued the organization should support a campus student escort service, the Herald reported.

events.title: University Senate honored Rains for a Frankfort budget-cut rally
events.body: The WKU University Senate adopted Resolution R92.11, commending SGA president Joe Rains for taking part in a rally at the state capitol in Frankfort asking the legislature to stop cuts to higher-education funding. TopSCHOLAR records the resolution's history running from 11 December 1992 to its adoption on 29 January 1993.

events.title: The renamed SGA elects its representatives
events.body: In its first weeks under the new name, the Student Government Association held elections for its representatives. The Herald covered the vote at the start of the fall semester.

events.title: Support gathers for a rally
events.body: The Herald's index for this issue records the new SGA winning support for a campus rally that October, under the headline "Student Government Association Gets Support for Rally."

events.title: An invitation to get involved
events.body: An opinion piece by Paul Weathers urged students to get involved in the Student Government Association, part of the Herald's running commentary on the body during its first semester under the new name.

events.title: Donald Smith rolls to victory
events.body: The Herald called the spring election with the headline "Student Government Association Election: Donald Smith Rolls to Victory." Smith would succeed Rains for the 1993-94 term.

events.title: Fall opened with a new logo and discount cards
events.body: At its first meeting of the fall on August 25, 1992, the student government discussed a new logo, student discount cards, a voter registration drive and committee assignments. The group was still transitioning from the Associated Student Government name to SGA, and its minutes from this year appear under both titles.

events.title: Resolution asked WKU to spare academics from budget cuts
events.body: Resolution 92-7-F asked the university to exempt academic units from a round of proposed budget cuts. State funding pressure ran through the whole fall; the same weeks produced repeated plans for a student rally in Frankfort.

events.title: President Meredith addressed the student congress
events.body: WKU President Thomas Meredith came to the October 13 meeting to talk about computers, laundry facilities, cable television, lighting and Potter Hall. The same minutes record discussion of budget cuts, homecoming elections, a newsletter and joint forums with the Residence Hall Association.

events.title: Congress honored the Lady Toppers
events.body: Resolution 92-8-F honored the WKU women's basketball team for its runner-up finish in the NCAA tournament. It was one of a string of numbered resolutions the congress produced that fall on subjects from drop-add fees to parking.

events.title: Just Ask Joe radio program and Project Western
events.body: The December 1 minutes record plans for a Just Ask Joe call-in radio program, the Project Western campus cleanup, a President for a Day event, recycling bins and student health insurance. The meeting closed out a semester dominated by tuition and budget worries.

events.title: Meredith returned to pitch Potter Hall as a student service center
events.body: President Thomas Meredith addressed the February 2 meeting about campus laundry, cable television and turning Potter Hall into a student service center. Members also discussed tuition increases, resignations and general education requirements.

events.title: Spring closed with elections and Earth Day plans
events.body: The April 13 meeting took up the budget, spring elections, the annual banquet, a one-card ID system, smoking policy, Adopt-a-Spot and Earth Day. It was the last full meeting recorded in the digitised minutes for the year.

events.title: Herald previews the race and the rename referendum
events.body: The Herald previewed the Associated Student Government presidential race under "Mistianna Holcomb, Joe Rains Vying for Presidency," profiled candidate Susan Mitchell under "Susan Mitchell Has a Fresh Perspective," and reported that students would soon vote on a referendum to rename the Associated Student Government the Student Government Association. No source found confirms what office Mitchell sought or whether she won it.

events.title: Turnout worries and candidate profiles filled the ballot issue
events.body: The same issue that reported Rains' win ran the Herald's concern piece "Many Students Won't Vote" alongside profile pieces on the other candidates: "Mark Miller's Involvement Makes Him a Leader," "Mistianna Holcomb Takes a Stand for Students," and "Melony Jones Loved & Respected by Peers."

events.title: Sixteen thousand savings cards and a Vote About It drive
events.body: At the first meeting of the year President Joe Rains reported that sixteen thousand student savings cards were ready for distribution, and public relations vice president Patrick Monahan told members they could begin handing them out. Administrative vice president Susan Mitchell, chairing the Vote America committee, announced a voter registration drive for mid-September and a later drive on absentee voting under the theme VOTE ABOUT IT. The same meeting recorded the summer's new SGA logo, new furniture and a computer, and the loss of the agency account that had let the organisation buy things as it needed them.

events.title: Forums between congress members and hall governments
events.body: Bill 92-05-F, introduced 6 October 1992 and passed unanimously on 13 October, set up forums between on-campus residents and SGA in conjunction with the hall governments. The reasoning was that congress members attending hall government meetings could answer questions hall officers could not, and that the on-campus population made up a significant part of the student body.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-05-F, Establishing Forums Between Campus Residents and SGA

events.title: Adopt-A-Spot put on a contract footing
events.body: Bill 92-09-F, introduced by Eric McWilliams and Kevin Moore on 20 October 1992 and passed unanimously, had SGA finance and run an Adopt-A-Spot programme in which student organisations took contractual responsibility for keeping a designated patch of campus clean. The Campus Improvements Committee oversaw the scheme and divided the university into geographical areas, and of the more than 120 student organisations on campus many were judged to have the numbers to look after a spot. Groups that failed to do what they had agreed were required to make complete restitution to SGA.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-09-F, Contractual Agreement for Adopt-a-Spot Program

events.title: SGA puts $100 behind the Topperettes' trip to Dallas
events.body: Bill 92-14-F, introduced 1 December 1992, joined SGA with other university departments in contributing one hundred dollars towards sending the WKU Topperettes to the national competition in Dallas in early January. The bill said the squad enhanced student life at Western with their skills and had worked hard to qualify. The team finished ninth in the nation, and the SGA secretary reported in January that a letter of congratulation had been sent.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-14-F, Funding for Topperettes

events.title: President for a Day raffle tickets go on sale
events.body: At the 19 January 1993 meeting the administrative vice president's office reported that raffle tickets for President for a Day were going on sale that week, and tickets were handed out to congress members to sell. Public relations vice president Patrick Monahan pressed members to sell a lot of them. The same report noted that the radio show with President Joe Rains would now go out live rather than taped.

events.title: Project Western Week and the planned Don't Trash The Spirit clean-up
events.body: SGA's Project Western Week began on Monday 8 February 1993 and ran through the week. Its biggest part was to be a mass campus clean-up the next day under the motto Don't Trash The Spirit. President Joe Rains said students would start picking up trash at about 3:30 p.m. at the New Co-Ed and New Sorority dorms, spread out across the width of campus and finish at Cherry Hall, and about 600 people were expected. The campus was to be divided into 23 sections taken by organisations that had until 5 February to sign up and that would stay responsible for their areas until the end of the semester, with $500 from SGA for the group keeping the cleanest area.
events.money: $500 prize to the organisation with the cleanest area

executive.name: Susan Mitchell
executive.note: Chaired the ad hoc Vote America committee and ran a voter registration drive under the slogan "VOTE ABOUT IT", took applications for open Congress seats, and organised the September 1992 freshman elections. In February 1993 she reported that President for a Day had gone well.
profile: Susan Mitchell served as SGA Administrative Vice President for 1992-93, the first year under the association's renaming from ASG to SGA. She chaired the ad hoc Vote America committee and ran a voter registration drive under the slogan "VOTE ABOUT IT," took applications for open Congress seats, and organized the September 1992 freshman elections.
In February 1993 she reported to Congress that the President for a Day fundraiser, for which tickets had gone on sale that January, had gone well.

executive.name: Jeremy Sublett
executive.note: Instituted a fortnightly expense report and held organizational aid back while the loss of SGA's agency account was resolved; by February 1993 seventeen groups had signed up for Project Western.
profile: Jeremy Sublett served as SGA Treasurer for 1992-93. He instituted a fortnightly expense report and held organizational aid back while the loss of SGA's agency account was resolved.
By February 1993 he reported that seventeen student groups had signed up for Project Western.

executive.name: Ashley Rose
executive.note: Enforced the attendance rule, with more than ten minutes' lateness counting as an absence and five absences the limit for the year, and reported that Executive Council had vetoed Bill 93-2-S, which would have bought a fax machine for the SGA office.
profile: Ashley Rose served as SGA Secretary for 1992-93. She enforced the association's attendance rule, under which more than ten minutes' lateness counted as an absence and five absences was the limit for the year.
She reported that Executive Council had vetoed Bill 93-2-S, which would have bought a fax machine for the SGA office.

executive.name: Patrick Monahan
executive.note: Distributed the 16,000 student discount cards, announced that the state SGA conference would be held at Western over the weekend of 31 October 1992, and reported the kick-off of Project Western. He told Congress every committee needed to produce one piece of legislation a week. The minutes spell the surname both Monahan and Monohan.
profile: Patrick Monahan served as SGA Public Relations Vice President for 1992-93; the minutes spell his surname both Monahan and Monohan. He distributed 16,000 student discount cards and announced that the state SGA conference would be held at Western the weekend of 31 October 1992.
He reported the kick-off of Project Western and told Congress that every committee needed to produce one piece of legislation a week.

senate.note: Minutes from 25 Aug 1992 through 13 Apr 1993 survive, recording a congress occupied with state budget cuts, tuition increases and a Frankfort rally. Several committee chairs changed hands during the year (see committees below); no total Congress seat count is stated anywhere in the surviving minutes. TopSCHOLAR catalogues Minutes item 406 under 20 September 1992, which was a Sunday. The document itself is headed 22 September 1992, a Tuesday, as were the other dated congress meetings that autumn (8, 15 and 29 September, items 410, 408 and 405). The catalogue date is wrong and this archive follows the minutes. President Joe Rains called that meeting to order at 5.05 p.m., and the five members recorded here from item 406 — Laura Jo Bland, Ray Ezell, Eric Griggs, Crystal Smith and Robert Wagner — are all named in its roll call, each of them among the absences that night.

officers.name: Donald Smith
officers.note: Named Legislative Research chair by the Executive Council slate approved on 25 August 1992, and still chairing it in February 1993. He was elected president for 1993-94.
profile: The Executive Council slate approved on 25 August 1992 named Donald Smith chair of the Legislative Research Committee, a post he still held that February, ahead of the spring election in which he won the SGA presidency for 1993-94.

officers.name: Eric McWilliams
officers.note: Named Campus Improvements chair on 25 August 1992; by February 1993 he was chairing Student Affairs, whose resolution proposing a study day before exam week passed unanimously on 9 February 1993. He was one of the two authors of Resolution 91-6-F against Joe Iracane's re-election as board chairman.
profile: Eric McWilliams was named chair of the Senate's Campus Improvements Committee on 25 August 1992, in the first Congress meeting of Joe Rains's administration. By February 1993 he had moved to chair Student Affairs instead, whose resolution proposing a study day before exam week passed unanimously on 9 February. He was one of two authors of Resolution 91-6-F, which opposed Joe Iracane's re-election as chairman of the Board of Regents.

McWilliams ran for the Student Government Association presidency himself that spring, one of two juniors in the 1993 race against fellow committee chair Donald Smith. Smith won the 22 April 1993 election, which the Herald reported under the headline "Donald Smith Rolls to Victory."

profile: Mark Miller was named chair of the Senate's Public Relations Committee on 25 August 1992, at the start of Joe Rains's administration, and co-authored Resolution 91-6-F with Eric McWilliams, opposing Joe Iracane's re-election as chairman of the Board of Regents. An opinion piece in the Herald's 14 April 1992 special election issue, printed alongside endorsements for presidential candidates Joe Rains, Melony Jones and Mistianna Holcomb, argued that Miller's campus involvement made him a leader; it did not name which office he sought. Rains won that spring's presidency. Two years later the Herald printed an opinion piece by Donald Smith and a Mark Miller urging the Class of 1994 to give back to Western; the shared name and Smith's own service in the same Congress make it likely, but not certain, that this is the same Miller.

A year before taking the post, in February 1992, he had written an opinion piece for the Herald headlined "Associated Student Government: Don't Complain, Get Involved," urging students to take part in the organization he went on to serve in.

profile: Smith won the April 1993 election decisively. The Herald's headline was "Student Government Association Election: Donald Smith Rolls to Victory."

That September the Herald profiled the new president under the headline "Donald Smith Followed Grandfather's Lead All the Way to President's Office," tracing a family connection to the role he had just taken up.

Smith, from Elizabethtown, went on to become president of the College Heights Foundation. Interviewed by the Herald in 2022, he said that while the structure had changed over the years, "the fundamental principle for SGA to be a voice for the students has remained unphased," and that if SGA improves over time the WKU experience improves with it.

events.title: At least seventeen numbered resolutions in one semester
events.body: Resolutions 93-4-F through 93-20-F survive in the correspondence files - the fullest single-semester record in the collection, and the best available answer to how much a WKU student senate actually passes in a working term.

events.title: A delayed constitution reading
events.body: The fall semester opened with a stumble. The Herald reported that a scheduled reading of the SGA constitution had been delayed, in the same issue that covered rising tempers over campus parking.

events.title: Congress changes approved
events.body: The SGA approved changes to its congress in September while freshmen debated for open positions. The Herald covered both in a single mid-September issue.

events.title: Let's work together for change
events.body: The Herald ran an opinion piece under the heading "Let's Work Together for Change" and put the question of how SGA could reach more students to its People Poll. The paper also ran a Stacy Curtis editorial cartoon offering a "recipe for better representation."

events.title: A resolution on class attendance
events.body: An SGA resolution covered by the Herald would have let students skip class, reported under the headline "Attendance: Student Government Association Resolution Would Let Students Skip Class."

events.title: A disputed primary
events.body: The Herald reported that presidential candidate Scott Sivley had not followed SGA and university procedures during the election, in the same issue that carried the tallied results of the primary. The episode ran alongside the paper's get-out-the-vote editorial coverage.

events.title: Evans and Higdon ready to lead
events.body: The Herald closed the election season with "Rob Evans & Tara Higdon Ready to Lead Students." The same issue carried letters both defending the organization and, from future president Kristen Miller, a piece headlined "Student Government Association Defends Itself."

events.title: A new constitution came up first
events.body: Bill 93-1-F, introduced at the second meeting of the fall, proposed amendments to the SGA constitution. Constitutional revision stayed on the agenda through October, alongside the tuition rally the congress was planning.

events.title: Congress planned a tuition rally
events.body: The October 12 meeting discussed a tuition rally, the budget, the Plus System and parking. The rally kept appearing in the minutes for the next month as tuition increases moved through the state process.

events.title: Bill funded emergency phones on campus
events.body: Bill 93-6-F proposed purchasing and installing emergency telephones on campus. The Herald was still reporting on SGA's security phones the following February, and campus lighting and safety stayed on the agenda into the spring.

events.title: Memorial trees for students who die while enrolled
events.body: Bill 93-12-F proposed planting memorial trees in tribute to students who die while enrolled at WKU. It capped a heavy late-November run of legislation that also included child care grants for non-traditional students, a book exchange and opening the Downing University Center computer lab during finals.

events.title: President for a Day swapped a student into Meredith's office
events.body: The Herald reported that student Angelo Rodriguez would switch places with President Thomas Meredith through SGA's President for a Day program. The same issue covered SGA's security phones on campus and a proposal to let students retake C grades that was killed in committee.

events.title: A $3 fee to support the Big Red Card
events.body: Resolution 94-4-S proposed a three dollar student fee to support the Big Red Card program. The card system and its fees ran through the minutes for the rest of the spring.

events.title: Willard's resignation reached the floor
events.body: The March 29 meeting took up the resignation of basketball coach Ralph Willard along with the Big Red Card fee, teacher evaluations, emergency telephones, campus lighting and the coming elections. Dialogue Day and Adopt-a-Spot rounded out a crowded agenda.

events.title: A year-end banquet, and corners cut on the budget
events.body: The Herald closed the year with two SGA stories: the year-end banquet recognizing award winners and officers, and a report that the association was cutting corners with its budget.

events.title: Bill recognized President's Scholars
events.body: Bill 93-4-F proposed formal SGA recognition of President's Scholars at WKU, one of the seventeen numbered pieces of legislation the fall 1993 congress produced.

events.title: Executive Council pressed the administration on holiday housing
events.body: The SGA Executive Council, acting on Resolution 93-18-F, wrote to administrators Katherine Tolbert, Dave Parrott, John Osborne and Ann Stathos asking the university to address housing for students during holiday breaks.

events.title: SGA wrote guidelines for its public forums
events.body: The association adopted written guidelines governing how it would run student public forums, formalizing a process that had previously run ad hoc.

src.label: SGA Records: Guidelines for SGA Public Forums, Jan 1994

events.title: Head Start at congress, and members sent out to volunteer
events.body: Dr Jerry Wilder and Mike Gramling, director of the Head Start programme, were the guest speakers at the 12 October 1993 congress meeting. Public relations chairwoman Emily Brown then encouraged members to volunteer for Head Start. The treasurer reported the account balance that night at $38,977.50 with no expenditures since the previous meeting, and organizational aid interviews were being held on 12 and 13 October.

events.title: Word on Western named as the SGA radio show
events.body: Public relations chairwoman Emily Brown told congress on 12 October 1993 that Word on Western would be the name of the SGA radio show, to be heard on 91.7 FM at 2 p.m. on Wednesdays. It followed the taped and then live show the previous administration had run under Joe Rains. The same meeting heard that Adopt-A-Spot places were still open and that articles for the SGA newsletter, The Gavel, were due by 25 October.

events.title: $150 for a Book Exchanger board in Downing University Center
events.body: Bill 93-5-F, by Jill Reading and Eddie Myers for the Student Affairs Committee, allocated $150 to buy a large bulletin board and sign where students could list by category the books they wanted to sell. The board was to go on the first floor of Downing University Center across from the Marriott office. The bill argued that inflated book prices and minimal buy-back prices left students needing a place to sell to each other.

events.title: Angelo Rodriguez serves as President for a Day
events.body: President Donald Smith congratulated Angelo Rodriguez at the 22 February 1994 meeting for serving as President for a Day. Smith also reported that the Frankfort reception had gone well with seventy legislators attending and fifteen Western students present. The treasurer put expenditures since the last meeting at $320.62, leaving a balance of $21,139.97.

events.title: Cultural Diversity Week and Spirit Week in preparation
events.body: Administrative vice president Scott Sivley reported on 22 February 1994 that Cultural Diversity Week was almost set and that the Adopt-A-Spot committee would meet on 24 February. Public relations vice president Bert Blevins reported that letters were going out to all organisations about Spirit Week. Both weeks were SGA-run additions to the spring calendar alongside the campus clean-up and President for a Day.

events.title: The Points of Light programme and The Polaris
events.body: Bill 94-4-S, by Donald Smith and Scott Sivley, created the Points of Light programme to honour students who gave their time to help society, open to nomination by any campus organisation or individual and awarded by the executive officers at intervals through the year. Recipients were named in the Herald, given a certificate and honoured at SGA's annual banquet. The most outstanding recipient received an annual award called The Polaris, a commemorative plaque and a $100 SGA donation to the charity of their choice.
events.money: $100 donated to the Polaris winner's chosen charity

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-4-S, Points of Light Program

events.title: Nominations open for the year-end SGA awards
events.body: At the 29 March 1994 meeting the secretary took nominations for the year's awards: the Citizen's Award, Outstanding Congress Member, Outstanding Committee Member, the Dero Downing Award, the Kerrie Faye Stewart Memorial Award, the Mary Angela Norcia Memorial Award and the Dean Charles A. Keown Award. She also handed out certificates to past Committee and Congress Members of the Month. The banquet was set for 26 April at 6 p.m. in the Kentucky Museum.

events.title: Memorial trees, recycling bins and the book exchange board in hand
events.body: The 29 March 1994 meeting recorded Bowling Green Operation Pride agreeing to help find donated trees for the SGA memorial tree programme for students who died while enrolled. Campus Improvements reported that Coca-Cola was donating ten bins for aluminium can recycling, that Adopt-A-Spot winners would be announced that week, and that the grievance boards had been dropped. Student Affairs reported it was working on the Book Exchanger board.
events.money: ten aluminium recycling bins donated by Coca-Cola

events.title: SGA sets a Dialogue Day with administrators
events.body: President Smith told the SGA meeting of 29 March 1994 that 6 April would be Dialogue Day, when students could talk with administrators in Niteclass from noon to 2 p.m. The public relations committee handed out flyers for it alongside flyers for the coming election. The same minutes record that security phones were expected to be in place by 26 April, and report on the memorial tree programme.

events.title: Judge-executive candidates invited to congress
events.body: Administrative vice-president Scott Sivley told congress on 12 October 1993 that the Warren County judge-executive candidates, Miller and Buchanon, would be guests at the meeting of 26 October. The same minutes record speakers from Head Start before congress that evening.

events.title: $2,250 of organizational aid split between thirteen groups
events.body: Bill 94-2-S, introduced on 1 March 1994, disbursed the $2,250 budgeted for organizational aid after the committee spent more than four hours across three meetings deciding between the applicants. Phi Beta Sigma took $350; Alpha Phi Omega, Campus Crusade for Christ and Delta Sigma Theta took $250 each; Beta Alpha Psi $200; the Fellowship of Christian Athletes $150; the Association of Resident Assistants, the Legion of Veterans, Students' Right to Life and United Student Activists $125 each; and the International Club, SOTA and the Topperettes $100 each. It passed on second reading on 8 March 1994.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-2-S, Organizational Aid Recipients

events.title: Weekend in the Woods announced for 23 and 24 October
events.body: President Donald Smith told congress on 12 October 1993 that Weekend in the Woods would be held on 23 and 24 October. The minutes carry one line on it and record nothing about who went, where it was held or what it cost.

events.title: SGA hands out flyers for a Jesse Jackson Jr. speech
events.body: Administrative vice president Scott Sivley passed out flyers at the congress meeting of 29 March 1994 for a speech by Jesse Jackson Jr. set for 18 April. The minutes tie SGA to the publicity and to nothing else, naming no venue, sponsor or fee, and they do not show the speech took place.

events.title: SGA started a newsletter called The Gavel
events.body: Student government published a newsletter, The Gavel, whose first issue the archive dates October 1993. It ran beside the Word on Western radio show the congress named that same month. The archive holds a second issue filed under April 1994, though its catalogue description reads volume one, issue two, April 1992.

He required his own approval on all payments and reported expenditures and account balances to Congress: $308.06 in July 1993 and $5,467.56 in August, with the account standing at $38,977.50 on 12 October 1993, $16,839.28 on 22 March 1994 and $13,672.20 on 19 April 1994.

profile: Andrea Wilson served as SGA Secretary for 1993-94. She rewrote how legislation was filed, requiring it in by noon on Mondays on official forms or it would not be accepted, and she administered the constitutional rule sending members with five absences to Judicial Council.
She ran the end-of-year awards nominations and organized the 26 April 1994 banquet at the Kentucky Museum.

executive.name: Scott Sivley
executive.note: Announced the first reading of the constitutional revision for 7 September 1993, required every Congress member to serve on two committees, and ran the committee behind the 3 November 1993 rally against tuition increases. He ran the April 1994 primary, called the 19 April 1994 meeting to order, and the Herald reported him standing against Rob Evans for president in that election.
profile: Scott Sivley served as SGA Administrative Vice-President for 1993-94. He announced the first reading of a constitutional revision for 7 September 1993, required every Congress member to serve on two committees, and ran the committee behind the 3 November 1993 rally against tuition increases.

He ran the April 1994 primary and called the 19 April 1994 meeting to order. He was himself a candidate in that primary, and the Herald reported in its 14 April issue that he had not followed SGA and university procedures during the election; the paper closed the season a week later with "Rob Evans & Tara Higdon Ready to Lead Students."

profile: Running for president in April 1994, Evans was profiled by the Herald as the candidate who urged discussion of the issues. He faced Scott Sivley in a contested race; on election day, 19 April, the Herald reported Sivley had been warned by SGA for violating the organization's campaign policies, alongside an opinion piece urging a vote for "Rob Evans, Tara Higdon" and another arguing that "Sacrificing Student Government Association Means Saving Needed Programs." The same issue's editorial pages told students "The Choice Is Yours" in the SGA vote.
He won, and the Herald introduced the incoming leadership with "Rob Evans & Tara Higdon Ready to Lead Students." Higdon, elected alongside him, would succeed him as president a year later.

The SGA's 2001 list of presidents records Robert Evans of Owensboro as the 28th president, serving 1994-95, and marks him as having also served as student regent. The Board of Regents' quarterly meeting of 15 August 1994 swore him in alongside Joy Gramling and Cornelius Martin, and carried resolutions of appreciation for outgoing officers Donald Smith - his predecessor as SGA president and student regent - and Monnie Hankins. The Board's quarterly meeting of 22 September 1995 - the start of the following academic year - swore in Tara Higdon as his successor on the board, marking the end of his regency.

After his year leading the WKU student body, Rob Evans kept a statewide role: in April 1996 the Herald profiled him under the headline 'Rob Evans Representing Students from Across State,' describing his seat on the Kentucky Council on Higher Education, the body that then oversaw the state's public universities.

events.title: The 1994-95 budget passes
events.body: The SGA approved its budget for the year in early September, reported by the Herald under "Student Government Association Approves Budget for 1994-95."

events.title: Campus security shapes the spring campaign
events.body: The Herald reported that being stalked had influenced candidate Tara Higdon, putting campus security at the center of the spring election coverage.

events.title: A new beginning
events.body: The Herald's transition piece, "Tara Higdon Sees New Beginning," marked the handover from Robert Evans to his elected successor at the end of the academic year.

events.title: Expanded shuttle service draws attention
events.body: The Herald reported that expanded Big Red Shuttle bus service, a route the Student Government Association had pushed to extend, was drawing enthusiasm from local stores along its new stops.

events.title: An editorial defends the memorial trees
events.body: The same issue carried the opinion piece "Don't Destroy Trees," addressing the fate of the memorial trees the SGA had established the previous year to honor students who died while enrolled.

events.title: Evans defeats Sivley for the SGA presidency
events.body: Rob Evans faced Scott Sivley at the polls on election day; the Herald reported the same day that Sivley had been warned by SGA for violating the organization's campaign policies. Evans and running mate Tara Higdon won.

events.title: Security phone tops SGA's spring to-do list
events.body: The Herald reported a new security phone, a shuttle stop, and the memorial trees on the Student Government Association's agenda, under "New Security Phone, Shuttle Stop, Trees Lead to Student Government's To Do List." events.body: SGA's regular meeting took up the student escort service, a "President for a Day" promotion, a campus cleanup, and open positions on the body.

events.body: The Herald reported the spring election under the headline 'Tara Higdon Moves Up; Voting Down,' recording both the choice of the next president and a drop in voter participation. The election closed out the 1994-95 administration.

events.title: The Herald called visibility the key to SGA's success
events.body: As the year ended, the Herald ran an editorial package on the association, pairing a Stacy Curtis cartoon of student government in a glass box with the editorial 'Visibility Key to Student Government Association Success.' It was a summing-up of a year in which the paper pressed SGA to be seen doing its work.

events.body: SGA filed its list of representatives for the fall 1994 semester, part of the organization's routine paperwork under the Evans administration.

events.title: Bill 94-9-F establishes a series of public forums
events.body: Lena Sweeten's bill committed SGA to hold public forums at least three times a semester so students could raise concerns directly. It passed on second reading on 22 November 1994 and set the pattern for the forum programme SGA ran for the next decade.

events.title: Big Red Days and 500 red towels
events.body: Jason Young's Bill 94-10-F created Big Red Days, asking the whole student body to wear red on days Western played a men's or women's home basketball game. It directed SGA members to hand out 500 red towels costing $1.00 each at the games, and was written to revive the spirit of the E. A. Diddle era.

events.title: Two people show up for the campus clean-up

Flags recur in SGA's records through the decade, reappearing in the 1995-96 and 1996-97 minutes.

events.title: A non-circulating textbook library proposed
events.body: Resolution 94-18-F, dated 15 November 1994, asked the university to create a non-circulating textbook library so students could consult required texts without buying them. It sat alongside the book exchange the same administration had run in October.

events.title: Resolution 94-20-F sought to stop undergraduates grading papers
events.body: Resolution 94-20-F, dated 22 November 1994, asked that undergraduate teaching assistants be disallowed from grading papers and proctoring tests. It closed a fall session in which the congress also asked for faculty evaluations in both semesters, under Resolution 94-14-F of 8 November.

leaders.note: Plaque gives maiden name in parentheses - confirmed under Higdon. Named as SGA president for 1995-96 in Herald election coverage ("Tara Higdon Moves Up; Voting Down," 11 Apr 1995) and again as outgoing president in the 1996 succession coverage; the 1994-95 organization record independently names her as that year's Administrative Vice President, noting she would succeed Evans as president and student regent the following year.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Higdon's path to the presidency ran through the campus security debates of 1995. During the spring campaign the Herald reported that her experience of being stalked had influenced her, under the headline "Campus Security: Stalking Influenced Tara Higdon."

After a year as part of the elected leadership alongside Robert Evans, she won the presidency, and the Herald marked the transition with "Tara Higdon Sees New Beginning." Her term brought new emergency phones, a skywalk proposal, a campus store proposal and a push for longer visitation hours.
The SGA's 2001 list of presidents records Tara D. Higdon of Slaughters as the 29th president, serving 1995-96, and marks her as having also served as student regent.

Higdon won the presidency in April 1995, with the Herald reporting the result under the headline 'Tara Higdon Moves Up; Voting Down' - she moved up to the top office even as voter turnout fell. The paper's year-end editorial the following week argued that visibility would be the key to the association's success.

Her year ended in a contested, four-way race to succeed her, and Higdon took a public side: her letter 'Vote for Kristin Miller' ran in the Herald's April 16, 1996 issue, in the same election-week pages as the candidates' debate coverage and the campaign for SGA's constitutional amendments.

The spring of her term was the stormiest stretch in the association's decade of Herald coverage: within a single week in February 1996 the paper carried both SGA's skywalk proposal for the bottom of the Hill and a letter dismissing the association as a 'puppet' group, and by late April a columnist was asking whether students cared about student government at all.

events.title: Two more emergency phones
events.body: The year opened with a security win. The Herald reported that SGA had put two more emergency phones on campus, continuing the safety agenda that had shaped the previous spring's election.

events.title: A dress code, and a call for interest
events.body: September coverage included an SGA dress code and a piece headlined "Tara Higdon Seeks Student Interest in Group," as the new president worked to draw students into the organization.

events.title: Presidential pay compared
events.body: The Herald reported that pay for student government presidents was higher at other schools, an early airing of a compensation question that would recur in later decades.

events.title: The Herald pushes back
events.body: Five days after the skywalk proposal, the Herald ran a column telling SGA to "ditch the pie-in-the-sky idea," and its letters page carried Richard Malek's charge that the organization acted as a "puppet" group. Another letter, from Tracie Webb, defended officers Horace Johnson and Kristen Miller against the label "hair-brained." The episode set the combative tone of the spring semester.

events.title: Longer visitation hours
events.body: SGA asked the university for longer residence hall visitation hours, one of the quality-of-life requests that defined the organization's agenda that spring.

events.title: A student credited SGA for its trees
events.body: A Herald opinion piece ran under the headline 'Student Government Association Doing Good Job with Trees,' crediting the association's campus planting work. Trees and campus grounds were among the group's most visible projects that year.

events.title: Four candidates ran for the top office
events.body: The Herald reported that four students were running for SGA president. The campaign filled the opinion pages for the next three weeks, with endorsements, a debate and a proposed slate of constitutional amendments on the ballot.

events.title: A test-free week before finals
events.body: SGA proposed a test-free week before finals, one of the last legislative pushes of the year. The idea ran in the Herald alongside Board of Regents coverage of fee increases.

events.title: Debate, amendments and endorsements filled election week
events.body: The Herald covered the presidential debate under the headline 'Debate Reflects Attitudes,' while letters urged a yes vote on SGA's constitutional amendments. Outgoing officer Tara Higdon's letter backing Kristen Miller ran on the same pages.

events.title: New officers sworn in as a columnist shrugged
events.body: The Herald reported the swearing-in of SGA's new officers for 1996-97. A column in the same issue, 'Students Just Don't Care About Student Government Association,' summed up the year's running argument about relevance.

events.title: Student groups split up the SGA award
events.body: The Herald reported in November 1995 that campus organisations had divided an SGA award between them. The item is one of the few surviving traces of SGA's organisational funding in 1995-96.

src.label: Herald 71:20, 16 Nov 1995 - LaBelle, "Student Groups Split Up Student Government Association Award"

events.title: SGA proposed a pedestrian skywalk at the bottom of the Hill
events.body: SGA proposed a pedestrian skywalk at the bottom of the Hill. The same Herald issue of 8 February 1996 covered SGA's push to bring emergency phones to campus. The skywalk drew editorial fire and became the most argued-about SGA proposal of the spring.

events.title: SGA proposed a new store on campus
events.body: SGA proposed a new store on campus, the Herald reported, as the association kept producing campus improvement ideas through the spring. A week earlier the paper had covered SGA's wish that the next university president be promoted from within.

events.title: Tara Higdon's first meeting: a state conference and committee setup
events.body: The congress met on 29 August 1995 from 5.05 to 5.40 p.m. SGA's own record of the meeting describes business on the State Student Government Conference, elections and setting up committees, the first meeting of Tara Higdon's term held in the digitised minutes.

events.title: A voter registration drive, a pep rally and organizational aid
events.body: The meeting of 9 September 1995 took up a voter registration drive, a pep rally and organizational aid. It is the earliest record in this year of the three strands that made up most of SGA's public programme work: registering students to vote, backing athletics events and paying out money to campus clubs.

events.title: Bill 95-1-F tied organizational aid to showing up
events.body: Bill 95-1-F, dated 19 September 1995, required any organization receiving SGA aid to have a representative participating in SGA. It made attendance a condition of the money at a time when the Herald was reporting falling interest in the association.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 95-1-F, Organizational Aid Recipients on COA

events.title: Resolution 95-1-F asked for the running track to be replaced
events.body: Resolution 95-1-F, dated 19 September 1995, requested that the running track be replaced and widened. Track resurfacing had been an SGA request since Resolution 93-8-S, on resurfacing the Smith Stadium track, in 1993.

events.title: Weekend in the Woods
events.body: The meeting of 26 September 1995 discussed Weekend in the Woods, a code of conduct and open positions on the congress. The archive's record names the event but not its programme, so nothing is known here beyond that SGA had it in hand that autumn.

events.title: Homecoming, and members sent out to speak to classes
events.body: On 2 October 1995 the congress discussed homecoming, a plan for SGA members to speak to classes, and its open positions. Speaking to classes was the association's standing answer to the visibility problem the Herald returned to all year.

events.title: Midnight Mania, phone registration and a parliamentary workshop
events.body: The meeting of 10 October 1995 took up registration by telephone, a parliamentary procedure workshop for members, and Midnight Mania, the midnight start of basketball practice. The workshop ran again the following week.

events.title: Coach for a Game, a student leader reception and Topline
events.body: On 17 October 1995 the congress discussed Topline telephone registration, the parliamentary procedure workshop, the Coach for a Game contest and a student leader reception. Coach for a Game had been created by Bill 92-03-S in 1992 and was still running four years later.

events.title: Paving Creason lot, and a handrail
events.body: Two resolutions carry the date 17 October 1995. Resolution 95-3-F asked that the Creason parking lot be paved and Resolution 95-4-F requested a handrail by the Schneider Hall drive.

events.title: Faculty evaluations, a recycling plan and the New Level report
events.body: The meeting of 24 October 1995 discussed faculty evaluations, recommendations arising from the university's Moving to a New Level review, a recycling plan and a meeting with Dave Parrot. Faculty evaluations dominated the congress's autumn and ran into a missed deadline in November.

events.title: Discount cards, surveys and credit for hall assistants
events.body: On 31 October 1995 the congress discussed SGA surveys, discount cards and academic credit for residence hall assistants. A student discount card had been an SGA product since Bill 85-15-F a decade earlier.

events.title: Security cameras for the parking garage
events.body: Resolution 95-8-F, dated 7 November 1995, requested security cameras in the parking garage and the parking lots. It belongs to the run of campus-safety measures that began with the emergency phones of the previous spring and continued with the lighting resolution later that month.

events.title: Faculty evaluations, community service and door scanners
events.body: The meeting of 14 November 1995 ran from 5.00 to 5.50 p.m., the longest autumn meeting in the digitised minutes, and covered faculty evaluations, community service and door security scanners. Two days later the Herald reported that SGA would miss its deadline on the evaluations.

events.title: An academic service fee to cover add and drop costs
events.body: Resolution 95-9-F, dated 14 November 1995, asked for the creation of an academic service fee to cover the cost of adding and dropping classes. The Herald reported the following week that the congress would vote on the drop/add fee proposal.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Resolution 95-9-F, Establish an Academic Service Fee

events.title: SGA missed its deadline on faculty evaluations
events.body: The Herald of 16 November 1995 reported that the Student Government Association would miss its deadline for faculty evaluations, under Charbonee LaBelle's byline. Publishing evaluations had been SGA policy since Resolution 94-1-S and would still be an unfinished project when Amanda Coates revived it in 2000.

events.body: The Herald of 21 November 1995 reported that SGA would vote on a drop/add fee proposal. The proposal is Resolution 95-9-F of the previous week, which asked for an academic service fee to cover the cost of adding and dropping classes.

events.title: The spring opened with two contests and a reception for legislators
events.body: The first meeting of 1996, on 16 January, discussed emergency phones, a reception for state legislators, President for a Day and Coach for a Day. The legislators' reception recurs in the minutes of 23 January, 27 February and 5 March.

events.title: Healthy Loving Week and a Valentine's Day game show

events.body: The meeting of 30 January 1996 discussed changes in academic departments, the Russellville distance learning site and Bowl for Kids' Sake. The bowling fundraiser returned to SGA's agenda in November 1996 and again in January 1997.

events.body: The record of the 13 February 1996 meeting lists the search for a vice president for academic affairs, Healthy Loving Week, the President for a Day contest, vacancies, the budget, a newsletter, Coming Home and the University Boulevard skywalk.

events.title: Certificates for the president's and dean's lists
events.body: Resolution 96-4-S, dated 20 February 1996, asked that certificates be given to students who make the president's and dean's lists. Recognising high-achieving students had been an SGA project since Bill 91-7-S on presidential scholars.

events.title: Bill 96-2-S opened the constitution
events.body: Bill 96-2-S, dated 20 February 1996, requested changes in the SGA constitution. The amendments reached the ballot in April, when Herald letters urged students to approve them alongside the presidential vote.

events.body: The meeting of 5 March 1996 discussed Diddle Dollars, the legislative reception, WKU flags and a phonathon; the previous week's meeting of 27 February had covered Diddle Dollars, the legislator reception and open positions. profile: David Apple chaired the Academic Affairs Committee for two consecutive years, 1995-96 and 1996-97. In November 1995 he reported the committee had legislation up for first reading and was working on a measure about available internet hours for students.

By 1997-98 he sat on the Judicial Council. At the 21 April 1998 Congress meeting he announced the results of that spring's primary election from the floor: Brad Sweatt with 140 votes and Amy France with 95 advanced to the general election for Public Relations Director, ahead of Christoph Miller's 72.

officers.name: Darlene Lodmell
officers.note: Planned a forum on Career Services for January 1996 and was voted Committee Member of the Month on 14 November 1995.
profile: Darlene Lodmell and her sister Carlene were accepted onto Congress together as sophomore off-campus representatives in August 1995. Darlene chaired the Student Affairs Committee that year, planning a Career Services forum for January 1996, and Congress voted her Committee Member of the Month on 14 November 1995.

She served as secretary of Congress in 1996-97, signing that year's minutes and introducing a bulletin she called the Seconds, circulating important dates and the highlights of the previous meeting; she also set herself the goal of tracking legislation after Congress passed it. By 21 April 1998 she was serving on the Judicial Council.

officers.name: Carlene Lodmell
officers.note: Took the committee through the constitution in the spring and brought the resulting amendments to Congress as Bill 96-2-S, passed on second reading 5 March 1996 except for a proposed 2.5 GPA requirement for Congress members, which failed. Carlene and Darlene Lodmell were accepted onto Congress together as sophomore off-campus representatives in August 1995.
profile: Carlene Lodmell and her sister Darlene were accepted onto Congress together as sophomore off-campus representatives in August 1995. Carlene chaired the Legislative Research Committee that year, taking it through a review of the SGA constitution in the spring of 1996. The resulting amendments went to Congress as Bill 96-2-S and passed second reading on 5 March 1996, except for a proposed 2.5 GPA requirement for Congress members, which failed. Those amendments went before the student body that April; Shawna Whartenby, another Congress officer, urged a yes vote on them in a College Heights Herald piece printed 16 April 1996.

Lodmell was elected vice president for 1996-97, calling every Congress meeting of the year to order, running the residence hall elections and serving as the student member of the OAR board. She stood for president in the spring 1997 election and lost to Keith Coffman, who thanked her from the floor of Congress for running a good campaign.

officers.name: Steve Roadcap
officers.note: Worked on campus lighting through the autumn and wrote legislation in March 1996 about pay phones being removed from campus.
profile: Steve Roadcap chaired the Campus Improvements Committee in 1995-96, working on campus lighting through the autumn and writing legislation in March 1996 about removing pay phones from campus.

He was elected treasurer for 1996-97 and drew up that year's budget, cutting administrative costs while increasing organizational aid, the Glasgow campus budget, program funding and campus improvements; Congress rejected a motion to table the budget and approved it on 27 August 1996.

President Keith Coffman swore him in as Judicial Foreman on 9 September 1997, and Roadcap in turn swore in the new members of Congress, telling them the Judicial Council would be more involved than in previous years.

profile: Shawna Whartenby co-chaired the Public Relations Committee in 1995-96. She gathered more than 175 signatures on a petition for a bandstand on the south lawn of the Downing University Center, and Congress voted her Member of the Month for February 1996. That April she wrote in the College Heights Herald urging students to vote yes on the SGA constitutional amendments then on the ballot, a package the Legislative Research Committee under Carlene Lodmell had brought to Congress as Bill 96-2-S that March.

As Public Relations Director in 1996-97 she set the year's theme, recorded in the minutes as "SGA - Changing the Course of History At WKU!", ran publicity for the Provide-A-Ride service, and organized an AIDS Day banner with Student Health Services in December 1996.

leaders.name: Kristen Miller
leaders.note: Confirmed by Herald 71:54 (18 Apr 1996, election coverage headlined "It's Kristen Miller's Time") and Herald 72:46 (27 Mar 1997, term-end reflection piece), both naming her SGA president in the plaque year.

sources.label: Herald, 2 Feb 2016 - Ransdell retirement means search for new president
WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Miller had been a Herald columnist and an SGA officer before winning the presidency; her letters in the paper defending the organization date to 1994. In her first weeks as president in August 1996 she made a plan to drive party-goers home, the beginning of what became the Provide-A-Ride service.

As student body president she was the student representative on the committee searching for WKU's ninth president. Interviewed in 2016, she recalled serious talk of cutting football or academic programs, saying "there was one pot of money everyone was fighting over," and described how a late-arriving alumnus candidate named Gary Ransdell impressed the committee by pulling out a binder full of plans after his interview.

In March 1997 the Herald ran "Kristen Miller Reflects on Year as Student Government Association President" as her term wound down. The SGA's 2001 list of presidents records Kristen L. Miller of Louisville as the 30th president and marks her as having also served as student regent.

Miller won the SGA presidency in April 1996 at the end of a four-way race, with the Herald's news coverage declaring 'It's Kristen Miller's Time.' A week earlier the paper had profiled her campaign under the headline 'Kristen Miller Focuses on Experience in Student Government Association.'

Days into the fall semester, the Herald reported 'Kristen Miller Makes Plan to Drive Party-Goers Home.' The idea became Provide-a-Ride, the safe-ride program that appears in SGA's minutes throughout 1996-97 and was still being funded by the congress years later.

Near the end of her term, the Herald ran 'Kristen Miller Reflects on Year as Student Government Association President,' looking back on a year that included the creation of a Technology Committee, the Provide-a-Ride launch and SGA's narrow vote to back adding sexual orientation to Western's anti-discrimination policy.

events.title: A retreat opens the year
events.body: The Herald reported that an SGA retreat provided the opportunity for new discussion and legislation, setting the agenda for Kristen Miller's term before classes had fully begun.

events.title: A plan to drive party-goers home
events.body: The Herald reported "Kristen Miller Makes Plan to Drive Party-Goers Home," the earliest indexed coverage of the safe-ride idea that became Provide-A-Ride. The same issue reported SGA giving more money to campus clubs.

events.title: Thirty years of student government
events.body: The Herald's Homecoming edition carried Kim Leonard's feature "Student Government Association Has Grown in 30 Years," marking three decades since the Associated Students' founding in 1966.

events.title: Extending the shuttle route
events.body: SGA pushed to have the campus shuttle route extended, reported by the Herald in mid-November.

events.title: Provide-A-Ride needs support
events.body: The Herald reported that Provide-A-Ride needed SGA and student support to survive its first year. The service would outlast the doubts and still be running as a free weekend van service years later.

events.title: Legislation on the presidential search and the senior class campaign
events.body: On March 4, 1997, Resolution 97-4-S addressed the Presidential Search Committee as WKU sought a successor to Thomas Meredith, and Bill 97-3-S addressed a contribution to the WKU Senior Class Campaign.

events.title: Reaching beyond campus
events.body: In one April session the body took up Resolution 97-13-S to reactivate the Kentucky Students Association and Resolution 97-14-S to establish a student representative position on the Council for Postsecondary Education, both dated April 15, 1997, pushing WKU student interests into state-level policy.

events.title: Candidates prepare, and fire alarms get a deadline
events.body: The Herald covered candidates preparing for the spring elections alongside an SGA effort seeking faster shut-off times for fire alarms, a snapshot of the organization's mix of politics and practical fixes.

events.title: Officers sworn in at the first fall meeting
events.body: The August 27 meeting swore in officers and took up the retreat, an open house, the budget and homecoming. It opened the first full year of minutes in the digitised record since 1994.

events.title: SGA created a Technology Committee
events.body: The September 17 meeting created the SGA Technology Committee and discussed intramural facilities, photocopiers in dorms and Campus Clean Up. Student email accounts and other technology questions recur in the fall's minutes.

events.title: More lights proposed, and a veto recorded
events.body: The Herald reported SGA proposing more campus lighting while a resolution was vetoed. Campus lighting had been a steady SGA cause since the earlier emergency phones push.

events.title: SGA followed the presidential search
events.body: With Thomas Meredith's departure looming, the March 25 meeting discussed the university's presidential search along with an Orientation, Admissions and Registration Pal program, the Bridging the Gap forum and Campus Clean Up.

events.title: An anti-discrimination stand passed by a slim margin
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA passed a measure calling for gays to be included in Western's anti-discrimination policy by a slim margin, a week after covering the proposal's introduction. A letter in the same issue congratulated both SGA and the paper.

events.title: The year closed with a memorial tree dedication
events.body: The last recorded meeting of the year discussed the memorial tree dedication, elections, Earth Day, Thomas Meredith, Campus Clean Up, off-campus housing scholarships and a residence hall privatization study.

events.title: Few turn out for the election that chose Miller
events.body: The same Herald issue that declared "It's Kristen Miller's Time" also ran the headline "Few Turn Out for Election," continuing the decade's pattern of falling voter participation in SGA races.

events.title: Roller blades, skateboards, and a technology push
events.body: A September 24 meeting took up campus rules on roller blading and skateboards alongside Provide-A-Ride, a voter registration drive, a bonfire, Big Red Roar, the budget, and student email accounts.

events.title: Website, vacancies, and bylaws open the spring
events.body: The January 21 meeting discussed the organization's website, Provide-A-Ride, open vacancies on the body, the budget, and the by-laws, as the congress organized itself for the spring semester.

events.title: Keith Coffman took charge
events.body: The Herald announced the new administration with 'Keith Coffman Takes Charge,' and a companion piece reported the new president mapping his upcoming term. His term began as the spring semester closed.

events.title: Herald reports SGA giving students rides
events.body: The Herald of 23 January 1997 carried Matt Batcheldor's report that the Student Government Association was giving rides to students. The archive's index of the issue records the article's title and byline and nothing more about the service.

src.label: College Heights Herald 72:31, 23 Jan 1997 - Batcheldor, "Student Government Association Gives Rides to Students"

events.title: SGA favoured a housing idea
events.body: The Herald of 5 September 1996 carried Kim Leonard's report headlined "Student Government Association Favors Housing Idea." The same issue carried Jason Hall's report that Provide-A-Ride hinged on student involvement.

src.label: Herald 72:5, 5 Sep 1996 - Leonard, "Student Government Association Favors Housing Idea"

events.title: Intramural facilities, t-shirts and the budget
events.body: The meeting of 10 September 1996 discussed intramural facilities, the coming elections, t-shirts, the budget and campus improvements. Intramural facilities carried over into the following week's meeting.

events.title: Diddle Park dedication and Focus on Western
events.body: The meeting of 21 October 1996 took up online services, the dedication of Diddle Park, Focus on Western, homecoming, drug abuse, shuttle service and legislation. It falls in the week of the Herald's Homecoming edition, which carried a feature on thirty years of student government.

events.title: Organizational aid, the Hillraisers and the computer labs
events.body: On 29 October 1996 the congress discussed homecoming, dining services, the Hillraisers, campus lighting, the budget, computer labs, shuttle services and organizational aid. It is the only record of organizational aid being handled in Kristen Miller's autumn.

events.title: An AIDS lecture and the banquet
events.body: The meeting of 13 November 1996 covered a banquet, summer financial aid, flags, an AIDS lecture, the budget, computer labs and legislation. World AIDS Day appears again in the minutes of 19 and 23 November, so the lecture belongs to SGA's preparation for 1 December.

events.title: AIDS Day, Bowl for Kids Sake and designated drivers
events.body: On 19 November 1996 the congress discussed elections, Bowl for Kids Sake, Provide-a-Ride, AIDS Day, vacancies, the budget, campus lighting, designated drivers and the website. Designated driver cards were funded a year later by Bill 97-3-F.

events.title: The ride plan was announced to start
events.body: The Herald of 21 November 1996 announced that the ride plan was set to begin, under Kim Leonard's byline. This is the notice of Provide-a-Ride's start rather than a report of how it ran; the Herald's assessment came the following February.

src.label: Herald 72:26, 21 Nov 1996 - Leonard, "Ride Plan Set to Begin"

events.title: A Christmas banquet and a residence hall task force
events.body: The last meeting of 1996, on 3 December, covered Bowl for Kid's Sake, a Christmas banquet, meeting attendance, vacancies, the budget, a residence hall task force, the bylaws, Provide-a-Ride, a digital telephone book, counselling, housing refunds, housing contracts and check cashing.

events.title: A plan to put SGA meetings on television
events.body: The Herald of 16 January 1997 reported that SGA planned to broadcast its meetings on television, under Matt Batcheldor's byline. The plan belongs to the same push for visibility as the website discussed in the January minutes.

src.label: Herald 72:30, 16 Jan 1997 - Batcheldor, "Student Government Association Plans to Broadcast Meetings on TV"

events.title: Designated driver cards and the Poland Hall computer lab
events.body: The meeting of 28 January 1997 discussed the Poland Hall computer lab, campus lighting, Provide-a-Ride, Bowl for Kids Sake, the budget, diversity, designated driver cards and email accounts. Designated drivers had first reached the minutes the previous November.

events.title: A diversity forum, and an executive council that met the same night
events.body: On 4 February 1997 the congress discussed Provide-a-Ride, the Academic Council, Healthy Toppers, vacancies, the budget, the Drug Council, a diversity forum and bike racks. The Executive Council met an hour later on memorial trees, a Judicial Council vacancy and Coming Home.

events.title: Thomas Meredith accepted a job in Alabama
events.body: The Herald of 6 February 1997 reported that president Thomas Meredith had accepted a position in Alabama. His departure set off the presidential search that SGA followed through the spring, taking a seat on the search committee under Resolution 97-4-S.

src.label: Herald 72:35, 6 Feb 1997 - Stamper, "Thomas Meredith Accepts Alabama Position"

events.title: Provide-a-Ride got high marks
events.body: Two and a half months after the service began, the Herald reported it was getting high marks, under Matt Batcheldor's byline. The report came a fortnight after the same paper had written that the programme needed SGA and student support to survive.

src.label: Herald 72:36, 11 Feb 1997 - Batcheldor, "Provide-a-Ride Gets high Marks"

events.title: Child care grants return to the agenda
events.body: The meeting of 18 February 1997 covered Provide-a-Ride, Thomas Meredith, dead week, the budget, an NAACP meeting, the bylaws, fire alarm keys and child care grants. The grants stayed on the agenda through 25 February and 4 March.

events.title: A Crimestoppers breakfast and a charity lockup
events.body: The meeting of 4 March 1997 discussed a Crimestoppers breakfast, a muscular dystrophy association lockup, child care grants, the budget, faculty evaluations, the presidential search, parking lots and vacancies. The same day the congress passed Resolution 97-4-S on the presidential search committee.

events.title: Bridging the Gap, a senior class gift and the spring clean-up
events.body: On 11 March 1997 the congress discussed elections, banquets, the senior class gift, dining services, the budget, faculty evaluations, the Bridging the Gap forum, Campus Clean Up, Pearce-Ford Tower safety and fax machines. Resolution 97-5-S on installing two fax machines on campus carries the same date.

events.title: A job fair, and the state's student body presidents
events.body: The meeting of 1 April 1997 covered a memorial tree, the Kentucky student body presidents, the Bridging the Gap forum, the website, the budget, faculty evaluations, a job fair, Campus Clean Up, awards, fax machines and student seating at basketball games. Bill 97-4-S, funding two fax machines, carries the same date.

events.title: A student day at the baseball game
events.body: The meeting of 8 April 1997 discussed the memorial tree dedication, elections, a student day at a baseball game, vacancies, the budget, a drug programme, Campus Clean Up, student seating at basketball games and a request for an Easter holiday break. Resolution 97-12-S on the Easter break carries the same date.

events.title: Students called SGA elitist
events.body: Twelve days before the election the Herald ran Matt Batcheldor's report that students were questioning the association's "elitist attitude." It belongs to a run of complaints that year about how far SGA reached beyond its own membership.

src.label: Herald 72:50, 10 Apr 1997 - Batcheldor, "Students Question Student Government Association's Elitist Attitude, Concern"

executive.name: Ryan Faught
executive.note: Accepted by Congress as Coordinator of Committees on 21 January 1997, moving across from the Legislative Research chair.
profile: Ryan Faught chaired the Legislative Research Committee in the autumn of 1996. Giving his last remarks as chair on 21 January 1997, he told the bylaws committee that legislation could not be reviewed without its author present.
Congress accepted him as Coordinator of Committees the same day, 21 January 1997, moving him across from the Legislative Research chair.

executive.name: Shawna Whartenby
executive.note: Set the year's theme and announced it at the first meeting; the minutes record it as "SGA- Changing the Course of History At WKU!" She ran the Provide-A-Ride publicity and organised an AIDS Day banner with Student Health Services in December 1996.
profile: Shawna Whartenby co-chaired SGA's Public Relations Committee in 1995-96, gathering more than 175 signatures on a petition for a bandstand on the DUC south lawn and was voted Congress Member of the Month for February 1996. That April she wrote a Herald letter urging students to "Vote Yes on Student Government Association Ballot for Amendments," the constitutional amendments Carlene Lodmell's Legislative Research Committee had brought to a second reading the previous month.

She was named public relations director for 1996-97, setting the year's theme - recorded in the minutes as "SGA- Changing the Course of History At WKU!" - and announcing it at the first meeting. She ran the Provide-A-Ride publicity and organised an AIDS Day banner with Student Health Services in December 1996.

committees.name: Technology Committee
committees.note: Created at the 17 September 1996 meeting to take up student email accounts and other technology questions.

senate.note: Archive does not preserve a full senate officer list or seat count for this year.

officers.name: Jeff Yan
officers.note: Swore in the Congress members elected the previous spring at the opening meeting of 27 August 1996, and then swore in the newly approved members, after serving as vice president in 1995-96.
profile: Jeff Yan (also written Jeffery Yan in the minutes) was elected SGA vice president on 18 April 1995 and called every Congress meeting of 1995-96 to order. He designed the winning entry in SGA's Western flag contest, chosen by Congress on 14 November 1995.
In 1996-97 he moved to Judicial Council Foreman, swearing in the Congress members elected the previous spring at the opening meeting of 27 August 1996 and then swearing in newly approved members.

officers.name: Josh Detre
officers.note: Received one of the Public Relations awards handed out on 19 November 1996.
profile: Josh Detre served as parliamentarian in 1996-97 and received one of the Senate's Public Relations awards at the 19 November 1996 meeting.

officers.name: Chad Lewis
officers.note: Named with the parliamentarian as a Public Relations award winner on 19 November 1996.
profile: Chad Lewis was elected to Congress as a freshman council member in the fall of 1995. He served as Sergeant of Arms in 1996-97, and Congress named him, alongside the parliamentarian, a Public Relations award winner on 19 November 1996.

As treasurer in 1997-98 he presented a budget of $41,756 for approval in September 1997 and reported that November that expenditures to date stood at $11,150.68 against a balance of $30,605.32. In April 1998 the Herald covered his campaign for vice president as a contested race against Laura Hancock, under the headline "Race for Student Government Association Vice Presidency Heats Up." He was elected executive vice president for 1998-99.

As executive vice president he called Congress to order through the year in place of the president, and set goals of a spring turnout of 1,400 voters, every Congress seat filled, and a doubling of Provide-A-Ride use. By January 1999 he reported more than 100 people had used the ride service in the last week of the fall semester.

officers.name: David Apple
profile: Apple chaired the Academic Affairs Committee across two years running. By November 1995 he was reporting for the committee, which by then had passed from Terra Swanson's initial August appointment to him; on 14 November 1995 he reported legislation on internet hours. He continued as Academic Affairs chair into the following year, named again to the post at the SGA meeting of 27 August 1996.

In 1997-98 Apple sat on the Judicial Council instead. At the SGA meeting of 21 April 1998 he announced from the floor the results of that spring's primary election for Public Relations Director, reporting vote totals of Brad Sweatt 140, Amy France 95 and Christoph Miller 72, which sent Sweatt and France to the general election.

officers.name: Stephanie Cosby
officers.note: Met Charlie Wolfram of Facilities Management about campus lighting and recommended three pieces of legislation on it; Resolutions 96-5-F, 96-9-F and 96-10-F on lights near Gilbert, East and West Halls and the Diddle parking lot went to first reading on 19 November 1996. She was president two years later.

officers.name: Ryan Faught
officers.note: Chaired LRC in the autumn of 1996 and gave his last remarks as chair on 21 January 1997, telling the bylaws committee that legislation could not be reviewed without an author present.
profile: Ryan Faught chaired SGA's Legislative Research Committee in the autumn of 1996-97 and gave his last remarks as chair on 21 January 1997, telling the bylaws committee that legislation could not be reviewed without an author present. Congress accepted him as Coordinator of Committees the same day, moving him from the committee chairmanship into the cabinet.

officers.name: Andy Gailor
officers.note: Accepted by Congress as LRC chair on 21 January 1997; he also served as SGA's City Commission representative.
profile: Congress accepted Gailor as chair of the Legislative Research Committee on 21 January 1997; he also served as SGA's City Commission representative that year. He continued as Legislative Research chair into 1997-98, and on 18 November 1997 reported that the committee had reviewed eleven pieces of legislation that session, voting down Resolution 97-17-F for insufficient research and untabling Resolution 97-10-F.

officers.name: Leigh Ann Sears
officers.note: Ran the Designated Driver card scheme and the spring campus clean-up, and worked with treasurer Steve Roadcap on the gazebo project. Elected vice president for the following year.
profile: Leigh Ann Sears chaired the Campus Improvements Committee in 1996-97, running the Designated Driver card scheme and the spring campus clean-up, and working with treasurer Steve Roadcap on a gazebo project. She was elected vice president for the following year.

As vice president in 1997-98 she presided over Congress all year, ran the Weekend in the Woods retreat, and reported Provide-A-Ride ridership week by week, telling Congress on 18 November 1997 that 52 people had ridden the service the previous Thursday night. In April 1998 she announced that year's presidential debate and the dates of the general election.

officers.name: Heather Rogers
profile: Heather Rogers chaired the Public Relations Committee in 1996-97, and became Director of Public Relations the following year. In that post she revived SGA's old newsletter, The Gavel, set up a monthly SGA and University Center Board calendar in the College Heights Herald, and organized a blood drive in West Hall Cellar in December 1997; she asked every committee to file three goals for the spring.
She was named to the Judicial Council at the executive retreat in July 1998, moving into that role after her year running public relations.

officers.name: Kip Carr
officers.note: Chaired the new Technology Committee and the Bylaws Committee. He built SGA's web page, surveyed peak usage of the computer labs, and was voted Congress Member of the Month in November 1996; he had also filled in as acting secretary and typed the minutes the week before.
profile: Kip Carr chaired both the newly created Technology Committee and the Bylaws Committee in 1996-97. He built SGA's website, surveyed peak usage of the campus computer labs, and was voted Congress Member of the Month for November 1996; the week before, he had filled in as acting secretary and typed the minutes himself.
