documents.title: Congress minutes, August 27, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Carlene Lodmell called the year's first meeting to order and Judicial Council swore in the congress members elected the previous spring. After a motion to table the vote failed, congress adopted Treasurer Steve Roadcap's fall budget and confirmed Erin Schepman as Coordinator of Committees.
documents.extract: A motion to table the budget vote failed, and the budget passed.

documents.title: Congress minutes, September 3, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Kristen Miller opened an extended floor discussion on the university's requirement that freshmen and sophomores live on campus, and congress filled several open Sophomore and Junior Off-Campus seats by unanimous consent.
documents.extract: Miller asked congress's opinion on requiring freshmen and sophomores to live on campus.

documents.title: Congress minutes, September 10, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Congress confirmed Joshua Detre as Parliamentarian and Chad Lewis as Sergeant at Arms, and President Miller announced that Andy Gailor would represent WKU on the Bowling Green City Commission with a biweekly report back to congress.
documents.extract: Andrew Gailor will be representing Western Kentucky University on the Bowling Green City Commission.

documents.title: Congress minutes, September 17, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. On its first reading, congress suspended the bylaws and immediately passed Bill 96-2-F establishing an SGA Technology Committee, correcting several wording errors by floor amendment before the vote.
documents.extract: Establishing a SGA Technology Committee

documents.title: Congress minutes, September 24, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Congress passed Bill 96-1-F recommending SGA members obtain e-mail accounts. Rick Malek questioned how Judicial Council Foreman Jeff Van had been seated without a congress vote; the executive council explained it had approved him over the summer at the executive retreat, when congress was not in session.
documents.extract: The executive council had approved him over the summer without a congress vote.

documents.title: Congress minutes, October 1, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Vice President Lodmell reported 150 people registered at that week's Voter Registration Drive. Congress passed Resolution 96-1-F designating rollerblade and skateboard areas and Resolution 96-2-F on bike rack placement, and gave first reading to a resolution for parking-lot lighting.
documents.extract: 150 people turned out and registered

documents.title: Congress minutes, October 8, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller gave Kip Carr an award for compiling an official list of past presidents of Western's Student Government, and congress passed Resolution 96-3-F installing lights in the parking lots on second reading.
documents.extract: Kip Carr won an award for compiling an official list of past SGA presidents.

documents.title: Congress minutes, October 15, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Kip Carr delivered part one of his researched History of Western's SGA, covering 1966-1980, and congress passed Resolution 96-4-F on posting syllabi on second reading.
documents.extract: Kip Carr reported to congress the History of Western's SGA part one, 1966-1980

documents.title: Congress minutes, October 21, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller reported on a visit to the University of Kentucky's student senate and on the Board of Student Body Presidents meeting's discussion of an MSU-UK dispute. Congress confirmed Jason Cole as Student Affairs Vice Chair and gave first reading to Bill 96-6-F installing a television in Garrett.
documents.extract: she had the opportunity to sit in on one of their senate meetings

documents.title: Congress minutes, October 29, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Secretary Lodmell reported that Facilities Management could not fund the lighting congress had requested that fall but would consider it for the 1997-98 budget. Congress suspended the bylaws to pass Bill 96-7-F distributing $6,175 in Organizational Aid the same night, and a roll-call motion to reconsider Jason Cole's confirmation as Student Affairs Vice Chair failed 19-10.
documents.extract: the funding is not available, but they will consider it for the 97-98 budget

documents.title: Congress minutes, November 13, 1996
documents.summary: President Kristen Miller herself called the meeting to order, with both Vice President and Secretary Lodmell absent; Kip Carr served as Acting Secretary. Miller reported that the Board of Regents had adopted a strategic plan at its retreat that week, and congress unanimously passed Resolution 96-6-F for a 24-hour Poland Hall computer lab and Resolution 96-7-F for an Egypt-to-Thompson shuttle on second reading.
documents.extract: the Board adopted the strategic plan

documents.title: Congress minutes, November 19, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Congress amended the October 29 minutes to add the roll-call vote names Rick Malek had objected were missing, and agreed to move the following week's meeting to Saturday to accommodate a visiting Board of Student Body Presidents gathering. Three lighting resolutions for Gilbert, East and West Halls, and the Diddle parking lot got first reading.
documents.extract: Malek objected that the prior minutes omitted how members voted on a roll call.

documents.title: Congress minutes, November 23, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided over a Saturday meeting attended by visiting members of the statewide Board of Student Body Presidents. Congress passed three lighting resolutions, for Gilbert, East and West Halls, and the Diddle parking lot, and Kip Carr announced that his written History of SGA, covering 1966-1996, would be available in the SGA office the following week.
documents.extract: he had the written form of the History of SGA from 1966-1996

documents.title: Congress minutes, December 3, 1996
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided at the last meeting before the annual Christmas Banquet, held immediately afterward. Resolution 96-8-F on housing refunds passed 22-17 by roll-call vote after a wording amendment, and Bill 96-8-F establishing counseling groups and two more resolutions, on the housing agreement and check-cashing availability, also passed.
documents.extract: The Resolution passed with 22 yes and 17 no

documents.title: Congress minutes, January 21, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided at the first meeting of spring semester; President Miller was absent, attending the presidential inauguration. Congress confirmed Ryan Faught as Coordinator of Committees and Andy Gailor as the new Legislative Research Committee chair, succeeding Faught in that role.
documents.extract: Miller was unable to attend due to her attendance at the Presidential Inauguration

documents.title: Congress minutes, January 28, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller reported that the fall's legislation had produced results: Poland Hall's computer lab was now 24-hour and more campus lighting was being budgeted. Congress confirmed Erin Schepman as Judicial Council Foreman by a roll-call vote of 22 in favor, none opposed, and five abstaining.
documents.extract: Schepman was confirmed 22 in favor, none opposed, five abstaining.

documents.title: Executive Council minutes, February 4, 1997
documents.summary: The Executive Council met with all officers present. Members discussed the Memorial Tree Program, the vacant Judicial Council seat, the red towels to hand out at the Coming Home game, and delegated jobs for it to the officers. The document dates the game to 15 January, a date already past; Congress was told on 28 January that it would fall on 4 February, and on 11 February that it would be held on the 15th.
documents.extract: Various jobs were delegated to the officers

src.label: SGA Executive Council Minutes, February 4, 1997, TopSCHOLAR item 621

documents.title: Congress minutes, February 4, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller publicly defended the new Provide-A-Ride program after critical Herald coverage, and reported on committee heads' weekend trip to a conference in Lexington. Congress confirmed Jeff Oliver to the Judicial Council and gave first reading to Resolution 97-1-S on bike rack placement.
documents.extract: President Miller gave a response to the article about Provide-A-Ride in the Herald

documents.title: Executive Council minutes, February 11, 1997
documents.summary: The Executive Council met with all officers present. Kip Carr raised concerns about the Technology Committee, and members discussed candidates for the open Judicial Council seat and arranged for Coordinator of Committees Ryan Faught to meet with all committee heads.
documents.extract: Kip Carr shared with the Executive Council his concerns of the Technology Committee

src.label: SGA Executive Council Minutes, February 11, 1997, TopSCHOLAR item 620

documents.title: Congress minutes, February 11, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller announced that President Meredith was leaving WKU and that a search process was underway, and that SGA would give away a free parking spot at the Coming Home game. Congress selected Shawna Whartenby to represent SGA in the Mountain Laurel Pageant and gave first reading to Bill 97-1-S, a full revision of the By-Laws.
documents.extract: President Miller discussed the leaving of President Meredith

documents.title: Congress minutes, February 18, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. The Child Care Grant Committee voted unanimously to raise its per-family award from $1,000 to $1,500 after finding demand higher than expected. Congress voted 21-16 by roll call to table the By-Laws revision so the administration could review it, then suspended the bylaws to pass Bill 97-2-S naming Child Care Grant recipients the same night.
documents.extract: The Committee voted unanimously to increase from $1000 to $1500

documents.title: Congress minutes, February 25, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller reported that the Board of Regents was forming a search committee for a new university president and that she had dined with Governor Patton to discuss higher education funding. Congress limited debate to five minutes and, after a week on the table, passed the By-Laws revision, Bill 97-1-S.
documents.extract: a Search Committee for President is being formed

documents.title: Congress minutes, March 4, 1997
documents.summary: President Kristen Miller herself called the meeting to order, with both Carlene and Darlene Lodmell absent. Congress suspended the bylaws to pass Resolution 97-4-S, a Legislative Research Committee resolution on the Presidential Search Committee, and the Constitutional Committee reported it had rewritten the SGA constitution's preamble and reviewed Article I.
documents.extract: the committee sponsored the President's Search Committee Resolution

documents.title: Congress minutes, March 11, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller laid out the spring election calendar, filing March 27 through April 3, the primary April 15, the general election April 22, and the year-end banquet April 29, and announced the presidential search committee had hired the firm Lamalie Amrop to conduct its search for a new WKU president.
documents.extract: They selected Lamalie Amrop to conduct the search

documents.title: Congress minutes, March 25, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Congress adopted Judicial Council's proposed election procedures for the spring by a roll-call vote of 17 in favor, 6 against, and 3 abstaining, and gave first reading to Resolution 97-7-S adding sexual orientation to SGA's non-discrimination policy. Nominations opened for the year's end-of-year awards, including the Ego Downing and Citizen's Awards.
documents.extract: Congress adopted the election procedures 17 to 6, with three abstentions.

documents.title: Congress minutes, April 1, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller reported on a press conference in Frankfort with other Kentucky student body presidents and on the successful Bridging the Gap forum held with NAACP. Congress passed Resolution 97-6-S requiring faculty attendance at commencement by a 20-4 roll-call vote and Bill 97-4-S authorizing SGA to purchase two fax machines.
documents.extract: Miller reported on a press conference in Frankfort with other student body presidents.

documents.title: Congress minutes, April 8, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. President Miller announced the full slate for the spring officer election: Keith Coffman against Carlene Lodmell for President, David Apple against Leigh Ann Sears for Vice President, three candidates for Secretary, and Chad Lewis against Steve Roadcap for Treasurer, with Heather Rogers running unopposed for Public Relations Director. Congress passed Resolution 97-8-S on supervision of student basketball seating on second reading.
documents.extract: for President Keith Coffman is running against Carlene Lodmell

documents.title: Congress minutes, April 15, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided. Kip Carr raised concerns about the election process after Secretary candidate Matt Bastin was disqualified, which President Miller attributed to an oversight. Congress passed Resolution 97-7-S adding sexual orientation to SGA's non-discrimination policy by a close roll-call vote of 13 in favor, 12 against, and 3 abstaining.
documents.extract: The resolution passed by a close vote of 13 to 12.

documents.title: Congress minutes, April 22, 1997
documents.summary: Vice President Lodmell presided over the year's final regular meeting. President Miller announced the results of the spring election: Keith Coffman as President, Leigh Ann Sears as Vice President, Heather Rogers as Public Relations Director, Jamie Fite as Secretary, and Chad Lewis as Treasurer. Congress passed Resolution 97-11-S recommending a residence hall privatization study but voted down Resolution 97-13-S to reactivate the Kentucky Students Association.
documents.extract: President, Keith Coffman; Vice President, Leigh Ann Sears

leaders.name: Keith Coffman
leaders.note: Outgoing letters from this period cover the Dogwood Drive crosswalk and student seating at athletic events. Confirmed by Herald 72:54 (24 Apr 1997, "Keith Coffman Takes Charge") and the SGA's own 2001 presidents list naming him the 31st president, 1997-98.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Coffman presided over one of the busiest legislative years in the surviving 1990s record. The SGA's own legislation archive for 1997 preserves at least 24 numbered bills and resolutions from his fall semester alone, from the Dogwood Drive crosswalk to the ten-point grade scale, student e-mail addresses in the directory and ice machines in every residence hall.

The SGA's 2001 list of presidents records Keith Coffman of Russellville as the 31st president, serving 1997-98, and marks him as having also served as student regent. His term coincided with Gary Ransdell's first year as university president.

Coffman's presidency opened with the Herald's April 24, 1997 headline 'Keith Coffman Takes Charge,' paired with a story in the same issue in which the new Student Government Association president mapped out his upcoming term.

events.title: A crosswalk on Dogwood Drive
events.body: One of a run of outgoing letters in these years covering student seating at athletic events, ice machines in residence halls, campus safety, professors posting office hours, food court hours, housing scholarships for off-campus students and student health services.

events.title: More student seats at the games
events.body: SGA secretary Jamie Fite wrote to interim president Barbara Burch requesting additional student seating in Diddle Arena and Smith Stadium. The letter survives in the SGA records collection.

events.title: The ten-point scale fight begins
events.body: Resolution 97-6-F called for reinstatement of the ten-point grade scale, and Resolution 97-5-F addressed charitable organizations and solicitation of funds the same evening. The grading fight would run on for years at WKU.

events.title: A career fair for summer jobs
events.body: Bill 97-1-F addressed a Summer Job and Internship Career Fair, the first bill numbered in the fall 1997 legislative archive.

events.title: Designated driver cards
events.body: Bill 97-3-F allocated $900 of Campus Improvement funds to print designated driver cards, which entitled the designated driver to free soft drinks in place of alcohol. The bill argued that the scheme could prevent alcohol-related road accidents and recorded that restaurant and community support was already in place. It had its first reading on 4 November 1997 and passed on second reading a week later.

src.label: SGA Bill 97-3-F, Designated Driver Cards, 4 Nov 1997

events.title: Typewriters for the library
events.body: Bill 97-4-F addressed buying typewriters for the library. The legislative archive gives the bill's subject and date; whether it passed is not established here.

events.title: A November flood of resolutions
events.body: Between November 2 and 18 the legislative archive records at least fifteen numbered resolutions, covering a speed hump for the Regents Avenue lot, fifteen-minute parking spaces, working ID scanners, new sidewalks at Thompson and Grise, ice machines, soap and sanitary restrooms in residence halls, picnic tables, bicycle racks and recognition for honors graduates. It is one of the densest legislative months in the surviving 1990s record.

events.title: Housing stipends for off-campus students
events.body: Jamie Fite wrote to Academic Affairs Vice President Barbara Burch about applying housing stipends to off-campus housing, following up resolutions on the subject passed in both 1997 sessions.

events.title: Spring bills: watch signs and a teaching award
events.body: The spring session's surviving record includes Bill 98-4-S for Neighborhood Watch signs on April 19 and Bill 98-5-S creating an Excellence in Teaching Award on April 21.

events.title: A push for action on stalled legislation
events.body: As the term closed, secretary Jamie Fite wrote to Provost Barbara Burch requesting action on several pieces of legislation, pressing the administration to answer what the congress had passed.

events.title: Paper towels for the Downing University Center
events.body: Resolution 97-9-F asked that paper towels be placed in the restrooms of the Downing University Center. It is one of only two pieces of legislation from the year in the digitised SGA collection.

events.title: Picnic tables for the bottom of campus
events.body: Resolution 97-23-F requested picnic tables for the campus area near Zacharias Hall, Meredith Hall and Pearce-Ford Tower. Its numbering shows the congress had produced at least 23 fall resolutions by mid-November.

events.title: Coffman gets high marks as candidates line up
events.body: The Herald ran "Keith Coffman Served Students Well" alongside a People Poll asking students what they thought of his job performance, in the same issue that reported candidates preparing for the spring election.

events.title: A $15,000 electronic sign and a campaign for scholarships
events.body: In election week the Herald polled students on how they would spend $15,000 of SGA's money, ran a column arguing the money for a big electronic message sign could be better used, and printed dueling letters on whether the association served students. Its campaign coverage reported that candidate Stephanie Cosby wanted more scholarships.

events.title: Stephanie Cosby rolled to a huge victory
events.body: The Herald reported 'Stephanie Cosby Rolls to Huge Victory' in the SGA election that closed the year, alongside a story on how taxing election day was for officer candidates. Cosby would lead the association in 1998-99.

events.title: SGA buys a 20-foot tent for outdoor events
events.body: Bill 97-5-F authorised roughly $2,500 for a 20-by-20-foot tent for homecoming, tailgating and other outdoor events. The authors argued that one-day rentals started around $200 and that SGA could rent the tent cheaply to other student organisations to recover the cost.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 97-5-F, SGA to Purchase 20' Tent

events.title: Child care grants of $1,020 split among six students
events.body: Bill 98-1-S disbursed $1,020 in child care grants to six students in the WKU child care programme. The awards ran from $100 to $240 each and were set by the Child Care Grant Committee.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-1-S, Child Care Grant Recipients

events.title: Faculty Appreciation Day set for 23 April 1998
events.body: Bill 98-2-S declared 23 April 1998 Faculty Appreciation Day and committed SGA to a catered reception in the faculty's honour. It began an annual event SGA repeated every spring for the rest of the decade.

events.title: The first Meet Your Dean Reception, 7 April 1998
events.body: Bill 98-3-S sponsored a catered Meet Your Dean Reception on 7 April 1998 so students could meet the dean of their college. The authors noted that many students did not know who their dean was.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-3-S, Meet Your Dean Reception

events.title: Designated driver cards announced for distribution
events.body: The Herald of 17 February 1998 reported that the Student Government Association's designated driver cards would be distributed the following day. The archive holds the issue as a contents listing, which gives nothing about the scheme beyond the headline.

events.title: Gary Ransdell got the top job
events.body: The Herald of 11 September 1997 reported that Gary Ransdell had been chosen as Western's president, ending the search SGA had followed since February. The Board of Regents, on which the student regent sits, approved his contract on 4 November and he took office the following week.

src.label: Herald 73:6, 11 Sep 1997 - Back, "Gary Ransdell Gets Top Job"

events.title: Organizational Aid paid out $6,200 in Coffman's first autumn
events.body: Bill 97-2-F, dated 28 October 1997, disbursed $6,200 to a listed set of student organizations. The same sum was budgeted for Organizational Aid again the following autumn, when Bill 98-9-F split it among forty-one groups.

events.title: The Academic Council amended SGA's no-test proposal
events.body: The Herald of 28 October 1997 reported that the Academic Council had amended the no-test proposal, under Charlie Lanter's byline. The dead week campaign had been running since Resolution 96-2-S of 20 February 1996, which asked for a reading week before finals.

src.label: Herald 73:18, 28 Oct 1997 - Lanter, "Academic Council Amends No-Test Proposal"

events.title: Sober drivers got free drinks
events.body: The Herald of 13 November 1997 reported that sober drivers were getting free drinks, under Charlie Lanter's byline, nine days after Bill 97-3-F allocated $900 to print designated driver cards offering the driver free soft drinks. The archive holds the issue as a contents listing, so the report's own detail is not established here. The cards were announced for distribution the following February.

src.label: Herald 73:23, 13 Nov 1997 - Lanter, "Sober Drivers Get Free Drinks"

events.title: The Regents upheld the $5 student fee
events.body: The Herald of 3 February 1998 reported that the Board of Regents had upheld a $5 student fee, in coverage tying the decision to Detrex Field and the Student Government Association. The student regent sat on the board that took the vote.

src.label: Herald 73:32, 3 Feb 1998 - Felkins, "Regents Uphold $5 Student Fee"

executive.name: Leigh Ann Sears
executive.note: Elected 22 April 1997 and presided over Congress all year. She ran the Weekend in the Woods retreat and reported Provide-A-Ride ridership week by week, telling Congress on 18 November 1997 that 52 people had ridden the previous Thursday night. In April 1998 she announced the presidential debate and the dates of the general election.
profile: Leigh Ann Sears was elected vice president on 22 April 1997 and presided over Congress meetings throughout Keith Coffman's term. She organized the Weekend in the Woods retreat and gave Congress weekly ridership counts for the Provide-A-Ride van service, reporting on 18 November 1997 that 52 students had used it the previous Thursday night.
In April 1998 she announced the SGA presidential debate and set the dates of that spring's general election.

executive.name: Chad Lewis
executive.note: Presented a 1997-98 budget of $41,756 for approval in September 1997 and reported in November that expenditures to date were $11,150.68 against a balance of $30,605.32. Elected executive vice president for the following year.
profile: Chad Lewis served as treasurer under Keith Coffman, presenting a 1997-98 budget of $41,756 for Congress's approval in September 1997. By November he reported expenditures of $11,150.68 against a remaining balance of $30,605.32.
He was elected executive vice president for the following year.

src2.label: Herald 73:50, 16 Apr 1998

executive.name: Jamie Fite
executive.note: Signed outgoing SGA correspondence to the administration throughout the year, on athletic seating, housing stipends and stalled legislation.
profile: Jamie Fite served as secretary under Keith Coffman and signed SGA's outgoing correspondence to the university administration throughout the year, including letters pushing for more student seating at athletic events, housing stipends for off-campus students, and action on legislation that had stalled with the administration.

executive.name: Stephanie Cosby
executive.note: Convened the committee heads after each meeting, organised a secret santa for Congress in December 1997, and authored Resolution 97-20-F recognising honours graduates, which passed unanimously on 18 November 1997.
profile: Stephanie Cosby served as coordinator of committees under Keith Coffman. She convened the committee heads after each Congress meeting, organized a secret Santa exchange for Congress in December 1997, and authored Resolution 97-20-F recognizing honors graduates, which passed unanimously on 18 November 1997.

executive.name: Heather Rogers
executive.note: Revived SGA's old newsletter The Gavel, set up the monthly SGA and University Center Board calendar in the College Heights Herald, and organised the December 1997 blood drive in West Hall Cellar. She asked every committee to file three goals for the spring.
profile: Heather Rogers served as director of public relations under Keith Coffman. She revived SGA's newsletter, The Gavel, and arranged a monthly SGA and University Center Board calendar printed in the College Heights Herald. She organized a blood drive in West Hall Cellar in December 1997 and asked every Congress committee to file three goals for the spring semester.

senate.note: The archive preserves at least 24 numbered bills and resolutions from the fall 1997 session alone and a further spring 1998 session, but no full officer list or seat count survives beyond the president and secretary.

officers.name: Steve Roadcap
officers.note: Sworn in by President Coffman on 9 September 1997 and then swore in all new members of Congress, telling them the Judicial Council would be more involved than in previous years.

officers.name: Ryan Boyer
officers.note: Recorded as a guest of Congress with the other Judicial Council members at the meeting of 21 April 1998.
profile: Boyer is recorded as a guest of Congress alongside the other Judicial Council members at the meeting of 21 April 1998.

officers.name: David Apple
officers.note: Announced the results of the April 1998 primary election from the floor of Congress: Brad Sweatt 140 votes, Amy France 95, Christoph Miller 72, sending Sweatt and France to the general election for Public Relations Director.
profile: Apple chaired the Academic Affairs Committee across two years running. By November 1995 he was reporting for the committee, which by then had passed from Terra Swanson's initial August appointment to him; on 14 November 1995 he reported legislation on internet hours. He continued as Academic Affairs chair into the following year, named again to the post at the SGA meeting of 27 August 1996.

In 1997-98 Apple sat on the Judicial Council instead. At the SGA meeting of 21 April 1998 he announced from the floor the results of that spring's primary election for Public Relations Director, reporting vote totals of Brad Sweatt 140, Amy France 95 and Christoph Miller 72, which sent Sweatt and France to the general election.

officers.name: Darlene Lodmell
officers.note: Present as a Judicial Council member on 21 April 1998, after serving as secretary in 1996-97.

officers.name: Josh Detre
officers.note: Moved on 9 September 1997 that all candidates running unopposed be accepted by acclamation. He stood for president in spring 1998 and lost to Stephanie Cosby.
profile: Detre continued as parliamentarian in 1997-98, moving at the 9 September 1997 meeting that all candidates running unopposed be accepted by acclamation. He ran for the presidency himself in spring 1998, and the Herald profiled him on election day under the headline "Josh Detre Doesn't Fit Traditional Mold." Stephanie Cosby won the election.

src2.label: Herald 73:52, 28 Apr 1998

officers.name: Matt Bastin
officers.note: Took the dead week proposal to Academic Council and authored Resolution 97-15-F on announcing syllabi in the schedule bulletin, passed unanimously on 18 November 1997.

officers.name: Jason Cole
officers.note: Researched a career and job fair for the University and authored Resolution 97-12-F to extend ten-minute parking spaces to fifteen minutes, which Congress defeated 20-28 on 18 November 1997.
profile: Jason Cole chaired the Student Affairs Committee in 1997-98 and researched a proposed career and job fair for the university. He authored Resolution 97-12-F to extend campus parking spaces limited to ten minutes up to fifteen minutes; Congress defeated it 20-28 on 18 November 1997.

officers.name: Andy Gailor
officers.note: Reported on 18 November 1997 that LRC had reviewed eleven pieces of legislation, voting down Resolution 97-17-F for insufficient research and untabling Resolution 97-10-F.
profile: Congress accepted Gailor as chair of the Legislative Research Committee on 21 January 1997; he also served as SGA's City Commission representative that year. He continued as Legislative Research chair into 1997-98, and on 18 November 1997 reported that the committee had reviewed eleven pieces of legislation that session, voting down Resolution 97-17-F for insufficient research and untabling Resolution 97-10-F.

officers.name: Anne Guillory
officers.note: Chairing LRC by April 1998, having chaired the Constitutional Review subcommittee that drafted the new constitution. She also authored Resolution 98-16-S establishing a student mentor programme, passed unanimously on 21 April 1998.
profile: Anne Guillory chaired the Constitutional Review Committee, which spent 1997-98 revising SGA's constitution, and was chairing the Legislative Research Committee by April 1998. She authored Resolution 98-16-S, establishing a student mentor program, and argued for it on the ground that students find it easier to talk to their peers; Congress passed it unanimously on 21 April 1998.

officers.name: Anne Guillory
officers.note: Chaired the Legislative Research subcommittee set up to prepare a revised constitution for a student vote at the spring 1998 election. She reported on 18 November 1997 that the committee had reworked the draft with the Executive Council.

officers.name: Callie Varner
officers.note: Set the committee's goals as a more accessible campus for disabled students, finishing the Designated Driver cards and further work on the gazebo project.
profile: Callie Varner chaired the Campus Improvements Committee in 1997-98, setting the committee's goals as a more accessible campus for disabled students, finishing the Designated Driver card scheme, and continuing work on the gazebo project.

officers.name: Christoph Miller
officers.note: Vice-chair in November 1997 and chair by April 1998. He authored Resolutions 98-13-S on on-campus phones in Grise Hall and 98-18-S on maintaining lights on the sidewalk between DUC and Preston, both passed unanimously on 21 April 1998.

officers.name: Jenny Stith
officers.note: Authored Resolution 97-10-F applying housing scholarships to off-campus housing, which was discussed heavily, with voices raised on both sides, and passed 35-15 on 18 November 1997 after she spoke in its favour.
profile: Jenny Stith chaired the Public Relations Committee in 1997-98 and authored Resolution 97-10-F, extending housing scholarships to off-campus housing. The minutes record it as heavily discussed, with several voices in favour and several against, before Congress passed it 35-15 on 18 November 1997; she had spoken in its favour and taken questions from the floor.

officers.name: Jason Heflin
officers.note: Chaired the Hillraisers, an ad hoc committee created in 1997 to raise student turnout at athletic events, with free membership, t-shirts and prizes at games. The surname is also written Hefler in the 2 September 1997 minutes.
profile: Jason Heflin chaired the Hillraisers, an ad hoc committee created in 1997 to raise student turnout at athletic events with free membership, t-shirts and game-day prizes. The 2 September 1997 minutes also render his surname as Hefler.

leaders.name: Stephanie Cosby
leaders.note: Letters survive on ice machines in the residence halls, campus safety, food court hours and professors posting office hours. Confirmed as SGA president for 1998-99 by Herald election coverage ("Stephanie Cosby Rolls to Huge Victory," 30 Apr 1998) and by the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' fall 1998 dues letter addressed to her by name and title.

sources.label: WKU SGA, Former SGA Presidents roster, archived 24 Sep 2001

profile: Cosby is documented in office from the start of the 1998 fall semester, when the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents billed its dues in a memo addressed to "SGA president Stephanie Cosby." Her congress passed at least thirteen numbered bills that fall, from Murray State fire relief to Bookswap.com, and her officers answered public charges of unproductiveness with a written record of what had passed.
The SGA's 2001 list of presidents records Stephanie Cosby of Greenville as the 32nd president, serving 1998-99, and marks her as having also served as student regent.

Cosby campaigned on financial aid, with the Herald's election-week coverage reporting that she wanted more scholarships. She won the presidency in a rout: the paper's April 30, 1998 election story ran under the headline 'Stephanie Cosby Rolls to Huge Victory,' next to a report on how taxing election day had been for the officer candidates.

Midway through her term she picked up a second title, with the Herald reporting 'Stephanie Cosby Named Queen of Hill' at homecoming in October 1998. Her year in office produced a steady advising-reform push, the failed University Boulevard widening request, the Kappa Alpha aid fight, and ended with the Judicial Council overturning the election to choose her successor.

events.title: Dues to the state association
events.body: The treasurer of the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents wrote to president Stephanie Cosby requesting payment of the 1998-99 dues, evidence of WKU's continuing seat at the state student leadership table.

events.title: Relief funds for Murray State
events.body: Bill 98-2-F addressed allocation of funds to the Murray State University Fire Relief Fund on September 30, 1998, one of the rare occasions the body's legislation directed money off campus.

events.title: A coffee house for Pride Week and a Homecoming float
events.body: In a single October session the legislative record lists Bill 98-5-F for a coffee house for Pride Week and Bill 98-6-F for a joint SGA and Hillraiser Homecoming float, both dated October 20, 1998. The fall slate also included bills for a W.O.W. conference, ashtrays outside residence halls and an SGA survey.

events.title: An anonymous complaint about the room
events.body: An anonymous congress member wrote to the Executive Council about the tone and mood of SGA meetings. Mitchell Bailey issued a written response a week later, and both documents survive in the SGA records collection.

events.title: Betting on Bookswap.com
events.body: Bill 98-12-F addressed SGA sponsorship of Bookswap.com, an early attempt to use the web against textbook prices, and Bill 98-13-F, the next day, addressed funding for the 1999 Camp Fair -- the last item recorded in the fall 1998 legislative archive.

events.title: Answering the charge of doing nothing
events.body: Vice president Matthew Bastin circulated a memo of the fall's passed legislation to the SGA advisor, officers, committee heads and the Herald's editor, answering accusations that SGA had been unproductive. The list itself was the rebuttal.

events.title: Concerns about student health services
events.body: Vice president Matthew Bastin wrote to president Gary Ransdell expressing SGA's concerns about student health services, closing the year by taking a student welfare issue to the top of the administration.

events.title: Dorm sprinklers and an advisor checklist
events.body: The Herald reported SGA wanted sprinklers added in the dorms, while Bill 98-1-F created a checklist of questions for students to ask their advisors. Days earlier the paper had counted the association's legislative efforts trailing the previous year, and a letter in this issue accused it of wasting time and money.

events.title: SGA asked for a wider University Boulevard
events.body: Resolution 98-7-F requested that University Boulevard be widened and that a traffic island be added for pedestrians. The Herald reported the following week that the University Boulevard proposal had failed, but the advising checklist was approved and grew into a run of advising-reform legislation through the fall.

events.title: The SGA president was crowned homecoming queen
events.body: The Herald reported 'Stephanie Cosby Named Queen of Hill' at homecoming. SGA had its own stake in the festivities that fall, funding a joint homecoming float with the Hillraisers.

events.title: A bill to help the burned-out Kappa Alphas
events.body: Bill 98-10-F proposed allocating funds to the Kappa Alpha fraternity after its house burned. The proposal set off the sharpest fight of the fall.

events.title: The Kappa Alpha aid vote failed, loudly
events.body: The Herald reported some SGA members were upset after the group voted down aid to the fraternity, and a companion letter said SGA had 'abandoned' the Kappa Alphas. Letters defending and attacking the decision ran for the rest of the semester.

events.title: Turbulent elections declared complete
events.body: The Herald reported the spring elections finished under the headline 'Turbulent Elections Complete,' while an opinion piece charged that SGA offered no leadership and a letter questioned the probe of candidate Will Jones. The turbulence was not over.

events.title: The Judicial Council overturned the election
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA's Judicial Council overturned the spring election, with coverage centering on candidate Joe Matheis, an editorial cartoon on nasty campaigns, and an opinion piece describing a 'swath of scandal' around the elections.

events.title: A final rush of legislation amid the election mess
events.body: Two days later the Herald reported SGA passing a final rush of legislation, while the election fallout continued in the letters column and a story urged students to vote again on Monday. The same issue introduced the incoming president as a self-described workaholic.

events.title: Recount narrows Coates and Martin's win to three votes
events.body: Amanda Coates and running mate Cassie Martin initially led Will Jones and Kara Yeckering 616-611 for president and vice president; after the Coates-Martin ticket asked for a recount to be sure of the win, the recount that night found an even closer margin, 614-611. A write-in ticket of Dwight Campbell and Kerri Richardson finished third with 145 votes. Total turnout was 1,436 students.

events.title: Griffey and Bastin win the remaining executive seats
events.body: Brandon Griffey defeated Amanda Kirby 729-652 for vice president of administration, and Matt Bastin defeated Duan Wright 806-570 for vice president of public relations, completing the 1999-2000 executive slate.

events.title: $300 to the second Women of Western Conference
events.body: Bill 98-4-F contributed $300 to the second annual Women of Western (W.O.W.) Conference. The conference paired a keynote address with workshops on women's issues, leadership and communication, presented in part by WKU faculty and staff.

events.title: Bill 98-5-F sets the Pride Week coffee house for 5 November
events.body: Bill 98-5-F funded a coffee house co-sponsored with the African-American Players, scheduling it for Thursday 5 November 1998 at 9.30 p.m. in Niteclass. The bill described it as a place for students to share their creative talents and as the academic component of Pride Week. The bill is the plan for the evening; no report of how it went has been found.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-5-F, Coffee House for Pride Week

events.title: SGA co-sponsors the 1999 Camp Fair
events.body: Bill 98-13-F committed SGA to co-sponsor the 1999 Camp Fair with the Career Services Center on 4 February 1999 in Downing University Center. Over 100 companies were to be invited, and the bill noted that the previous year's fair had drawn positive comment from employers and students.

events.title: Faculty Appreciation Day and the Excellence in Teaching Award
events.body: Bill 99-1-S set 11 March 1999 as Faculty Appreciation Day with a catered reception at the Faculty House at 4 p.m. The reception was chosen as the occasion to present the Teacher Excellence Award to the outstanding faculty member of the year.

events.title: Excellence in Teaching Award opened to all six colleges
events.body: Bill 99-4-S built a nomination procedure around the existing Excellence in Teaching Award so that one faculty member in each of WKU's six colleges could be honoured. Students nominated a professor on a form due in the SGA office by 4 p.m. on 1 March 1999, and the awards were presented at the 11 March reception.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-4-S, Excellence in Teaching Award Implementation

events.title: Child care grants of $996 split six ways
events.body: Bill 99-15-S disbursed $996 in child care grants, giving $166 each to six students in the WKU child care programme. The committee decided the awards with a representative of WKU Child Care.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-15-S, Child Care Grant Recipient

events.title: $300 toward the KASWE conference on campus
events.body: Bill 99-12-S contributed $300 to the WKU Student Social Workers Organization to help host the Kentucky Association of Social Work Educators conference on 8 and 9 April 1999. Its theme was "Strength through Diversity" and it drew registrants from universities and community agencies across the state.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-12-S, Allotment of Funds for KASWE Conference

events.title: A co-ed volleyball tournament before finals
events.body: Bill 99-19-S allocated up to $350 for a co-ed volleyball tournament on 22 and 23 April 1999. The authors wanted a recreational event to bring students together in the run-up to finals.

events.title: The electronic sign money is turned into a stage
events.body: Bill 99-18-S reallocated the funds set aside under Bill 98-4-S for an electronic display board, having found the sign badly underestimated, and put them toward a stage for the south lawn of Downing University Center. The bill argued the stage would carry tailgates, band concerts and other outdoor events.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-18-S, Reallocation for Downing University Center South Lawn Stage

events.title: A coffee house in Helm Library for finals week
events.body: Bill 99-21-S sponsored a coffee house in the Helm Library student lounge during finals week, as an incentive to use the library and a place to take a study break. It passed on 20 April 1999.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-21-S, Sponsoring of Finals Coffee House

events.title: Library hours pushed to 2 a.m. for finals
events.body: Bill 99-20-S committed SGA to work with the university to keep Helm-Cravens open until 2 a.m. from 3 to 6 May 1999. It passed on 20 April 1999.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-20-S, Extending Library Hours During Finals Week

events.title: A candidate promises the Dave Matthews Band
events.body: Amanda Coates campaigned for the SGA presidency in April 1999 on a pledge to bring a major act to the Hill, with the Dave Matthews Band named in her Herald column. The archive records the promise; it records no booking.

src.label: Herald 74:47, 13 Apr 1999 - Coates, "Dave Matthews Band Could Come to Hill"

events.title: Organizational Aid pays out $6,200 to 41 groups
events.body: Bill 98-9-F divided the $6,200 budgeted for Organizational Aid among 41 student organisations, a list the committee settled in two meetings running to over six hours. Awards ran from a floor of $100 to the Residence Hall Association's $205, and reached groups from Free the Planet to the Jewish Student Organization.

src.label: SGA Bill 98-9-F, Organizational Aid Recipients, 27 Oct 1998 (TopSCHOLAR)

events.title: A homecoming float committee was created
events.body: Bill 98-3-F, dated 6 October 1998, created a homecoming float committee. Two weeks later Bill 98-6-F funded the joint SGA and Hillraiser float itself.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-3-F, Creation of Homecoming Float Committee

events.title: Thirty ashtrays for the campus
events.body: Bill 98-7-F, dated 23 October 1998, authorised SGA to buy thirty ashtrays for campus. Cigarette receptacles had been an SGA request since Resolution 93-3-F on sand barrels five years earlier.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 98-7-F, Placing Ashtrays Outside Residence Halls & Campus Buildings

events.title: A weekend activities survey
events.body: Bill 98-8-F, dated 26 October 1998, provided for a survey of weekend activities. The congress was under public pressure that autumn over what it did, and answered the charge directly in the Herald in December.

events.title: Orientation made mandatory for new members
events.body: Bill 98-11-F, dated 30 November 1998, proposed mandatory SGA orientation for incoming members. It was filed in the same week as the Bookswap.com sponsorship and the 1999 Camp Fair funding.

events.title: An open forum for students
events.body: Bill 99-5-S, dated 16 February 1999, provided for an open forum for students. Public forums had been SGA business since Bill 94-9-F established a series of them in 1994.

events.title: SGA officers written onto the University Center Board
events.body: Bill 99-13-S, dated 23 March 1999, amended the SGA constitution to make officers representatives on the University Center Board, the body that programmed campus entertainment. It passed in the same session as the child care grants and the KASWE conference funding.

src.label: TopSCHOLAR - Bill 99-13-S, SGA Representatives to University Center Board

events.title: The Herald reported SGA bending its election rules
events.body: The Herald of 6 April 1999 reported that SGA had bent its election rules, under Ryan Clark's byline. The disputed spring election ran on through a recount and a Judicial Council ruling that overturned the result later that month.

src.label: Herald 74:48, 6 Apr 1999 - Clark, "Student Government Association Bends Election Rules"

events.title: Congress ordered its own legislation filed in the library
events.body: Resolution 99-2-S, Legislation to be Filed at Helm Library, is dated 16 February 1999. It called for a set of SGA resolutions to be kept on file at Helm Library.

events.title: A constitutional amendment bill in the spring session
events.body: Bill 99-7-S, amending the SGA constitution, is dated 2 March 1999 in the legislative archive. The text was not retrievable, so what it changed and whether it passed is not established here.

events.title: Congress legislated on eligibility for its own seats
events.body: Bill 99-16-S, Congressional Eligibility Requirements, is dated 30 March 1999 in the legislative archive; its own description says it amended the constitution's Judicial Council requirements. The text was not retrievable, so its full content and whether it passed are not established here.

events.title: A voided vice president of finance race was re-run
events.body: The Herald reported on 27 April 1999 that Ryan Morrison had won a Student Government Association election. This followed the Judicial Council's 20 April decision overturning an election tied to candidate Joe Matheis, whom the Council had already questioned in an article printed 13 April. No source found independently names the office Morrison and Matheis contested; this repository's own research file identifies it as vice president of finance, but that specific claim is not otherwise sourced.

src.label: Herald 74:54, 27 Apr 1999, "Ryan Morrison Wins Student Government Association Election"; repository file .research/fillins-1985-2000.json

events.title: The Judicial Council questioned Joe Matheis
events.body: Two days before the general election the Herald reported the Judicial Council questioning candidate Joe Matheis, under a Ryan Clark and Dan Hieb byline.

executive.note: Of Greenville; also served as student regent.

executive.name: Chad Lewis
executive.note: Called Congress to order through the year in place of the president. He set himself goals of a spring turnout of 1,400 voters, every Congress seat filled and a doubling of Provide-A-Ride use, and reported in January 1999 that more than 100 people had used the ride service in the last week of the autumn semester.
profile: As executive vice president under Stephanie Cosby in 1998-99, Chad Lewis called Congress to order in the president's absence throughout the year. He set goals of turning out 1,400 voters in the spring election, filling every Congress seat, and doubling use of the Provide-A-Ride service, and reported in January 1999 that more than 100 students had used the ride service in the final week of the fall semester.

executive.name: Matthew D. Bastin
executive.note: Signed the minutes all year as vice president of administration, called the roll, read Resolution 98-1-F on a Normal Drive crosswalk for first reading, and set the spring 1999 election calendar. He co-authored Bill 98-10-F, the failed grant to Kappa Alpha after its house fire, circulated the fall 1998 legislative record to answer charges of unproductiveness, and wrote to president Gary Ransdell on student health services in April 1999. This archive recorded him for a time only as Vice President; the minutes give the fuller title.

executive.name: Carleton Ruminer
executive.note: Presented the 1998-99 budget to Congress on 1 September 1998 against a balance of $41,783, and reported weekly through the autumn. His goals for the year included extending library hours and creating a book exchange. The surname appears as Rumenier and Rumienier in the 1997 minutes.
profile: Carleton Ruminer served as vice president of finance under Stephanie Cosby, presenting the 1998-99 budget to Congress on 1 September 1998 against a balance of $41,783 and reporting on it weekly through the fall semester. His stated goals for the year included extending library hours and creating a book exchange. His surname appears as Rumenier and Rumienier in SGA's 1997 minutes.

executive.name: Ryan Morrison
executive.note: Giving the finance report by 13 April 1999, having begun the year as Chief Justice. He reported a balance of $15,276.24 that week. He won a re-run election for vice president of finance for 1999-2000 a fortnight later, on 26 April 1999, after the initial 15 April result was voided.
profile: Ryan Morrison began 1998-99 as chief justice of the Judicial Council. By 13 April 1999 he was serving as vice president of finance, reporting a balance of $15,276.24 to Congress that week.
A fortnight later he won a 26 April 1999 re-run election for vice president of finance for 1999-2000, after the initial 15 April result was voided.

executive.note: Appointed at the July 1998 executive retreat and introduced himself to Congress at the first meeting of the year.
profile: Christoph Miller was appointed coordinator of committees at the executive retreat in July 1998 and introduced himself to Congress at its first meeting of the year, on 1 September 1998.

profile: Amanda Cole was appointed historian at the executive retreat in July 1998. She also chaired the Public Relations Committee from the start of the year and set the theme for the 1999 Coming Home celebration, "Mardi Gras on the Hill."

profile: Brad Sweatt was elected vice president of public relations in the spring 1998 general election, after leading the primary with 140 votes. He launched SGA's new web page, crediting Jeff Baynham as its designer, and read Congress's theme for the year at its first meeting of 1998-99.

profile: Cassie Martin introduced herself to Congress as the new vice president of public relations on 19 January 1999. She took over the Coming Home and Bowl for Kid's Sake events and handled SGA's advertising in the College Heights Herald.

senate.note: Congress numbered its fall 1998 legislation sequentially, at least 98-1-F through 98-13-F, covering everything from an advisor checklist to Murray State fire relief; no full senate officer list, committee structure, or seat count survives beyond the executive officers named in the record.

officers.name: Ryan Morrison
officers.note: Sworn in by President Cosby at the first meeting of 1 September 1998, then swore in all committee chairs, appointed officers and class and dorm representatives. He was still swearing in new members on 19 January 1999.

officers.name: Jeff Baynham

profile: Jeff Baynham was appointed parliamentarian at SGA's executive retreat in July 1998. He designed the organization's new web page, for which the vice president of public relations thanked him at Congress's first meeting of the year.

officers.name: Leslie Bedo
officers.note: Called the Congress meeting of 13 April 1999 to order while the president and executive vice president were counting election ballots.

officers.name: Joe Murrell
officers.note: Appointed at the July 1998 executive retreat. A Joe Morel moves the adjournment in the January and April 1999 minutes; the spellings are not reconciled in the record.
profile: Joe Murrell was appointed sergeant of arms at SGA's executive retreat in July 1998. The Congress minutes of January and April 1999 record a "Joe Morel" moving to adjourn the meeting; the spelling is not reconciled with his in the record.

officers.name: Mitchell Bailey
officers.note: A correction: the archive lists him among the executive officers with an unstated title. The minutes of 17 November 1998 describe him as the Pearce-Ford Tower representative, addressing Congress with remarks attached to the minutes; he held no executive office that the minutes record.
profile: Mitchell Bailey represented Pearce-Ford Tower in SGA's Congress for 1998-99. The archive's two sources on him disagree on his role: one credits him with issuing the Executive Council's written response to an anonymous Congress member's complaint about the tone of SGA meetings in November 1998, while the Congress minutes of 17 November 1998 record him only as the Pearce-Ford Tower representative, addressing Congress with remarks attached to the minutes, and note he held no executive office. Both describe the same November 1998 episode over the complaint about meeting tone.

officers.name: Larry Murphy
officers.note: Co-authored Bill 98-10-F allocating $250 to the Kappa Alpha Order fraternity after its house burned on 17 November 1998; the bill failed on second reading on 1 December. He reported that the teacher block resolution had been shelved because Dr Barbara Burch had already implemented it.
profile: Larry Murphy chaired SGA's Academic Affairs Committee in 1998-99. He co-authored Bill 98-10-F, which would have allocated $250 to the Kappa Alpha Order fraternity after its house burned on 17 November 1998; the bill failed on its second reading on 1 December. He also reported to Congress that a proposed teacher block-scheduling resolution had been shelved because Dr Barbara Burch had already put the change in place.

officers.name: Dwight Campbell
officers.note: Recommended Resolution 98-15-F on publishing the SGA advisor checklist in the schedule bulletins, and postponed Resolution 98-11-F on teacher education indefinitely. He co-authored Resolution 98-7-F with President Cosby on widening University Boulevard, which failed on 13 October 1998, and authored Resolution 99-3-S releasing the Student Health Service reserve fund, which passed on 13 April 1999.

officers.name: Tim Hatton
officers.note: Ran the spring 1999 camp fair, worked on a weekend survey and a proposed SGA scholarship, and authored Bill 99-20-S to extend library hours during finals week, postponed on 13 April 1999 over the cost of student workers' overtime.
profile: Tim Hatton chaired SGA's Student Affairs Committee in 1998-99. He ran the spring 1999 camp fair, worked on a weekend student survey and a proposed SGA scholarship, and authored Bill 99-20-S to extend library hours during finals week; Congress postponed the bill on 13 April 1999 over the cost of paying student workers overtime.

leaders.name: Amanda Coates
leaders.note: The plaque reads "Amanda Lich". No source from her SGA year uses that surname; the Herald has her winning the presidency in a recount on 15 April 1999, covers her as president through the autumn, and ran her year-end reflection on 25 April 2000, all as Amanda Coates. The two names are now confirmed as one person, from two sittings of the Kentucky Council on Postsecondary Education: its minutes of 13 November 2000 introduce the incoming holder of the council's statewide student seat as Amanda Coates, "a graduate of Western Kentucky University", and its minutes of 30 July 2001, recording Governor Patton's appointment of her successor, name the outgoing member "Amanda Coates Lich." The first carries the Coates of Western into the seat and the second carries the surname Lich out of it. This site does not otherwise report what became of her after her SGA service, in keeping with its rule against publishing a living person's post-office life absent a source tying it directly to that service or a notable public career.

profile: Contemporaneous records give her name as Amanda J. Coates. The SGA's own 2001 list of presidents records Amanda J. Coates of Brownsville as the 33rd president, serving 1999-2000, and marks her as having also served as student regent. The organization's website during and just after her term consistently refers to "President Amanda Coates."

She won the presidency in a contested April 1999 race against Will Jones, in results so close the Coates-Martin ticket demanded a recount: the initial 616-611 tally over Jones and running mate Kara Yeckering narrowed to 614-611 on the recount. A write-in ticket, Dwight Campbell and Kerri Richardson, took 145 votes. The same election saw a bitter down-ballot fight for vice president of finance, where Joe Matheis beat Ryan Morrison 700-688 only after SGA's judicial council reviewed - and let stand - his victory over a campaign-flier violation, and a Herald letter to the editor questioned SGA's handling of an investigation into racially charged fliers that had targeted Jones, the first Black SGA presidential candidate in years. The Herald's pre-election issue had separately reported SGA questioning an election-eve pizza party Jones held, and a debate over dropping the rule requiring a year of SGA service before running for office.

Her signature project was publishing faculty evaluations. From February 2000 she led meetings with the university president, the Faculty Senate chair and the senate's executive committee, and in April she co-authored Resolution 00-2-S with Adam Howard asking the Faculty Senate to approve a mandatory published evaluation beginning that fall.

At the end of her term the SGA website opened with the words "What SGA has done for you," showcasing three things: the faculty evaluations project, the fight over the Vice President of Student Affairs position and the Provide-A-Ride service. It is as close to a self-written record of her administration's priorities as survives.

As her term closed, the Herald ran an exit interview, "Amanda Coates Reflects on Year as President," in its April 25, 2000 issue. The election to succeed her, held in late March 2000, was contested between Cassie Martin and Duan Wright; Martin won, and by the following issue the Herald was asking the incoming president to "stand up on tough issues" while confirming that the faculty evaluations Coates had championed would be conducted and published starting that fall.

The Herald introduced the incoming 1999-2000 president on April 22, 1999 under the headline 'New Student Government Association Leader Workaholic.' The paper's index records the new leader's name as Amanda Coates, and she took office in the aftermath of a spring election that SGA's Judicial Council had overturned two days earlier.

Her congress spent the fall of 1999 building institutions: it created an Information Technology Director and website guidelines, established a senior awards banquet and hall of distinguished seniors, launched the toll-free Topline activity line, and publicly opposed an administrative move in Student Affairs while asking that Vice President Jerry Wilder be retained.

Her public service continued past her SGA year at the state level. Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education carries a statewide student member, and the council's minutes of 13 November 2000 record a district judge swearing her in, introducing her as Amanda Coates, a graduate of Western Kentucky University then studying public policy at the University of Kentucky. The council's minutes of 30 July 2001 record Governor Paul Patton appointing Christopher J. Pace to replace the outgoing student member, named there as "Amanda Coates Lich." Those two records together are what tie the Coates who led WKU's SGA in 1999-2000 to the surname the SGA Chambers plaque uses for the same year.

events.title: Jones and Coates square off amid a pizza-party dispute
events.body: The Herald's pre-election issue covered the presidential race between Will Jones and Amanda Coates, alongside a report that SGA was questioning an election-eve pizza party Jones had held, a debate over eliminating the rule requiring a year of SGA experience to run for office, and a heated treasurer's race between Ryan Morrison and Joe Matheis.

events.title: A turbulent election puts Amanda Coates in office
events.body: The Herald's coverage of the spring SGA election was headlined "Turbulent Elections Complete"; the same issue carried an opinion piece, "Student Government Association Offers No Leadership," challenging the incoming administration to prove itself.

events.title: Students vote for R&B acts
events.body: SGA ran a student vote on Rhythm & Blues concert programming for campus, reported by the Herald under "Students Vote for R&B."

events.title: Keep our voice: a rally at Wetherby
events.body: About fifty students gathered outside the Wetherby Administration Building to urge the university to retain both the Vice President of Student Affairs and the Dean of Student Life positions, chanting "It's not your choice. Keep our voice." The SGA's own account said president Ransdell appreciated how the students conducted themselves and would keep an open mind.

src.label: WKU SGA site, V.P. of Student Affairs Update (archived 2000)

events.title: Provide-A-Ride in full operation
events.body: During this year SGA ran Provide-A-Ride as a free service giving safe and sober rides anywhere in the Bowling Green and campus area on Thursday and Friday nights from 11 p.m. to 2 a.m. A fifteen-passenger blue van answered calls within about fifteen minutes, and all a rider needed was a valid Western ID.

events.title: The faculty evaluations campaign opens
events.body: President Amanda Coates opened a campaign to publish faculty evaluations as a tool for students choosing professors, starting with a February 22 meeting with the university president and the Faculty Senate chair. The SGA published a step-by-step timeline running through a March 23 presentation to the full Faculty Senate, saying it did not want to win the tool at the expense of unnecessarily upsetting faculty.

events.title: Resolution 00-2-S: publish the evaluations
events.body: Resolution 00-2-S, authored by Amanda J. Coates and Adam Howard and sponsored by the Legislative Research Committee, asked the Faculty Senate to approve a mandatory SGA-sponsored faculty evaluation to be published beginning in fall 2000. Its attached questionnaire asked practical questions such as whether an instructor takes attendance, offers extra credit or gives comprehensive finals.

events.title: Martin and Wright battle to succeed Coates
events.body: The Herald reported that Cassie Martin and Duan Wright were competing to succeed Amanda Coates as SGA president in the spring election.

events.title: Two tickets make their case to succeed Coates
events.body: In the campaign's final week the Herald covered both tickets on the ballot to succeed Coates: Duan Wright with running mate Dwight Campbell, and Cassie Martin with running mate Leslie Bedo, each laying out a platform on the SGA's current issues.

events.title: Martin elected; faculty evaluations move forward
events.body: As Coates's term ended, the Herald's post-election coverage reported Cassie Martin had won the SGA presidency, running an opinion piece titled "Cassie Martin Must Stand Up on Tough Issues," and separately confirmed the SGA-sponsored faculty evaluations Coates's administration had pushed would be conducted and published starting that fall.

events.title: Matheis survives a flier scandal to win vice president of finance
events.body: Joe Matheis defeated Ryan Morrison 700-688 for vice president of finance in the campaign's most contentious race. Two hours after the initial result, SGA's judicial council placed the race under review after fliers Matheis had distributed turned up left on classroom desks and in computer labs overnight, violating election code; the council warned Matheis could lose the seat if he had not made a good-faith effort to collect them. The council let the result stand the next day, and Morrison filed a complaint with the judicial council disputing that decision, saying fliers were still on desks in Garrett and the fine arts center.

events.title: A letter to the editor questions an SGA probe of racially charged campaign fliers
events.body: A Herald letter to the editor reported that fliers reading "Vote for Will Jones in Racism," written in black ink, had circulated in dorms during the campaign, and that SGA opened an investigation into whether they were racially motivated. The letter's author named Jones - described as the first Black candidate for SGA president in years - as a suspect despite his denial of any involvement, and questioned whether the investigation was following proper procedure rather than targeting him by assumption. No source found reports how, or whether, the investigation was resolved.

events.title: A senior awards banquet and hall of distinguished seniors
events.body: Bill 99-5-F established a senior awards banquet and a hall of distinguished seniors, with a companion bill creating an ad hoc committee to run the event. A Meet Your Dean reception bill passed through the same September meetings.

events.title: Congress asked WKU to keep Jerry Wilder
events.body: Resolution 99-1-F requested that Jerry Wilder remain vice president of Student Affairs. The Herald reported the following week that SGA members opposed the move in Student Affairs.

events.title: Topline, a toll-free campus activity line
events.body: Resolution 99-4-F proposed creating a toll-free activity phone line called Topline. The same weeks produced resolutions on WKU banners and suggestion boxes in residence halls.

events.title: Members took the Student Affairs fight public
events.body: The Herald reported that Student Government Association members opposed the administrative move in Student Affairs. The story followed the congress's resolution asking that Vice President Jerry Wilder be retained.

events.title: SGA endorsed ending Flip Friday
events.body: A fall resolution endorsed the schedule proposed by the Class Schedule Review Committee to do away with Flip Friday. It was the association's formal word on one of the era's odder scheduling experiments.

events.title: VarsityBooks.com came to the SGA website
events.body: Bill 99-17-F had SGA join VarsityBooks.com and post a link from its website, and a same-day bill extended library hours during finals week. The dot-com partnership marked the first e-commerce deal in the digitised SGA record.

events.title: SGA proposed its own faculty evaluations
events.body: Resolution 00-2-S proposed creating an SGA faculty evaluation to help students select courses, reviving an idea the congress had pushed since the mid-1990s. It is the last piece of spring 2000 legislation in the digitised collection.

events.title: Herald reported SGA membership still declining
events.body: The Herald ran a story headlined "Student Government Association Membership Still Declining," tracking a drop in participation as the Martin administration prepared to take office.

events.title: Coates's quest for a concert continues
events.body: By the opening of the autumn 1999 term the Herald was reporting that President Amanda Coates was still pursuing a campus concert. The story ran under the headline "Amanda Coates' Quest for Concert Continues."

src.label: Herald 75:1, 26 Aug 1999 - Lynch, "Amanda Coates' Quest for Concert Continues"

events.title: Professional development workshops for upperclassmen
events.body: Bill 99-2-F committed SGA to run a series of free professional development workshops with the Career Services Center and Housing and Residence Life across both semesters of 1999-2000. They were aimed at sophomores, juniors and seniors preparing to move from study into work.

events.title: An autumn campus clean-up on 18 October 1999
events.body: Bill 99-3-F established a campus-wide clean-up at 3 p.m. on 18 October 1999, the first held in an autumn term. Other campus organisations could take part and count the time as community service, and the date was chosen because alumni would be on campus all that week.

profile: Cassie Martin, a junior from Glasgow, was elected SGA president in April 2000 to lead the association for 2000-2001. With running mate Leslie Bedo, she defeated the ticket of Duan Wright and Dwight Campbell by 654 votes to 541, and the win also made her the student representative on Western's Board of Regents. The race followed weeks of Herald coverage of proposed SGA election-code reforms meant to close loopholes and set spending limits, and the Martin-Wright contest itself was covered from the candidacy announcement in late March through a pre-election issues debate.

Her most visible stand of the year came at the Board of Regents meeting on October 27, 2000, when the board voted 8-2 to raise the student athletic fee by $80 in two installments. Martin was one of only two dissenters, alongside Faculty Regent Mary Ellen Miller. She said she understood the need for the additional funding but questioned the timing and the amount, and disagreed with raising student fees in the middle of an academic year.

SGA's congress in 2001 passed legislation putting $13,000 toward a campus gazebo that was never built. In October 2002 the Herald reported that the money had mistakenly gone back into SGA's general fund and been spent on other things, including computers, and SGA's finance vice president said leaders from the past two years, including former presidents Martin and Leslie Bedo, were all partly responsible for not properly earmarking it.

Cassie Martin, a junior from Glasgow, was elected SGA president in April 2000 to lead the association for 2000-2001. With running mate Leslie Bedo, she defeated the ticket of Duan Wright and Dwight Campbell by 654 votes to 541, and the win also made her the student representative on Western's Board of Regents.

events.title: Election-code debate turned to fairness and spending limits
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA's proposed election codes were meant to ensure fairness between candidates and set campaign spending limits, continuing coverage begun two weeks earlier of loopholes in the existing rules.

events.body: The Herald reported that Cassie Martin and Duan Wright would face off for the SGA presidency in the coming spring election, the first coverage of what became the Martin-Bedo versus Wright-Campbell race.

events.body: The day before the election, the Herald ran a piece by Rex Hall in which presidential candidates Cassie Martin and Duan Wright discussed the issues facing the campaign.

events.title: Martin-Bedo ticket won SGA presidency
events.body: Students elected Cassie Martin, a junior from Glasgow, as SGA president for 2000-2001, a post that also made her the student representative on Western's Board of Regents. Her ticket with vice presidential candidate Leslie Bedo defeated Duan Wright and Dwight Campbell by 654 votes to 541 in the Thursday election. In the only other contested race, Amy Caswell defeated Billy Lyons 706 to 461 for finance vice president, while Adam Howard and Leslie McClard ran unopposed for the administration and public relations vice presidencies.

events.title: Regents raised athletics fee over Martin's dissent
events.body: The Board of Regents voted 8-2 to raise the $16 student athletic fee by $40 in January 2001 and another $40 in fall 2001, to fund a Diddle Arena renovation, a larger football budget for WKU's move to the Gateway Conference, and the athletic department's budget shortfall. Student Regent Cassie Martin and Faculty Regent Mary Ellen Miller cast the two votes against. Martin said she understood the need for the funding but questioned the timing and the amount, and disagreed with raising student fees in the middle of an academic year.

events.title: Bedo ticket stood unopposed to succeed Martin
events.body: SGA's candidate page for the 2001 officer elections listed a single ticket for the top job: executive vice president Leslie Bedo for president with Jamie Sears as her running mate. The only race with two names was for vice president of public relations, between Mark Rawlings and Holly Skidmore, while Aaron Spencer and Jamil Sewell stood alone for the finance and administration vice presidencies. The date shown is the Internet Archive capture date; the page itself carried no date and no results or turnout figures were found in allowed sources.

events.title: SGA planned to conduct and publish faculty evaluations
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA planned to conduct student evaluations of faculty and publish the results starting in fall 2000, in the same issue that covered the close of the Martin-Bedo campaign. The same issue carried an editorial titled "Cassie Martin Must Stand Up on Tough Issues," urging the incoming president to take firmer positions once in office.

The university hired the clinic's 17 employees on a temporary basis through the end of the spring semester, and the vice president for Student Affairs promised students would see no reduction in health services.
