profile: Robert "Rob" Watkins, a Bowling Green student, wrote the SGA constitution adopted in 2004 and was elected the first speaker of the senate under it on 15 April 2004, defeating Brittany Fausey 9 votes to 8 in a result immediately contested over what quorum the new constitution required; the vote was upheld later that month.

Watkins won the SGA presidency in the 13 April 2006 online election, defeating Berea junior Kara Ratliff after more than a week courting TopNet voters, with results announced at a crowded Revolution 91.7. He took office for 2006-07 alongside Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen, who by October was tightening the budget after the prior administration left roughly $24,000 unspent.

Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent on 28 November 2006, with the resignation read into the senate's own minutes at that day's regularly scheduled Tuesday meeting, after senators had aired concerns about him at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. (A Herald account this site had followed gave the date as 30 November; the primary senate minutes are treated as authoritative here.) A Herald editorial the same week was headlined "SGA actions an embarrassment to Western." The resignation left students without a voting voice on the Board of Regents for at least a month and put junior Jeanne Johnson, already serving as his executive vice president since the 5 September season-opening meeting, in as a fill-in leader for the rest of the term, formally sworn in as president at the 5 December Winter Banquet.

leaders.name: Jeanne Johnson
leaders.note: Succeeded to the presidency partway through 2006-07. SGA's senate minutes record Rob Watkins's resignation read into the meeting of 28 November 2006 and Johnson sworn in as president at the Winter Banquet on 5 December, and she then won the special election for the vacant student regent seat in February 2007. The Chambers wall carries her only for 2007-08, the full term she was elected to in her own right, so the plaque understates her service by about five months.

sources.label: Herald front page, 3 Feb 2007 (Wayback) — front-page capture, not the specific article
Daily News, 27 Jan 2007 - Board OKs 7.8 percent tuition hike at WKU

profile: Jeanne Johnson was executive vice president when Rob Watkins resigned the presidency and the student regent seat in November 2006. The senate minutes for 28 November record his resignation being read to the chamber and senators being told she would be sworn in at the Winter Banquet on 5 December; the minutes of that meeting list the executive vice presidency as vacant because she had moved up.

The regent seat did not pass with the presidency, and Western went about two months without a student on its governing board. At the Board of Regents meeting of 26 January 2007 she spoke against the size of a 7.8 per cent tuition increase for online and distance learners without holding a vote, saying tuition increases were inevitable but that distance learners should not carry the burden. She won the special election for the seat the following week with 688 votes, 41 per cent of those cast.
She was elected to a full term in her own right and sworn in as president and student regent at the SGA banquet on 1 May 2007, where she also received the Dero Downing Award.

events.title: SGA tightened its budget after leaving $24,000 unspent
events.body: The Herald reported that SGA had left about $24,000 of its $115,000 budget unspent at the end of 2005-06, money that returned to Western's general fund. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen said SGA was cutting money from areas where it went unspent, adding almost $10,000 to organizational aid and $3,000 to the miscellaneous fund. Allen called the previous year a bad budgetary year but also a learning year.

events.title: Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent
events.body: SGA's own senate minutes record that president and student regent Rob Watkins's resignation was formally read into the meeting at the senate's regularly scheduled Tuesday session, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. Senators had voiced concerns about Watkins at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. A Herald front-page account (Wayback, 2 Dec 2006) covered the same resignation but gave the date as 30 November; this entry follows the primary senate minutes, which date the reading of the resignation to 28 November, leaving students without representation on Western's governing board for at least a month.

events.title: Fill-in SGA leader Jeanne Johnson challenged tuition plan at regents meeting
events.body: The Board of Regents approved a 7.8 percent tuition increase for 2007-08, bringing tuition and fees to $6,417 a year including the higher athletics fee. Jeanne Johnson, a junior economics and finance major from Marion described as a fill-in for the former SGA president, opposed the size of the increase for online and distance-learning courses, though she had no vote. She said 'We know tuition increases are inevitable' but argued distance learners should not carry that burden.

events.title: Provost rejected plus/minus grading; Johnson credited SGA's campaign
events.body: Provost Barbara Burch told the University Senate she would not implement the plus/minus grading system the senate had passed 36-23 in March. SGA President Jeanne Johnson said she was grateful for the decision, noting SGA had raised awareness and led student protests, and pledged that students would keep fighting if the issue returned. She said 'I'm confident that the students' opinions have been expressed.'

events.title: SGA banquet closed the year and swore in 2007-08 officers
events.body: At its annual banquet on May 1, SGA presented awards and swore in officers for 2007-08, with Jeanne Lynn Johnson of Marion becoming the new SGA president and student regent and receiving the Dero Downing Award. Johnathon Boles of Elizabethtown became executive vice president, Kayla Shelton speaker of the Student Senate, and Cherieth Lea Lineweaver administrative vice president. Amanda Beth Allen received the Charles A. Keown Award, SGA's highest honor.

events.title: SGA-run referendum showed students favored the I-A football move
events.body: In an online referendum SGA arranged alongside the homecoming queen election, 64.6 percent of voting students, 1,095, supported WKU's proposed move to Division I-A football, with 600 against. A total of 2,136 students voted in the poll, and the 1,695 who answered the football question represented about 9 percent of enrollment. SGA President Rob Watkins, who held the student seat on the Board of Regents, said the poll would help him define a position but noted the homecoming tie-in likely drew football-friendly voters.

events.title: SGA introduced a resolution backing the I-A football move
events.body: Resolution 06-06-F, restating the referendum's numbers, proposed that the Student Government Association support WKU's move to Division I-A football. The surviving copy of the resolution records a first reading on 31 October 2006 and leaves the second-reading and pass/fail fields blank, so the archive cannot confirm from this document alone that it passed, still less that it did so unanimously. No digitised Herald issue within a week of the 2 November 2006 Board of Regents vote on the same question has been found to confirm it either way; a Wayback capture of the paper's front page from 5 November 2006, which would likely cover both votes, could not be loaded this run.

src.label: SGA Resolution 06-06-F, first reading 31 Oct 2006, TopSCHOLAR

events.title: Johnson won the student regent election; SGA seated a full senate
events.body: Jeanne Johnson, SGA president and Marion junior, won the special election for Western's vacant student regent seat with 688 votes, 41 percent of ballots cast — confirmed by the front page's own headline, subhead and lede. The same Herald issue was also recorded as reporting that SGA began the spring semester with its first full senate attendance since fall 2004; the captured front page lists that story's headline, announcing SGA had begun the spring with a full senate, but carries none of its text, so the detail that the attendance was the first since fall 2004 remains unconfirmed.

src.label: Herald, "Johnson wins regent election," 1 Feb 2007 — the article's own URL was never independently archived, but the Wayback capture of the 3 Feb 2007 front page preserves this story's headline, subhead ("SGA president took 41 percent") and lede in full

events.title: Senate passed Books for Africa bill and a printing-quota resolution
events.body: At the same Nov. 28 meeting where Watkins's resignation was read into the record, the senate unanimously passed Bill 11-06-F, sponsored by Lucas Humble, to collect textbooks the university bookstore would not buy back and send them to Africa. Senators also unanimously passed Resolution 08-06-F, sponsored by Seth Norman, backing a university study of a computer-lab printing quota after administrators told SGA's Student Affairs committee how many pages some students were printing.

events.title: Senate heard Douglas Keen Hall was next for renovation
events.body: In a University Committees report to the senate, a member reported that the Student Life Foundation had discussed campus housing renovations and that Douglas Keen Hall would be the next residence hall to be renovated, within about three years. The same report covered a Budget Council discussion of rolling several student organizations' budgets, including SGA's, into the university's base budget.

events.title: Fifth SGA opened its year, swore in eight senators
events.body: At the first meeting of that year's Senate, called to order with 8 of 18 senators present, eight new senators were sworn in: Chris Anderson, Diane DeRosa-Reynolds, Leah Keys, Amanda Kidd, Suzie Moghaddam, Seth Norman, Tori Theiss and Christa Wilcox. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen reported $30,000 in organizational aid for the year, and the senate nominated committee heads and Judicial Council members, including Matt Holland as chief justice. The minutes record Jeanne L. Johnson delivering the executive vice president's report.

events.title: Senate tabled two resolutions for lack of quorum at Winter Banquet meeting
events.body: With 16 of 31 senators present, the senate lacked quorum to act on Resolution 09-06-F on vending machine prices and Resolution 10-06-F on special events parking, so both were tabled. Executive Vice President was listed vacant, since Jeanne Johnson had moved into the presidency after Robert Watkins's resignation. The Judicial Council reported meeting on the time requirements for the student regent seat. Winners of the Outstanding Senator and Outstanding Committee Member awards, chosen by secret ballot, were announced later that evening at the Winter Banquet.

events.title: SGA entered a team in Up 'til Dawn
events.body: Bill 06-03-F proposed that SGA sponsor a team in Up 'til Dawn. The senate minutes of 12 September 2006 record Up 'til Dawn and Habitat for Humanity being discussed together among the autumn's commitments.

events.title: Campus Cleanup set for 16 October and advertised on Facebook
events.body: Bill 04-06-F proposed 16 October 2006 as campus cleanup day. A companion bill, 05-06-F of 26 September, asked for an advertisement on Facebook to promote it. Both are proposals; the minutes of 10 and 17 October show the clean-up still being worked on but do not report how it went.

events.title: Dialogue Day revived with $800 behind it
events.body: Resolution 03-06-F of 2 October 2006 proposed a Dialogue Day at which students could meet university administrators, and Bill 08-06-F requested $800 to host it. Dialogue Day had been organised the previous autumn, when it ran through three sets of October 2005 minutes.

events.title: Organizational aid of $30,000 went out to student groups
events.body: Bill 06-06-F proposed disbursing $30,000 in organizational aid to a listed set of student organisations. The archive holds both readings, and the catalogue notes that the list of organisations in the first reading differs from the second, so groups were added or dropped between the two.

events.title: Buy-a-Book put $2,000 of book scholarships into students' hands
events.body: Bill 10-06-F proposed $2,000 in book scholarships for the spring 2007 semester. The programme left a full paper trail: a broadside advertising it, a press release announcing the 2006 winners on 1 December, and the form letter used to award them on 7 December. The senate renewed it for the following autumn on 27 February 2007.

events.title: Buy-a-Book winners announced by press release
events.body: SGA issued a press release on 1 December 2006 announcing the winners of that year's Buy-a-Book scholarships. A form letter used to award the scholarships is dated 7 December, and a broadside advertising the programme survives from the same week.

events.title: A resolution on vending machine prices reached a fifth reading
events.body: Resolution 09-06-F asked the university to reset vending machine prices. The archive holds its second reading and a revised fifth reading, both dated 24 November 2006, and the minutes of 5 December record it being tabled for want of quorum.

events.title: Senate asked for library serials funding to be restored
events.body: Resolution 04-06-F requested the restoration of library funding for serials, one of a run of academic-side measures that autumn. A report on the amount and cost of printing in the student technology computer labs survives from the same month.

events.title: SGA Week established by resolution
events.body: Resolution 02-07-S established a Student Government Association Week. SGA Week appears in the minutes of 27 February, 20 March, 27 March and 3 April 2007 as the officers organised it, and again in those of 25 March and 30 September 2008, so the resolution created a fixture rather than a one-off.

events.title: Dollies for Dorms bought moving equipment for residence halls
events.body: Bill 05-07-S proposed establishing an SGA Dollies for Dorms programme, buying dollies for students to use moving in and out of the residence halls.

events.title: Senate created Professor and Advisor of the Year awards
events.body: Bill 06-07-S proposed awards for professor and advisor of the year. It came in the same meeting as Dollies for Dorms and the spring campus clean-up resolution, in a session the minutes record as also covering professor accountability and a planned sit-in at a Regents meeting.

events.title: Spring campus clean-up set for 29 March 2007
events.body: Resolution 03-07-S proposed a campus clean up on 29 March 2007. This is the announcement rather than the event; the minutes of 20 March record the clean-up being organised but no later minutes report what happened on the day.

events.title: SGA created study abroad and field trip scholarships
events.body: Bill 07-07-S proposed an SGA study abroad scholarship and Bill 08-07-S proposed funding field trip scholarships. Both application forms survive in the archive dated the same day, so the programmes were built and opened rather than merely voted. They were still running when SGA described its services in 2009.

events.title: Study abroad scholarships proposed to be named for Caitlin Hammaren
events.body: Resolution 07-07-S proposed that the SGA study abroad scholarships be named in honour of Caitlin Hammaren, a Virginia Tech student killed in the April 2007 shooting. The senate had discussed the shooting at its meeting of 17 April, a week earlier.

events.title: SGA paid to keep the library open longer during finals week
events.body: Bill 11-07-S proposed SGA funding to extend library hours during finals week. The senate had discussed finals-week library hours as far back as December 2005; this is the first surviving measure putting SGA money behind it, and the Herald reported Helm-Cravens Library staying open later during finals week in April 2008.

events.title: Senate bought scantrons and blue books for exams
events.body: Bill 12-07-S proposed the purchase of scantron forms and blue books for student exams. SGA was still running the service in September 2009, when its website reported the senate approving 1,000 scantrons and 500 blue books for free distribution across campus.

events.title: Senate backed the Outlet Resource Center
events.body: Resolution 07-07-S proposed support for the Outlet Resource Center, described in the archive's catalogue as a safe haven for Western's gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgendered and questioning students. The same meeting took a resolution proposing a child care facility on or near campus for faculty and staff.

events.title: SGA printed a broadside for the plus-minus grading protest
events.body: A surviving SGA broadside promoted a plus/minus grading protest held in the Garrett Hall ballroom. The senate minutes of 20 March 2007 record a planned sit-in at a Board of Regents meeting, and those of 27 March record the protest itself being organised. The provost dropped the grading proposal that April.

documents.title: SGA Senate minutes, 5 September 2006
documents.summary: Minutes of the first meeting of that year's senate, with 8 of 18 senators present before eight more were sworn in. Officers gave welcome-back reports, committee heads and Judicial Council nominees were named, and Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen reported the year's $30,000 organizational aid budget.

President Robert Watkins's resignation was read into the record, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. The senate also passed a bill and a resolution, heard committee reports, and voted on semester awards.

documents.summary: Minutes of the thirteenth meeting of that senate, held the evening of the Winter Banquet. The senate lacked quorum to act on two tabled resolutions, heard that the executive vice presidency was vacant after Jeanne Johnson's move into the presidency, and heard a Judicial Council report on student regent time requirements.

executive.note: Gave the EVP's report at the 5 Sep. 2006 season-opening meeting; the seat was vacant by the 5 Dec. 2006 meeting after she moved into the presidency following Watkins's resignation.
profile: Jeanne Johnson was one of the candidates the Herald introduced in its 15 March 2005 special election edition ahead of that spring's SGA vote. By December 2005 she had risen to speaker of the senate, elected by her fellow senators at the meeting of 8 December that year, and in April 2006 she and Amanda Allen ran against each other in that spring's election, under a Herald headline arguing "Experience Helps Jeanne Johnson."

She took office as executive vice president for 2006-07 and gave the office's report at the season-opening senate meeting on 5 September 2006. Her seat was vacant by the 5 December 2006 meeting because she had moved up to the presidency after Rob Watkins's resignation; the fuller account of that succession is in her presidential profile for 2006-07.

profile: Amanda Allen was confirmed Director of Information Technology at SGA's first meeting of 2005-06, on 6 September 2005. She rebuilt the SGA website, photographed every senator for it, and sent the organization's first mass email to students who had registered for its iPod giveaway drawing.

Elected administrative vice president for 2006-07, Allen moved up to executive vice president when Jeanne Johnson, the sitting executive vice president, succeeded to the presidency partway through the year. By the 6 February 2007 meeting she was reporting to the Senate as executive vice president, telling members the Listen Up Legislators calling campaign had passed sixty callers on its first day, and raising a point of information at the same meeting on rounding vending-machine prices in Resolution 09-06-F. She received SGA's highest honor, the Charles A. Keown Award, at the May 2007 banquet.

senate.note: Jeanne Johnson served as a fill-in leader after Watkins' resignation and was elected president in her own right for 2007-08 at the May 2007 banquet. Senate size, officers and committee chairs per the 28 Nov. 2006 meeting minutes; 22 of 31 senators were present that night. The senate opened the year on 5 Sep. 2006 with 18 seats and 8 senators present, swearing in eight more that night; it had grown to 31 seats, 22 present, by 28 Nov. 2006. Jeanne Johnson served as executive vice president from the 5 Sep. 2006 opening meeting until Watkins's resignation, then as a fill-in leader before her own election in 2007-08. Growth continued into the spring: the minutes of 30 Jan. 2007 record the chamber reaching "a full senate" after eleven more were sworn in, though the roll call that night, taken before the oath, still counted 22 seats; from 6 Feb. 2007 the dated roll calls count the chamber as 35 — 27 of 35 present on 6 Feb., 24 of 35 on 27 Feb. — the figure this record now uses.

leaders.name: Jeanne Johnson
leaders.note: Confirmed against primary Board of Regents records: a resolution read into the 18 Jul 2008 board minutes states she served as the board's student member from 27 Apr 2007 to 18 Jul 2008, and the same minutes record Johnathon Boles taking the oath to replace her that day. Also confirmed in Herald coverage of the 24 Apr 2008 Board of Regents meeting, where she is named 'Student Government Association President Jeanne Johnson.'

sources.label: WKU Board of Regents minutes, 18 Jul 2008 (TopSCHOLAR)
Herald 83:51, 29 Apr 2008 - "Regents approve 9 percent tuition increase, finalize 07-08 budget cuts"

profile: Jeanne Lynn Johnson, a Marion senior and Kappa Delta member, had served as SGA's president pro tempore after Rob Watkins's November 2006 resignation and won the February 2007 special election for the vacant student regent seat with 688 votes. She became SGA president and student regent for 2007-08 in her own right, sworn onto the Board of Regents on April 27, 2007, and installed as president at SGA's May 2007 banquet.

That fall her administration reported record interest in the senate election, 25 candidates for 20 seats, and she and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles helped organize a mock gubernatorial election that drew 127 student voters. She pushed a senate resolution asking the state for more funding after Western received only 54 percent of its recommended budget increase, and organized Walk Out Western, an Oct. 25 class walkout protesting state budget cuts that President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone.

As student regent, Johnson voted against the scale of the board's 9 percent tuition increase at the April 24, 2008 quarterly meeting, seconding Louisville regent Larry Zielke's motion to cap the increase at 6 percent and push the General Assembly for more funding instead; the motion died with only two votes. At the same meeting she argued the $370,000 budgeted for the Honors College should be cut, saying the college "only benefits 900 students" and other students should not have to pay for it; Ransdell defended it as part of the university's strategic plan.

In the spring, as her administration ran the election to choose her successor, Johnson defended the one-week campaign window written into election codes she said were inherited from past administrations, warning that longer campaigns could hurt candidates' schoolwork and that "too much PR hurts." She pointed to new turnout efforts her administration tried, including holding the debate during SGA week and adding candidate profiles and questionnaires to the SGA website.

Johnathon Boles won the March 2008 election and was installed as SGA president at the spring banquet, but Johnson kept the Board of Regents seat until the board's next quarterly meeting; a resolution read there on July 18, 2008 thanked her for "able leadership, faithful service, and dedication" and Boles took the oath as student regent the same day.

In the spring, as her administration ran the election to choose her successor, Johnson defended the one-week campaign window written into election codes she said were inherited from past administrations, warning that longer campaigns could hurt candidates' schoolwork and that "too much PR hurts." She pointed to new turnout efforts her administration tried, including holding the debate during SGA week, arranging extra credit for students who attended it, and adding candidate profiles and questionnaires to the SGA website.

events.title: Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like
events.body: After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection.

events.title: Fall senate election drew 25 candidates for 20 seats
events.body: SGA reported record interest in its fall senate election, with 25 students running for 20 available seats, the most applications President Jeanne Johnson said she had ever seen. Elections were set for Sept. 19 and 20 through TopNet, with an informational table in Downing University Center on Sept. 18. Public relations director Liz Goddard said more competition would produce harder workers.

events.title: SGA co-sponsored mock gubernatorial election
events.body: SGA and the Office of the Secretary of State co-sponsored a mock gubernatorial election at Centennial Mall as part of Secretary of State Trey Grayson's Civic Literacy Initiative of Kentucky. The 127 students who voted chose challenger Steve Beshear over incumbent Gov. Ernie Fletcher, 74 to 50. President Jeanne Johnson and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles called the event a success.

events.title: Resolution demanded more state funding for Western
events.body: At its Oct. 9 meeting SGA passed a resolution asking the state government to appropriate more money to Western, which had received 54 percent of the funding the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended for fiscal year 2008. President Jeanne Johnson argued that tuition increases to cover the shortfall hurt students. The resolution stated Western needed the full recommended amount to meet its 2020 educational goals.

events.title: SGA organized Walk Out Western budget protest
events.body: SGA sponsored Walk Out Western, asking students to leave class at 12:20 p.m. on Oct. 25 for a rally at the Colonnade to protest state budget cuts, with empty seats meant as a message to Frankfort legislators. President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone students walking out of class and doubted a single-campus protest would affect state funding. Johnson said other state universities declined to join but were watching how it worked at Western.

events.title: Committee proposed $1,995 educational video subscription
events.body: SGA's Academic Affairs Committee, chaired by Drew Eclov, prepared legislation to buy a roughly $1,995 subscription to United Streaming, a Discovery Channel-owned site with about 45,000 educational video clips that Eclov called a version of YouTube for higher education. The committee planned to survey students and professors before bringing it to a vote. SGA also scheduled a vote on a resolution placing $1,000 in a field trip fund to support learning outside the classroom.

events.title: Athletics director asked SGA for help on football attendance
events.body: Athletics Director Wood Selig came to the SGA meeting to ask senators for ideas on getting more students to football games as Western moved to the Football Bowl Subdivision, which required an average attendance of 15,000 to keep bowl eligibility. Senators suggested advertising on Western's website and Facebook rather than email, and later game times. Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles, who sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics, arranged the consultation.

events.title: SGA planned Listen Up Legislators lobbying campaign
events.body: SGA began laying groundwork for Listen Up Legislators, a spring lobbying campaign in which senators would meet legislators one-on-one in Frankfort to push for university funding, after the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended a $174 million increase for public universities. Chief of staff Skylar Jordan said the traditional February rally had not worked, pointing to Western receiving only 54 percent of the recommended increase. Other state student governments expressed interest in coordinating lobbying dates.

events.title: Spring session opened with ONE Campus bill
events.body: At its first spring meeting on Jan. 29, SGA introduced legislation by Senators Matt Vaughan and Doug Tate asking the senate to recognize Western as a ONE Campus, part of the national campaign against global AIDS and extreme poverty. SGA also released its spring schedule, including Listen Up Legislators on Feb. 14, the Frankfort rally for higher education on Feb. 20 and the annual banquet on April 29. In the semester's opening handout, Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles pointed members to the constitution's purpose of serving the student body equally.

events.title: Spring election closed amid low-turnout criticism
events.body: Voting for three executive seats and 28 senate seats ended after a one-week campaign that candidates criticized as part of SGA's low-involvement problem; turnout had been 1,424 the year before and 1,376 the year before that. Red Towel Party presidential candidate Tedde Harden promised to rework what he called outdated election codes, while opponent Johnathon Boles agreed campaign time should be extended. President Jeanne Johnson said her administration inherited the codes and had tried new turnout methods, including extra credit for attending the debate.

events.title: Ransdell announced 9 percent tuition increase
events.body: President Gary Ransdell announced at campus forums that he would recommend a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09, abandoning a plan to hold increases at 6 percent. The change followed a state budget crisis in which Gov. Steve Beshear ordered a 3 percent cut to postsecondary education in December 2007 and proposed an additional 12 percent, later reduced by the General Assembly to 3 percent. Ransdell said the swing from expected state revenue was about $11 million to $12 million.

events.title: Student regent Johnson opposed scale of 9 percent tuition increase
events.body: The Board of Regents approved a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09 and finalized $2.5 million in cuts to the 2007-08 budget. Louisville regent Larry Zielke moved to cap the increase at 6 percent and push the General Assembly for more funding instead; SGA President and student regent Jeanne Johnson seconded the motion, but it died with only two votes. Johnson also argued the $370,000 budgeted for the Honors College should be reduced, saying the college benefited only 900 students and other students should not have to pay for it.

events.title: Johnson's regent term ended as Boles took the board oath
events.body: The Board of Regents read a resolution thanking Jeanne Johnson for her service as the board's student member from April 27, 2007 to July 18, 2008, calling her term one of "able leadership, faithful service, and dedication." Johnathon Boles, who had already been installed as SGA president that spring, took the oath of office as student regent the same day, formally completing the transition between administrations.

events.title: Spring Oasis gave out exam supplies during finals week
events.body: On 22 April 2008 the senate voted $250 for Spring Oasis, then in its second year, a programme meant to relieve the cost of finals week. The money bought scantrons, exam books, pencils, pens and highlighters. SGA allocated a further $500 to provide refreshments for students in the library.

events.title: Senator pushed WKU to join the Ruckus free music service
events.body: Kevin Smiley, senator and chair of the student affairs committee, wrote legislation asking administrators to apply for membership of Ruckus, a download service that let anyone with a .edu address stream music and films free from a company-supplied server. The senate was due to consider it on 22 April 2008. Smiley said the software was already available to students but could not run on WKU computers until the university joined, and that installing the server would cost the university nothing.

events.title: SGA held an autumn cookout
events.body: The senate minutes of 9 and 16 October 2007 both record a cookout being organised, alongside Walk-Out Western. The minutes name the event but record nothing about how it went.

events.title: SGA planned a finals week Oasis and a holiday dinner
events.body: The executive council minutes of 13 November 2007 record the finals week oasis being planned along with cafeteria hours and computer labs. The senate minutes of 27 November carry it forward together with a holiday dinner, and those of 4 December record the oasis again. The following April the senate voted $250 for a Spring Oasis, then in its second year.

events.title: Senate worked on an end-of-semester study day
events.body: An end-of-semester study day appears in the senate minutes of 9 October and 6 November 2007 and in the executive council minutes of the same date, alongside homecoming and Walk-Out Western. It returned in the spring, appearing in the minutes of 1 April 2008.

events.title: Gatton Academy students asked for a seat in SGA
events.body: The executive cabinet minutes of 24 March 2008 record a discussion of Gatton Academy students participating in SGA, alongside plus/minus grading, the Hall of Distinguished Seniors and a block party. The Herald of 27 March carried an article headed that the Gatton Academy of Math and Science wanted representation too.

events.title: The Herald turned its opinion page on SGA during the election
events.body: The Herald of 27 March 2008 ran an editorial cartoon depicting SGA as clowns, an editorial saying the organisation needed to change its election process, and rival opinion pieces from candidates Johnathon Boles and from Theodore Harden, Kevin Smiley and Reagan Gilley. On 8 April a further cartoon and an editorial headed that SGA needed an overhaul followed.

events.title: Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party
events.body: The Herald of 8 April 2008 reported that Skylar Jordan had filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party, the slate that had campaigned to energise SGA. Two days later the paper reported the Judicial Council was addressing both a tie and the campaign complaint, and that SGA would have to elect a new Speaker of the Senate. The archive does not record how the council ruled.

events.title: Spring campus clean-up rescheduled to Thursday
events.body: The Herald of 8 April 2008 reported that SGA had rescheduled the campus clean-up for Thursday. The senate minutes of 25 March and 1 April both record the clean-up being organised.

events.title: Western won the national ONE Campus Challenge
events.body: The Herald of 10 April 2008 reported that Western had won the ONE Campus Challenge, the national campaign against extreme poverty and global AIDS. SGA had introduced legislation asking the senate to recognise Western as a ONE Campus at its first spring meeting on 29 January, and the Herald of 24 April reported ONE leaders advocating an education bill in Washington.

events.title: The Ruckus free music bill was shelved over IT concerns
events.body: The Herald of 24 April 2008 reported that the Ruckus bill had been shelved because of information technology concerns, a week after the senate was due to consider it.

events.title: Senate rejected a diploma proposal and backed the SEAT
events.body: The Herald of 24 April 2008 reported that SGA had rejected a diploma proposal and that it was in favour of the Student Engagement Activities Transcript, the record of learning outside the classroom that SGA was still promoting to students in 2009. The same issue reported Helm-Cravens Library staying open later during finals week.

executive.note: Sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics and arranged the November 2007 consultation with Athletics Director Wood Selig; ran to succeed Johnson as president in the March 2008 election.
profile: Johnathon Boles served as executive vice president for 2007-08. He sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics and helped arrange a November 2007 consultation with athletics director Wood Selig on increasing football attendance. In March 2008 he ran to succeed Jeanne Johnson as president, facing Tedde Harden in a Herald-hosted candidate forum on 25 March, and published campaign op-eds on 27 March and 3 April arguing that a diverse student body needed "one voice" through SGA and asking students to use their vote as "an instrument for your voice." He won that election and served as president for 2008-09, detailed in his own presidential profile.

She continued as administrative vice president in 2007-08, telling the Senate at its 4 September 2007 meeting that SGA had about $110,000 for the year, including $2,000 earmarked for Campus Improvements to build new shuttle shacks, and that every executive money request had to be turned into a purchase order through her office.

profile: Reagan Gilley was director of academic and student affairs for 2007-08. He authored Resolution 07-07-S, which named SGA's study abroad scholarship, passed at the year's first senate meeting on 4 September 2007, and that year he also worked toward opening the university library for 24-hour hours and on the study abroad and film scholarships. In the spring 2008 campaign he ran for administrative vice president against Skylar Johnson, and co-wrote a 27 March Herald op-ed with presidential candidate Theodore Harden and executive vice-presidential candidate Kevin Smiley arguing that student representation needed a change. Harden was running against Johnathon Boles, so the three op-ed signatories stood as a slate opposed to Boles; the same issue carried a report on a Red Towel Party seeking to energize SGA, and in April a complaint was filed against that party, but the surviving index does not state which candidates belonged to it. Gilley won his race and served as administrative vice president for 2008-09.

profile: Lisa Kappler was seated as a Justice on the Judicial Council in the Senate's minutes of 29 January 2008, alongside fellow justice Lamiaya Page.

By the 2008-09 year the Senate's minutes of 14 October 2008 recorded her as Clerk of the Judicial Council, and by February 2009 the Herald was referring to her as SGA's Chief Justice. She cast the dissenting vote when the council ruled 2-1 on 10 February 2009 to hold a special election for the student regent seat left vacant by Johnathon Boles' resignation, arguing the constitution's requirement for one was a gray area. She resigned two days later, on 12 February 2009, in a letter to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, writing that she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the Senate would elect a new chief justice at its next meeting, with the special regent election only two weeks away. The Herald of 19 February 2009 reported that the Senate had approved Corey Bewley as her replacement.

leaders.name: Johnathon Boles
leaders.note: Confirmed against Herald election coverage. Boles led the "Red Towel Party" ticket - with Theodore Harden, Reagan Gilley, Skylar Johnson, Kayla Shelton and Kevin Smiley also on the March 2008 candidate slate - in the spring 2008 SGA election. After the vote, Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party; the SGA council took no action on it on 22 April 2008, letting the result stand. profile: Johnathon Boles ran for SGA president in spring 2008 on the "Red Towel Party" ticket, a slate that also carried Theodore Harden, Reagan Gilley, Skylar Johnson, Kayla Shelton and Kevin Smiley as candidates for other executive and senate offices. After Boles's ticket won, Skylar Jordan filed a complaint against the Red Towel Party; the SGA council took no action on it on 22 April 2008, and the result stood. Boles, a junior from Elizabethtown, served as SGA president and student regent for 2008-09. In November 2008, Gov. Steve Beshear appointed him and fellow SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of the governor's College Access Work Group on college affordability, and Boles traveled to Frankfort for its first meeting, where he raised the burden of textbook costs. "I'm honored the governor chose me to represent WKU," he said.

In December 2008, Boles led SGA through its first mid-year budget cut, after a state shortfall required the university to trim about 4 percent. He and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley cut $4,100 from SGA's $110,000 budget while protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride, and Boles addressed the senate about the cuts, saying he would keep fighting for the affordability of higher education. He also worked to arrange charter buses to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against cuts to higher education.

Boles resigned on Jan. 30, 2009, for health reasons, midway through his term. Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton took his place as president but not as student regent, and the student body went 26 days without a regent until Reagan Gilley won a special election on Feb. 25. Gilley said he planned to contact Boles the day after his win to get up to date on Board of Regents business.

leaders.name: Kayla Shelton
leaders.note: Plaque plate reads "2009" and had been filed under 2009-10, overlapping Kevin Smiley there; moved to 2008-09. Shelton was executive vice president, elected in spring 2008 alongside Johnathon Boles, and became president - but not student regent - when Boles resigned on 30 Jan 2009, finishing out his 2008-09 term. Kevin Smiley won the next regular election on 16 April 2009 for the 2009-10 term, so Shelton's presidency did not extend into 2009-10. Confirmed: the Herald of April 2009 describes her as the sitting Student Government Association president, having taken office after Johnathon Boles resigned, and previously senator, student affairs chair, speaker of the senate and executive vice president. She did not take the seat on the Board of Regents with the presidency: that seat had been vacated by Boles's resignation and was filled separately by Reagan Gilley in a special election in February 2009.

profile: Kayla Shelton ran on Johnathon Boles's "Red Towel Party" ticket in the spring 2008 SGA election and served as executive vice president for 2008-09. When Boles resigned as president and student regent on 30 Jan. 2009 for health reasons, Shelton succeeded him as president but not as student regent, leaving the regent seat vacant.

As president, Shelton backed the SGA Judicial Council's 2-1 decision to hold a special student regent election rather than leave the seat vacant, over the dissent of Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan, saying "That's what they decided, so I support it" and that her main focus remained serving the student body. She also accepted Chief Justice Lisa Kappler's resignation in mid-February, which came with the regent election two weeks away. Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley won that special election on 25 Feb. 2009, taking over the regent's seat while Shelton continued as president through the rest of the term.

Shelton presided over the senate through the spring, including a Feb. 24 meeting where senators debated and rejected, 13 votes to 9, a bill to cover an extra $82.27 for water bottles SGA had earlier agreed to fund as prizes for a Housing and Residence Life energy-saving contest. Shelton said she thought it was great that the senate debated something it felt passionate about rather than casting "just a general yes or no."
Shelton did not continue as president into 2009-10; Kevin Smiley won the regular spring election for that term on 16 April 2009.

Kayla Shelton, who had been executive vice president, became SGA president after Johnathon Boles resigned, serving out the rest of the 2008-09 year. She inherited a dispute over whether to hold a special election for the vacant student regent seat, and when the Judicial Council voted 2-1 in February to hold one despite objections from other executives, she backed the decision. "That's what they decided, so I support it," Shelton said, adding that her main focus remained serving the student body.

leaders.name: Reagan Gilley
leaders.note: Elected student regent in a special election held 25-26 February 2009, beating Nate Eaton 477 to 224 of 701 votes cast. Then the administrative vice president, Gilley took the Board seat that Johnathon Boles vacated when he resigned the presidency on 30 January 2009; Kayla Shelton succeeded Boles as president but did not take the regent seat, so for the rest of that year the two offices were held by two people. The Board of Regents minutes of 24 April 2009 record the constitutional oath being administered to him as student regent. The split closed at the regular summer handover: the Board's roll call of 31 July 2009 lists Kevin Smiley as student regent.

profile: Reagan Gilley was a Pineville senior and the Student Government Association's administrative vice president when he won the special election for student regent held 25-26 February 2009, filling the seat left empty for 26 days after President Johnathon Boles resigned on 30 January for health reasons. He beat Fairdale senior Nate Eaton, the speaker of the senate, 477 votes to 224 of the 701 cast, and Chief Justice Corey Bewley announced the verified result at 12:17 a.m. Thursday in the SGA office. Gilley had campaigned on short notice through a Facebook group, announcements in classes and a YouTube video built around the Rick Astley song "Never Gonna Give You Up," and after the count he handed Eaton a plaque he had bought at Kroger that day. He said he planned to contact Boles the next day to catch up on Board of Regents business and then to contact Faculty Regent Patricia Minter, and that he wished more students had voted. "I am very relieved but excited for things to come," he said.

Gilley took the constitutional oath of office from Board Chair Lois Gray at the second quarterly meeting on 24 April 2009, where President Gary Ransdell presented him with the regent's pin, and he answered the roll call as student regent. He seconded Larry Zielke's motion to approve the naming of designated facilities and rooms, and seconded Yevette Haskins's motion to accept the 2008-09 second quarter statement of revenues and expenditures for filing. On the 2009-10 tuition and fees schedule, which carried a 4 percent increase, Gilley asked to amend the motion to strike the proposed per credit hour fee on course loads above 15 hours; the amended motion was seconded by Zielke and carried unanimously. He then moved to add a drop/add fee of $50 per transaction to the schedule, which Zielke seconded and which also carried unanimously, and afterwards told the Board that tuition increases were a major concern of the student body and that "for the record, I meant to vote in opposition to the tuition increase." During a long exchange over personnel actions and campus morale, in which the faculty and staff regents described resignations and low morale, Gilley said that on behalf of the student body there was concern about fewer staff being available for classes. The minutes list the Board's next meetings as a special budget meeting on 19 June 2009 and the third quarterly meeting on 31 July 2009.

His time on the Board was over by the summer. The minutes of the special budget meeting of 19 June 2009 record the constitutional oath of office being administered to Kevin Smiley as student regent, again by Chair Lois Gray and with the regent's pin presented by President Ransdell, and the roll call for that meeting lists Smiley rather than Gilley. Gilley's name does not appear in those minutes at all, so the quarterly meeting of 24 April 2009 was the only Board meeting that fell within his tenure, and the record of his service as student regent runs to that single day of votes. Gilley's name does not appear in those minutes, so the handover had happened by 19 June 2009, earlier than the 31 July roll call previously recorded here.

events.title: Fall senate election drew above-average turnout
events.body: SGA seated nine new student senators after a two-day fall election in which 18 candidates competed. Seven seats had been open, four reserved for freshmen, and two more opened when two senators resigned the Monday before the vote. A total of 687 students voted, which President Johnathon Boles said was higher than the average for a fall election.

events.title: Boles and Smiley appointed to governor's college affordability group
events.body: Gov. Steve Beshear appointed SGA President Johnathon Boles and SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of his College Access Work Group, which was charged with recommending ways to make Kentucky higher education more affordable. The two traveled to Frankfort for the committee's first meeting, where they raised the impact of textbook costs, which Boles put at an average of $800 a year.

events.title: Senate voted to launch a Textbook Subsidy Program
events.body: The SGA senate voted to contribute $500 to start a Textbook Subsidy Program, an effort developed with the University Bookstore, which pledged another $500, to build an endowment that would lower textbook costs for students. The senate also created a program board of nearly 20 members, including Boles, bookstore representatives and members from each college, to work out funding and distribution.

events.title: SGA made its first mid-year budget cut
events.body: Facing a state shortfall that required the university to cut about 4 percent of its budget, SGA cut $4,100 from its $110,000 budget, the first time it had cut its budget in the middle of an academic year. Boles and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley chose to cut a $2,600 surplus from the fall retreat and $1,500 from organizational aid, protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride. Boles said he was working to get charter buses to send students to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against higher education budget cuts.

events.title: Judicial Council ordered a special student regent election over executive dissent
events.body: After Boles' resignation left the student regent seat empty, the SGA Judicial Council voted 2-1 on Feb. 10 to hold a special election on Feb. 24 and 25. Chief Justice Lisa Kappler cast the dissenting vote, calling the constitution's requirement a gray area, and Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan presented a letter arguing the election was unnecessary. President Kayla Shelton said she supported the council's decision.

events.title: Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned
events.body: SGA Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned Thursday night in a letter sent to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, saying she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the senate would vote on a new chief justice at the next meeting because the special election for student regent was two weeks away.

events.title: Reagan Gilley won the special student regent election
events.body: Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley, a Pineville senior, defeated Speaker of the Senate Nate Eaton 477 votes to 224 in the special election for student regent, with 701 students voting. The seat had been vacant for 26 days after former President Johnathon Boles resigned on Jan. 30 for health reasons; Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton had taken his place as president but not as regent.

events.title: Kevin Smiley won the SGA presidential election
events.body: The Herald reported Kevin Smiley's win in the spring SGA presidential election under the headline "All Smiles, Kevin Smiley Wins Student Government Association Election," ending Kayla Shelton's term as the president who had finished out Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 year. Smiley took office as president and student regent for 2009-10.

events.title: SGA negotiated removal of proposed $30 per-credit-hour fee
events.body: SGA and university officials agreed to strike a proposed $30 fee for every credit hour over 15 from the Board of Regents agenda, replacing it with a proposal to raise the add/drop fee from $20 to $50. SGA canceled a planned protest after the compromise, and Student Regent Reagan Gilley called the outcome "really a win-win for everyone."

events.title: Ice storm hit campus, injuring a student and closing regional campuses
events.body: A winter storm coated campus in ice during the week of Jan. 27, part of the second-largest power outage recorded in Kentucky. A falling tree limb struck a sophomore near Grise Hall, who was treated and released, and WKU canceled classes at its Elizabethtown, Owensboro, Glasgow, Fort Knox and Radcliff campuses as well as evening classes on the main campus. AT&T cell outages kept officials from reaching students by text message.

events.title: Shots fired outside Pearce-Ford Tower put dorms on lockdown
events.body: Campus police responded to a report of shots fired at about 3 a.m. Saturday in the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot, where a witness said a man got out of a vehicle, fired a gun and drove away. Police found shell casings but no damage, no one was hurt, and all dorms went into lockdown after the incident.

events.title: Senate refused an extra $82.27 for Reduce Your Use water bottles
events.body: A bill passed on 18 November 2008 had given Housing and Residence Life $650 to buy 420 water bottles as prizes for the Reduce Your Use contest, a competition between dorms to cut energy use and increase recycling, won by Minton Hall. When the bottles came in $82.27 over the quote, the senate voted nine to thirteen on 24 February 2009 against covering the difference. Administrative vice president Reagan Gilley said he had not wanted to take the money from the SGA budget without asking the senate.

src.label: Herald, 26 Feb 2009 - "SGA denies money for HRL to purchase more water bottles" (Wayback)

events.title: Organizational aid and $2,000 for The Come Up
events.body: At its meeting on 31 March 2009 the senate passed two bills awarding $9,029.04 in organizational aid to 21 student organizations. A third bill gave $2,000 to the Office of Diversity Programs for The Come Up, a programme to help black men build skills in academics, health and etiquette. The senate voted down a resolution urging WKU to enforce its existing campus smoking policy.

events.title: SGA put $500 into WKU's herb garden
events.body: On 7 April 2009 the senate passed a bill supporting WKU's herb garden, on the path between Downing University Center and South Lawn, giving the office of sustainability $500 to buy more varieties of plant. Recycling coordinator Cristin Lanham said the garden had been planted two years earlier so students, staff and faculty could pick herbs free, and that Fresh Food Company chefs sometimes cut from it. The garden was used to teach a workshop at the Campus Community Partnerships for Sustainability Conference that month.

events.title: A Nappy Roots concert came before the senate
events.body: The senate minutes of 16 September 2008 record a Nappy Roots concert on the agenda alongside football games, Western Wednesdays and appointments, and the minutes of 23 September record it again together with the campus safety walk and Buy-a-Book. The archive shows the concert being arranged; it does not record whether it took place or what it cost.

events.title: Western Wednesdays began as an SGA programme
events.body: Western Wednesdays appears in the senate minutes of 16 and 23 September 2008. By March 2010 SGA was running Western Wednesdays as a discount scheme rewarding students for wearing Western apparel in Bowling Green, with twenty-two participating businesses.

events.title: SGA Week, homecoming and campus cleanup day set for the autumn
events.body: The senate meeting of 30 September 2008 was given over to SGA Week, homecoming and campus cleanup day. Homecoming returns in the minutes of 21 and 28 October and 3 November, so it occupied the senate for more than a month.

events.title: SGA ran a mock election before the 2008 presidential vote
events.body: The senate minutes of 7 October 2008 record a mock election alongside organizational aid and Buy-a-Book. SGA had run a mock gubernatorial election with the Secretary of State's office the previous autumn, in which 127 students voted.

events.title: Senate took up the 22 October campus lockdown
events.body: The senate minutes of 28 October 2008 record a discussion of the lock down of campus on 22 October, together with homecoming, Buy-a-Book scholarships and committee appointments. The Herald of 23 October carried a timeline of events, an article headed that gunfire was unconfirmed and the investigation continuing, and a piece reporting the university pleased with its emergency response.

events.title: Senate resolved in support of an emergency communications system
events.body: Resolution 01-08-F was a resolution in support of a crisis management system for the university. It came five days after shots were reported outside Pearce-Ford Tower and six weeks before the October campus lockdown.

events.title: Senate approved Corey Bewley as chief justice
events.body: The Senate approved Corey Bewley as SGA's new chief justice, a week after Lisa Kappler resigned the post. Bewley had been serving as a Justice on the Judicial Council.

events.body: Academic Affairs Committee chair Brittany Wick wrote a Herald column encouraging students to get involved with the Student Government Association, arguing anyone could take part.

profile: Reagan Gilley served as administrative vice president for 2008-09, alongside Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton, though the two had run in the spring on opposing slates. He presented the year's budget to the senate line by line at its first meeting, 26 August 2008 - $8,000 for two student workers, $9,050 for executive stipends, $1,000 for travel and $5,000 for senate programming - and told senators the budget was now in their hands. He represented SGA that year on the Budget Council, Faculty Welfare and the University Calendar Committee. When President Johnathon Boles resigned in January 2009, Gilley won the special election for the vacant student regent seat that February; his time on the Board of Regents is recorded in his separate regent profile for 2008-09.

executive.name: R. Skylar Jordan
executive.note: Nominated on 26 August 2008 after serving pro tem; he built a master schedule of every committee's meeting times and told senators to bring him their legislative questions.
profile: Skylar Jordan first held SGA office in 2005-06 as director of academic and student affairs, reporting by early April 2006 on the Distinguished Senior awards and the opening of the Student Success Center; the Senate minutes of that meeting give his full name as Ricky Skylar Jordan. He held the same post in 2006-07, reporting in February 2007 that he had met with the university about textbook ordering at the bookstore, was looking into space for a Gay and Lesbian Resource Center, and was researching SGA's own history in the Kentucky Building archives.

Jordan moved to chief of staff for 2007-08, laying groundwork that fall for the "Listen Up Legislators" spring lobbying campaign after a February Frankfort rally alone had failed to move the legislature. That April, after Johnathon Boles's "Red Towel Party" ticket won the SGA election, Jordan filed a complaint against the party; the SGA council took no action on it on 22 April 2008, and the result stood. He returned to serve as Boles's chief of staff again in 2008-09, nominated on 26 August 2008 after serving in the role pro tem, and built a master schedule of every SGA committee's meeting time for senators to consult.

In September 2009, after Boles had resigned and been succeeded by Kevin Smiley, Jordan publicly criticized Smiley's decision to nominate his own brother, Eric Smiley, as chief of staff. The Herald identified him in that report as "former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan" — a title and surname variant not otherwise recorded for him in SGA's own minutes, which consistently give his office as director of academic and student affairs and then chief of staff, never executive vice president.

profile: Nathan “Nate” Eaton chaired the Campus Improvements Committee for two consecutive years before rising to Speaker of the Senate. He took over the chairmanship by 6 February 2007, after Tori Theiss stepped down, and reported to the Senate that night that the committee was working on more ashtrays around campus and looking into new benches; returning as chair in 2007-08, he named finishing a shuttle stop begun the year before as his priority.

The Senate elected him Speaker for 2008-09 on 15 April 2008, by a vote of 13 to 8 with two abstentions over Matthew Vaughan and Brittany-Ann Wick, after an hour of questioning on parliamentary procedure and on his having publicly endorsed three candidates; the Herald's headline on the result called him the chamber's longest-serving senator.
In February 2009 he ran for the open student regent seat against Reagan Gilley. The Herald reported Gilley's election to the seat on 26 February 2009.

profile: Kevin T. Smiley, a senior from Danville, served as SGA president and student regent for 2009-10. His executive branch included Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, and four appointed officials, among them his brother Eric Smiley as chief of staff.

Smiley opened his term with controversy in September 2009 when he nominated his brother, Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, for the paid chief of staff position, saying he chose him because he had no previous political agenda and was "somebody I truly trust." Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the move "completely unethical," though Thurman defended the president's right to pick a qualified adviser.

In October 2009 three senators resigned after Smiley nominated Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, with Michel Stephens charging the pick was not based on merit. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded, described the resignations as a misunderstanding, and said he would begin contacting fall election candidates to fill the vacant seats. His term ran through the April 2010 election of his successor.

events.title: Smiley nominates his brother as chief of staff
events.body: SGA President Kevin Smiley announced Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, his brother, as his nominee for chief of staff, a paid voting position on the executive cabinet. Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the nomination "completely unethical," while Smiley said he chose his brother because he had no previous political agenda. The senate was set to vote on all nominations Sept. 8, with a two-thirds majority needed for approval.

events.title: Fall election opens; SGA gives $2,000 to Residence Hall Association
events.body: At the Sept. 15 senate meeting, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that SGA gave $2,000 from its budget to the Residence Hall Association. President Kevin Smiley announced that voting in the fall SGA election had started on TopNet, with polls open until Wednesday night and results announced about midnight. Smiley also urged senators to join the Campus Safety Walk, in which participants looked for dimly lit or overgrown areas on campus.

events.title: SGA sponsors forum on new tailgating policy
events.body: About 30 people attended an SGA-sponsored forum where students and administrators discussed Western's amended tailgating policy, which banned vehicles from campus lawns on game days. Howard Bailey, vice president for student affairs, told students the policy would stay the same, and Speaker of the Senate Wade Pierce suggested tent giveaways to ease the transition. President Kevin Smiley said he was pleased with the attendance and that SGA would keep questioning the policy.

events.title: Three senators resign over publications committee appointment
events.body: Senators Michel Stephens, Emmett Stephens and Daniel Shaw resigned at the Oct. 20 meeting. Michel Stephens cited President Kevin Smiley's nomination of Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, which helps choose the Herald's editor-in-chief, saying the pick was not based on merit or experience. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded and said the seats would stay vacant until he appointed replacements for senate approval. SGA's own minutes of the same meeting name the resigning senators "Mitchell Stephens" and, for the third, only "Emmitt" with no surname recorded; this Herald account and the contemporaneous minutes disagree on the spelling and are given here as printed, unresolved.

events.title: Judicial Council removes senator for unexcused absences
events.body: Chief Justice Stuart Kenderes reported that the Judicial Council removed Senator Theodore Harden, a graduate student from Otisville, N.Y., from SGA for excessive unexcused absences; Harden did not attend the council meeting to defend himself. The council also reviewed Senator Vashae Swope for absences but voted to let her remain. Attendance guidelines were posted in the SGA office window, and Rachel Wilcox was approved as a new senator at the same meeting.

events.title: WKU begins weighing a smoke-free campus
events.body: After the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville went smoke-free, the Faculty Welfare Committee of Western's University Senate prepared a smoking survey for students, faculty and staff to take in February. SGA President Kevin Smiley said he would encourage the whole campus to take the survey, and President Gary Ransdell said he would look to SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council for direction on any policy.

events.title: Two more senators resign; Frankfort rally buses announced
events.body: At the Jan. 27 meeting, Aaron Pawley and Eileen Forsythe resigned as senators, Pawley because of a difficult course load and Forsythe because she was studying abroad in England. President Kevin Smiley announced free buses to carry 75 students to a Feb. 9 rally in Frankfort where advocates from Kentucky's public universities would lobby legislators on higher education funding. Western student Colton Jessie was slated to speak at the rally.

events.title: SGA organizes trip to Rally for Higher Education
events.body: SGA and the Provost's office offered free bus transportation for 75 students to the Rally for Higher Education on Feb. 9 at the Kentucky State Capitol, a year after winter weather derailed the previous attempt. Students who registered through the SGA website received an excused absence. This is a preview published before the rally; the archive holds no later report of how it went.

events.title: SGA passes election codes and two funding bills
events.body: The senate passed the spring 2010 election codes, a bill giving $500 to the Agriculture Students Striving for Effective Tomorrows conference for high school students, and a bill designating $1,200 for lodging for FIJIs Across America, in which eight Phi Gamma Delta members planned to cycle across the country for Alzheimer's research. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that all but three approved organizations had received their organizational aid checks.

events.title: Colton Jessie elected SGA president for 2010-11
events.body: Bowling Green junior Colton Jessie won the SGA presidency with 63 percent of the vote, taking 726 votes to 424 for Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, on a platform of sustainability, handicap accessibility and changing the tailgating policy. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president with 731 votes to Currie Martin's 415, and Wade Pierce ran unopposed for administrative vice president with 1,016 votes. Results were announced at midnight Wednesday.

events.title: Senate passes funding bills for baseball, a sorority event and study abroad
events.body: At its Feb. 22 meeting the senate unanimously passed a funding bill and, with single dissents apiece, a bill funding the baseball program and a $1,300 allocation for an Alpha Kappa Alpha event. It also unanimously approved several study-abroad reimbursement bills and confirmed Daniel Shaw as parliamentarian, along with a new Academic Affairs committee chair nominee and a new Student Affairs chair.

events.title: Provide-A-Ride was suspended and students started their own taxi
events.body: Parking and Transportation Services announced in September 2009 that Provide-A-Ride was suspended because the contract with Bowling Green Shuttle Service had ended. Three students, Zac Newton, Devon Hilderbrandt and Ryan Holland, set up Topper Taxi in the gap, charging $5 for one rider and $1 for each additional passenger. SGA administrative vice president Justin Thurman sat on the 18 September panel that reviewed bids from prospective providers, with a new operator due to be named on 1 October.

events.title: Western T-shirt swap traded rival logos for WKU red
events.body: SGA sponsored a T-shirt swap during finals week of spring 2010, letting students trade in shirts carrying other universities' logos for a Western shirt at the SGA office in DUC 130. Student affairs committee head Emmy Woosley introduced the idea; executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said the collected shirts would go to a philanthropy, though which one had not been decided. SGA also planned an event near Java City in Helm Library during the extended library hours it paid for that week.

events.title: SGA sets a dinner with lawmakers
events.body: SGA set its Dine with the Decision Makers for the evening of 8 December 2009, from 4:30 to 6 p.m. in the Cupola Room of Downing University Center, so students could talk about higher education with elected officials over dinner. President Kevin Smiley said 25 students had signed up through an online RSVP, a number capped by the cost of the dinner, and that five legislators and Bowling Green mayor Elaine Walker would attend. The event came out of a decision by the Board of Student Body Presidents that autumn that Kentucky's public universities should each mount student lobbying events.

events.title: Hall of Distinguished Seniors opened for autumn 2009
events.body: SGA extended the deadline for its autumn 2009 Hall of Distinguished Seniors applications on 12 November, to 2 p.m. the following Monday. SGA's website described the award as the highest recognition given to graduates by the student body.

events.title: Senate approved a $109,040.66 operating budget
events.body: At the second meeting of the eighth senate, with 19 of 23 senators present, the senate approved the 2009-10 operating budget of $109,040.66, capping organizational aid at $40,000 and Provide-A-Ride and non-emergency medical transport at $15,000, and leaving $20,000 for the senate to spend as it saw fit. The same meeting confirmed the president's cabinet, including his brother Eric Smiley as chief of staff on a vote with two abstentions; student Skylar Jordan then told the senate from the floor, speaking only as a student and not a member of the body, that he questioned the Senate's integrity for approving that appointment.

events.title: Skylar Jordan resigned, a week after three other senators
events.body: Senator Skylar Jordan resigned at the senate's meeting of 27 October 2009, held with 19 of 30 senators present, a week after Mitchell Stephens, Emmitt and Daniel Shaw had resigned at the meeting of 20 October. The Judicial Council reported it had made four decisions that night: one on office hours, two concerning senators' resignations, and one on attendance.

events.title: Senate elected next year's speaker as the Judicial Council certified the spring election
events.body: The senate elected Austin Wingate speaker of the Student Senate at its meeting of 13 April 2010. The Judicial Council reported at the same meeting that it had met and approved the spring election results, and that it was bringing three senators up for judicial review.

events.title: Judicial Council still working out office hours and attendance rules
events.body: At the eighth meeting of the eighth senate, held with 24 of 32 senators present, the Judicial Council reported it had met the previous week, had questions about office hours with an official decision planned the following week, and said it was still working out how to handle attendance.

events.title: Senate suspended its bylaws to seat an associate justice
events.body: At the senate's meeting of 2 March 2010, held with 21 of 30 senators present, the senate unanimously approved four presidential appointments as student senators — Kat Johns, Lucy George, Christopher Jankowski and Paul Shively — then suspended its bylaws to move Artilla Scisney from appointments to approvals, and voted unanimously to approve her as associate justice.
