leaders.name: Colton Jessie
leaders.note: Named as SGA president throughout the year's Herald coverage, including a dedicated year-end profile.
profile: Jessie opened the 2010-11 year having spent the summer preparing with his executive board, which attended the Kentucky Leadership Academy at Barren River State Park alongside SGAs from Kentucky's other public universities. His early priorities included building a closer relationship with international students, whom SGA hosted at a dinner during orientation, planning a study away program for students to study elsewhere in the country, and setting up a forum for South Campus concerns. "We are trying to reach out to South Campus," he said, and he and Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan reallocated the budget to fund scholarship and study abroad programs.

By the end of his term, SGA had given out more scholarship money than ever, with the scholarship fund raised by $8,000 and organizational aid increased to $40,000, and the senate had passed first-of-their-kind bills reimbursing CLEP exam fees and buying test prep books for libraries. Jessie called the DUC renovation "one of the biggest things SGA has done in a while," and Ransdell credited him with taking the initiative to start the renovation talks. A senior, Jessie handed the office to Billy Stephens and left for Chicago after graduation to work for Teach for America.

events.title: SGA raised scholarship budget to $20,000
events.body: After running out of scholarship money the previous year, SGA increased its scholarship budget from $12,000 to $20,000 and lowered general senate funding from $20,000 to $12,000 to cover the change. Study abroad awards were capped at $500 for a semester trip and $250 for a winter or summer term so more students could receive money. SGA also finalized a new study away scholarship for travel inside the country and set aside $400 for it in the winter term.

events.title: Twelve senators elected in fall election with 847 voters
events.body: Twelve students won seats in the fall senate election, in which 847 total voters cast ballots on TopNet. Keyana Boka, Natalie Broderick and Eppiphanie Benton were elected freshman senators, running unopposed, while 25 students competed for the at-large seats. Winners included Diego Leal Ambriz, who would run for president that spring.

events.title: Ransdell brought $49 million DUC renovation plan to SGA
events.body: President Gary Ransdell and head architect Jeff Stivers told SGA at its Nov. 16 meeting that officials were moving ahead on a plan to completely renovate Downing University Center at a cost of up to $49 million. Students would pay about $140 extra per year in fees for up to 20 years, and Ransdell promised students would be involved in every decision. SGA had to pass resolutions on the design and fees before the Board of Regents could approve the project.

events.title: Senate tabled DUC resolution over lack of student input
events.body: Senators tabled the bill supporting the DUC renovation at the Dec. 7 meeting, saying they had not received enough student input just three weeks after learning of the project. Jessie backed the delay, saying he wanted to hear students' voices before moving forward, even though it pushed SGA's presentation to the Board of Regents from January 21 to April 22. Campus Improvements Chair Kaylee Egerer said many students did not yet know they would pay $140 a year for the project.

events.title: Herald reported Greeks held 40 percent of SGA seats
events.body: The Herald reported that 21 of SGA's 50 members belonged to Greek organizations, more than 40 percent, while less than 8 percent of the student body was in a fraternity or sorority. Sixteen of the 21 were fraternity men, and two fraternities, Sigma Chi and Lambda Chi Alpha, accounted for nine of them. Officers defended the imbalance, and the story noted SGA's operating budget for 2010-11 was $121,335, drawn from tuition.

events.title: SGA unanimously passed DUC renovation resolution
events.body: SGA unanimously passed the resolution supporting DUC renovations at its Feb. 22 meeting, the bill's second reading. Project costs were capped at $49,128,545, with a student fee of up to $70 per semester for 20 years and $1.5 million per year from WKU. The resolution, authored by Kaylee Egerer, asked for assurance of a 24-hour study space and called for construction to begin as soon as possible while interest rates were low.

events.title: SGA members joined Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort
events.body: SGA members traveled to Frankfort on March 1 for the annual Rally for Higher Education, where SGA secretary Katie Stillwell was the keynote speaker representing students statewide. Her speech urged legislators to protect money already set aside for higher education. Jessie, the previous year's keynote speaker, joined chief of staff Charlie Harris and other state SGA officers for a lunch with Gov. Steve Beshear.

events.title: Stephens won presidency with 56 percent of 1,066 votes
events.body: Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, defeated senior Diego Leal Ambriz for SGA president, taking 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes in results announced just after midnight on April 7. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president and Devon Hilderbrandt won administrative vice president, both unopposed. All 35 senate candidates were elected to the 36 open seats, each needing just one vote to win.

events.title: Senate tabled tobacco-free campus resolution
events.body: After nearly 45 minutes of debate, the senate tabled a resolution supporting a tobacco-free campus until the next semester. The resolution rested on a survey of more than 400 students in which 47.82 percent supported a ban, but senators argued the survey was biased because tombstones displaying the dangers of smoking had been laid outside DUC the day it was given. The campus improvements committee then said it would not support a ban until the two-year on-campus living requirement was removed.

events.title: SGA funds extended library hours for finals week
events.body: The senate approved $600 to keep the library open until 2 a.m. during finals week, covering extra staff time and lighting. President Colton Jessie said continuing the service was never in question, calling finals "an important time for students."

events.title: Administrative Vice President Wade Pierce to hand post to fraternity brother
events.body: Pierce, who chaired the organizational aid committee, said he would be succeeded as administrative vice president by Devon Hilderbrandt, his committee co-chair and his "little brother" in Lambda Chi Alpha. Hilderbrandt ran unopposed in that spring's election.

events.title: SGA listed its signature services, including Western Wednesdays
events.body: In a commentary published on 10 September 2010, executive vice president Kendrick Bryan set out SGA's standing services: organizational aid of more than $40,000 a year with up to $500 per group, Provide-A-Ride, study abroad scholarships and scholar development grants, free blue books and Scantron forms in the SGA office at DUC 130, and Western Wednesdays, a discount for students wearing WKU apparel honoured by thirteen restaurants. SGA was operating on a budget of $110,000.

leaders.name: Billy Stephens
leaders.note: Named as SGA president throughout the year's Herald coverage, from his April 2011 election through spring 2012 budget and personnel stories.
profile: Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, was elected SGA president in the spring 2011 election, announced just after midnight on April 7. He defeated Diego Leal Ambriz, a senior from Monterrey, Mexico, with 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes. Outgoing president Colton Jessie called him "a fantastic candidate for the job," and Kendrick Bryan and Devon Hilderbrandt were elected unopposed as his executive and administrative vice presidents.

Stephens opened his term in August 2011 with a revamped public relations campaign built around asking students what SGA could do for them. "I want PR to be visible on campus," he said, complaining that new students often did not hear about SGA until the second semester. The campaign aimed to raise turnout in the fall senate elections, produce contested races and fill all 36 senate seats.

The fall brought open conflict: the senate voted down, 19-8, a resolution to rename Downing University Center that campus improvements chair Keyana Boka had written, the Herald editorial board told Stephens to focus on his own platform promises instead, two senators were dismissed for absences, and SGA was surprised by a $15,000 bill for the prior administration's unpaid Provide-A-Ride service. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell resigned before the spring semester was out; Stephens replaced her with Eric Smiley, who had held the same post two years earlier under his brother's administration. The senate passed a spring budget of $50,026 in February 2012, down from $54,000 in fall spending.

events.title: Senate reconvenes, appointments confirmed, tobacco vote postponed
events.body: At the semester's first senate meeting, held after the previous week's session was canceled, senators postponed a vote on the tobacco-free campus resolution so new members could review it first. President Billy Stephens made all of his executive-branch, judicial-committee and committee-chair appointments in a single blanket vote that passed unanimously, and Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer told senators to keep generating new ideas for their committees.

events.title: SGA passes tobacco-free campus resolution with housing condition
events.body: The SGA senate voted unanimously for a resolution supporting a campus-wide tobacco ban, but only if WKU dropped its requirement that students live on campus for two years. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a ban until SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council all passed resolutions. SGA was the only body to attach the housing stipulation.

events.title: SGA to lend iPads through WKU's Educational Resource Center
events.body: SGA partnered with the Educational Resource Center in Gary Ransdell Hall to provide two first-generation iPads for the ERC to load textbooks onto and lend out to students at no cost, part of President Billy Stephens' push to make the organization more visibly useful to students.

events.title: Senate defeats the DUC name change resolution 19-8
events.body: A resolution to rename Downing University Center as Downing Student Union, written by campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, was defeated 19-8 with one abstention after a long open debate; a motion to table it was voted down as well. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan had suggested putting the question to students on the spring ballot, as was done in 2006, but senators noted that the architects working on the DUC renovation would need an answer sooner than that.

events.title: Herald editorial tells SGA to drop renaming and keep its promises
events.body: The Herald editorial board wrote that SGA should focus on student issues rather than renaming a building honoring former president Dero Downing, who had recently died. It said Stephens had barely addressed his platform promises, including a dead day before finals and an improved Provide-a-Ride service, which had seen no visible progress since SGA cut ties with Franklin Taxi.

events.title: Chief of Staff Eric Smiley approved after Stillwell's resignation
events.body: The senate approved President Billy Stephens' choice of Eric Smiley as chief of staff after Katie Stillwell resigned the post; Smiley had served as chief of staff two years earlier under his brother Kevin Smiley's administration. The same meeting passed five bills, including two Organizational Aid grants of $500 each to six campus groups (the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, Geology Club, Chinese Music Club, Relay for Life, International Club and Baptist Campus Ministry), $500 toward the April 19 International Night, $398 reimbursing two Kindle Fires raffled at the WKU Student Research Conference, and $500 toward Big Red's trip to the 2012 Mascot Nationals. Senators also passed a resolution for a second campus cleanup on April 17 and moved $3,000 from general senate funds to Organizational Aid so SGA could spend down its budget before the semester's end; announcements noted that spring executive elections would open at 12:01 a.m. the next day.

events.title: Dodds elected SGA president for 2012-13; Boka and Alvey win uncontested VP races
events.body: Cory Dodds was elected SGA president for 2012-13 with 44 percent of the vote, over senator Corey Johnson with 35 percent and former senator Austin Wingate with 21 percent. Sophomore Keyana Boka was elected executive vice president and Cain Alvey administrative vice president; both vice-presidential races were uncontested.

events.title: SGA ties tobacco ban support to ending two-year housing rule
events.body: The SGA senate passed a tobacco-free campus resolution that supported a ban only if the requirement for students to live on campus for two years was eliminated. Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer said SGA backed the ban "if and only if" the housing requirement went. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a tobacco-free campus until the University Senate, Staff Council and SGA each passed their own resolutions.

events.title: SGA waives its own process to oppose faculty regent term limits
events.body: SGA passed a resolution recommending that the Faculty Regent seat on the Board of Regents carry no term limit, following a University Senate recommendation the week before. The senate waived the usual two-week process of a first reading followed by a vote the next week. A bill funding the Cage the Elephant concert received its first read at the same meeting.

events.title: SGA spent $8,000 on Cage the Elephant concert, approving part of it afterward
events.body: SGA co-sponsored the Sept. 21 Cage the Elephant concert with the Campus Activities Board, splitting the costs. President Billy Stephens said the executive cabinet took $5,000 from executive discretionary money, which does not require senate approval, while a bill allocating a further $3,000 in senate funding passed on the Tuesday after the concert had already taken place. Stephens said there had been no rush for the funding because CAB had already covered the expenses up front.

events.title: Ransdell tells SGA the two-year housing requirement cannot be dropped
events.body: In his first visit to SGA that semester, President Gary Ransdell told senators that eliminating the two-year on-campus housing requirement did not work "from a business standpoint." He said debts remained to be paid on dormitory renovations, so a certain number of students had to live in the dorms. SGA had been the only campus governing body to make removal of the housing requirement a condition of its tobacco ban resolution.

events.title: Organizational aid bill passes for five student groups
events.body: SGA passed an organizational aid funding bill covering Black Men at Western, Women in Transition, the Western Kentucky Pre-Dental Society, Students in Free Enterprise and the Kentucky Public Health Association student chapter. A second aid bill received its first read, proposing $1,000 from the organizational aid fund for the Black Student Alliance and the WKU Habitat for Humanity campus chapter. Senators also discussed continuing work on Provide-A-Ride.

events.title: Speaker says she never expects Regents to adopt SGA's tobacco ban version
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer said she did not expect the Board of Regents ever to enact SGA's version of the tobacco ban because the housing requirement was such a key factor. She said linking the two was necessary because requiring tobacco users to live on a tobacco-free campus was "infringing on students' rights." Egerer called the proposed ban "totally unfair and unrealistic."

events.title: SGA funds extended library hours and $2,500 in organizational aid
events.body: SGA passed a bill allocating $600 to Helm-Cravens Library to stay open until 2 a.m. from Sunday through Thursday of finals week, an annual practice. A second bill allocated $2,500 total to the Student Affairs Graduate Association, MBA Student Association, Topper Well, WKU Eco-Club, WKU Black Graduate Student Association and Kappa Alpha Psi. Three scholarship allocation bills received first reads.

events.title: SGA cancels $1,175 bus to Frankfort rally after eight sign up
events.body: SGA canceled the bus it had planned to run to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, arranging carpools instead. As of that Friday only eight people had confirmed they were attending, and the bus would have cost $1,175, about $150 per student. The Tuesday night meeting, previously canceled for the rally, was reinstated.

events.title: Herald editorial says SGA should and could do more
events.body: A Herald editorial said that after two short meetings and no new plans on the agenda, SGA appeared not to be on the ball, and urged it to do more before the semester ended. The editorial singled out the loss of the Provide-A-Ride service and the failure to find a replacement provider despite an offer from Parking and Transportation Services. SGA had said it would work toward a new service but admitted it was not feasible before the semester ended.

events.title: Free speech resolution on student handbook delayed four weeks
events.body: A resolution supporting removal of the "External Computer Use and Ethics" section from the student handbook, which its backers said restricted freedom of speech, was scheduled for a second read. Its author, senator Christopher Costa, pushed it back four weeks to do additional research. The section warned that student posts on sites such as Facebook could be seen by university officials and that communications deemed inappropriate might lead to discipline.

events.title: Senator removed for absences is reappointed by the president
events.body: Louisville sophomore Kevin Adams, removed from the senate the previous semester for excessive absences, returned through a presidential appointment by President Billy Stephens. Adams said he was less busy and had more time for SGA. Stephens said Adams had overbooked himself and that the two were good friends who had stayed close after the removal.

events.title: Chief of staff resigns over grades; predecessor takes the job back
events.body: Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell announced her resignation at the Tuesday senate meeting, having officially resigned March 16. She said she stepped down because her grades were slipping ahead of a May graduation. President Billy Stephens named former chief of staff Eric Smiley as her replacement quickly enough that she did not need to serve out her two weeks' notice.

events.title: Spring election postponed a day by TopNet failure
events.body: The spring election, set to run from March 27 to 28, was pushed back to March 28-29 because of campus-wide problems with TopNet. Director of Information Technology Cory Dodds said the election would slip another week if repairs were not finished in time. The executive cabinet made the decision with Charley Pride, director of student activities and organizations.

events.title: SGA gave about $34,000 in organizational aid to roughly 50 groups
events.body: Administrative Vice President Devon Hilderbrandt said SGA distributed around $34,000 in organizational aid over the year, helping about 50 organizations. Groups applied online, met with the organizational aid committee, and could receive a maximum of $500 each. Senator Corey Johnson, who served on the committee, said the committee had been strict about what it funded.

events.title: Transgender inclusion resolution tabled after debate
events.body: A resolution by senator Kevin Asbery supporting policies more inclusive of transgender and gender-nonconforming students was tabled after debate. The resolution would have encouraged the university and its departments to revise policies and stated that WKU lacked adequate gender-neutral facilities, including housing and restrooms. Asbery said the issue had recently been brought to his attention.

events.title: Transgender resolution passes 18-5 at final meeting of the year
events.body: At the last meeting of the year the senate passed the transgender and gender-nonconforming support resolution 18-5, with four senators abstaining. The resolution encouraged WKU to create gender-neutral housing and restrooms in all university buildings and to revise policies to be more inclusive. Students who were not SGA members attended specifically to watch the vote, and debate covered student safety, cost and whether separate housing would isolate students.

events.title: Safe ride program finalized to replace Provide-A-Ride
events.body: President-elect Cory Dodds said SGA had finalized a partnership with Parking and Transportation to run a safe ride program in the fall, after a year without one. SGA's share would cost $15,000 for the school year, the same as under Provide-A-Ride. The earlier service had been a $30,000 contract split with Parking Services until original provider Franklin Taxi ceased its affiliation with WKU.

events.title: Free scantrons and blue books, a sponsored football game and a tailgate
events.body: At the meeting of 27 September 2011 SGA reported that free scantrons and blue books were now available in its office. It was sponsoring that Saturday's football game and an accompanying tailgating event for which students could register online, and it hosted a forum in DUC on the coming renovations from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Campus Cleanup was set for 11 October with service credit offered.

src.label: Herald, 28 Sep 2011 - "SGA to host unveiling of DUC renovations"

events.title: Campus Clean-up ran during Make A Difference Week
events.body: Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka organised the Campus Clean-up for 11 October 2011, with service credit offered and gloves donated by the biology department. Seventeen senators volunteered alongside student athletes and a fraternity pledge class, and the group worked from Centennial Mall up the Hill to Cherry Hall and back to DUC. Boka said the clean-up ran twice a year, in Make A Difference Week each autumn and during Greek Week each spring.

src.label: Herald, 10 Oct 2011 - "WKU's SGA organizing Tuesday's Campus Clean-up"

events.title: Croakies handed out at the Homecoming tailgate
events.body: SGA gave away croakies, straps that hold sunglasses round the neck, from its tent on South Lawn at Homecoming tailgating in October 2011. Administrative vice president Devon Hilderbrandt said the idea came from a summer retreat where members looked at what Kentucky and Eastern Kentucky handed out, and that croakies were cheaper than T-shirts or cups at about 75 cents each. The senate allocated up to $350 for roughly 250 of them.

events.title: Thanksgiving dinner for students who stayed on campus
events.body: SGA and the Department of Housing and Residence Life co-sponsored a free Thanksgiving dinner on the 27th floor of Pearce-Ford Tower on 24 November 2011, open to PFT residents, international students, university police and anyone else left on campus. Attendance was expected at 50 to 60. SGA provided $220 for food and supplies; the funding bill gave the dinner an educational purpose, teaching international students about American Thanksgiving. It was the sixth year of the dinner and SGA's third as a co-sponsor.

src.label: Herald, 24 Nov 2011 - "SGA co-sponsors Thanksgiving dinner for those at WKU"

events.title: Third Dine with Decision Makers added the regents
events.body: SGA held its third Dine with Decision Makers on 1 December 2011 in the Cupola Room, free to students who booked online. President Billy Stephens said it was the first year the Board of Regents and university administration had been invited alongside legislators, and Gary Ransdell attended. Fourteen decision makers were confirmed, including the mayors of Glasgow, Owensboro and Elizabethtown, Warren County Judge Executive Mike Buchanon and Kentucky State Police Commissioner Rodney Brewer.

src.label: Herald, 2 Dec 2011 - "WKU administrators, government officials attend Dine with Decision Makers"

events.title: SGA cancelled its meeting for an NCAA tournament viewing party
events.body: SGA called off its senate meeting on 13 March 2012 and instead hosted a free viewing of WKU's NCAA tournament game against Mississippi State in the Mass Media and Technology Hall Auditorium, with doors at 5 p.m. and food and drinks provided. Executive vice president Kendrick Bryan said SGA had first hoped to hand out tickets to the game in Dayton but distribution proved impossible because the tickets were sold through Ticketmaster at the University of Dayton. A second viewing was planned if WKU advanced.

src.label: Herald, 13 Mar 2012 - "SGA cancels Tuesday night meeting to host viewing party for NCAA game"

events.title: SGA co-sponsored International Night with $500
events.body: The senate passed a bill on 27 March 2012 giving $500 to International Night 2012, held free in DUC 224 on 19 April with food, a culture expo and a concert headlined by the Brazilian swing group Trio Ginga. SGA's co-sponsors were Downing University Center and the office of International Programs. Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, a bill author, said supporting diversity was part of what SGA was.

events.title: Campus Cleanup and Safety Walk on the same afternoon
events.body: SGA ran its spring Campus Cleanup from 4 to 5 p.m. on 17 April 2012 and held the Campus Safety Walk immediately after the senate meeting the same evening. Campus improvements chair Keyana Boka said the two were paired because neither took long. On the walk members noted dim areas and blue emergency lights that were not working.

src.label: Herald, 10 Apr 2012 - "SGA organizes events to improve campus"

events.title: Senate gave $200 to Invisible Children after a fight over it
events.body: On 17 April 2012 the senate passed a bill allocating $200 to WKU's chapter of Invisible Children for its Cover the Night event, held that Friday at 9 p.m. in the Mass Media Auditorium to publicise the hunt for Joseph Kony. Several senators objected; Poorvie Patel was the first to challenge how the national campaign spent donations. The bill passed despite the debate.

src.label: Herald, 18 Apr 2012 - "SGA awards $200 to WKU's Invisible Children after debate"

events.title: Senate funds a transcript voucher programme
events.body: The first bill passed at the SGA meeting on Tuesday 28 February 2012 allocated $1,225 for transcript vouchers, so that students applying for scholarships, jobs and graduate or professional school could get copies of their official transcripts free. A total of 175 vouchers were to be available, with a limit of two per student. A second bill put $500 of general senate funding into five $100 Study Away scholarships, and a further $2,300 went to Scholar Development Grant Awards and Study Abroad Awards. An organisational aid bill allocating $2,400 to five student groups had its first reading at the same meeting.
events.money: $1,225 for 175 vouchers; $500 in Study Away scholarships; $2,300 in grants; $2,400 organisational aid on first reading

events.title: Two senators dismissed for absences as ten of 36 faced judicial review
events.body: Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from committee and full senate meetings. Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston were dismissed after failing to attend their judicial hearings, and Justice Chris Jankowski said each had between eight and 10 absences. Chief Justice David Spalding said the council treated a failure to appear at a review as intent to resign. The other senators received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements for the two empty seats.

events.title: SGA paid a surprise $15,000 Provide-A-Ride bill from aid and scholarship funds
events.body: SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive charge for the previous year's Provide-A-Ride service, taking $7,500 each from the organizational aid and student scholarship funds. President Billy Stephens said he was "shocked" to be notified of the payment the week before, and that Parking Services had no record of receiving the money from the previous administration. Because the SGA budget does not roll over between years, no prior-year money was available to cover it. 2010-11 president Colton Jessie said his administration had budgeted the payment.

events.title: Fall senate election filled 11 seats with 977 votes cast
events.body: SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 senators elected from a field of 20 candidates and 977 students voting. Those elected were Kelley Boothe, Hannah Garland, Corey Johnson, Elizabeth Wininger, Mallory Chaney, Mallory Treece, Kevin Asbery, Christopher Costa, Jordan Campbell, Nolan Miles and Ross Nowland. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he had got the contested race he wanted.

events.title: SGA approved a $50,026 spring budget after spending $54,000 in the fall
events.body: The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, of which $43,476.17 remained. It was divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid, $12,000 for scholarships and $5,500 in stipends already spent. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment.

events.title: Cage the Elephant played to several thousand on South Lawn
events.body: SGA and the Campus Activities Board co-sponsored a free outdoor show on South Lawn on the Wednesday night, with Manchester Orchestra also on the bill. The hour-long set was nearly shut down halfway through when the crowd pressed the front guard rail hard enough that singer Matt Shultz was asked to warn people back, telling them legs were being broken. The concert doubled as the launch party for the Starry Nights Music Festival, which had been cancelled that year, and its founder Bryan Graves worked the front of the stage holding the gate up and pulling out crowd surfers.
events.money: several thousand in the crowd, by the promoter's estimate

events.title: SGA announced a DUC forum for the day the regents saw the plans
events.body: At the 27 September 2011 meeting SGA said it would host an unveiling of the Downing University Center renovation plans at DUC from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., following the Board of Regents meeting that Friday at which the plans were to be shown. It was to be set up as a forum so students could learn about the renovation. This is what was announced; the Herald report was printed before the event and does not say how it went.

events.title: Four SGA members attend Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort
events.body: WKU sent four representatives to the statewide Rally for Higher Education: Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan, Director of Information Technology Cory Dodds, Associate Justice Chris Jankowski and Senator Mallory Treece. President Billy Stephens stayed behind for class and the senate meeting. The rally protested a proposed 6.4 percent cut to Kentucky's postsecondary education budget; WKU's delegation was smaller than in past years, when 12 to 30 students had attended.

events.title: Treece named public relations committee head
events.body: SGA passed its first bill of the spring semester, an organizational aid bill funding seven campus groups, at the same meeting where Jane Wood returned as public relations director and senator Mallory Treece was named public relations committee head.

events.title: Costa elected new speaker of SGA senate
events.body: Senators elected Christopher Costa the 2012-13 speaker of the student senate over fellow senator Poorvie Patel and public relations committee head Mallory Treece. Costa, a sophomore and Army veteran, told senators his military service taught him to follow before he learned to lead.

src2.label: Herald, 20 Apr 2012

events.title: New SGA officers sworn in at banquet
events.body: Incoming president Cory Dodds, executive vice president Keyana Boka, administrative vice president Cain Alvey and speaker of the senate Christopher Costa were sworn in for 2012-13 at SGA's end-of-year banquet; Costa received the speaker's gavel from outgoing speaker Kaylee Egerer. Outgoing president Billy Stephens credited Dodds with running a strong campaign.

executive.name: Kendrick Bryan
executive.note: Won re-election unopposed after Katie Stillwell dropped out of the EVP race.
profile: Kendrick Bryan was elected executive vice president for 2009-10 under President Kevin Smiley, and won re-election to the post twice more: in the March 2010 election over Currie Martin, campaigning in a Herald commentary for students to "vote for an organization you can stand up and cheer for," and again in March 2011, unopposed after his only declared challenger, Secretary of the Senate Katie Stillwell, dropped out of the race. He served three consecutive years as executive vice president, under presidents Smiley, Colton Jessie and Billy Stephens.

As EVP under Jessie in 2010-11, Bryan helped reallocate the SGA budget toward scholarship and study-abroad funding. He was also hired to teach a section of University Experience, WKU's freshman orientation course, in the autumn after his final term ended. Keyana Boka, who ran to succeed him as EVP that spring, said she had worked closely with Bryan on SGA projects and that he had helped her learn the office; Bryan said he had not recruited a successor himself but backed her decision to run.

After leaving SGA, Bryan ran as a Democrat for the Kentucky House's 25th District against incumbent Jimmie Lee, in an election the Herald reported on 24 May 2012. He took 18.62 percent of the vote to Lee's 77.63 percent and third-place candidate Glenn Fonda's 3.75 percent, campaigning on government transparency and university funding without accepting outside campaign contributions, spending roughly $1,000 of his own money. He said afterward he could see himself running again. In July 2013, identified by the Herald as a former SGA officer, he wrote a commentary defending President Cory Dodds's decision to keep the Downing University Center's name against a later administration-driven change to Downing Student Union, arguing the Student Senate had already voted against renaming it and student opinion had not shifted.

profile: Devon Hilderbrandt joined SGA in fall 2010 after his fraternity big brother, administrative vice president Wade Pierce, encouraged him to get more involved on campus. He joined the organizational aid committee under Pierce, became his co-chair, and ran unopposed to succeed him as administrative vice president for 2011-12.

As administrative vice president, Hilderbrandt oversaw SGA's organizational aid program, which gave out roughly $34,000 to about 50 student organizations that year. Students applied online, and Hilderbrandt read every application himself before an organization could meet with the organizational aid committee; the maximum award to any one organization was $500.

executive.name: Katie Stillwell
executive.note: Resigned before spring 2012 was out; succeeded by Eric Smiley on 28 Mar 2012.
profile: Katie Stillwell served as secretary of the student senate for 2010-11. In March 2011 she ran against Kendrick Bryan for executive vice president, saying she had worked hard in the legislative branch and felt she could help on the executive side; she later dropped out, and Bryan was re-elected unopposed.

Named chief of staff for 2011-12, Stillwell announced her resignation at the Senate meeting of 20 March 2012, telling it she had always taken the position seriously but that her grades had slipped over the year under the combined load of a part-time job and roughly 10 hours a week of SGA work, and that continuing without doing the work properly would not have been ethical. President Billy Stephens thanked her for her service, and named former chief of staff Eric Smiley — who had held the post two years earlier under President Kevin Smiley, his brother — to finish out the term.

executive.note: Director of academic and student affairs in 2011-12. He said the transcript voucher programme mattered because it offset student costs, and that SGA had held it back a semester over budget problems, scheduling difficulties and planning rather than run a programme that would fail.

executive.name: Cory Dodds
executive.note: Launched SGA's off-campus housing site earlier in the autumn of 2011 and rebuilt the SGA website in December to match WKU's new university template, a change mandated because SGA sits under the Student Activities Office. He was an author of the transcript voucher bill and one of four WKU members at the February 2012 Frankfort rally.

committees.note: Authored the failed resolution to rename Downing University Center. Spelling of first name unverified against "Keyanna," used for the same person's later presidential term.

officers.name: Kaylee Egerer
profile: Kaylee Egerer was Speaker of the Senate in 2011-12, under President Billy Stephens. At the semester's first meeting on 6 September 2011 senators postponed a vote on the tobacco-free campus resolution so new members could review it, and Stephens's executive, judicial and committee-chair appointments were confirmed in a single unanimous vote.

Egerer became a leading voice for SGA's position on the proposed tobacco ban. When the Senate passed its resolution on 13 September 2011 she said SGA supported a campus ban "if and only if" the requirement that students live on campus for two years was ended. She later said she never expected the Board of Regents to adopt SGA's version because the housing link was so central, and called the ban as proposed unfair and unrealistic.
At SGA's end-of-year banquet on the night of 8 May 2012 she handed the speaker's gavel to her successor, Christopher Costa, as the incoming 2012-13 officers were sworn in.

officers.name: Rachel Calhoun
officers.note: Secretary of the student senate in 2011-12. She also worked on organisational aid, which gave out around $34,000 to about fifty student organisations that year, and said funding had to reach a lot of students rather than pay for a party.
profile: Rachel Calhoun served as secretary of the student senate in 2011-12 and worked on SGA's organizational aid committee, which distributed roughly $34,000 to about fifty student groups that year in grants capped at $500 each. She said one of the criteria for funding was that a grant should not simply pay for a party unless the event was open to a large number of students: "It had to affect a lot of students and be legitimate." She recalled a trip by a group of Chinese students touring Kentucky's sites and culture as one of the more memorable requests the committee funded. In May 2012 she spoke in the senate's debate over a resolution backing gender-neutral and transgender-inclusive campus housing, arguing that student government was there to listen to students and that SGA should support a group of them who said they didn't feel safe; the resolution passed.

officers.name: David Spalding

He ran the November 2011 judicial reviews in which senators Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston were dismissed after failing to attend their hearings, saying the council reads a failure to appear as intent to resign. Ten of the senate's 36 senators were called up for excessive absences; the rest were warned, and Spalding was to administer the oaths to the two replacements.
profile: David Spalding was SGA's chief justice in 2011-12. That November he ran the semester's judicial reviews after nearly a third of the senate's 36 members were called up for excessive absences; two senators, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed after failing to attend their own review hearings, which he said the judicial council read as an intention to resign. Spalding said the rest were given the sternest of warnings and that the branch would administer oaths to their replacements, calling the episode a "very minor speed bump" and noting some senators flagged for review had simply had trouble submitting absence excuses to the right place on SGA's website. In February 2012, after President Billy Stephens moved to reappoint Adams to the senate, Spalding said Stephens had not needed the judicial branch's sign-off but the two had discussed the situation; he noted SGA's constitution has no rule barring a removed senator's return, so long as they affirm they again have the time for it.

officers.name: Chris Jankowski
officers.note: Explained the council's absence rules to the Herald and trailed a judicial opinion reinterpreting the constitution to give senators more leeway; he was one of four WKU members at the February 2012 Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort.
profile: Chris Jankowski was appointed an associate justice of SGA's Judicial Council on 29 March 2011, alongside Aaron Pawley, when Art Scisney was elevated to chief justice. He continued on the council into 2011-12, when nearly a third of the senate's 36 members were called before judicial review for excessive absences; Jankowski said the two dismissed senators, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, had racked up eight to ten absences across senate and committee meetings, while Chief Justice David Spalding said the council read a failure to appear at a review hearing as intent to resign. Jankowski told the Herald the council would soon issue a judicial opinion reinterpreting the constitution to give senators "a little more leeway" on absences. In February 2012 he was one of four WKU SGA members who traveled to Frankfort for the Rally for Higher Education, held to protest a proposed 6.4 percent cut to Kentucky's post-secondary education budget, telling the Herald that students needed to get their voice out and make themselves heard on the need for funding.

members.name: Kevin Adams

Corroborates the dismissal already noted on Chief Justice Spalding's entry. Reappointed as a senator at large on 28 February 2012 and remained active in debate through the spring.

members.name: Cain Alvey
members.note: Accepted as a senator alongside Andreu Edge on a motion passed 15 November 2011 and sworn in the same night by Chief Justice Spalding. Went on to serve as administrative vice president in 2012-13 (already recorded separately for that year).

members.name: Mallory Chaney
members.note: Introduced herself as the incoming 2012-13 Campus Improvements committee chair on 28 August 2012, saying "Last year I was a senator." The minutes record a "Senator Chaney" offering a friendly amendment on 14 February 2012, consistent with this self-description.

members.name: Hannalore Clause
members.note: Accepted as a senator on a motion by Senator Cottrell on 18 October 2011, filling the Gatton Academy Senator-at-Large seat, and sworn in the same night by Chief Justice Spalding. The document itself spells the name both "Hannalore Clause" and "Hannahlore Clause"; spelling unverified.

members.name: Tori Conyers

members.name: Christopher Costa

members.name: Richard Crumbie
members.note: Approved as a senator at large in a blanket vote on 28 February 2012, alongside JD Shadburne, Hayley Wilkins, Catherine Havel, Tori Conyers and Kevin Adams. Spoke in favor of the gender-neutral housing resolution on 1 May 2012, saying the senate should vote for what students need. Continued as a senator into 2012-13 (recorded separately for that year).

members.name: Andreu Edge
members.note: Accepted as a senator alongside Cain Alvey on a motion passed 15 November 2011 and sworn in the same night by Chief Justice Spalding. Continued speaking in floor debate that spring, including questioning funding for the Invisible Children "Cover the Night" bill on 17 April 2012.

members.name: Hannah Garland
members.note: Active as "Senator Garland" through spring 2012, including offering a friendly amendment on 21 February 2012. Full name confirmed via Hannah Garland, who introduced herself that August as the incoming 2012-13 Academic Affairs committee chair; no other Garland appears in the corpus.

members.name: Catherine Havel
members.note: Approved as a senator at large in a blanket vote on 28 February 2012, alongside JD Shadburne, Hayley Wilkins, Richard Crumbie, Tori Conyers and Kevin Adams. Continued as an active senator into May, questioning the gender-neutral housing resolution on 1 May 2012.

members.name: John Hughes
members.note: Accepted as a senator on a motion by Senator Patel on 27 September 2011 and sworn in the same night by Chief Justice Spalding.

members.name: Mac Mullins
members.note: Named as "Mac Mullins" in Secretary Calhoun's announcement urging students to support him, Cory Dodds and Billy Stephens at a game; the same 14 February 2012 meeting's minutes record "Senator Mullins" moving to adjourn, tying the two together. Active as a senator through spring 2012 before chairing the Public Relations committee in 2012-13 (already recorded separately for that year).

members.name: Josh Newman
members.note: President Stephens said "Josh Newman is on the committee" during debate on Bill 7-11-F on 25 October 2011, and Senator Newman spoke immediately afterward in the same exchange, tying the full name to the senator title.

members.name: Kevin Preston
members.note: Named in full by Judicial Council member Chris Jankowski as one of two senators removed from the senate for failing to attend an absence-review hearing, reported to the Senate on 1 November 2011 ("we reviewed thirteen senators and ended up removing Kevin Preston and Kevin Adams"). Corroborates the dismissal already noted on Chief Justice Spalding's entry. A "Senator Preston" gave an officer announcement on 6 September 2011, before the dismissal. No further record of him in the corpus after 1 November 2011; later mentions of "Preston" in the corpus refer to the Preston Center building, not this person.

members.name: JD Shadburne
members.note: Approved as a senator at large in a blanket vote on 28 February 2012, alongside Hayley Wilkins, Catherine Havel, Richard Crumbie, Tori Conyers and Kevin Adams. Continued moving Senate business as "Senator Shadburne" through the spring, including Bill 20-12-S on 24 April 2012.

members.name: Daniel Shaw
members.note: Named as the author of the Campus Improvements committee's legislation in Keyana Boka's committee report on 14 February 2012 ("written by Daniel Shaw"). A "Senator Shaw" is one of the most frequent speakers in floor debate throughout 2011-12, moving amendments and questioning bills at nearly every meeting.

members.name: Eric Smiley
members.note: Introduced himself to the senate on 27 March 2012 as the nominee for chief of staff, saying he had been chief of staff in 2009-10 "and then served as a senator the next year." A "Senator Smiley" is recorded moving and debating senate business through the fall of 2011 (e.g., moved to adjourn on 4 October 2011, questioned a bill on 15 November 2011), and no other Smiley appears in the corpus. Became chief of staff for the rest of 2011-12 succeeding Katie Stillwell (already recorded).

members.name: Hayley Wilkins
members.note: Approved as a senator at large in a blanket vote on 28 February 2012, alongside JD Shadburne, Catherine Havel, Richard Crumbie, Tori Conyers and Kevin Adams. Introduced herself on 28 August 2012 as the incoming 2012-13 Public Relations committee chair, saying "I was a senator last semester." Mac Mullins had taken over as Public Relations chair by February 2013, so she held the post for only part of 2012-13.

leaders.name: Cory Dodds

sources.label: WKU Office of Scholar Development, 2 May 2012
WKU Office of Scholar Development, 15 Nov 2012
University of Kentucky J. David Rosenberg College of Law faculty profile

profile: Cory Dodds, a junior political science major from Smithland, Kentucky, was elected SGA president for 2012-13 in spring 2012 over Austin Wingate and Corey Johnson, after two years as SGA's director of information technology, during which he built a legislation and minutes archive for the SGA website that he said promoted transparency and accountability. Under the merged offices, Dodds also served as the student regent representing students on WKU's Board of Regents.

In office, Dodds led SGA in unanimously opposing an administration proposal to shift tuition to a per-credit-hour, bi-term model, which Provost Gordon Emslie dropped in February 2013 after student and faculty pushback. His administration also drafted a teaching assistant evaluation program the senate passed in February 2013, worked to restart a dormant student government at WKU's Glasgow campus, donated cameras to the Teaching and Learning Resource Center, and passed a resolution opposing a new $150 Study Abroad application fee; a Dodds amendment to bar SGA members from receiving SGA-awarded study-abroad scholarships, after 11 of 125 such awards had gone to SGA members that year, failed.

Dodds's term ended amid a contested succession: his successor, Keyana Boka, was elected in April 2013 but disqualified five days later by the Judicial Council 3-2 over a campaign email, then reinstated after appealing to Vice President for Student Affairs Howard Bailey. Later in 2012 Dodds was named a finalist for the Harry S. Truman Scholarship and, that November, WKU's first finalist for the George J. Mitchell Scholarship, the only Kentuckian among 20 national finalists. He went on to earn a law degree from Georgetown University, worked as directing attorney of the Children's Law Center and as a legal services staff attorney representing low-income clients in public benefits, housing and family law matters, and by the mid-2020s was a visiting professor at the University of Kentucky's J. David Rosenberg College of Law teaching Civil Procedure and Children and the Law, with research on rural "legal deserts" and the attorney shortage.

events.title: SGA worked to restart a student government for the Glasgow campus
events.body: SGA officials traveled to WKU's Glasgow campus to help restart its dormant student representative body and connect it to main campus. Dodds said Glasgow students had no mechanism for their voices to be heard except contacting main-campus SGA. Roy Ratliff, nominated interim president of the Glasgow student body, said its top priority was establishing a writing center, for which the group had set aside $2,700.

events.title: Provost Emslie cancelled the bi-term proposal SGA had opposed
events.body: Provost Gordon Emslie announced at the Feb. 21 University Senate meeting that he was dropping his bi-term emphasis proposal and had no plans to revive it, citing input from students and faculty. Both SGA and the University Senate had passed resolutions against it. Dodds said the revocation was in the student body's best interest, saying "I strongly opposed it."

events.title: Executive candidates debate ahead of spring election
events.body: Outgoing President Cory Dodds opened a candidates' debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium by describing to the audience how much influence the students elected to SGA's executive positions would actually have on WKU's campus, ahead of the election that would choose his successor.

events.title: Boka, Reeves and Seay won the spring executive elections
events.body: Executive vice president Keyana Boka was elected 2013-14 SGA president with 626 votes, 47 percent, over administrative vice president Cain Alvey with 419 votes and Austin Wingate with 300. Mark Reeves won executive vice president with 632 votes, 57 percent, over Brad Cockrel, and Nicki Seay ran unopposed for administrative vice president. Twenty-six student senators were also elected.

events.title: Judicial Council disqualified president-elect Boka, 3-2
events.body: In an emergency meeting, SGA's Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up and outgoing administrative vice president Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request, sent by Honors College graduate assistant Destiny Savage, violating the election code. The disqualification would have made Alvey, who had placed second in the April 4 vote, the incoming president; Boka said she would appeal.

events.title: Judicial Council declined to contest Bailey's reinstatement of Boka
events.body: In an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council unanimously decided not to challenge Bailey's memorandum reinstating Boka, saying it did not believe it had the power to do so, while expressing official disapproval. Chief Justice Seth Church called the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent. Boka said the council had conflicts of interest and needed to be held accountable by a neutral party in the administration.

events.title: Fall senate seats filled after two resignations
events.body: Two senators resigned over time commitments and student Shea Wyatt was named to fill in. New freshman senators Barrett Greenwell, Taylor Ruby, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles were sworn in along with Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz and graduate senators Mark Reeves and Katie Martin.

events.title: Retention official addressed the senate and got no feedback
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Christopher Costa opened the floor to Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for retention and student services, who asked senators for ideas on keeping students enrolled through to graduation. No senators offered feedback during the meeting, and Carter encouraged members to contact her later. SGA's current budget was circulated at the start of the meeting, showing the remaining balance and the money spent.

events.title: Senate amended the constitution, adding regional-campus seats
events.body: After two to three years of executive discussion, the senate passed most of a package of constitutional amendments, replacing class-year senate seats with college-based representation and guaranteeing seats for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro. A bylaw that would have made SGA members permanently ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships was stripped out and did not pass.

events.title: Costa stepped down as speaker; Settles elected to succeed him
events.body: Christopher Costa did not seek another term as speaker of the senate, and senators elected Paige Settles to replace him. The same meeting confirmed presidential appointments Roy Ratliff as senator-at-large and Jackie Stewart as associate justice, with Chief of Staff Travis Taylor and public relations chair Mac Mullins giving reports.

src2.label: Herald, 23 Apr 2013

events.title: Senate opposed automatic athletic-fee increases ahead of C-USA move
events.body: The senate passed a resolution against the annual automatic increase in the student athletic fee, arguing the revenue-sharing WKU would gain on joining Conference USA that July would outweigh the roughly $40,000 the university lost annually in the Sun Belt. Executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who introduced it, said the resolution set a precedent against automatic fee increases generally.

events.title: Senate creates a long-term goals committee by executive action
events.body: SGA voted unanimously on an executive action establishing a special long-term goals committee of at least eight members, including students from outside SGA appointed by President Cory Dodds. Dodds said the committee could draw up a set of goals to focus on for the next few years. A bill to distribute $800 in senate funding as eight $100 Study Away scholarships received its first read.

events.title: ID voucher pilot program introduced covering 80 student IDs
events.body: A bill in first read would have SGA pay $10 toward each regular-priced student identification card under an identification voucher pilot program, partially covering the cost of 80 cards. A second bill sought $225 for the Sigma Gamma Rho sorority's Hair Show Spectacular. A resolution setting the fall campus clean-up date was held over because it had not reached the Legislative Research Committee.

events.title: SGA adopts a new voting system and holds the South Campus food court resolution
events.body: At its eighth meeting SGA implemented a new voting system and gave a first read to an organizational aid bill covering the Student Veteran's Alliance ($175), the WKU chapter of the American Society for Microbiology ($150) and the Academic Competition Club ($275). A resolution supporting a food court at South Campus, due for a second read, was instead held in new business.

events.title: Glasgow campus ratifies its own student government constitution
events.body: Glasgow's Associated Student Body ratified its constitution on Nov. 16 by unanimous vote with no abstentions. Interim president Roy Ratliff said the goal was to give SGA a presence on the regional campus and give regional students a vote in student government. The Glasgow body adopted the same bylaws as SGA and began selecting committees for the spring.

events.title: Provost pitches value-added grading to SGA at final fall meeting
events.body: Provost Gordon Emslie and University Senate member Guy Jordan addressed SGA on a proposed value-added grading system under which students in the top third of B and C grades would receive an extra quality point and a plus designation. Emslie said an earlier plus-minus proposal had taken several years to develop "only to be dashed at the last minute." Jordan argued the value-added version worked because faculty gave something up and students did not.

events.title: Senate rejects the value-added grading resolution in a close vote
events.body: The value-added grading resolution failed on a close vote, disappointing President Cory Dodds, who called it a tangible benefit that increased student competitiveness and said it was "a real shame that our senate didn't see that." Provost Gordon Emslie had introduced the system to SGA and the University Senate in fall 2012. Some senate members opposed the change.

events.title: Constitution overhaul passes but senate strips the scholarship conflict rule
events.body: SGA adopted a package of constitutional and bylaw amendments with one exception: the senate rejected the bylaw that would have made serving SGA members ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships. Administrative Vice President Cain Alvey said executives had been discussing changes for two to three years and had gone through the constitution article by article, first presenting the changes on Feb. 19. Alvey said an amendment guaranteeing representation for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro was the one he liked most.

events.title: Four SGA leaders publicly accuse the senate of rejecting accountability
events.body: President Cory Dodds, Travis Taylor, Brittany Crowley and Drew Mitchell wrote a commentary attacking the senate for rejecting the amendment that would have barred serving SGA members from SGA-sponsored scholarships and grants. They wrote that 11 SGA members had received such scholarships or grants since the spring of 2011. The authors said this amounted to a breach of student trust and a conflict of interest.

events.title: Regents committee approves SGA's teaching assistant evaluation policy
events.body: SGA announced that the Board of Regents had unanimously approved the teaching assistant evaluation resolution at its March 29 committee meeting, with the full board to take it up on April 26. President Gary Ransdell said he had recommended approval and that there was little discussion because students and faculty were in agreement. The policy would require departments to provide a way for students to evaluate teaching assistants.

events.title: SGA votes to end the automatic annual athletic fee increase
events.body: The senate passed a resolution supporting an end to the automatic annual increase in the student athletic fee once WKU joined Conference USA on July 1, 2014. Senator and executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who initiated it, argued that increased revenues made the automatic increase unnecessary. The resolution stated that WKU athletics paid $80,000 in the Sun Belt Conference but received only $40,000 back in revenue sharing.

events.title: Budget cuts strip SGA's automatic inflation increase
events.body: University budget cuts announced that week removed the automatic increases that SGA, the Campus Activities Board and leadership programs normally received under the Higher Education Price Index, saving the university $8,000. Charley Pride, director of Student Activities and SGA's adviser, said no money was taken away, which was better than losing money. Incoming President Keyana Boka said the loss could affect new programs SGA had wanted to start.

events.title: Former officer defends SGA's stance as administrators rename DUC anyway
events.body: Former Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan wrote after the Administrative Council decided the building would be called Downing Student Union. He wrote that former President Cory Dodds had correctly told campus officials students preferred Downing University Center, noting the student assembly had voted against the change in 2011 when asked to do so by administrators. Bryan wrote that student opinion had not changed since that vote.

events.title: Senate bought T-shirts for the autumn Campus Clean-up
events.body: The senate unanimously approved funding on 9 October 2012 for promotional T-shirts for volunteers at the Campus Clean-up on 23 October, timed with Make a Difference Day. Committee chairman Mallory Chaney said dark grey shirts with the SGA logo would read something like "Tops making a difference" and would give students an incentive to turn out. Executive vice president Keyana Boka called the twice-yearly clean-up an important tradition, one the Herald traced back to WKU president Henry Cherry.

src.label: Herald, 12 Oct 2012 - "SGA bill funds Campus Clean-up"

events.title: Picnic with the president in the Ransdells' back garden
events.body: Gary and Julie Ransdell hosted SGA's executive board, student senators and the WKU Administrative Council for a cookout at their home on 22 October 2012, business casual. Ransdell said he had come up with the idea after months of talks with SGA president Cory Dodds about connecting his office to SGA. Dodds said the picnic had been running for several years and was an SGA tradition.

src.label: Herald, 17 Oct 2012 - "Picnic with the president a SGA tradition"

events.title: iPad lending programme opened with the Educational Resources Center
events.body: SGA and the Educational Resources Center launched an iPad-lending programme giving students, staff and faculty access to tablets loaded with test preparation applications such as MCAT materials. ERC coordinator Roxanne Spencer said SGA had approached the centre wanting the iPads available for a pilot project. Executive vice president Keyana Boka said SGA had bought the iPads the previous year but could not start lending until they were secured against tampering.

src.label: Herald, 30 Nov 2012 - "SGA, ERC collaborate for iPad program"

events.title: Dine with Decision Makers moved to the Kentucky Museum
events.body: SGA held Dine with Decision Makers at the Kentucky Museum on 5 December 2012, seating officials from across Kentucky and WKU administrators at tables matched to students by interest or field. President Cory Dodds opened the evening and executive vice president Keyana Boka said the prayer. Wadsworth, Ohio senior Sarah Brazier gave the keynote, arguing that higher education built a productive economy and an informed citizenry rather than only advancing individuals.

events.title: Safe Rides purple line returned for the spring
events.body: SGA's Safe Rides service, known on campus as the purple line, continued into spring 2013 after autumn 2012 became the first semester WKU ran a fixed-route late-night bus rather than a taxi contract. President Cory Dodds said the consistency of set pick-up points and times was why it worked where Provide-A-Ride had not. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said Provide-A-Ride had been an unreliable taxi service by comparison.

src.label: Herald, 8 Feb 2013 - "SGA's safe rides program will continue for the spring semester"

events.title: ID voucher programme halved the cost of a replacement card
events.body: SGA's ID voucher programme, running since the middle of the autumn 2012 semester, let students pay $10 rather than $20 for their first replacement student ID. The bill behind it allocated $800 to part-cover 80 cards. Administrative vice president Cain Alvey said the idea came from his job as a resident assistant in McCormack Hall, and that SGA covered only the first loss so as to teach responsibility and spread the benefit. Vouchers were collected from the SGA office in Cravens Library room 13.

src.label: Herald, 12 Feb 2013 - "SGA provides vouchers to replace lost IDs"

events.title: Eight Study Away scholarships funded as transcript vouchers ran on
events.body: The senate passed a bill on 12 February 2013 allocating $800 for eight $100 Study Away scholarships covering the spring and summer 2013 programmes. SGA reported that 30 of the semester's transcript vouchers had been used, with 70 left. Campus improvements chair Mallory Chaney set the spring Campus Safety Walk for 26 February.

src.label: Herald, 13 Feb 2013 - "SGA approves bill for Study Away scholarships"

events.title: Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term calendar and per-credit-hour tuition
events.body: SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing the administration's proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. The bi-term plan would have put students in 80-minute classes on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Fridays, and President Gary Ransdell had said it would let a student carry a full load plus a summer or winter course and graduate in three years. President Cory Dodds objected chiefly to the per-credit-hour shift, arguing it would charge students more because full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear.

events.title: Senate tabled Hannah Garland's plus-minus grading resolution
events.body: Academic Affairs chair Hannah Garland's resolution to add plus and minus grades to As, Bs, Cs and Ds was tabled at the Tuesday meeting after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first, and most of the senate agreed. Garland said the system would make GPAs more exact and might make WKU more competitive. President Cory Dodds said the executive board had discussed putting the question directly to students on the spring ballot. A similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007.

src2.label: Herald, 21 Feb 2013

events.title: Senate passed the teaching assistant evaluation resolution
events.body: On 5 February the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program President Cory Dodds had campaigned on and developed with his executive officers before pitching it to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the measure, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. Dodds said the idea had been worked on for many years. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate.

events.title: SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 study abroad application fee
events.body: The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, due to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach. Executive Vice President Keyana Boka said SGA took a formal stance because the fee had come up so suddenly, and the University Senate passed a similar resolution seeking to delay the fee until fall 2013. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds, to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded study abroad scholarships, failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants awarded that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest.

events.title: Judicial Council issued three written opinions, each carried 5-0
events.body: On 28 August 2012 Chief Justice Chris Jankowski published three opinions, each recording a unanimous 5-0 vote of the council. One set out the judicial review procedure, one interpreted the attendance policy and defined excused and unexcused absences, and one ruled on two surplus at-large senators, letting them serve out their terms while barring the president from refilling those two seats until the constitutional composition was met.

src2.label: Judicial Council opinion, judicial review, 28 Aug 2012

events.title: Judicial Council reviewed and approved the constitutional package before the senate voted
events.body: Resolution 5-13-S, first read on 19 February 2013 and read a second time on 26 February, records in its whereas clauses that the proposed amendments had been reviewed and approved by the Judicial Council under clause 4.5.9 of the constitution. Seth Church is listed among the resolution's contacts, though the document gives no title for him there, and it is not established that he already held the chief justiceship on this date. The resolution referred the amendments to the student body for ratification on the spring 2013 ballot.

executive.name: Cory Dodds
executive.note: Also served as student regent under the merged offices.

executive.name: Keyana Boka
executive.note: Elected uncontested alongside Dodds in March 2012; went on to be elected 2013-14 president, spelled "Keyanna" in that year's coverage. Spelling unverified between the two forms.
profile: Keyana Boka, a Bowling Green sophomore, was elected executive vice president uncontested alongside presidential candidate Cory Dodds in the March 2012 SGA election. She was sworn into office at SGA's end-of-year banquet on 8 May 2012, succeeding executive vice president Kendrick Bryan. She said she had big shoes to fill after Bryan's two years in the office. She went on to be elected SGA president for 2013-14, where her name appeared in that year's coverage spelled "Keyanna"; the spelling is unverified between the two forms.

src2.label: Herald, 9 May 2012 - "New SGA officers sworn in at banquet"

executive.name: Cain Alvey
executive.note: Ran unsuccessfully for president in the April 2013 election as outgoing administrative vice president.
profile: Cain Alvey served as administrative vice president for 2012-13 under President Cory Dodds. He ran for president in the April 2013 election, finishing second with 419 votes (31 percent) to winner Keyana Boka's 626 (47 percent) and third-place candidate Austin Wingate's 300 (22 percent). A later SGA president, Nicki Taylor, recalled in 2015 that Alvey had spent his full $350 campaign-spending limit on posters and handbills, paying a photojournalism student to photograph him and a design student to produce his materials.

Alvey continued serving as a senator into 2013-14 under Boka's administration. In October 2013 he amended a Campus Improvements bill funding phone-charging stations, moving one planned location from a library periodicals room to the Commons at Cravens Library, though the executive council vetoed the whole bill later that same night. In February 2014, when a senator questioned whether members understood a constitutional amendment increasing the Judicial Council to seven justices and shifting justice appointments to the executive branch, Alvey argued in the amendment's defense that senators had had two weeks to read and study it before the vote.

src2.label: Herald, 2 Apr 2015, "SGA candidates balance campaign financing"

src4.label: Herald, 30 Oct 2013, "Charging station bill vetoed by executive council"

executive.name: Travis Taylor
profile: Travis Taylor was SGA's director of academic and student affairs in 2011-12. The senate funded a transcript-voucher program that February, providing 175 vouchers, and when the Herald followed up in March, Taylor said SGA had held the program back a semester over budget problems, scheduling difficulties and planning, rather than launch one that would fail.

He moved up to chief of staff for 2012-13 under President Cory Dodds. In March 2013 he joined Dodds, Brittany Crowley and Drew Mitchell in a Herald commentary accusing the senate of rejecting a constitutional amendment that would have barred sitting SGA members from receiving SGA-administered scholarships and grants, writing that eleven members had received such awards since spring 2011 and calling it a conflict of interest. The following month he gave the cabinet's report to the senate at the meeting that elected Paige Settles to succeed Christopher Costa as speaker.

executive.office: Director of Academic and Student Affairs
executive.name: Brittany Crowley
executive.note: Signed the cabinet's December 2012 statement supporting the "value added" grading scale and its March 2013 commentary on the senate's rejection of the scholarship conflict-of-interest rule.
profile: Brittany Crowley served as SGA's director of academic and student affairs in 2012-13. She signed the cabinet's December 2012 statement backing the provost's proposed "value-added" grading scale, which the Senate went on to reject in February 2013.

In March 2013 Crowley joined President Cory Dodds, Travis Taylor and Drew Mitchell in a Herald commentary attacking the Senate for rejecting an amendment that would have barred sitting SGA members from receiving SGA-sponsored scholarships and grants; the four wrote that 11 SGA members had received such scholarships or grants since spring 2011 and called it a breach of student trust and a conflict of interest.

executive.name: Sarah Hazelip
executive.note: Held the post SGA's own site described as one of the four appointed executive offices, and signed the cabinet's December 2012 grading statement; she stayed on under Boka in 2013-14.
profile: Sarah Hazelip held SGA's director of information technology post from 2012-13 through 2014-15, one of the four appointed executive offices listed on SGA's own site, and stayed in the role as Keyana Boka's administration took over for 2013-14.

In October 2013 she told the senate she was working to put SGA's newly finalized $125,000 budget online. By September 2014, at an executive cabinet meeting with only four officers present, she moved approval of Senate Bill 3-14-F and then moved to adjourn; both motions passed unanimously.
