executive.name: Drew Mitchell
executive.note: Signed both of the cabinet's collective statements to the Herald, backing the provost's "value added" grading proposal in December 2012 and accusing the senate of rejecting accountability in March 2013. A Bowling Green senior, he received the Dero Downing Award at the May 2013 banquet.
profile: Drew Mitchell, a Bowling Green senior, served as SGA's director of public relations in 2012-13. He signed the cabinet's December 2012 statement backing the provost's proposed "value-added" grading scale.

In March 2013 Mitchell joined President Cory Dodds, Travis Taylor and Brittany Crowley in a Herald commentary accusing the Senate of rejecting accountability after it voted down an amendment barring sitting SGA members from SGA-sponsored scholarships and grants. He received the Dero Downing Award at SGA's May 2013 banquet.

src2.label: Herald, 8 May 2013, "SGA swears in executive officers for the coming school year"

officers.name: Christopher Costa
officers.note: Did not seek another term; Paige Settles was elected to succeed him in April 2013 for 2013-14.
profile: Christopher Costa was elected to the senate in the fall 2011 election with 977 students voting. By spring 2012 he had joined the four SGA members who traveled to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort to protest a proposed 6.4 percent cut to the state's postsecondary education budget. On 18 April 2012 the senate elected him speaker of the student senate for 2012-13, over fellow senator Poorvie Patel and public relations committee head Mallory Treece; he told senators his time in the Army had taught him to follow before he learned to lead, and he was sworn in at SGA's end-of-year banquet on 9 May 2012, receiving the gavel from outgoing speaker Kaylee Egerer.

As speaker, Costa presided over a year in which SGA rewrote its own constitution, restructuring senate seats by college rather than class year and adding representation for the Glasgow and Owensboro regional campuses. During floor debate in September 2013 he spoke against a separate proposal, opposing a dedicated Navitas/ESL international senate seat even though he supported the broader goal of international student involvement, arguing the seat would function as a band-aid; the amendment passed anyway. Throughout his term Costa said his hardest task was remaining impartial as speaker, saying it was hardest "when there were issues present which I had a strong position or opinion on."

Costa chose not to seek a second term, and the senate elected Paige Settles to succeed him as speaker on 16 April 2013. He said at the time that the responsibilities of the office had grown difficult to balance with his coursework as he entered his senior year, and that he intended to return to an ordinary senate seat after the spring semester ended.

officers.name: Mallory Treece
officers.note: Listed as secretary on SGA's own senate leadership roster; she moved to Public Relations committee chair the following year.
profile: Mallory Treece, a Smiths Grove freshman, was elected to the SGA senate in the fall 2011 election. By February 2012 she had been named public relations committee head, and the same semester she was one of four SGA members who traveled to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, telling the Herald she wanted to "come to the state capitol and rally for something I really care about."

In April 2012 Treece ran for speaker of the student senate against Christopher Costa and Poorvie Patel, telling senators she had fallen in love with SGA at her first meeting and believed her passion for the organization qualified her for the role; she lost to Costa. As public relations committee head that spring she co-authored the bill funding SGA's sponsorship of International Night, and she was a guest at the SGA delegation's picnic with WKU President Gary Ransdell in October 2012, by then serving as secretary of the senate, a post SGA's own leadership roster credited to her for 2012-13. She moved from secretary to public relations committee chair the following year.

src.label: WKU SGA site, legislative branch, 21 Oct 2012 (archived)

officers.name: Christopher Jankowski
officers.note: Headed the Judicial Council at the start of the year on the roster SGA published on 29 August 2012, after two years as an associate justice; by the April 2013 election dispute the chief justiceship had passed to Seth Church.
profile: Christopher Jankowski was appointed an associate justice of SGA's Judicial Council on 29 March 2011 by President Colton Jessie, filling out the council alongside Aaron Pawley after Chief Justice Dajana Crockett's resignation. In that role during the 2011-12 year he explained the council's meeting-absence rules to the Herald after ten of the senate's 36 members were called in for excessive absences, two of whom were dismissed; he said committees, not the full senate, were where senators actually shaped legislation. He also said the council was preparing a judicial opinion that would give senators more leeway on absences, and in February 2012 he was one of four SGA members who traveled to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, telling the crowd it was important that students "make ourselves heard."

SGA's own roster, published 29 August 2012, named Jankowski chief justice of the Judicial Council for 2012-13 after his two years as an associate justice. By the time of the disputed April 2013 presidential election, however, the chief justiceship had passed to Seth Church, and the archive has found no further record of Jankowski's SGA service after that transition.

profile: Seth Church served on SGA's Judicial Council, becoming chief justice by April 2013 after having been an ordinary justice as of the previous August. As chief justice he announced the council's 3-2 vote disqualifying president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional campaign email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request. When Howard Bailey overruled the disqualification and reinstated Boka, the council voted unanimously not to challenge his decision but registered its disapproval; Church called Bailey's intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent.

Church remained chief justice for 2013-14. In April 2014 he delivered the council's Opinion 2014SP-002, holding that senators who abstain neither vote yes nor no but concur with the majority of those voting, and that they still count toward quorum; Julia Payne and Jackie Stewart joined the opinion, and Megan Lemmons took no part.

He moved into the executive branch as chief of staff for 2014-15 under President Nicki Taylor. Church wrote the resolution supporting private spaces on campus for expressing breast milk, prompted by a non-traditional student who had just had her third child and found the existing unlocked room uncomfortable; it passed unanimously without debate. He proposed and chaired a new Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee developed in collaboration with Taylor, and wrote the resolution rewriting the Glasgow regional campus's constitution after Glasgow struggled to keep members. He also argued against a smoke-free campus resolution that the senate passed and the Executive Cabinet then vetoed, saying a ban was unfair to students required to live on campus for two years, and objected that a proposed $10 million parking garage had moved too fast and left out the regional campuses.

profile: Boka, the outgoing executive vice president, was elected 2013-14 SGA president on 4 April 2013 with 626 votes (47 percent), beating administrative vice president Cain Alvey (419 votes) and Austin Wingate (300). Five days later the Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify her after Alvey, the runner-up who stood to become president if she were removed, complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at her request. Boka appealed to Howard Bailey, WKU's vice president for Student Affairs, who reinstated her; the Judicial Council declined to contest his ruling in an emergency meeting on 16 April, with Chief Justice Seth Church calling the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and Boka countering that the council itself had conflicts of interest.

In office, Boka's fall 2013 senate created a new international student senate seat for Navitas/ESL students and finalized a $125,000 budget, part of which sent her and executive vice president Mark Reeves on a Washington, D.C. higher-education lobbying trip. She fielded student anger over new two-tier priority registration rules at a November open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie, and announced the permanent closure of Thompson Complex North Wing, long slated for demolition. A senate attempt to reverse SGA's support for the Talisman's student fee was struck down by the Judicial Council as unconstitutional, as was the underlying 2005 policy.

In spring 2014 Boka organized a Frankfort rally against a $1.8 million state budget cut to WKU and opposed a senate amendment stripping the president's sole power to appoint Judicial Council justices, which was sent back to committee after the council found too few senators had been present to pass it. At the year's final meeting she announced a 4.8 percent tuition increase for the coming year, and the senate passed a resolution backing a Good Samaritan policy to protect students who called 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

events.title: Priority registration complaints spurred open forum
events.body: Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate.

events.title: Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently
events.body: Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly.

events.title: Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal
events.body: After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options.

events.title: SGA reconvened and planned a Frankfort rally against budget cuts
events.body: At the first spring meeting President Keyana Boka announced SGA would organize a trip to Frankfort called Rally for Retention in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves outlined the two-year state budget then being voted on, warned that tough cuts were coming and said students needed to be involved. The body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process, and Boka reported talks with dining services about 24-hour dining with Einstein's Bagels under consideration for a 24-hour study area; five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats.

events.title: Final meeting passed the Good Samaritan resolution and cleared funding bills
events.body: At the last meeting of the semester President Keyana Boka announced a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most students, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance and a one percent faculty salary adjustment. The senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills on first read, beginning with Bill 17-14-S allocating $1,817.10, funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses, and Speaker Paige Settles said one remaining scholarship bill would be handled at a short meeting during the end-of-year banquet.

events.title: Senate passed international student seat amendment
events.body: President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat.

events.title: Presidential debate drew full field of candidates
events.body: Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups.

events.title: Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar
events.body: At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson.

events.title: SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals
events.body: SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate.

events.title: Judicial Council strikes down the international senate seat amendment
events.body: SGA announced that the Judicial Council had ruled unconstitutional a constitutional amendment proposed by President Keyana Boka and Executive Vice President Mark Reeves. The amendment would have changed the senate's composition by adding one seat for an international student. The ruling was reported to the senate at its second meeting of the semester.

events.title: Emergency Judicial Council meeting clears reworded international seat
events.body: SGA called an emergency Judicial Council meeting to review revisions to the amendment the council had rejected on Aug. 29 for violating WKU's non-discrimination clause. Boka and Reeves changed the wording from "one international student senator" to a Navitas or English as a Second Language international student seat. Boka said the emergency session was routine protocol for any meeting outside the council's regular schedule.

events.title: Herald editorial questions SGA's handpicked approach to diversity
events.body: A Herald editorial examined the proposed permanent senate seat for an international student, ruled unconstitutional on Aug. 29 and then revised and approved in a six-minute emergency meeting. The editorial said it supported SGA's effort to expand representation but questioned whether a designated seat was the most effective means. Boka and Reeves had said their intention was to better represent WKU's international student population.

events.title: Student petition for 24-hour dining collects 700 signatures for SGA
events.body: Bowling Green sophomore Nick Conrad, a McCormack Hall resident assistant, gathered more than 700 signatures in about a week on a petition asking for a 24-hour dining option on campus, with a stated goal of 5,000. Conrad said he studied late and knew many students on similar schedules. He had met with SGA representatives who were interested in the petition.

events.title: Senate funds transcript vouchers with $300
events.body: SGA passed a bill allotting $300 to the Transcript Voucher Program fund, letting students collect vouchers from the SGA office instead of paying the $7 transcript fee. Academic Affairs committee head Megan Skaggs, who wrote the bill, said students already paid a great deal in tuition and fees. Funding for the long-running program had to be renewed by senate vote each time more money was needed.

events.title: Resolution targets the internet policy behind WKU's FIRE red light rating
events.body: A resolution by Director of Public Relations Laura Harper received its first read, supporting amendment of university internet usage policies that the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education had deemed a violation of free speech. FIRE had given WKU a red light rating because at least one handbook policy violated the First Amendment. Computing Policy 12-13, covering email content likely to be perceived as offensive or disparaging, was the specific cause.

events.title: Internet policy resolution and ID voucher bill pass at a short meeting
events.body: With attendance thinned by a home football game where SGA ran a Safe Ride promotional booth, the senate passed Resolution 3-13-F on internet usage policies and Bill 2-13-F funding identification vouchers. Two further bills went into first read, one on organizational aid and one funding six winter term scholarship sessions. Laura Harper introduced the internet policy resolution.

events.title: SGA proposes $1,598 toward five KwikBoost charging stations with the libraries
events.body: SGA and WKU Libraries proposed installing five KwikBoost phone and laptop charging stations, each with eight charging attachments, at $799 apiece. SGA's bill, introduced for first reading that Tuesday, would pay $1,598 for two of the five: one at the Glasgow campus and one in the Helm 2 periodicals room. WKU Libraries would fund the other three, planned for the Educational Resources Center, Helm 100 and the Owensboro campus. President Keyana Boka said Dean of University Libraries Connie Foster brought her the idea.

events.title: Provost and registrar face students at SGA's priority registration forum
events.body: SGA hosted an open forum on priority registration during its weekly meeting, with Provost Gordon Emslie and University Registrar Freida Eggleton answering questions. The policy, already in effect for spring registration, split priority registration into a need tier and a benefit tier and capped qualifying students at 16 credit hours until open registration. Seniors and graduate students still registered first and were not subject to the cap.

events.title: South Campus forum turns on the closing of the campus store
events.body: SGA held its weekly meeting at South Campus as an open forum and President Keyana Boka asked those present to discuss the recent closing of the South Campus WKU store. Senators debated the lack of communication between the officials who closed the store and South Campus students. Executive Vice President Mark Reeves said the same thing had happened the previous year when the food court closed, calling it part of a broader failure to consult South Campus students.

events.title: Talisman brings its funding shortfall to SGA
events.body: Talisman representatives met President Keyana Boka and Brad Cockrel on Nov. 29 to discuss long-term options for paying for the yearbook. The previous May the Talisman had faced a proposed $93,000 cut, 47 percent of its $198,000 budget, before an alumni-backed "Save the Talisman" campaign reduced the cut. Its budget stood at $127,000, including $45,000 in one-time university funds.

events.title: Student on crutches brings a bus stop bench proposal to the senate
events.body: Covington senior Logan Eckler went before SGA on Nov. 19 to propose benches at campus bus stops after several days on crutches following a judo injury. He said the bus system was invaluable for students who had difficulty walking but that few stops had seats. Eckler said the same problem affected pregnant students and people with disabilities, and that SGA senators he knew had recommended he bring it forward.

events.title: SGA unanimously backs taking the Campus Pride Index
events.body: An SGA proposal that WKU take the Campus Pride Index, a survey measuring campus friendliness toward LGBT students, passed unanimously and was submitted to the Administrative Council. Student Identity Outreach president Andrew Salman first proposed it to the Office of Diversity, and senator Nicki Seay carried it into SGA. Salman said the index would diagnose areas where the university was not meeting the needs of its queer students, and Seay said WKU had never taken it before.

events.title: Turnout falls to 908, down 555 votes from the previous year
events.body: A Herald editorial reported that SGA voter turnout for the spring election was 908, down 555 votes from the year before. The editorial called turnout below 1,000 pathetic and said the student body could and should do better. It noted that the SGA president represents students at the Board of Regents and that SGA funds organizational aid and extended library hours.

events.title: Safe Ride ran a booth at Homecoming tailgating
events.body: SGA members staffed a Safe Ride promotional booth during tailgating for the home football game on 15 October 2013 and gave a presentation at halftime. Attendance at that evening's senate meeting was lighter than usual as a result, and the meeting was cut short, though a resolution on internet usage policy and a bill funding identification vouchers both passed.

events.title: SGA opened Earth Week by planting the community garden
events.body: SGA and the Office of Sustainability kicked off Earth Week on 21 April 2014 with a planting party in the community garden behind the sustainability house at 503 Regents Avenue. President Keyana Boka said she was glad SGA could support the garden, which SGA's campus improvement committee then took on maintaining, growing tomatoes, squash, sunflowers and peppers. Garden coordinator Beth McGrew said the aim was to build community through sustainability and strengthen students' connection to their food.

events.title: Campus-wide safety walk from Centennial Mall
events.body: SGA held a campus safety walk starting at Centennial Mall at 6:30 p.m. on 24 April 2014, inviting students to point out anywhere they felt unsafe, whether dark or unstable. President Keyana Boka said the purpose was to promote safety.

src.label: Herald, 24 Apr 2014 - "SGA hosts campus wide safety walk"

events.title: Executive Council voided the amendment stripping the president's judicial appointments
events.body: An amendment removing the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the council to seven justices passed at the Tuesday meeting, over President Keyana Boka's objection that it bypassed both presidential appointment and the senate. Boka said the president is elected by the student body to make appointments in all three branches and that she was wary of the direction, while Chief Justice Seth Church argued that vesting appointments in the executive branch as a whole created a fairer system. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution, found too few senators had attended for the vote to count and declared the amendment unconstitutional, sending it back to first read. The SGA office had temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

events.title: 564 voted in the fall election; referendum created the Navitas/ESL seat
events.body: A total of 564 students voted in the fall SGA election. The referendum creating a Navitas and English as a Second Language international student senate seat drew 426 votes and passed with 310 yes votes, 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, led by Jay Todd Richey with 27 percent, along with two graduate senators, a Gatton Academy senator and an Arts and Letters senator. Most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

events.title: Herald editorial faulted SGA over the priority registration policy
events.body: A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority registration policy, which capped students with priority registration at 16 hours on their priority day and exempted seniors and graduate students. The editorial said executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at the University Senate on 10 September without SGA questioning or debating it first. It also faulted SGA for scheduling an open forum for 12 November, after the policy was already set to govern fall registration. Representing students was SGA's one job, the editorial argued, and it had not been done on this issue.

events.title: SGA finalized a $125,000 budget after a planned increase fell through
events.body: SGA finalized a 2013-14 budget of $125,000 drawn from student tuition, after a planned funding increase did not come through. Director of Public Relations Laura Harper said the figure equated to about $6.25 per student. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each, and the executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay, who built the budget, said senate discretionary spending required a senate majority and executive discretionary spending an executive committee majority.

events.title: Mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus
events.body: SGA's mid-year report on its $125,000 budget showed a surplus of $46,883.62. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay said the budget had changed little since December and that she had more funds to allocate back to the student body, and $54,000 had gone to the legislative branch for items such as organizational aid and grants. The senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index. Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart were approved as senators, leaving six senate seats open.

events.title: The Purple Line got a third bus after carrying close to 20,000 riders
events.body: The Safe Ride shuttle SGA had created with Parking and Transportation in 2012 to replace Provide-A-Ride, known on campus as the Purple Line, entered its second year with a third bus added. Transit manager Stephen Rowland said SGA wanted to keep the line's 15-minute run time and the extra bus was needed to hold the schedule across 16 stops and a 45-minute circuit, and that the line had carried close to 20,000 passengers in its first year. The line ran Thursday, Friday and Saturday from 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. Driver Quinten Haynie said Homecoming week and the opening weeks of class were the busiest.
events.money: close to 20,000 passengers in its first year

events.title: Nicki Seay ran unopposed as SGA's homecoming queen candidate
events.body: At the first meeting after the fall election, the senate nominated and voted on its homecoming queen candidate. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay was nominated, ran unopposed and took the nomination. The same meeting swore in fifteen new senators and heard that the Campus Improvements Committee was developing a community garden with GreenToppers.

events.title: Judicial Council structure amendment adopted, referred to the spring ballot
events.body: Resolution 1-14-S, first read on 4 February 2014, proposed to expand the Judicial Council from five justices to seven, have the Chief Justice chosen by majority vote of the council rather than appointed by the president, and create a new Associate Chief Justice office, with a related bylaw change moving minute-taking duty to that new office. The resolution's text calls for referring the amendments to the student body on the spring 2014 ballot, but the copy posted by SGA gives a second-reading date of 25 March 2014 with the Pass/Fail field left blank, so this document alone does not confirm the resolution actually passed that day. SGA's constitution as currently published does carry all of these exact provisions, confirming the changes were adopted at some point.

events.title: Council created an Election Code Advisory Board
events.body: In Opinion 2013FA-005 the Judicial Council established an Election Code Advisory Board under section 4.5.8 of the constitution, to rewrite election codes it described as having proven inadequate. The board was chaired by the chief justice, open to any SGA member or student willing to serve, and required to report to the Senate monthly until dissolved by a majority vote of the council. Its recommendations were not binding on the council.

events.title: Council overruled its own year-old joint campaigning rule
events.body: In Opinion 2014SP-001, In re joint campaigning (II), the Judicial Council overruled its 2013 opinion on candidates campaigning together and set a new formula: the lowest expenditure cap among joint campaigners, divided by their number, was the most each could put into shared material, and each then subtracted the whole joint total from their own allowance. The opinion worked the arithmetic for a senator pair and for a three-way presidential ticket, and said the council would take good-faith compliance leniently because the rule was new.

events.title: Council ruled abstentions count toward quorum
events.body: In Opinion 2014SP-002 the Judicial Council was asked whether Resolution 5-14-S had passed properly. It held that abstaining members cast neither a yes nor a no vote but concur with the majority of those voting, citing a 1988 Kentucky Attorney General opinion, and that abstaining members do count toward quorum because quorum refers to the number present. Since no senator had noted a lack of quorum, quorum was presumed throughout and the resolution passed. Chief Justice Seth Church delivered the opinion, joined by Julia Payne and Jackie Stewart; Megan Lemmons took no part.

events.title: Senate passes charging-station funding, then the executive council vetoes it
events.body: The Senate amended and passed the $1,598 charging-station bill, moving one station from Helm 2 to the Commons at Cravens Library at Sen. Cain Alvey's request. After the meeting adjourned, the Executive Council vetoed the bill, saying SGA could not unilaterally change the stations' locations without consulting its partner, WKU Libraries. Under SGA bylaws the Executive Council had 14 days to act on passed legislation; a two-thirds Senate vote could still override the veto.

events.title: An outdated charging-station bill is tabled again
events.body: The charging-station bill returned to the Senate floor, altered from its vetoed version, but senators tabled it after finding an outdated draft had been presented rather than the corrected one. A senator noted voting on the wrong version would violate SGA's constitution.

executive.name: Mark Reeves
profile: Mark Reeves, a Louisville graduate student, was sworn in as a graduate senator in September 2012 before running for executive vice president the following spring. He won the April 2013 general election with 632 votes, 57 percent, defeating Brad Cockrel's 485; asked how it felt, he said he was "really privileged and honored that the students chose this" and that he appreciated the chance to serve.

As executive vice president in 2013-14, Reeves co-authored with President Keyana Boka a constitutional amendment creating a senate seat for Navitas and English-as-a-second-language international students; the Judicial Council initially struck the wording down as unconstitutional before the senate passed a revised version. He also introduced a resolution opposing WKU athletics' automatic annual fee increase ahead of the move to Conference USA, arguing that WKU paid $80,000 in Sun Belt Conference dues but received only $40,000 back in revenue sharing. A Herald editorial later criticized him for voting for a new priority-registration policy at the University Senate without first bringing it to SGA for debate.

Reeves also spoke to senators about the state budget, warning in February 2014 that further cuts were likely, and joined Boka on a Washington, D.C. lobbying trip that year. At a South Campus forum that November he said WKU had made the same mistake it made when it closed the South Campus food court, again failing to consult South Campus students before closing the campus store there.

executive.name: Nicki Seay
profile: Nicki Seay was appointed SGA's parliamentarian in February 2012 and later served as legislative research chair in 2012-13 before she was elected administrative vice president for 2013-14, alongside presidential candidate Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves, in the April 2013 election. By the time she ran unopposed for president in April 2014, the Herald reported she had been on SGA for three years and wanted to use Adobe Connect to broadcast SGA meetings to students who could not attend in person. Asked at an executive candidates' debate on 2 April 2014 whether she could balance the presidency with a double major, she said she planned to take 12 hours with no Friday classes that fall. She won the presidency in that election; the year opened under "Nicki Seay" before her name changed partway through to "Nicki Taylor," and the fuller account is in her presidential profile for 2014-15.

executive.name: Brad Cockrel
executive.note: Named as chief of staff on SGA's own executive roster for 2013-14, last modified 3 September 2013.
profile: Brad Cockrel ran for executive vice president in the spring 2013 election, one of the candidates in the presidential and vice-presidential debate that March. He lost the April 2013 general election to Mark Reeves, taking 485 votes, 43 percent, to Reeves's 632.

Cockrel was nonetheless named chief of staff for 2013-14, and that November he and President Keyana Boka met with Talisman staff to discuss long-term funding options for the yearbook after it reported a funding shortfall, with its budget at $127,000.

executive.name: Hannah Garland
executive.note: Academic Affairs committee chair on SGA's 2012-13 senate leadership roster before joining the cabinet as director of academic and student affairs for 2013-14.
profile: Hannah Garland chaired SGA's Academic Affairs committee in 2012-13, where she wrote a resolution to add plus and minus grades to the existing A/B/C/D scale, arguing the change would make GPAs more exact and could make WKU more competitive. The senate tabled it in February 2013 after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal with more student input first; President Cory Dodds said the executive board had discussed putting the question to students on the spring ballot instead.
Garland joined the cabinet as director of academic and student affairs for 2013-14 under President Keyana Boka.

executive.name: Laura Harper
executive.note: Explained SGA's finalised $125,000 budget to students as the equivalent of $6.25 a head, the money coming out of tuition.
profile: Laura Harper served as SGA's director of public relations for 2013-14. That October she introduced a resolution supporting changes to WKU's internet-usage policies after the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education gave the university a red-light rating over Computing Policy 12-13, which covered email content deemed likely to be perceived as offensive or disparaging; the resolution passed later that month at a lightly attended meeting held during a home football game.
When SGA finalized its $125,000 budget that October, Harper explained the figure to students as the equivalent of about $6.25 a head.

senate.note: Twenty-six student senators were elected in the April 2013 spring election alongside the executive officers. Executive Council minutes for 10 Sept 2013 list cabinet members Sarah Hazelip, Hannah Garland, Paige Settles, Laura Harper and Brad Cockrel alongside Boka, Reeves and Seay; Samantha Johnson was sworn in that night to a seat vacated by Keith Watson's resignation.

officers.name: Paige Settles
officers.note: A Floyds Knobs, Indiana freshman, named speaker of the senate in the spring 2013 election and sworn in by outgoing president Cory Dodds at the SGA awards banquet on 7 May 2013.
profile: Paige Settles, a Floyds Knobs, Indiana freshman, was elected speaker of the student senate in April 2013, succeeding Christopher Costa, and was sworn in by outgoing president Cory Dodds at SGA's awards banquet that May. She said she felt qualified for the job because she had already spoken with Costa about its responsibilities, and that her priority was fostering senators working well together; Costa in turn said she had "a lot of talents that will be very useful for the position."

In 2014-15 Settles moved from the speakership to chair the Legislative Research Committee, a post SGA's own records rendered inconsistently as "Paige Settle." She returned to the speaker's chair for 2015-16, calling the first meeting of the Fourteenth Senate to order on 1 September 2015, and in February 2016 she reported that she was updating the senate's records and procedures.

officers.name: Linda Cruz
officers.note: Held the Gatton Academy senate seat in 2012-13 before being named secretary.
profile: Linda Cruz held the Gatton Academy of Mathematics and Science's dedicated senate seat in 2012-13, sworn in as a freshman senator that September alongside Barrett Greenwell, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles. The following year SGA's own legislative branch page named her secretary of the student senate for 2013-14, a promotion from her Gatton Academy seat the year before.

leaders.name: Nicki Taylor
leaders.note: The chambers plaque carries two consecutive plates for this year: "Janet 'Nicki' Seay" and "Nicki Taylor." Herald coverage shows one continuous officeholder, not a succession: she opened the year as "Nicki Seay" (Herald, 28 Aug and 25 Sep 2014), was already being called "Nicki Taylor" by the very next issue on 15 Oct 2014, and was still SGA president under that name through the 2 Apr 2015 election that chose her successor - no election, resignation or hand-off for a second officeholder appears anywhere in that span. Treated here as a single president who changed her surname partway through the term.
profile: Nicki Seay had been SGA's Legislative Research Chair in 2012-13 and ran successfully for administrative vice president in the spring 2013 election. She took office as SGA president in August 2014, a Crofton senior, alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles, and named student involvement, retention and graduation her priorities. Her administration opened the year by expanding SGA's summer and winter need-based scholarship program from $6,000 to $21,000.

By the middle of October 2014 the Herald was referring to the same sitting president as Nicki Taylor; no election or resignation separates the two names in the paper's coverage. As Taylor, she presided over a fall senate that voted down a nonsectarian prayer resolution, saw its smoke-free campus resolution vetoed by the Executive Cabinet and sustained on a failed override vote, and passed a resolution backing changes to the campus alcohol policy. She addressed WKU's December 2014 commencement as SGA president, telling graduates, "You have the rest of your life to look forward to."

In the spring semester the senate under Taylor passed a limited-smoking-campus resolution and a resolution backing a $10 million parking garage funded by a new student fee; President Gary Ransdell responded formally to both. She also sat, by virtue of the office, on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking measure because of that seat. Her term ended with the 2 April 2015 election of Jay Todd Richey as her successor.

events.title: An election result challenged and upheld
events.body: Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

events.title: SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program
events.body: SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities.

events.title: President Taylor addressed December graduates
events.body: SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October.

events.title: President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent
events.body: The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat.

events.title: Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11
events.body: SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by 13-11. It would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas and call on the Administrative Council to draw up a plan reducing those areas and gradually phasing them out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted; the existing policy allowed smoking anywhere on campus at least 30 feet from buildings. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester.

events.title: Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524
events.body: Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats.

events.title: Commuter focus group brings parking fixes to the senate
events.body: Campus Improvements Committee Chair Tyler Scaff reported that a commuter focus group had proposed solutions to campus parking problems, including adding a function to the iWKU app that would list each lot with the number of spaces available. A South Campus park and ride was also proposed. Scaff said the committee was working on other projects including an SGA garden plot at the Office of Sustainability.

events.title: SGA funds an emergency food program for students with frozen accounts
events.body: Bill 10-14-F passed without debate, allocating $500 from legislative discretionary funds toward the $3,600 Emergency Food Pilot Program. The program gave the first 50 students who could show their university account was locked 10 free meals through Fresh Food Company waivers. Author William Berry said it would let those students eat for a few days while they worked on paying their bills.

events.title: Glasgow rewrites its constitution after struggling to keep members
events.body: Amendments to Glasgow's SGA constitution received their first read on the main campus. Chief of Staff Seth Church said Glasgow's constitution had been modeled on the main campus document and that the regional campus had struggled with student involvement and retaining SGA members, so it was decided to change the constitution drastically. Glasgow's SGA had already voted to approve the amendments, leaving the main campus senate to ratify them.

events.title: President establishes a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee
events.body: SGA created a Cultural and Diversity Affairs Committee chaired by Seth Church, who developed the idea for a leadership practicum focused on diversity within SGA and on campus. Church said he collaborated with President Nicki Taylor to create it. Taylor said making SGA more diverse had been an ongoing conversation since her first year and that establishing ad hoc committees was a power she held as president.

events.title: SGA pursues new student fees; Ransdell calls even $4 difficult
events.body: SGA said it would pursue further fee resolutions after passing one the previous semester supporting a $4 per year fee for the Student Legal Services Clinic, and had begun asking students about a roughly $30 fee to fund an estimated $10 million parking structure. President Nicki Taylor said the ideas grew out of student interest in conversation with President Gary Ransdell. Ransdell said approving even a $4 fee would be difficult and that he would be reluctant to take it to the Board of Regents.

events.title: Breast milk expression resolution passes unanimously without debate
events.body: Resolution 4-15-S, supporting creation and maintenance of private areas on campus where students, faculty and staff could express breast milk, passed unanimously and without debate. Chief of Staff Seth Church, who wrote it, said a non-traditional student who had just had her third child brought the problem to him and found the existing unlocked room in a department hall uncomfortable. Church said he wanted no fewer than three permanent spaces.

events.title: Campaign spending caps range from $350 for president to $50 for senators
events.body: Under the spring 2014 election packet, SGA presidential candidates could not spend more than $350, executive vice president candidates $300, administrative vice president candidates $250 and senatorial candidates $50. President Nicki Taylor said she ran unopposed and did not spend a cent, but pointed to the contested 2013 race between Cain Alvey and Keyana Boka. Taylor said Alvey spent every dollar of his $350 limit.

events.title: Two hours of debate over an African Student Union reimbursement
events.body: Bill 8-15-S, allocating $500 to the WKU African Student Union as reimbursement for attending a conference at the University of Kentucky, passed 12 to four with many senators abstaining, after a meeting that ran two hours and ended with fewer senators present. Acting president Henry Nottinson said the reimbursement would lessen the burden on members who had paid out of pocket. He said the group did not have enough money to keep going.

events.title: Former senator publishes a letter alleging corruption in organizational aid
events.body: Jody Dahmer, who had joined SGA as a freshman, published a letter to the editor arguing that a precedent set during the past session had damaged the organizational aid process. He described the standing system under which organizations could receive up to $500 per academic year, reviewed by the administrative vice president and senators under existing bylaws with forms posted on the SGA website. Dahmer wrote that organizations met the committee outside the senate and that reports were then forwarded and voted on quickly.

events.title: SGA funds a $825.95 surveillance camera for the DSU ATMs
events.body: Bill 10-15-S allocated $825.95 to buy and install a surveillance video camera on the ground floor of the Downing Student Union near the ATMs, passing 15-5 after debate. Author J. William Berry said a camera would be far cheaper than relocating the ATMs to an area with more foot traffic. Campus improvements committee chair Tyler Scaff questioned the plan, and Berry noted DSU closes at midnight.

events.title: Richey posts the SGA budget publicly and says he has no figures
events.body: President Jay Todd Richey used social media to be, in his words, "very transparent with the WKU Student Government Association budget." SGA had not yet received its budget for the coming fiscal year, and the Executive Cabinet controlled the budget over the summer. Richey said he had not been given a concrete amount of how much money remained from that year.

events.title: Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening
events.body: WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials.

events.title: Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators
events.body: SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union, before a crowd of about 15 people. There were 742 voters and 17 senators elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive and said not everyone who ran won a seat. The senators-elect were sworn in at the 30 September meeting.

events.title: Senate failed to override the smoking veto and passed an alcohol resolution
events.body: At the final meeting of the fall semester, which ran two and a half hours, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free campus resolution. President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement, which cited enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

events.title: Senate defeated the nonsectarian prayer policy resolution
events.body: After more than 20 minutes of debate the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. Chief of Staff Seth Church explained that a nonsectarian prayer differs from a sectarian one referring to a specific deity. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways, among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all, and that the division sank the resolution. The same night senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

events.title: SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 per semester tuition rise
events.body: SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a $10 million parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build, and the resolution suggested a temporary gravel lot on the site of Tate Page Hall after its anticipated demolition. President Nicki Taylor said the structure had been before the parking and transportation committee for the whole academic year. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out the regional campuses.

events.title: Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution hours after it passed
events.body: The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, and the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued a ban was unfair to students required to live on campus for two years, while author William Berry said he left the location of any smoking areas to the administration and that the ban infringed no student's rights. Senator Haley Jones countered that smoking is legal and that students over 18 can buy tobacco. The policy would not have covered other tobacco products or electronic cigarettes, and senators kept the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

events.title: Ransdell answered four SGA resolutions in an email to faculty and staff
events.body: President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions, on limited smoking, amending the alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct for students over 21, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. On smoking he announced a six-person ad hoc committee of students, faculty and staff to recommend how to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017. On alcohol he said a restaurant facility would be built in the Garrett Conference Center where beer, and possibly wine, could be served in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

events.title: Preston Center memberships cut in half for sixty part-time students
events.body: The senate passed Funding for the Preston Membership Voucher Program, allocating $1,050 so that 60 part-time students could buy a semester membership to the Preston Center at half price. The semester fee for part-time students was $35, and a voucher brought it down to $17.50. It was one of two voucher bills passed that night.

events.title: Fifty ID vouchers, restricted to students who had not lost a card
events.body: After suspending its bylaws to take the bill the same night, the senate passed Funding for the Identification Vouchers Program, allocating $500 to cover half the $20 cost of a WKU ID card for 50 students. The voucher was available only to students who had not previously lost an ID card.
events.money: $500 covering half the cost of 50 cards

events.title: Transcript vouchers handed out first come, first served
events.body: Bill 3-14-F was the only bill to pass that night, allocating $500 to a programme covering the $7 cost of an official transcript request for 60 students, two vouchers to a student. Academic Affairs Committee Chair Josh Knight, who wrote the bill, said $7 might not seem much but some students could not carry the extra expense, and that SGA would consider adding vouchers if demand required it.

events.title: A thirty-nine dollar sticker survey asked students what to fix
events.body: Bill 4-14-F allocated about $39 from legislative discretionary funds to the Campus Improvements Committee for flip charts and multi-coloured dots, to be used in a walk-up survey asking students what they wanted improved on campus. Author Elizabeth McGrew, a Henderson graduate student, said online surveys took too much of students' time and drew fewer responses than a visible one would.
events.money: about $39 for flip charts and dot stickers

events.title: Study Away scholarships funded at $1,200 for a second year
events.body: Bill 6-14-F passed with no debate, allocating $1,200 from Academic Affairs Committee funding for additional scholarships for students applying to Study Away, the programme for travel within the United States rather than abroad. Committee chair Joshua Knight said the same amount had been given the previous year and had been used up, so the committee thought it fair to repeat it.
events.money: $1,200, the same as the year before

events.title: SGA picked its director of public relations as homecoming nominee
events.body: At the same meeting SGA voted Director of Public Relations KJ Hall as its 2014 Homecoming nominee, and swore in newly elected senators.

events.title: Student Legal Services Clinic opened with an SGA resolution behind it
events.body: WKU's Student Legal Services Clinic was set to open on Friday 30 January in Tate Page Hall room 252, after four years of on-and-off preparation by paralegal studies professor Julie Shadoan. It was open to all students including part-time, transfer, international and regional campus students, drew on about twelve volunteer attorneys, and charged $30 an hour against roughly $300 an hour for an average attorney. SGA President Nicki Taylor said SGA had passed a resolution supporting the clinic and the creation of a $4 student fee to pay for an in-house attorney.
events.money: $30 an hour against about $300 for an average attorney

events.title: Five hundred dollars to promote the Community Farmers Market
events.body: Bill 4-15-S, Funding to Support the Community Farmers Market, passed unanimously and without debate, allocating $500 from legislative discretionary funds to the Office of Sustainability to promote the market to students. Co-author Brian Chism said the point was to let students know what food options were available to them.

events.title: Senate passed a $138,500 budget for the year
events.body: The SGA budget for the year was passed at $138,500 at the same meeting that swore in three new senators and approved the Preston and identification voucher programmes. Seats remained open and election applications were due 15 September.

events.title: Senate asked WKU to let unused meal swipes roll over
events.body: Resolution 5-14-F passed with no debate, supporting an amendment to university dining policy so that meal swipes left at the end of a week could carry forward as meal plans or meal plan dollars rather than being forfeited on Sunday. Author William Berry said students paid for those swipes and should not lose them. He said Aramark was running a feasibility test on whether meal plan prices would have to rise to make a rollover work.

events.title: Both attempts to change discretionary funding died at the final meeting
events.body: At the last meeting of the spring the senate took up two competing approaches to Legislative Discretionary Aid. Resolution 11-15-S by Senator Jody Dahmer, which would have stopped SGA giving discretionary money directly to individual students and organisations and pushed them to the Organizational Aid Committee, failed 11-7 for want of a two-thirds majority; Dahmer argued that without a system, senators could end up promising kickbacks for votes, while Senator Josh Knight opposed any blanket ban on recognising special cases. Bill 15-15-S, which would have split the remaining discretionary money between five organisations that had missed the organizational aid deadline, tied 7-7 and Speaker of the Senate Jay Todd Richey broke the tie against it.

events.title: Senate adopted amendments to the Glasgow campus constitution
events.body: Resolution 6-14-F was first read on 28 October 2014 and passed on 11 November. It stated that the Glasgow Student Body, incorporated as a regional affiliate two years earlier, had been unable to raise enough student interest to fill and maintain an executive cabinet, student senate and judicial council. Seth Church wrote it, with GSBA president Samantha Johnson listed as a contact.

events.title: Bylaw amendment required roll-call voting and posted minutes
events.body: Resolution 3-15-S, first read 24 February 2015 and passed 3 March, added Bylaw 2.7 requiring every vote in any branch to be taken by roll call or electronic voting, recorded in the minutes, and posted by the Director of Information Technology or the Secretary of the Senate within one week. The text set the amendment to take effect on 17 March 2015. Zach Jones and Seth Church wrote it.

src.label: SGA Resolution 3-15-S, Resolution to Adopt an Amendment to the Bylaws to Increase Accountability

events.title: Senate introduces resolution over being left out of the Gatton housing decision
events.body: SGA senator Cole McDowell introduced a resolution responding to Housing and Residence Life's decision to move Gatton Academy students into Bates-Runner Hall, pushing current Bates residents into Gilbert Hall, without consulting SGA first. The resolution was postponed to the following week's meeting to await the outcome of a joint SGA, Gatton and Housing meeting called by Campus Improvements Committee Chair Tyler Scaff. McDowell said the resolution was not a judgment on the decision itself, but a statement that senators had not been given the chance to represent students' views on it.

events.title: Five new committee chairs take over at first fall meeting
events.body: SGA's first meeting of 2014-15 opened in new senate chambers with the induction of eight new members and new committee chairs: Josh Knight for Academic Affairs, Kasey Glasgow for Student Affairs, James Line for Public Relations, Paige Settles for Legislative Research and Tyler Scaff for Campus Improvement. President Nicki Seay said she was looking forward to the year's leadership.

events.title: SGA publishes open letter defending its election process
events.body: After a competitive 2015 executive and senate election drew heavy Herald coverage and produced appeals over campaign posters, SGA published an open letter as a letter to the editor thanking the paper for its attention, defending the Judicial Affairs Council's handling of the appeals as fair and transparent, and announcing a coming "rebranding period" meant to improve diversity, transparency and public understanding of SGA's role. Director of Public Relations Sawyer Coffey was listed as the contact for questions.

executive.name: Nicki Taylor
executive.note: Took office in August 2014 as Nicki Seay; called Nicki Taylor in coverage from mid-October 2014 on.

executive.name: Nolan Miles
profile: Nolan Miles won a senate seat in the fall 2011 election, one of eleven senators elected from a field of twenty with 977 students voting.

He served as executive vice president for 2014-15 alongside President Nicki Seay — who was going by the surname Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October that year — and Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler. Miles ran unopposed for a second term as EVP in the spring 2015 election that made Jay Todd Richey president, and that August, opening the new term, said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event.

executive.name: Liz Koehler
profile: Liz Koehler served as SGA's administrative vice president for 2014-15, taking office that August alongside President Nicki Seay and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles.

Koehler won a second term in the spring 2015 election, taking 66 percent of the vote over J. William Berry, in the same election that made Jay Todd Richey president and returned Miles unopposed for a second term as executive vice president. That September, after SGA's budget fell $19,500 — largely because a one-time $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut a further $4,500 — she reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss. The following February she reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, a loss of $1,301.27, amid the senate's debate over a state tuition-freeze bill.

executive.office: Director of Academic and Student Affairs
executive.name: Barrett Greenwell
executive.note: Held the post in the autumn of 2014, attending the 26 August cabinet orientation and the 28 October meeting; by February 2015 Megan Skaggs held the office.
profile: Barrett Greenwell won a senate seat as a freshman in September 2012, one of four new senators sworn in that fall alongside two resignations. SGA's cabinet records list him as Student Affairs Committee chair in 2013-14.

Greenwell joined the executive cabinet as director of academic and student affairs for 2014-15, attending the cabinet's August 26 orientation and its October 28 meeting; by February 2015 Megan Skaggs held the post instead. He returned to the office for 2015-16, named on the executive cabinet's minutes from December 2015.

executive.office: Director of Academic and Student Affairs
executive.name: Megan Skaggs
executive.note: Recorded in the office at the 10 February 2015 cabinet meeting and absent from the 14 April 2015 meeting.
profile: Megan Skaggs was head of the Academic Affairs committee in the Student Government Association senate in fall 2013, when she authored a bill re-funding SGA's Transcript Voucher Program, which let students get a transcript free with a voucher instead of paying the $7 fee, limited to two per student under this funding round. The bill passed unanimously at the senate meeting the Herald reported in its 26 September 2013 issue. Skaggs told the Herald, "students pay quite a bit as it is for tuition and other fees."

By the start of the spring 2015 semester SGA had appointed her director of Academic and Student Affairs; the appointment was reported at the senate's first meeting back from winter break, alongside President Nicki Taylor announcing several other new positions.

Skaggs ran for senate in the April 2015 elections and won one of the 20 seats filled out of 34 candidates. By the fall 2015 semester the Herald identified her with legislative research in its coverage of a late-September SGA meeting, where senators also voted her the organization's Homecoming queen candidate.

profile: Sawyer Coffey was in office as SGA's director of public relations by the cabinet's 10 February 2015 meeting, succeeding KJ Hall, and on 14 April 2015 she seconded and voted for Senate Resolution 7-15-S. After a competitive and closely watched 2015 executive and senate election, SGA published an open letter thanking the Herald for its election coverage and announcing a coming "rebranding period," listing Coffey as the contact for questions.

Coffey continued as public relations director in 2015-16. That November she said SGA removed "Spirit Masters" from its "Dub the Pub" naming contest for the new Garrett Conference Center pub "out of respect for the organization," after WKU administrators objected that it demeaned the university's student ambassador group. In spring 2016 she reported to the senate that a promotional video for SGA and WKU had reached 28,000 views and 27 shares.

officers.note: The cabinet minutes call him Cole McDowell; the SGA senate leadership page rendered the name Patrick Mcdowell. Both records are for the same office in the same year and the archive should not resolve the two without better evidence.
profile: Cole McDowell was sworn in as a freshman senator in September 2012, representing the incoming class alongside Barrett Greenwell, Paige Settles and Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz. As a senator in 2014-15 he authored a resolution objecting that SGA had not been consulted before Housing and Residence Life decided to move Gatton Academy students into Bates-Runner Hall, introduced and reported to the senate on 11 November 2014, where it was postponed to await a joint SGA, Gatton and Housing meeting; he said the resolution was not a judgment on the decision itself, but a statement that senators could not represent student views on decisions they were never told about. SGA's cabinet minutes also name him secretary of the student senate that year, though the senate's own leadership page rendered the name "Patrick Mcdowell" for the same office — a discrepancy the archive has left unresolved rather than guessed at.

The Senate reappointed McDowell secretary for 2015-16, this time named by Speaker Paige Settles and approved at the senate's first meeting on 1 September 2015; he asked fellow senators that December to tell him if they did not plan to return in the spring. In that capacity he argued in February 2016 for lowering SGA's own senator GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, saying "if a 2.0 is good enough for the university, then it's good enough for me" — the amendment failed. The same spring he brought a resolution asking WKU to include a faculty and staff salary increase in the 2016-17 budget and to guarantee raises in future years, citing a Herald report that administrators were considering the idea; President Gary Ransdell had already expressed support for a raise, though the archive has found no record of the resolution's ultimate fate.

profile: James Line chaired SGA's public relations committee in 2014-15, one of five new committee chairmen named at the first senate meeting of the year on 3 September 2014, alongside Josh Knight, Kasey Glasgow, Paige Settles and Tyler Scaff.
