events.title: Narrower DACA solidarity resolution passed 32-1
events.body: At its 7 November meeting the senate passed, by 32 votes to 1, a resolution co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and former senator Francisco Serrano standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. It was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community rather than call on legislators, which Dahmer said kept it within "a jurisdiction that we do have." Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last schools in Kentucky to pass a measure of this kind. The same meeting unanimously funded the Go With the Flow program, allocating over $580 for free menstrual products in five campus buildings.

events.title: Senate voted 29-1 for a required sexual assault course in the Colonnade
events.body: Resolution 1-17-F, supporting the addition of a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to Colonnade requirements for first-year students, passed 29-1 with two abstentions at the Tuesday night meeting. It was co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three other members, and argued that existing options such as HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. Hurst said a student could pass four years at WKU without any sexual assault training, calling that "a disgrace, to say the least." Senator Alex Sergent described the resolution as closing holes in an existing net rather than adding a graduation hurdle, and the same meeting funded a No-Shave November beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws.

events.title: All seven justices censured a senator on a ten-student petition
events.body: At a second emergency meeting the council took up a censure request signed by ten students, both senators and other WKU students, over Senator William Hurst's profanity, gestures and walking out of the previous emergency meeting. Chief Justice Annalicia Carlson refused Hurst's request for the petitioners' names and referred further inquiries to SGA adviser Charlie Pride. Hurst apologised for the outburst and argued a censure required neglect of duties. All seven justices voted in favour of the censure.

src.label: Judicial Council emergency meeting minutes, 4 Feb 2018

events.title: Council dismissed a senator from the Senate
events.body: Meeting online, the Judicial Council dismissed Senator Annabelle Ford from the Senate for failing to notify the Judicial Council, President Andi Dahmer or Speaker Ryan Richardson of the reasons for her multiple unexcused absences.

events.title: Council censured a senator and ruled voting records public
events.body: The Judicial Council voted unanimously to censure Senator Dallas McKinney. On a request from student Jayden Thomas, who wanted senators' voting records viewable, it held that section 1.4 of the constitution required public records to be accessible to any member of student government and that section 2.6 of the bylaws could mean any official area such as the website or the SGA office. It also ruled that SGA could not endorse a candidate although other organisations could, and named Jacob McAndrews as the next chief justice with Lane Hedrick continuing as associate chief justice, both pending Senate approval.

events.title: On appeal the council reduced the disqualification to a suspension
events.body: Both disqualified campaigns appealed with the ten signatures that obliged the council to hear them. Chief Justice Annalicia Carlson abstained on the MEA ticket's appeal; Isaac Keller, Jacob McAndrews and Caroline Simpson voted to suspend the campaign and require an apology, Megan Armstrong and Lane Hedrick again to disqualify, so the suspension stood. The council voted unanimously to reinstate the McAvoy campaign. Fifty-five guests were recorded present, including Herald reporter Nicole Ziege.

executive.name: Savannah Molyneaux
profile: Molyneaux chaired SGA's Sustainability committee in 2016-17 before running for re-election as executive vice president in April 2018 on a ticket with presidential candidate Conner Hounshell and Administrative Vice President Kara Lowry. Days before the vote, the Judicial Council disqualified, then suspended, the rival Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson ticket over a Pepe the Frog meme in its campaign chalking; Stephen Mayer's ticket was reinstated to run and won, with Hounshell's ticket placing second. Molyneaux, Lowry and Hounshell were all elected senators instead.

In February 2018 she joined President Andi Dahmer, Lowry and Hounshell in writing Resolution 3-18-S opposing the scale of a renegotiated Aramark dining-fee increase, which would have raised a per-semester fee on students without meal plans from $75 toward $350 over ten years; the Senate passed it unanimously.

At the Senate's final meeting of the year, Molyneaux spoke about what she called an "awful" year for the executive board, describing sexism and misogyny within the Senate and backing Dahmer's account, reported the same week, of harassment she said she had faced as president. Molyneaux cited the threatening note left on Dahmer's car and the derogatory names used in the SGA offices, and told senators who had taken part in it to think about what they had done.

executive.name: Conner Hounshell
profile: Hounshell served as SGA's Chief of Staff in 2017-18 and ran for president that April on a ticket with Executive Vice President Savannah Molyneaux and Administrative Vice President Kara Lowry, both seeking re-election. Days before the vote the Judicial Council disqualified, then suspended, the rival Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson ticket over a Pepe the Frog meme in its campaign chalking. Hounshell's ticket won 33 percent of the presidential vote to Mayer's 35 percent; all three were elected senators instead.
In February 2018 he co-authored Resolution 3-18-S with President Andi Dahmer, Molyneaux and Lowry, opposing the scale of a renegotiated Aramark dining-fee increase on students without meal plans.

He had recommended Garrett Edmonds, whom he met when Edmonds joined SGA in fall 2017, for the chair of the Campus Improvements committee, but by the following fall told the Herald his opinion of Edmonds had completely changed after the chalking controversy. The Herald's account of that criticism, and Edmonds's own answer to it, are in the article cited here; the archive does not restate one side of it in the other man's record.

He became chair of the Committee of Diversity and Inclusion in February 2018, replacing Corey Newsome, who had stepped down over scheduling conflicts. The same week, on 13 February, the senate unanimously passed Resolution 1-18-S, which Clark co-authored with Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell and Kara Lowry, supporting an integrated LGBTQ-health curriculum at WKU.

profile: Ian Hamilton was a WKU SGA senator for 2016-17 and 2017-18. He authored a bill at the Senate's April 2017 meeting to move the power to appoint Senate committee heads from the SGA president to the speaker of the Senate; President Jay Todd Richey argued the change would compromise the speaker's meant-to-be-impartial role, and the bill failed 15-3. Hamilton was elected a senator-at-large for 2017-18 in that spring's election.

As chair of the Sustainability Committee once it became a permanent SGA committee that fall, Hamilton co-authored Bill 10-17-F, funding a "No-Shave November" beard-growing contest; he amended its budget down from $250 to $100 at the September 2017 meeting, and it passed 25-3. He also co-authored Bill 16-17-F, funding an Interfaith Workshop on Sustainability and Social Justice, which passed unanimously, and, with Senator Garrett Edmonds, Bill 17-17-F, funding a chalk campaign for Mission: Thank You Veterans. The following February he authored Bill 10-18-S, funding the 2018 Earth Day Festival.

At the Senate's 24 January 2018 meeting, called amid a dispute over a postponed appointment and a reported "irregularity" in that year's SGA election, Hamilton was one of four students who addressed the chamber; he read aloud a letter from former senate member Luke Edmonds, who could not attend, expressing condolences after the shooting at Marshall County High School.

profile: Ryan Richardson was Speaker of the Senate in 2017-18, under President Andi Dahmer. He presided over the Senate's contentious spring 2018 business on funding Lavender Graduation stoles for LGBTQ students: the bill passed 28-5 on 20 March with Senator Dallas McKinney speaking against it without giving a reason, and at the following meeting on 27 March McKinney returned to explain that vote, citing his reading of the Bible, after which other senators spoke against deciding university business from scripture.

Earlier that month, on 6 March 2018, the Judicial Council met online and dismissed Senator Annabelle Ford from the Senate for failing to notify the Judicial Council, President Dahmer or Speaker Richardson of the reasons for her unexcused absences.

officers.name: Annalicia Carlson
officers.note: Swore in the committee chairs, the senators elected in spring 2017 and the members of the executive cabinet at the first meeting of the sixteenth Senate on 29 August 2017, and swore in the Secretary of the Senate the same night. On 10 April 2018 she told the Senate the council would elect its new Chief Justice that evening.
profile: Carlson served as associate chief justice of the Judicial Council for 2016-17, the year Cody Cox was chief justice, and was chosen by the council to succeed him as chief justice for 2017-18 in March 2017, pending Senate confirmation.

As chief justice she swore in committee chairs, senators and cabinet members at the Senate's first meeting of the year on 29 August 2017, and in January 2018 chaired an emergency Judicial Council session on discrepancies in a fall referendum on constitutional amendments. In April 2018 she led the council through the most consequential ruling of her term: an emergency meeting disqualified the Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson presidential ticket, and separately senator candidate Anna McAvoy, for using a Pepe the Frog meme in campaign chalking that the council found violated the election code's ban on inappropriate depictions in sidewalk chalk and the constitution's anti-discrimination clause. Carlson told the Herald the whole ticket was held responsible because executive vice presidential candidate Garrett Edmonds had put the candidates' names on the chalking, and had been told the meme was used as a hate symbol but did not have it removed.

After a senate meeting drew unusually large attendance from students objecting to the ruling, the Senate created a new appeal process, and the council itself voted 3-2 with one abstention to reduce the MEA ticket's penalty from disqualification to suspension with a required apology, later doing the same for McAvoy. The reinstated Mayer-Edmonds-Anderson ticket went on to win the election. Carlson's term ended in April 2018 when the Senate elected Associate Justice Jacob McAndrews to succeed her.

Carlson returned to the council as an associate justice for 2018-19. In the spring of 2019 she argued against confirming President Stephen Mayer's nominee to a vacant council seat, saying the council itself preferred Erika Puhakka. In May 2019, in her final weeks as a graduating senior, an impeachment petition was brought against her alleging she had inconsistently listed spring 2019 candidates' preferred and legal names on the ballot and had overstepped her role during Wood Brown's confirmation hearing to advance Puhakka's candidacy instead. Carlson rebutted the naming allegation directly, saying names were checked for GPA eligibility, and more generally said that after four years in SGA she "would never intentionally jeopardize it." The Senate canceled the hearing for lack of attendance the day it was scheduled, and the archive found no record it was ever rescheduled.

profile: Jayden Thomas was a senator in WKU SGA's 2017-18 session. With Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell and senator Mark Clark, Thomas co-authored Bill 13-18-S, allocating $250 from Senate Discretionary, matched by $250 from Executive Discretionary, to purchase stoles for graduates attending WKU's Lavender Graduation ceremony on 8 May 2018, honoring the university's LGBTQ and ally graduates. The bill passed on second reading, 20 March 2018.

By 2018-19 Thomas chaired the Sustainability Committee. As chair, Thomas authored Bill 17-18-F, which passed 32-1 and put $100 toward a Sustainability Day gift basket for 14 November 2018, and presented Bill 33-19-S at the 23 April 2019 meeting, funding paid to Downing Student Union to cover the cost of an Earth Day festival, which passed 20-0.

officers.name: Lucas Knight
profile: Lucas Knight was elected one of two senior student senators in the April 2017 SGA election and served through 2017-18, additionally holding the title Fairness Representative. At the Sept. 12, 2017 meeting he co-authored, with Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell, the bill funding SGA's support for Bowling Green's inaugural Pride Festival, and said he had "supported this concept for the past three years," a reference to Bowling Green's long-stalled Fairness Ordinance. In November 2017 he was a named senator on Resolution 7-17-F, asking Bowling Green to pass a Fairness Ordinance and voicing support for WKU's LGBTQ students.

Knight co-authored, with William Hurst, a bylaws amendment fixing set election windows for constitutional amendments, and, with Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell, Matthew Barr and Dallas McKinney, a constitutional amendment restructuring several senator seats around transfer, non-traditional and Intercultural Student Engagement Center students. At the March 20, 2018 meeting he spoke in favor of funding stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates, calling it "a very small way of giving back to the LGBTQ+ community"; the bill passed 28-5 after Senator Dallas McKinney spoke against it without giving his reasoning.

profile: Amanda Harder served as an SGA senator during the 2017-18 year. She co-authored, with senator Logan Hornback, Bill 15-18-S, which the Senate passed unanimously on March 20, 2018 to fund $300 for the newly formed WKU Students for Breast Cancer Awareness and its "#WhyIFight" fundraising campaign. Harder said her mother had been diagnosed with breast cancer and that the cause was "something I'm really passionate about."

By the 2018-19 year Harder chaired the Academic and Student Affairs Committee. She was lead author, with students Mary Fyfe, Alec Zaffiro, Krystal Neal and Taylor Vowels, of Resolution 5-19-S, which the Senate passed 23-1 on April 23, 2019 to support installing a $5 student fee funding the College Heights Herald, citing SGA's past legislation backing the Herald in its public-records lawsuit against WKU.

officers.name: Logan Hornback
profile: Logan Hornback was a senator-at-large in WKU SGA's 2017-18 session. With senator Amanda Harder, Hornback co-authored Bill 15-18-S, allocating $300 to the newly formed WKU Students for Breast Cancer Awareness for its #WhyIFight fundraising campaign, and was among six senators and officers named on Bill 17-18-S, which put $500 toward Take Back the Night event T-shirts during Sexual Assault Prevention Month. Both bills passed on second reading in March 2018.

Student Body President Stephen Mayer nominated Hornback to fill a vacant at-large Senate seat at the meeting of 16 October 2018. A vote-counting software error initially reported that the confirmation vote had failed; the error was found and corrected later that night, and it was ruled Hornback had in fact been elected to the seat, the Herald reported two months later when a second contested nomination revived the story. Hornback continued serving into spring 2019 and spoke in favor of a $5 student fee to fund the Herald at the 23 April 2019 meeting, saying that although the fee would add to tuition, "at least we know it will benefit the rest of the students."

profile: Alex Sergent chaired SGA's Public Relations Committee during the 2016-17 year. At the Nov. 29, 2016 meeting he argued the proposed Jonesville Memorial Scholarship should be open to all minority students rather than African American students alone, asking whether the goal was repaying Jonesville specifically or, in his words, "extending that same hand toward all minorities that are currently struggling on campus;" the Senate kept the scholarship limited to African American recipients.

Sergent continued in the Senate as a senator at large through 2017-18, by his own account his third year in SGA. He was a named senator on two November 2017 resolutions, one asking WKU to add a required sexual-assault-education course and one supporting restoration of the Major Redz student organization's traditional reserved football-stadium section, and he made the motion, passed unanimously, to let student speakers address the Senate first at the April 17, 2018 meeting on the disqualification of the MEA executive ticket. As Public Relations Committee vice chair, he stepped in as interim chair when Will Hurst missed the March 20, 2018 meeting, telling the Herald, "I have not been given any details as to what is going on."

Describing the Senate's fractious 2017-18 year, Sergent compared the tension to a storm, where "two major thoughts start to collide and they mix," and said the result was not inherently bad. He said the friction came from new senators challenging established norms, and that this was something worth celebrating.

profile: Lily Nellans was a senator in WKU SGA's 2016-17 session. With senators Brian Anderson, James Line and Jay Todd Richey, she co-authored Bill 20-17-S, "Bill to Encourage Inclusivity in Student Organizations," requiring student organizations to commit to inclusivity before receiving Organizational Aid funding, written in response to a Kentucky law signed 20 March 2017 that let campus organizations discriminate when it aligned with their beliefs. The bill passed 17-9-1 on second reading, 28 March 2017.

In the April 2017 SGA election, Nellans ran for student body president and placed third, with 212 of 1,579 votes cast, behind winner Andi Dahmer (930 votes) and Kenan Mujkanovic (305 votes). In the same election she was elected one of twelve senators-at-large for 2017-18. That session, with senator Mark Clark and WKU student Francisco Serrano, she co-authored Resolution 7-17-F, "Resolution to Support Our LGBTQ Students," calling on the Bowling Green City Commission to pass a Fairness Ordinance protecting residents from discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity; it passed second reading 28 November 2017.

leaders.name: Stephen Mayer
leaders.note: Confirmed by an independent WKU record outside the plaque: the University Senate's Nov. 15, 2018 meeting agenda lists him under reports as "SGA President: Stephen Mayer."

sources.label: WKU University Senate meeting agenda, 15 Nov 2018

profile: Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent in April 2018 on the MEA ticket with Garrett Edmonds and Harper Anderson, taking 35 percent of 2,378 presidential votes against Conner Hounshell's 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic's 32 percent; 2,447 students voted overall. His ticket won only after the Judicial Council reversed a disqualification it had imposed days before the election over the campaign's use of a Pepe the Frog meme chalked on campus sidewalks, downgrading the penalty to a campaign suspension.

A biology and chemistry double major who had served three semesters as a senator and studied at Harlaxton College, Mayer opened his term in September 2018 promising greater transparency from both the Board of Regents and SGA, and required senators to log a weekly office hour. As student regent he was an outspoken critic of WKU's fee structure, especially the $450 online academic fee, and opposed that year's 4 percent tuition increase, saying he did not see the need to put the financial burden "on the students' backs."

events.title: Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term
events.body: The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week.

events.title: Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries
events.body: The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience.

events.title: First Year Village housing plan presented to SGA
events.body: Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention.

events.title: Senate creates a recurring $2,000 first-generation scholarship
events.body: A bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr establishing a $2,000 scholarship awarded once per academic year to first-generation students passed 31-1; the Herald cited a 2017 WKU Fact Book study finding an estimated 34.8 percent of first-year, first-time students in fall 2016 were first-generation. The senate also passed organizational aid Bill 11-18-F, sending $1,400 to Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club, and allocated $100 to advertise the Campus Safety Walk.

events.title: Contested appointment and Identity Evropa denouncement ended the fall term
events.body: President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of former SGA adviser Charley Pride, to a vacated senate seat produced roughly an hour and a half of debate; a motion to table failed 8-19-1, and Senator Kara Lowry opposed the nomination over Pride's work on Braxton Powell's earlier presidential campaign. Pride was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F.

events.title: Senate voted 29-1 to move the Confederate capital marker
events.body: After lengthy debate the senate passed Resolution 1-19-S by 29-1 with one abstention, calling for the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky to be relocated to a display inside the museum. Authors Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin argued the marker was a reminder of oppression against people of color, and an amendment made before the resolution was presented changed the ask from removal to relocation, which Lowry called "a good compromise for people who believe that [the marker] is preserving history." Mayer said the resolution would go to the WKU Administrative Council rather than the University Senate, and the senate allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament.

events.title: Mayer declined to seek re-election as election codes were set
events.body: Stephen Mayer told the senate he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical school. The spring 2019 election codes passed 31-1 after every proposed amendment was struck down but one friendly amendment from Senator John May barring sitting Judicial Council members from running, with campaigning to begin April 1 and voting on TopNet April 15-16; Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews then announced he would resign from the Judicial Council to campaign. The senate also passed four spending bills and tabled a bill creating a first-generation senate seat, while Bill 19-19-S, which would have let senators substitute tabling for office hours, failed 18-10 for want of a two-thirds majority.

events.title: No-confidence vote and provost's resignation shook the university
events.body: After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs.

events.title: WGK ticket won the spring executive elections
events.body: The ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, defeating the ticket of Asha McWilliams, Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. Harris was elected student body president to succeed Mayer, Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president, and Mujkanovic defeated Whalin for administrative vice president, with results announced at SGA's election party on April 16.

events.title: Former SGA president sues WKU, Caboni and two administrators
events.body: Andi Dahmer filed suit against WKU, President Timothy Caboni, Assistant General Counsel Andrea Anderson and Director of Student Activities Charley Pride, citing verbal, mental and emotional abuse and alleging sex discrimination and failure to follow the university's Discrimination and Harassment Policy. The university called the allegations "maliciously untrue" and said it would vigorously defend the claims. WKU said its Title IX office found no Title IX violation but did find Student Code of Conduct violations, for which students were sanctioned.

events.title: Senate votes down both of the new president's executive nominees
events.body: Stephen Mayer's nominees were rejected in his first confirmation votes: Wood Brown for associate justice failed 8-7 with one abstention and one exemption, and Anna McAvoy for director of academic and student affairs failed 6-9, both short of the required two-thirds. Senators questioned Mayer's ability to judge candidates when he had been sequestered from the Judicial Council's interviews. The 2018-19 budget of $100,000, a $15,000 reduction from the prior year, passed 13-4.

events.title: WKU denies Dahmer's claims in court filing
events.body: WKU filed its response on Sept. 19 denying that Dahmer suffered a hostile educational environment or sexual harassment during her presidency, and stating she never reported to the Office of Student Conduct or the Title IX coordinator but instead told her residence hall director, who triggered the investigation. The university said the investigation found Student Code of Conduct violations by certain SGA members, who were sanctioned. It argued the GroupMe messages were never intended for Dahmer and so caused her no harm. Dahmer is seeking $75,000 in damages.

events.title: Bill to cut off Greek organization funding postponed 17-15
events.body: Bill 10-18-F, written by Senator Amy Wyer and Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark to bar SGA funding to Interfraternity Council and Panhellenic Council chapters, was pulled from the agenda and postponed to Oct. 16 on a 17-15 vote because of its content. Two funding bills moved forward the same night, giving $150 to the student ID voucher program and $1,500 to the Office of Study Away.

events.title: Greek defunding bill fails by one vote after long debate
events.body: Bill 10-18-F was defeated 16-17. Author Amy Wyer, herself a member of Alpha Gamma Delta, cited the University of Alabama's Machine coalition and said only one non-Greek member had been elected to that student government since 1914, warning "I fear we have the potential to move in this direction." Former senator Alex Sargent argued against telling students who pay the same tuition that their social needs matter less. A motion to table failed 21-14, short of two-thirds.

events.title: Colonnade textbook library tabled amid questions about the bookstore
events.body: Bill 18-18-F, allocating $1,000 to stock a used-textbook library for Colonnade courses in the SGA offices, was tabled 24-3 with one abstention after debate over funding and over whether the collection would stay current as Colonnade courses change. Senator Amy Wyer asked why the WKU Bookstore was "making us buy books they can't resell." Two bylaw amendments passed the same night, one adding flexibility in appointing regional ambassadors and one adding protection against discrimination on the basis of gender identity.

events.title: Senate votes 30-0 to defend transgender student protections
events.body: Resolution 7-18-F, written by Diversity and Inclusion Chair Mark Clark in response to reports that the Trump administration was considering narrowly redefining sex, pledged to preserve and improve protections for transgender and nonconforming students regardless of federal action. It passed 30-0. Resolution 8-18-F requiring all new campus buildings to meet LEED standards passed 29-0, and Bill 23-18-F tightening executive board appointments to require a two-thirds senate vote passed 28-1.

events.title: Nine senators forced to step down, leaving the chamber depleted
events.body: SGA opened the spring semester with vacant seats after nine senators were required to step down from their positions. Mayer presented a slate of nominees to fill them, to be voted on the following week. No new legislation was introduced at the meeting.

events.title: Study abroad scholarship bill pulled after five competing motions
events.body: Bill 2-19-S, which would have barred students who had already received an SGA study abroad scholarship from reapplying, was pulled from the agenda after debate produced five motions ranging from amendments to a 30-second cap on further speeches. Its author, Jayden Thomas, argued that repeatedly awarding the scholarship to the same students was unfair. Speaker Asha McWilliams said the debate showed the senate "doing what it is supposed to do."

events.title: Rewritten study abroad bill passes with a first-timer bonus
events.body: Bill 7-19-S replaced the outright ban on repeat applicants with a 15 percent scoring bonus for students who had not previously studied abroad. Senator Josh Zaczek argued during debate that the change was "detracting from a merit-based scholarship" and that applicants' claims could not be verified. Authors Jayden Thomas and Amanda Harder had rewritten the bill after concerns about its exclusionary effect.

events.title: Dahmer adds a retaliation claim, alleging Caboni pulled a Rhodes recommendation
events.body: Dahmer moved to amend her complaint to add retaliation, claiming Caboni withdrew his endorsement of her Rhodes Scholarship application "without any reason or explanation" after she sued. Text messages from Office of Scholar Development Director Audra Jennings indicating Caboni would endorse her were submitted as evidence, along with a later email in which Jennings said "I cannot discuss the matter with you." Dahmer continued to seek $75,000 in damages.

events.title: Senate votes 23-1 for a $5 student fee to fund the Herald
events.body: Resolution 5-19-S endorsed a $5 per-student publications fee to support the College Heights Herald, noting the University of Kentucky charges $2 for the Kernel and Texas State charges $8 for the University Star. Academic and Student Affairs Chair Amanda Harder said SGA had previously backed the Herald in its ongoing lawsuit against WKU. Senators also unanimously amended the constitution to require the SGA website be kept updated and to use gender-neutral pronouns, and elected Nathan Terrell speaker 15-11.

events.title: Judge orders WKU to release records to Dahmer
events.body: A judge ruled in favor of releasing records Dahmer sought in discovery, including complaints relating to Charley Pride, Title IX investigation statements, and records of other SGA members' discrimination or harassment complaints since August 2017. WKU had objected broadly on the grounds that the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act excluded the material as educational records. Dahmer and attorney Lindsay Cordes argued the records were "relevant to prove an atmosphere of discrimination."

events.title: Impeachment hearing for a Judicial Council member called off
events.body: SGA scheduled and then canceled an impeachment hearing for Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson after determining too few senators would attend. The petition accused her of inconsistently listing spring 2019 candidates by preferred or legal name, noting Garrett Edmonds appeared as "James" with his surname misspelled, and of overstepping during Wood Brown's failed confirmation. Carlson, who graduated that week, said legal names were used because a GPA check was required, and called the effort a waste of resources that showed "the pettiness of the organization."

events.title: Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day and to loosen the conduct code
events.body: SGA passed Resolution 5-18-F 15-0, asking the university to cancel classes on 6 November 2018 so students could get to the polls, and Bill 7-18-F, giving $300 to the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote. Francis Wilson of Reg 2 Vote told senators that of 290,000 Kentucky students registered in 2016, only about 13 percent voted. Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike Student Code of Conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings, both passed 14-0. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

events.title: Senate passed a transparency resolution 30-2 after the dean's sudden resignation
events.body: A week after Potter College Dean Larry Snyder resigned abruptly, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by 30 votes to 2, saying top university officials must explain major decisions and carry them out in a manner that protects the dignity of those involved. Mayer's renomination of Wood Brown to the Judicial Council was struck down 17-11, short of two-thirds, after Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson said the council preferred Erika Puhakka. A bill creating a senate seat for first-generation college students passed 33-0. A resolution brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization, asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, also passed 33-0.

events.title: Almost 900 students voted in a fall election with nearly 70 candidates
events.body: Voting for the SGA senate ran on TopNet on 17 and 18 September, with almost 900 students casting ballots among nearly 70 candidates. SGA held a results party in the Senate Chambers, and the counts came in about fifteen minutes past midnight on 19 September. Student Body President Stephen Mayer called the turnout amazing. Seven senators at large, three freshman senators and an Intercultural Student Engagement Center senator were seated.
events.money: almost 900 votes cast for nearly 70 candidates

events.title: A hundred and fifty dollars of Subway for the campus safety walk
events.body: Bill 15-18-F passed, allocating $150 for Subway catering at the WKU Campus Safety Walk set for 14 November. The Herald report was printed before the walk and says only what was funded.

events.title: A hundred dollars for a Sustainability Day basket
events.body: Bill 17-18-F, written by Sustainability Committee Chair Jayden Thomas, passed 32-1 and put $100 towards a basket for Sustainability Day on 14 November, sponsored jointly by SGA and its Sustainability Committee. This records the funding; the report predates the day itself.

events.title: Twenty-four SGA members went to the Rally for Higher Education
events.body: SGA sent 24 members, the executive board and selected senators, to the annual Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort, joining delegations from Murray State and other universities across the Commonwealth. The WKU delegation was led by Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, who said higher education was not just about students but about culture and communities. Director of Information Technology Paul Brosky said he hoped the students would be heard by legislators. The Herald report was printed on the morning of the rally.

events.title: Second Unite for Fairness night filled DSU with handwritten letters
events.body: SGA and the Queer Student Union held the second Unite for Fairness event in Downing Student Union, where students wrote letters to Bowling Green city commissioners in support of a fairness ordinance. State Representative and WKU history professor Patti Minter, a member of the Bowling Green fairness movement since 1999, gave a presentation on its history before students began writing. SGA Director of Public Relations Noah Moore, who had helped organise the first event the previous semester, said a handwritten letter would reach a commissioner more than an email or a phone call.

events.title: Two hundred and fifty dollars for Lavender Graduation
events.body: Bill 25-19-S passed 25-0, allocating $250 for Lavender Graduation, the ceremony recognising the achievements of LGBT graduates and their allies. The money covered stoles, decorations and food.

events.title: Women's Forum funding doubled on the floor to $200
events.body: Bill 28-19-S came to the floor asking $100 for the upcoming Women's Forum and was friendly amended to $200, half from the food budget and half from the senate discretionary fund, and to add buttons alongside the brownies, cookies and light refreshments. It passed 25-0.

events.title: Two justices confirmed and six spending bills passed in one night
events.body: With President Stephen Mayer absent ill and his report read by Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, the senate confirmed Erika Puhakka as an associate justice 27-0 and Isaac Keller, the longest-serving member of the Judicial Council at two years, as chief justice 28-0. Six spending bills followed, among them Bill 22-19-S giving $1,700 in organizational aid to eight groups, Bill 24-19-S giving $500 to Blaq Art Nouveau for a Carpe Diem recruiting event, Bill 27-19-S giving $75 to the Queer Student Union for bracelet-making materials it had been unable to request in time because its advisor changed, and Bill 26-19-S reserving $108 to book indoor tables in case it rained on Earth Day.
events.money: six spending bills in one sitting

events.title: Fifty-three SGA scholarships awarded in one bill
events.body: Bill 29-19-S passed 25-0, funding the scholarships SGA awarded that year. Director of Academic and Student Affairs Aubrey Kelley presented them: 27 summer term scholarships totalling $8,100, 18 study abroad and student teach abroad scholarships of $300 each totalling $5,400, and eight first-generation student scholarships of $250 each totalling $2,000. The Herald headlined the bill as allocating $17,000.

events.title: Earth Day festival moved indoors and packed Downing Student Union
events.body: SGA organised WKU's annual Earth Day festival on the Thursday, moving it from Centennial Mall into Downing Student Union. Sustainability Committee member Jayden Thomas said the committee expected about 60 organisations to table, with live music in the DSU Auditorium. SGA's own table let attendees paint small flower pots, the Horticulture Club gave away potted plants, and the Bowling Green Fairness Campaign tabled alongside, with founding member and state Representative Patti Minter attending to support what she called intersectional justice.

events.title: Council found no election-code violation over a candidate list left at Bates-Runner Hall
events.body: On a complaint that a stack of printed sheets suggesting Senate candidates to vote for had been left at the Bates-Runner Hall front desk, the Judicial Council held 7-0 that there was no violation of election codes 3.4.1 or 3.4.3, which govern posters and signage, and no violation of 4.3.2, because each candidate had paid the full printing cost on their own expenditure sheet and a third party, not the candidates, had produced the endorsement.

executive.name: Stephen Mayer

executive.name: Harper Anderson

profile: Noah Moore was SGA's director of public relations in 2018-19. In April 2019 SGA and the Queer Student Union held the second Unite for Fairness night in Downing Student Union, where students wrote letters to Bowling Green city commissioners supporting a fairness ordinance. In the spring 2019 election McWilliams ran for student body president on a ticket with Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. They were defeated by the WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic, with results announced at SGA's election night, reported by the Herald on 17 April 2019.

profile: McAndrews was an associate justice on the Judicial Council in 2017-18 and took part in the council's January 2018 debate over whether the director of public relations had a constitutional duty to advertise a fall referendum. He argued it was "a little bit of a stretch" to read a referendum as one of the meetings, activities or programs a separate clause required the director to publicize, and separately that a clause on advertising filing dates read as written for senator and executive elections rather than referendums. In April 2018 the Senate elected him to succeed Annalicia Carlson as chief justice for 2018-19.

As chief justice he ran orientation sessions on the council for incoming senators in September 2018, swore in the year's new senators and asked that any legislation touching the constitution or bylaws be routed through him first. In March 2019 he presented that spring's election codes to the Senate, then announced his resignation as chief justice in order to run for an elected office; the Senate confirmed Isaac Keller as his successor the following month. Days later, by then a former chief justice, he co-authored with senators Mark Clark, Kara Lowry and Connor Hounshell a resolution supporting administrative transparency after the sudden resignation of a Potter College dean.

leaders.name: Will Harris
leaders.note: From Glasgow. Sworn in as student regent 2 August 2019. His term ran into the March 2020 campus shutdown. His term ran past its normal end. SGA voted on 20 April 2020 to postpone the spring election to the autumn because the campus had closed for COVID-19, and Harris stayed in office under that postponement: he was still president when the senate met for the first time since April on 15 September 2020, and gave the election update at the meeting of 22 September. Garrett Edmonds was elected on 29 September and took over in October. The extension is not a second term and Harris is counted once, for 2019-20.

profile: Harris won the student body presidency in April 2019 at the head of the WGK ticket with Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic, defeating Asha McWilliams. After the results were announced at SGA's election party, he said he looked forward to "making a positive impact for all students here at WKU" and to collaborating with the opposing ticket. He took office at SGA's annual banquet and presided over his first meeting the following Tuesday.

The defining controversy of his fall semester was Resolution 4-19-F, the senate's push to punish Alpha Xi Delta after a video showed members singing a racial slur. Harris abstained when his executive board vetoed the resolution 4-0, explaining that the discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct. When senators suggested his position as a knight of Alpha Xi Delta motivated him, he rejected the charge and said he wanted to reach an amicable outcome with the resolution's authors.

events.title: Harris-led WGK ticket wins SGA executive election
events.body: The WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, with Harris defeating Asha McWilliams for student body president. Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president and Mujkanovic defeated Symone Whalin for administrative vice president. Results were announced at SGA's election party, with the new officers set to take office at the annual banquet; the Herald's results story reported no turnout figures.

events.title: First meeting of the year confirms five executive appointments
events.body: At its first official meeting of the semester, the senate confirmed all five of President Will Harris's executive branch nominees: Aubrey Kelley as chief of staff, Ashlynn Evans as chief of public relations, Abbey Norvell as director of academic and student affairs, Paul Brosky as director of information technology and Josh Zaczek as Legislative Research Committee chair. Appointees outlined plans including wider use of counseling center fee vouchers and a revival of the need-based Earn-a-Computer program.

events.title: Senate blocked the budget over a special projects fund
events.body: At their second meeting the senate and executive branch failed to pass the year's budget, splitting over a $6,500 special projects fund the executive branch wanted for a sand volleyball court and hammock space at the First Year Village green space. Senators including Anthony Survance objected that the allocation cut into scholarship money, with Survance calling the motion "slimy", and the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships. The executive branch withdrew the budget, and rules required a full week before a revised version could be voted on.

events.title: Bill 1-20-S more than doubles menstrual product funding to $1,300
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Bill 1-20-S, funding the Go With the Flow programme that supplies menstrual products in campus restrooms, raising it from $588 the year before. Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr presented the bill at $1,176 before Senator Symone Whalin amended the figure to $1,300, drawn from the senate discretionary pool. The products were to go into Grise Hall, DSU, the Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms.

events.title: WKU extends spring break, moves classes online amid COVID-19
events.body: WKU announced it would extend spring break by one week and transition to "alternative delivery formats" for classes amid growing coronavirus concerns, with President Tim Caboni recommending that students who could safely return home do so. The announcement came after the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville suspended in-person classes. In-person instruction never resumed that semester, upending the rest of SGA's spring calendar.

events.title: Senate votes 17-15 to cancel a meeting for a sorority philanthropy event
events.body: A motion by Senator Hope Wells to cancel the Oct. 8 senate meeting for Kappa Delta's Shenanigans passed 17-15 after debate. Senator Anthony Survance argued that given recent controversies with Greek organizations SGA should not signal endorsement, while Senator Brigid Stakelum said the reason was practical, that quorum might not be met. Newly elected senators were sworn in at the same meeting by Chief Justice Isaac Keller.

events.title: Two SGA members organize protest against Alpha Xi Delta
events.body: Senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance organized a protest at the Shenanigans philanthropy event in response to a Twitter video showing WKU Alpha Xi Delta members singing a racial slur. Survance said the vote to cancel the senate meeting for the event helped prompt the protest, and the pair created a Facebook group titled "Demand Alpha Xi Delta's Removal." Whalin said administrative inaction signaled that minority students were not a priority.

events.title: Chief justice tells senate the AXiD resolution would be symbolic; student urges labor committee
events.body: Chief Justice Isaac Keller told senators the resolution would be purely symbolic because SGA cannot direct WKU to defund an organization on grounds of discrimination, and suggested supporters take the matter to the Title IX office or the Kentucky Human Rights Commission. Harris said no student had filed a formal discrimination charge. Former senator Jay Wells addressed the meeting urging SGA to form a labor committee, citing cut student worker hours and the CAPE committee's recommendation to suspend 101 academic programs.

events.title: SGA reports record 398 scholarship applications
events.body: Director of Academic and Student Affairs Abbey Norvell reported 398 scholarship applications, including 132 for winter term, 122 for the first generation scholarship, 81 for study abroad, 31 for scholar development, 10 for ISEC and 22 for the revived Earn-a-Computer program. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds reported First Year Village construction was on schedule and said a remaining building near the old library site would be torn down if incoming student numbers did not require the beds.

events.title: Senators quietly leave their seats, two committee chairs vacant
events.body: The Herald reported that senators and committee chairs had vacated positions since the fall semester, most leaving to study abroad or over schedule conflicts, weakening the senate's numbers. The SAVES and Sustainability committee chairs were both vacant with no replacements identified, and President Will Harris posted an open SGA application on social media to recruit. The meeting also covered planning for the March Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort.

events.title: Contentious senator confirmations turn on legislation records and party affiliation
events.body: Five senators and two committee chairs were confirmed, with Parker Raybourne and Kat Howard drawing scrutiny for having written no legislation and for not having read the 2019-2020 budget. Senator Anthony Survance questioned Raybourne's membership in WKU College Republicans and was cut off by Speaker Nathan Terrell, who said SGA was nonpartisan. Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr defended the nominees, saying committees exist to develop ideas together.

events.title: Greeks Go Green sustainability contest funded at $75
events.body: Bill 1-19-F allocated $75 from senate discretionary funding for prizes in Greeks Go Green, a competition between WKU's Greek organisations to run the most sustainable chapter house by logging environmentally friendly actions for points. The contest ran from 20 September 2019 through April, with winners announced at the Greek Week convocation. The bill passed its second reading on 10 September 2019.

src.label: SGA Bill 1-19-F, Funding for Greeks Go Green

events.title: Etiquette dinner for the Glasgow campus
events.body: Bill 2-20-S passed unanimously on 18 February 2020, funding a professional etiquette dinner for students at WKU's Glasgow regional campus and subsidising the ticket price, with Glasgow covering the rest. Executive vice president Garrett Edmonds, who brought the bill, said it was aimed at students from small towns who had never faced a table set with several forks and knives, and that to his knowledge it was the only etiquette dinner held at a WKU regional campus.

src.label: Herald, 19 Feb 2020 - "SGA motion to host professional etiquette dinner passes unanimously"

events.title: Senate passed Resolution 4-19-F seeking discipline against Alpha Xi Delta, 24-7
events.body: The senate voted 24-7 for Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing chapter members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students, wanting more than "an article from the Herald or an email from Bob Skipper." Before passage a motion struck the call for removal from campus out of the title and a friendly amendment substituted suspension from Greek affairs. Senator Mary Mayo said it was not SGA's job to act as a disciplinary committee, and the resolution was to be submitted to the Faculty Senate.

events.title: Executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F 4-0 and the senate sustained the veto
events.body: The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F, the Alpha Xi Delta resolution, by 4 votes to 0 with two of its six members abstaining, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the discrimination claim the resolution invoked would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and that the Office of Student Conduct had noted no violation. Co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out, and Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek disputed the reasoning. Senators raised Harris's standing as an Alpha Xi Delta knight, which he rejected as grounds for bias.

events.title: Budget passed with spending stipulations and campaign spending caps halved
events.body: All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a three-part compromise confined the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributed any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. Its passage let Bill 1-19-F, Greeks Go Green, and Bill 2-19-F, funding for Bowling Green Pride, pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds objected, calling SGA turnout awful and estimating 1,500 students voted the previous year, while Senator Symone Whalin said poorer students were less likely to run for executive office.

events.title: Senate approved a $5,000 hammock project after the volleyball court was dropped
events.body: The senate passed Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was judged too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris had run so SGA would be known for more than scantrons and greenbooks. Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek criticized having to vote without seeing budget numbers, said he had met friction getting figures from Edmonds and wanted assurance the money would be spent inclusively. Residence Hall Association President Emily Whitney backed the project and noted RHA's own budget cuts, and the senate kept the power to halt spending during planning.

events.title: Elections postponed, and a clause written to keep the officers in place
events.body: With the campus closed by COVID-19, SGA postponed its spring elections until at least September so that voting could happen in person, and passed an emergency clause amending the constitution to let cabinet terms run on until the following election under judicial oversight. Executive vice president Garrett Edmonds explained the amendment. President Will Harris said that once scholarships were awarded the remainder of SGA's budget would go to the WKU Opportunity Fund and the Emergency Relief Fund, and the organisation gave what was left in its food bank to the Office of Sustainability to redistribute. The cabinet kept meeting over Zoom every Tuesday. The clause is why the year that followed had no handover in the spring: Harris stayed in office through the summer and was still president when the senate met for the first time since April on 15 September, and Edmonds was not elected to succeed him until 29 September.

src.label: Herald, 20 Apr 2020 - SGA spring elections postponed until fall

events.title: SGA sponsored the third Bowling Green Pride Festival
events.body: Bill 2-19-F allocated $500 from senate discretionary funding to sponsor the Bowling Green Pride Festival held on 5 October 2019 at Circus Square Park by the Bowling Green Fairness group. The money bought a Silver Sponsorship, putting SGA's name and logo on the festival t-shirt and website and securing tabling space for the Committee for Diversity and Inclusion. The bill's authors, senators Conner Hounshell and Mark Clark, wrote that funding was necessary because LGBTQ+ students were not legally protected in Bowling Green for want of a Fairness ordinance, and noted this was the third such festival and that SGA had sponsored every one before it. The posted form records a first reading on 3 September 2019, a second reading on 10 September and a passing vote.

src.label: SGA Bill 2-19-F, Funding for the Bowling Green Pride Festival

events.title: Judicial Council filled out with four nominations
events.body: The senate confirmed four nominees to the SGA Judicial Council at the 24 September 2019 meeting, filling the body out ahead of that week's senate elections. President Will Harris had interviewed freshman Jason Herlick, junior Derek Collins, sophomore Turner Reynolds and freshman Holden Schroeder before the meeting, and all four brought experience from other student government organisations. Herlick was confirmed unanimously after Senator Anthony Survance asked whether he had read SGA's constitution and rules. Collins, who headed WKU's Students Demand Action chapter, spoke about the council's duty to hold the association to account.

src.label: Herald, 25 Sep 2019 - "SGA judicial council 'fully functional' following four nominations"

events.title: Diversity scholarship bill postponed over a Title IX conflict
events.body: Discussion of Bill 4-19-F, which would have created a diversity scholarship, was postponed at the 15 October 2019 meeting because the bill conflicted with Title IX, and no date was set for taking it up again while the Legislative Research Committee worked through it. At the same meeting Senator Symone Whalin announced a campus survey on the use of racial slurs and tried to show a clip from a slur-awareness video, which failed on technical grounds and was held over. Harris told senators he and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds had met administrators about the special projects fund and come away with costings.

events.title: Study Away scholarships renewed for a ninth year
events.body: Bill 5-19-F allocated $1,500 from the scholarship budget to WKU's Office of Study Away for the 2019-20 year, continuing a funding partnership the bill records as having run since 2011. Study Away sends WKU students to placements elsewhere in the United States rather than abroad, and the office had approached SGA to keep the arrangement going. The bill was authored by Administrative Vice President Kenan Mujkanovic, sponsored by Josh Zaczek of the Legislative Research Committee, and passed on 5 November 2019.

src.label: SGA Bill 5-19-F, Continuing a Partnership for Study Away Scholarships

events.title: Free buses to the Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort
events.body: SGA offered students free transport to the Rally for Higher Education at the state Capitol on 3 March 2020, with WKU attendees leaving Diddle Arena at 6 a.m. About 400 students from Kentucky's public, private and technical institutions were expected to fill the Capitol rotunda between 10 a.m. and noon. The rally is organised through the Board of Student Body Presidents, and President Will Harris said WKU's agenda was pension reform, increases under the performance-based budget model and asset preservation funding. This is the Herald's account of what was arranged; no follow-up report on the day itself appears in the archive.

events.title: Five hundred dollars voted to the 19th Healthy Days Fair
events.body: Bill 5-20-S proposed allocating $500 from senate discretionary funding to WellU towards the Healthy Days Fair set for Wednesday 25 March 2020, the nineteenth annual student health fair, in return for SGA's logo on the event's t-shirts, video boards, social media and email. The bill records that the fair had drawn over 487 participants and 34 health-related vendors, several of them promoting mental health resources, and that SGA had partnered with WellU to fund it in earlier years. The posted form gives a first reading on 25 February 2020 and a second reading on 3 March 2020 and carries no vote line, so the archive cannot say it passed, and holds no source saying whether the fair went ahead.

events.title: A scholarship aimed at counties with the fewest graduates
events.body: Bill 7-20-S proposed allocating $1,000 from senate discretionary funding to create a scholarship for students with financial need from Kentucky counties with low college graduation rates or a low share of residents holding bachelor's degrees. The bill argued those educational disparities track with lower incomes and higher unemployment and poverty, and directed the Director and Committee of Academic and Student Affairs to build an application identifying qualifying counties from data sources such as the Kentucky Council on Postsecondary Education. The award was to be made in the spring 2020 semester. The posted bill records a first reading on 3 March 2020 and no second reading, so the archive cannot say it passed.

events.title: A thousand dollars to the food pantry after the campus closed
events.body: Bill 9-20-S proposed donating $1,000 to the WKU Food Recovery Network for the Office of Sustainability food pantry, drawn as organisational aid with the organisational aid budget expanded by $1,000 from legislative discretionary funds. The bill records that the pantry's usual influx of donated food had dried up under COVID-19 while it had served over 150 students, faculty, staff, alumni and community members in the five weeks since the university closed, and lists what the money would buy: spaghetti sauce, juice, canned meat, macaroni and cheese, soup, condiments, rice bowls and other easily prepared meals. It was read first on 28 April 2020 and a second time on 5 May 2020; the posted form carries no vote line.

events.title: Council defined a Senate majority as a majority of those present
events.body: At its first meeting of the year the council had to decide whether a majority in the Senate chamber was measured against those present or against the full membership. Chief Justice Isaac Keller argued that a senator who is not present abstains and loses the right to vote. No justice objected, and the council ruled unanimously that a simple majority is based on senators present.

events.title: Council ruled the Alpha Xi Delta resolution's clause constitutional 7-0
events.body: Asked by Chief of Staff Conner Hounshell to rule on the discrimination clause in Resolution 4-19-F, the council heard President Will Harris argue that defining discrimination was a Title IX matter rather than SGA's. All seven justices found the whereas clause constitutional, noting vagueness in section 1.1 and that SGA already awarded scholarships on protected characteristics. The ruling was made pending university information, and the council said a university finding of illegality would change it.

events.title: Council convened a cross-branch rewrite of the constitution
events.body: Chief Justice Isaac Keller told the council that the executive and legislative branches wanted the constitution revamped to eliminate grey areas, and that three people from each branch would convene to work through changes. He said he would try to include the rest of the Judicial Council in the process.

events.title: Bill 8-20-S puts emergency clauses to the Senate
events.body: With campus closed by COVID-19, Bill 8-20-S had its first reading on 14 April 2020. Authored by Dawson McCoun and MJ Mayo, it provided that on a two-thirds Senate vote together with a majority of the Executive Cabinet and a majority of the Judicial Council, officers and senators could extend their terms until a new election was held, the president could extend the student regent position under KRS 164.321, and the rescheduled election would be held within three weeks of the start of the fall 2020 semester. The clause as later printed in the constitution allows four weeks and adds virtual Senate meetings.

executive.name: Garrett Edmonds
executive.note: Signed as J. Garrett Edmonds on legislation. He worked over the summer of 2019 with the Student Life Foundation on the WKU Commons and the green space by the new First Year Village, defended the executive special projects fund through the September budget fight, and co-authored Bill 3-20-S committing $5,000 to hammock areas across campus.

executive.name: Kenan Mujkanovic
executive.note: Prepared and presented the 2019-20 budget, dropping the athletic marketing sponsorship and reallocating the money; after the Senate amended it he and the executive team pulled the bill from the agenda. He authored the year's organizational aid bills and the study away scholarship bill.
profile: Kenan Mujkanovic ran for student body president twice before winning executive office. In April 2017 the Judicial Council granted him a constitutional exemption to run despite less than a semester's service, and he finished second behind Andi Dahmer with 305 of the 1,579 votes cast, ahead of Lily Nellans's 212. In April 2018 his campaign was suspended for an election-code violation and he finished third, taking 32 percent of the vote in the three-way race Stephen Mayer won.

In April 2019 he ran a third time, now for administrative vice president on the WGK ticket with Will Harris and Garrett Edmonds, and won, defeating Symone Whalin. As administrative vice president in 2019-20 he prepared and presented the year's budget, dropping the athletic-marketing sponsorship and reallocating the money, then joined the executive team in pulling the bill after the Senate amended it. He authored the year's organizational-aid bills and Bill 5-19-F, which continued a study-away scholarship partnership running since 2011 with $1,500 for 2019-20.

executive.name: Aubrey Kelley
executive.note: Confirmed 16-1 on 3 September 2019 after serving as Director of Academic and Student Affairs the year before, when scholarship applications reached a high of nearly 300. She sat on the university academic committee reviewing course fees and told the Senate that fees predating 2010 had to be resubmitted. The 2018-19 minutes spell her surname both ways, Kelly at her nomination and Kelley later; the SGA website and the 2019-20 minutes give Kelley.
profile: Aubrey Kelley served two years in the SGA executive branch, as director of academic and student affairs in 2018-19 and as chief of staff in 2019-20. She reached the first post in September 2018 only on the third attempt: the Senate confirmed her 24-3-4 after the initial nominee withdrew and a second nominee failed confirmation 6-9-1. As director she presented Bill 29-19-S in April 2019, which funded 53 SGA scholarships in a single bill — 27 summer-term awards, 18 study-abroad awards and eight first-generation awards.

Confirmed chief of staff 16-1 at the first meeting of 2019-20, she sat on the university academic committee reviewing course fees and told the Senate that fees predating 2010 had to be resubmitted. The 2018-19 minutes spell her surname both ways — Kelly at her nomination and Kelley afterward — and the SGA website and the 2019-20 minutes give Kelley.

profile: Mathews was confirmed to the Senate as parliamentarian on a 12-0-3 vote on 10 September 2019. profile: Zaczek was confirmed as chair of SGA's Legislative Research Committee in the first meeting of the 2019-20 year, on 3 September 2019, and for the term's first month was the Senate's only confirmed committee chair, which led him to insist that his own sponsorship of a bill and his committee's approval of it be treated as separate steps and that all legislation clear his committee before a first reading.

He was a persistent skeptic of executive spending plans that fall. During a September 2019 budget standoff over whether to fund scholarships or a special-projects fund for sand volleyball and hammock space in the new First Year Village, Zaczek argued the recreational spending did little more for student engagement than students already got from picnicking or playing frisbee, and the following week warned that halving campaign spending caps could shut low-income students out of running for office. When the hammock bill returned in March 2020, he pressed the executive board for a full accounting of how the money would be spent before he would vote for it, saying he wanted to know the funds were being used "in an all-inclusive way."

On legislation, Zaczek proposed an amendment during February 2019 debate on a study-abroad-scholarship bill, and after it was pulled and rewritten by its authors he remained critical of the revised version, saying it was "detracting from a merit-based scholarship" and questioning how SGA could verify applicants' answers. In October 2019 the Senate struck "removal from campus" from the title of a resolution seeking penalties against a sorority chapter over members' use of a racial slur in a video; Zaczek's friendly amendment put "suspension from Greek affairs" in its place, and the resolution passed 24-7.

profile: As a senator in 2018-19, Whalin ran for administrative vice president on a ticket with presidential candidate Asha McWilliams and Jacob McAndrews in the spring 2019 election; the ticket lost, with Kenan Mujkanovic defeating her for the AVP seat. In autumn 2019, by then Diversity and Inclusion committee chair, she and Senator Anthony Survance authored Resolution 4-19-F seeking Alpha Xi Delta's suspension from Greek affairs after chapter members sang a racial slur in a song posted online, and organized an October 2019 protest at Kappa Delta's Shenanigans philanthropy event to press the point after SGA voted to cancel that week's Senate meeting for the same event.
