leaders.name: J. Garrett Edmonds
leaders.note: The COVID year. Almost certainly the most unusual term in the organisation's history and worth a dedicated oral history. Took office in October 2020 rather than at the usual spring handover: SGA had voted on 20 April 2020 to postpone its election to the autumn because of the COVID-19 shutdown, so his predecessor stayed in the chair until the delayed vote was decided on 29 September.
profile: Edmonds, a senior from Island, Kentucky, spent his freshman year as chair of the Campus Improvements Committee, working with Vice President of Student Affairs Brian Kuster on projects including a campus safety walk, before winning election as executive vice president in April 2018 on a ticket with Harper Anderson and Stephen Mayer. He served two years as executive vice president under President Will Harris, pushing for a budget model geared toward campus amenities and recreational life and working to diversify Senate appointments with seats for underrepresented students.

He ran for the presidency in fall 2020 on the Edmonds-Norvell ticket, after his original running mate for administrative vice president, Nathan Terrell, dropped out and was replaced by Abbey Norvell. The campaign centered on a pledge to create a Director of Outreach position to close the communication gap between campus organizations and SGA, and the Sept. 24 Herald town hall covered WKU's COVID-19 response and the summer's Black Lives Matter protests on campus. Voting ran Sept. 28-29 on TopNet; Edmonds defeated senator MJ Mayo, becoming SGA president and, since the two offices had merged by then, student regent on the WKU Board of Regents. Norvell was elected administrative vice president alongside him, with the Herald reporting no decision yet made on a separate executive vice president post.

Taking office amid the pandemic, the senate confirmed Isaac Keller to a vice-president post 29-1 in October after Edmonds said he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him; the Herald's report on that vote first called the office executive vice president, then ran a correction changing it to administrative vice president -- the same title the Herald had given Norvell in September, a conflict the record does not resolve. Matt Barr, Ashlynn Evans, Kody Okert and Paul Brosky rounded out the executive and Shelby Robertson served as non-voting speaker of the senate. Early cabinet business set up officer office hours, an ad hoc outreach committee chaired by Me'Lon Craighead and a push toward inclusive pronoun language in Senate proceedings. That fall SGA petitioned WKU to restore Pass/D/Fail grading for COVID-disrupted students; Associate Provost Rob Hale initially rebuffed the request, calling the university's extended drop deadline sufficient, but by December the petition -- more than 3,500 signatures in three days -- had succeeded, and Edmonds thanked senators for the work behind it at the semester's final meeting alongside bills funding campus safe-driving signage and several student organizations.

In the spring his senate passed the organization's largest-ever organizational aid bill and a resolution seeking a codified vetting process for campus dining vendors after a controversial social media post by a local pizzeria owner, alongside legislation backing WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force in renaming buildings tied to racism, a community garden, and a diversity-event push by DEI chair Fatin Yaro. Near the end of his term he declined to fill the chief justice seat vacated by Erika Puhakka, saying the choice belonged to his successor: "I think that's the only thing that is right in this scenario." He also worried publicly that only 13 students were running for senate in the April election, and closed his term addressing the Class of 2021 at the delayed Fall 2020/Spring 2021 commencement, telling graduates their perseverance through "this past year" had brought them to their day of celebration.

events.title: Town hall debate pitted the sitting EVP against a senator
events.body: SGA held a town hall debate in the DSU auditorium between presidential candidates Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, and senator MJ Mayo. Edmonds's original running mate for administrative vice president, Nathan Terrell, had dropped off the Edmonds-Norvell ticket and was replaced by Abbey Norvell; the debate covered WKU's COVID-19 response and the summer's Black Lives Matter protests on campus.

events.title: Edmonds elected president over Mayo
events.body: Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, was elected student body president over senator MJ Mayo in balloting held on TopNet Sept. 28-29, succeeding Will Harris. Edmonds had campaigned on creating a Director of Outreach position to link campus organizations more directly with SGA.

events.title: Senate passed the annual budget 28-5 and elected Shelby Robertson speaker
events.body: At the first official senate meeting under the new leadership, Shelby Robertson defeated Brenna Matthews to become speaker of the senate and the budget passed 28-5. Edmonds emphasized a $6,000 Projects Fund, including $1,000 for Housing and Residence Life PPE and an expansion of the Go with the Flow menstrual products program into Pearce Ford Tower. Senator MJ Mayo challenged the balance of stipends; Edmonds said all senate stipends except the top three offices had been cut to feed the Projects Fund.

events.title: Cabinet set office hours, an outreach committee, and pushed inclusive language
events.body: At the executive cabinet's first recorded meeting, Edmonds set up officer office hours and an ad hoc outreach committee for RSO leadership. Speaker Shelby Robertson pushed to connect senators with similar legislative interests, adopt inclusive pronoun language in the chamber, and find a parliamentarian.

events.title: Isaac Keller confirmed administrative vice president 29-1; ad hoc committee created
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds nominated Isaac Keller as administrative vice president, saying he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him when they disagreed, and the senate confirmed Keller 29-1. Roderick Maul and Tess Welch were elected committee chairs, and senators voted to form a new ad hoc committee, electing Me'Lon Craighead as its chair.

events.title: Presidential task force sought input on slaveholding college namesakes
events.body: WKU's Presidential Task Force on Naming and Symbols, formed by President Timothy Caboni in fall 2020, collected input from students and the community on the namesakes of Potter College and Ogden College, both built on wealth from slave labor. Two Potter descendants said it was time to find a new name. The task force planned to audit names and send recommendations to the administration.

events.title: Chief justice resigned and the 'Vet Our Vendors' bill passed over the president's objection
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds announced that Chief Justice Erika Puhakka had stepped down and said he would not nominate a replacement so close to the elections, leaving the choice to the next president, and reported that only 13 people were running for senate. A bill by Kyle Phillips asking WKU to create a committee to vet campus dining vendors, prompted by a social media post by the owner of Lost River Pizza, passed 16-0 with two abstentions after Edmonds urged delay and a friendly amendment softened the wording. A separate organizational aid bill by Isaac Keller, funding five student groups, was described as the largest SGA had passed.

events.title: WKU relented and allowed pass grades after SGA's P/D/F campaign
events.body: Provost Cheryl Stevens told faculty that students who faced COVID-related problems could opt for a pass grade instead of a B or C, reversing the university's earlier refusal. The Faculty Senate had voted 40-9 in favor and SGA voted unanimously for the option, presenting nearly 20 pages of student testimony; SGA's petition had drawn over 3,500 signatures in three days. Students had to email their professor by Jan. 13, with the final decision left to the faculty member.

events.title: Edmonds addressed the Class of 2021 at the delayed commencement
events.body: As SGA president, Edmonds spoke at WKU's Fall 2020/Spring 2021 commencement ceremony, telling graduates that the class's perseverance through the pandemic year had brought them to their day of celebration.

events.title: Norvell elected administrative vice president; EVP still open
events.body: SGA held a virtual election party over Zoom to announce results. The Edmonds-Norvell ticket defeated MJ Mayo for the presidency, and Abbey Norvell was elected administrative vice president alongside Edmonds. The Herald reported no official decision had yet been made on a separate executive vice president post, with an announcement expected at the next SGA meeting.

events.title: Judicial nominations confirmed; senate revives a Pass/D/Fail request
events.body: The senate unanimously confirmed Edmonds's nominations of Derek Collins and Lexi Mayne as associate justices and Addison McCoun as senator at large. Senators passed a Tess Welch and Eric Barry bill to increase campus accessibility and agreed to split funding for SGA-branded masks and hand sanitizer evenly between the senate and SGA's PR team. A closing bill by Tate McClard and Jacob Congleton asked WKU to restore the Pass/D/Fail grading option it had offered in spring 2020 but declined to bring back that fall; Edmonds and Addison McCoun wanted every senator listed as a co-author.

events.title: Edmonds launched a P/D/F petition
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds released a student petition asking WKU to offer a Pass/D/Fail grading option for the fall semester, citing inconsistent course modalities and the strain of quarantine on students without an online-learning fallback. The petition reached half its 1,000-signature goal within an hour and the target was raised to 5,000.

events.title: Fall semester closed with a Pass/D/Fail win and a safe-driving pledge
events.body: At the last meeting of the fall semester Edmonds told senators that students could now request a pass if they received a B or C as a final grade, and credited senators and petition signers for the work that led to the new option. The senate unanimously passed a bill by Matthew Thomas committing SGA's social media to a Drive Safe Hilltoppers safety campaign, and unanimously funded a second bill supporting HonorsToppers, College Republicans, Zeta Phi Beta and the Sociology and Criminology Club.

events.title: Spring semester opened over Zoom with a late-fee pledge
events.body: At its first meeting of the spring semester, held on Zoom, SGA heard Edmonds say the provost search was in its final stage with interviews starting within weeks, and that he planned to look at changing or removing the late fees charged when a student's financial aid arrives late. Senators unanimously nominated Jamison Moorehead as director of IT and funded Dance Big Red and a Delta Sigma Pi virtual leadership conference.

events.title: Committee chairs set the spring priorities
events.body: A Herald preview of SGA's spring 2021 programmes reported Chief of Staff Matt Barr continuing Go with the Flow, which put vending machines dispensing free menstrual products in campus buildings. Diversity and Inclusion Chair Fatin Yaro announced a Feb. 24 diversity event and legislation to set consequences for discrimination within student organisations. Legislative Research Chair Dawson McCoun said the shift to remote meetings after March 2020 had made it harder to connect with students and pass legislation, but that the year had at least given members motivation to address students' problems; SGA planned a return to masked, socially distanced in-person meetings that semester.

events.title: New senator seated; $2,500 to the ISEC masquerade ball
events.body: SGA nominated pre-law sophomore Will Dykeman as a new senator. A bill by Me'Lon Craighead allocating $2,500 to ISEC's Black Magic Masquerade Ball passed with overwhelming consent, and a bill by Administrative Vice President Isaac Keller funding Amazing Tones of Joy, Black Women of Western, Queer Student Union and the Business Association for Development passed unanimously. Edmonds announced a virtual rally of student body presidents for March 26 that Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear would attend, and said he was working to add state Rep. Charles Booker.

events.title: Outreach signage and safe-driving bills pass
events.body: Guest speaker Ethan Logan, vice president of enrollment and student experience, briefed senators on how his office could help SGA. Edmonds pointed senators toward an upcoming provost-search update and urged them to consider running in the April officer elections. Senators unanimously passed a Me'Lon Craighead bill funding 50 laminated, QR-coded outreach signs for campus and a Matthew Thomas bill adding 12 safe-driving signs to campus parking lots; a bill on WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force was held for the following week.

events.title: Constitution amended; Caboni's contract extended
events.body: Edmonds told senators the WKU Board of Regents had extended President Timothy Caboni's contract four years. The senate elected Addison McCoun to head the Legislative Research Committee after Dawson McCoun's resignation, passed a Tess Welch/Erika Puhakka bill amending constitutional wording 19-4, and funded a Sustainability Committee spring photo contest on a bill by Matthew Waninger and Elizabeth DeLozier, whose money went on gift cards for the winning students. The Herald prints that senator's surname as Waninger; the archive records the president elected the following April as Matthew Wininger, and the difference is flagged rather than fixed.

events.title: SGA meets for the first time since April, plans to redirect study abroad money
events.body: SGA held its first meeting since April over Zoom, moving transition guides and election codes to a fully digital format. President Will Harris said the study abroad scholarship money would have flexibility to be reallocated because COVID-19 restrictions blocked travel. Senator Me'Lon Craighead outlined planned diversity legislation including consequences for racial offenses on campus and a mandatory course for students and workers.

events.title: Senate speaker resigns and quits the executive vice president race over slur video
events.body: Nathan Terrell, speaker of the SGA senate and a candidate for executive vice president, resigned after a video showing him using a racial slur was sent anonymously to the Herald. He initially denied being in the video, then confirmed it and issued a statement removing himself from the Garrett-Nathan-Abbey ticket. Terrell asserted the anonymous submitter had a political agenda against him and the ticket.

events.title: Town hall candidates split over conditions in the quarantine dorm
events.body: At the Herald town hall, presidential candidate MJ Mayo said the university had spread misinformation about the quarantine dorm at Barnes Campbell and relayed student testimony about uncleaned rooms, unclean bathrooms and expired vending machine goods. Garrett Edmonds said the university response had been more than adequate and that he was confident after meeting with the Board of Regents that the issues were resolved. Edmonds had told an SGA meeting that 234 quarantined students received 1,273 meals.

events.title: Cabinet slate confirmed; $1,000 of projects fund routed to quarantined students
events.body: Twelve nominations were confirmed, including Will Harris to the Judicial Council, Matt Barr as chief of staff, Fatin Yaro as Diversity and Inclusion chair and Dawson McCoun as head of the Legislative Research Committee. RHA representatives Emily Whitney and Me'Lon Craighead described using the $1,000 SGA projects fund allocation for goody bags, food, hygiene products and PPE for students quarantined in Barnes Campbell. Craighead said the goal was to make quarantined students feel connected to campus.

events.title: First bill of the year spends $2,334.45 on SGA signage in DSU
events.body: The senate passed the year's first bill 28-2, allocating $2,334.45 for rebranding, printing and installing new SGA signage in the Downing Student Union. Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell appointed Shelby Robertson, MJ Mayo and Kody Okert to the Faculty Senate. Edmonds told senators he had recently been in quarantine and reported the provost search was going well.

events.title: SGA backs Bottom of the Hill survey as scholarship applications lag
events.body: A bill by Matthew Waninger and Matthew Thomas committing SGA support to the Bottom of the Hill Revitalization Initiative passed unanimously, triggering a campus-wide survey on what should be done with the green space near the First Year Village. Director of Academic and Student Affairs Kody Okert said fewer than 20 applications had been received for the five SGA scholarships then open. A bill funding a book scholarship for international students was held over to the following week.

events.title: Five hundred dollars to Dance Big Red over Zoom
events.body: At SGA's first meeting of the spring 2021 semester, held on Zoom on 19 January, the senate passed a bill allocating $500 to Dance Big Red. Delta Sigma Pi also received funding for a virtual leadership conference at the same meeting. SGA planned to return to in-person meetings the following week.

src.label: Herald, 20 Jan 2021 - "SGA discusses Dance Big Red, Provost search, late fees in first meeting of semester"

events.title: QR-code signs and safe-driving signs went up round campus
events.body: On 9 February 2021 the senate unanimously passed a bill by senator Me'Lon Craighead funding 50 laminated signs with QR codes letting students send concerns or ideas straight to SGA. A second bill by senator Matthew Thomas added 12 signs on parking-lot poles reminding students to drive safely. Vice President for Enrollment and Student Experience Ethan Logan was the meeting's guest speaker.

src.label: Herald, 11 Feb 2021 - "SGA focuses on outreach, safe driving initiative in weekly meeting"

events.title: The five scholarships SGA was offering
events.body: A Herald guide of 11 February 2021 set out SGA's five student scholarships: Earn-a-Computer, which gave a free computer in return for logged service; the First-Generation Program for full-time students whose parents held no bachelor's degree; the ISEC Book Scholarship of $100 toward textbooks; the Scholar Development Scholarship of up to $500 for conferences, equipment, research or test preparation; and the Summer Term Scholarship for summer classes.
events.money: $100 book awards and Scholar Development grants of up to $500

src.label: Herald, 11 Feb 2021 - "5 SGA scholarships students can take advantage of this semester"

events.title: Senate backed renaming buildings tied to racism and funded a community garden
events.body: The senate passed legislation by Brenna Matthews and Tess Welch, after debate, offering SGA's support to WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force in changing the names of buildings with ties to racism or injustice. Matthews said ties to slave owning and the Confederate army were not something a public university dedicated to diversity would want on campus. Senators also unanimously funded a community garden outside the Office of Sustainability and allocated $3,500 to four student organizations. Title IX coordinator Deborah Wilkins opened the meeting by reviewing previous SGA legislation that potentially violated Title IX.

events.title: Provost's office rejected SGA's Pass/D/Fail request; computers bill passed 28-3
events.body: President Garrett Edmonds told senators that Associate Provost Rob Hale had defended the university's decision to extend the class drop deadline rather than restore Pass/D/Fail grading, and said he was "deeply disturbed" by the response. Edmonds urged senators to email the Faculty Senate and the provost and to keep circulating his petition, which had passed 3,000 signatures. Senator Brenna Mathews argued the policy left students choosing between attending in person and paying for an extra semester. The senate separately voted 28-3 to fund recycled computers for the SGA office, a number scaled back to meet CDC guidance.

events.title: Hammock stands finally going up, six months late
events.body: At SGA's second meeting of the semester, held over Zoom, presidential candidate Garrett Edmonds told senators the hammock project postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic would be built the following Monday in three locations: the Valley, Centennial Mall and South Lawn. President Will Harris also said this year had seen the highest turnout for senate seats, more than he had seen in four years in SGA, and the meeting announced the town hall for 24 September at 7.30 p.m. in the DSU Auditorium, with elections on TopNet on 28 and 29 September. This is what was announced at the meeting; the archive holds no later report confirming the build date.

src.label: Herald, 22 Sep 2020 - "Hammock project, elections discussed at second SGA meeting of the year"

events.title: Federal judge dismissed the former president's suit against WKU
events.body: U.S. District Court Judge David Hale dismissed the federal claims in the lawsuit brought by a former SGA president against WKU on 2 March 2021 and remanded the remainder to state court. The suit, filed in 2018, individually named President Timothy Caboni, General Counsel Andrea Anderson and Director of Student Activities Charley Pride, and alleged the university's response to on-campus harassment she reported violated Title IX and 42 U.S. Code. The court found WKU was not aware of the harassment until February 2018, when her residence hall director reported it to the Title IX office, and granted the three named officials qualified immunity after finding no constitutional violation was proved. The university had called the accusations maliciously untrue when the suit was filed; her attorney declined to comment on the dismissal.

src.label: Herald, 11 Mar 2021 - "Judge dismisses former SGA president's lawsuit against WKU"

events.title: Bill 12-21-S moved most Senate seats into the spring election
events.body: Bill 12-21-S, authored by Tess Welch, Dawson McCoun and Garrett Edmonds, had its first reading on 2 March 2021. It removed the academic-college senators, the international senator and three at-large seats from the fall ballot, leaving only three freshman, one graduate and one Gatton Academy seat to the autumn, and corrected a clause that still described two graduate senators. The bill argued that thirteen seats, nearly a third of the Senate, had been arriving too late to vote on the annual budget.

events.title: Council refused a candidate an exemption to run for president
events.body: Joey Dilliha asked the council for an exemption under section 2.2.5 of the constitution to run for president without having held an elected or appointed SGA position. He said he had attended about three meetings as a freshman and had been occupied with internships and a business. Justices Erika Puhakka, Holden Schroeder, Jason Herlick, Turner Reynolds and Isaac Keller each concluded he was not familiar enough with the office; the decision was unanimous, 5-0, that he could not run for president.

documents.title: SGA Executive Cabinet minutes, 13 October 2020
documents.summary: Minutes from the first recorded fall 2020 executive cabinet meeting under President Garrett Edmonds, covering officer office hours, an ad hoc outreach committee, and Speaker Shelby Robertson's push for inclusive language and a parliamentarian.
documents.extract: Ad hoc committee for outreach; inclusive language in senate; looking for a parliamentarian.

executive.name: J. Garrett Edmonds
executive.note: Also student regent on the WKU Board of Regents.

executive.name: Abbey Norvell
executive.note: Elected on the Edmonds ticket 29 September 2020. The senate minutes head her reports "Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell" from October 2020 through March 2021, settling a title conflict in the archive: Norvell was executive vice president and Isaac Keller administrative vice president. The Herald's election story had used the administrative vice president title later given, after a correction, to Keller, and as of its 30 September 2020 report no decision had been made on a separate executive vice president post. She sent out the Faculty Senate application form, kept track of which senators sat on which university committees, and urged students to bring concerns to the University Budget Committee.
profile: Abbey Norvell served on the SGA executive branch for two years. Confirmed director of academic and student affairs in September 2019 — a former at-large senator who had sat on the Organizational Aid and Public Relations committees — she built the scholarship grading rubric and in November 2019 reported a record 398 scholarship applications.

In 2020-21 she was elected on the Edmonds-Norvell ticket, which defeated MJ Mayo at a virtual election party in September 2020 after her running-mate slot opened when Nathan Terrell left the ticket. The Herald's election story called her administrative vice president and no decision had then been made on a separate executive vice president post; from October 2020 through March 2021 the Senate minutes headed her reports "Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell", with Isaac Keller confirmed administrative vice president that October. She sent out the Faculty Senate application form, tracked which senators sat on university committees, and appointed members to the Faculty Senate.

src2.label: Herald, 30 Sep 2020

executive.name: Isaac Keller
executive.note: Confirmed by the senate 29-1 on 20 Oct 2020. The Herald's report on this vote originally called the post executive vice president and ran a correction changing it to administrative vice president -- the same title the Herald's 30 Sep 2020 election story gives to Abbey Norvell, elected AVP alongside Edmonds. Sourcing does not resolve which title is correct.
profile: Isaac Keller came to the administrative vice presidency from the Judicial Council, where he had served two years and, as its longest-serving member, was confirmed chief justice 28-0 in April 2019. As chief justice in 2019-20 he ruled that a Senate majority is measured against those present rather than the full membership, told senators a resolution seeking to defund Alpha Xi Delta would be only symbolic because SGA cannot direct the university to defund an organization, and convened a cross-branch rewrite of the constitution.

In 2020-21 President Garrett Edmonds nominated him administrative vice president, saying he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him, and the Senate confirmed Keller 29-1 in October 2020. The Herald first called the post executive vice president and ran a correction to administrative vice president — the same title given to Abbey Norvell in the election coverage — so the sources do not fully resolve the two vice-presidential titles for the year. He authored organizational-aid bills, among them one in February 2021 funding four student organizations and, in March 2021, what the Herald called the largest organizational aid bill SGA had passed.

executive.name: Matt Barr
executive.note: Served as interim chief of staff under the outgoing cabinet in September 2020 and was still in the post in March 2021. He reported the three hammock sites finished, the new SGA signage and office computers installed over the winter break, and $2,870 spent on the Go With the Flow programme, which put five personal hygiene dispensers across campus.
profile: Matt Barr chaired the Campus Improvements committee in 2018-19, where he authored the bill creating a recurring $2,000 scholarship for first-generation students, passed 31-1 in October 2018. In February 2020, as Campus Improvements chair, he defended a contested slate of senator nominees, saying committees exist to develop ideas together.

He served as chief of staff in 2020-21, first on an interim basis under the outgoing cabinet in September 2020 and then confirmed that October. He ran the "Go With the Flow" programme, which put free menstrual-product dispensers across campus, reported the three hammock sites finished and new SGA signage and office computers installed over the winter break, and continued the programme into the spring semester.

executive.note: Reported 88 scholarship applications in March 2021, pushed the deadline back a day, and ran the Earn-A-Computer programme, through which two computers were given out that spring.
profile: Kody Okert was director of academic and student affairs in 2020-21. He was one of three senators Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell appointed to the Faculty Senate in October 2020. He ran the Earn-A-Computer programme, through which two computers were given out that spring, and reported the year's scholarship numbers to the Senate: fewer than 20 applications for the five SGA scholarships then open in late February 2021, and 88 applications by early March, when he pushed the deadline back a day.

executive.name: Paul Brosky

profile: Jamison Moorehead was nominated director of information technology in January 2021, when SGA's spring semester opened over Zoom, and was confirmed. He handled absence excuses that winter, reminding senators that an absence without an excuse form went to the Judicial Council, and for a time in January 2021 held the Senate secretaryship and the IT directorship together before Brenna Mathews returned as secretary in February. He was confirmed director of IT again for 2021-22.

She proposed buttons carrying the updated SGA logo and the committees, held the year's first tabling event in November 2020, and planned the LGBTQIA+ UNITE event; SGA brochures and nametags arrived in March 2021.
profile: Ashlynn Evans was SGA's director of public relations in 2019-20 and 2020-21. Confirmed 12-5 in September 2019 after chairing the Public Relations committee the previous semester, she said she had arranged the handover with the outgoing director, Noah Moore, and proposed keeping the Senator of the Week programme and adding a Student of the Month.

In 2020-21 she proposed buttons carrying the updated SGA logo, held the year's first tabling event in November 2020 and planned an LGBTQIA+ UNITE event; SGA brochures and nametags arrived in March 2021.

officers.name: Shelby Robertson
profile: Shelby Robertson was elected Speaker of the Senate on 6 October 2020, defeating Brenna Matthews at the first official Senate meeting of the year, at which the annual budget passed 28-5.

At the executive cabinet's first recorded meeting on 13 October 2020 she pushed to connect senators with shared legislative interests, to adopt inclusive pronoun language in the chamber, and to find a parliamentarian. Later that month, on 28 October, she was among the senators Executive Vice President Abbey Norvell appointed to the University's Faculty Senate.

officers.note: Gave the Judicial Council report to the Senate on 2 March 2021: the constitutional review committee would meet in person in the chambers, the constitutional amendment election was set for 18-19 March and the general election for 12-13 April. The senate minutes spell the surname "Puhhaka"; the Judicial Council's own minutes of 21 September 2020 give "Puhakka". The spelling is unsettled.
profile: Puhakka was the Judicial Council's preferred candidate for a vacant council seat in spring 2019. President Stephen Mayer nominated junior Wood Brown instead, and before the vote Associate Justice Annalicia Carlson told the Senate the council believed Puhakka was the better nominee. The Senate rejected Brown 17-11 in early April, short of the two-thirds majority appointments require, and Mayer nominated Puhakka the following week. She was confirmed an associate justice on a 27-0 vote on 9 April 2019 and sworn in by Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds.

Puhakka went on to become chief justice; she was in the post by March 2021, when she reported to the Senate that a constitutional review committee would meet in person and set the spring's constitutional-amendment and general election dates. On 30 March 2021 she stepped down as chief justice shortly before that spring's elections; President Edmonds told the Senate he would not nominate a replacement so close to the election and would leave the choice to his successor.

leaders.name: Matthew Wininger
leaders.note: Sworn in as student regent 6 August 2021, at the meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for Margaret Munday, WKU's first African American student to enrol.
profile: Wininger ran for student body president in the April 2021 SGA election, with voting held on TopNet April 12-13. In the Herald's ballot guide he said he wanted to make SGA "the most active and vibrant organization on campus." Me'Lon Craighead, who would serve as his executive vice president, ran for that office in the same election.

As president, Wininger opened the fall semester by welcoming new and returning senators to the second meeting of the 21st Senate. He presided over the unanimous confirmation of senators elected the previous semester and of his executive appointments, including Jamison Moorehead as IT director, Alexis Courtenay as public relations director and Parker Raybourne as chief of staff, and the senate adopted new election codes at the same meeting.

In spring 2022 Wininger welcomed senators back from winter break and announced an initiative to create a student resource handbook aimed particularly at underclassmen, encouraging all SGA committees to pitch in on the project. At that same first meeting of 2022, the senate he led responded to the December tornado disaster by unanimously passing a $1,000 bill to restock the Office of Sustainability food pantry.

events.title: Northeast Hall renamed for Margaret Munday
events.body: Student Regent Matthew Wininger was sworn in at the Board of Regents meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for WKU's first African American student to enrol - the first building on campus named after an African American.

events.title: Cole Bornefeld elected with 49% of 1,448 votes
events.body: Alexis Courtenay took 40% and Olivia Feck 11%. Sam Kurtz and Garrison Reed were elected to the two vice presidencies.

events.title: Students fill the 2022-23 class, at-large and college seats
events.body: The same April ballot filled the incoming Senate's class, college and at-large seats. Olivia Feck, Matthew Gadd and James Cecil won the senior class seats; Mallory Hardesty, Aniya Johnson and Preston Romanov the junior class seats; and Ethan Taylor, Reed Hensley and Jakob Briggs the sophomore class seats. Ten students were elected senators-at-large, including Antonina Clementi and Ethan Huffaker, and Elizabeth DeLozier won the College of Health and Human Services seat, one of five college seats decided that day.

events.title: SGA opened the fall term with confirmations and new election codes
events.body: SGA held its first meeting of the fall semester, the second meeting of the 21st Senate, with President Matthew Wininger welcoming new and returning senators. All senators present were confirmed by unanimous consent and sworn in by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, along with executive appointments Jamison Moorehead as IT director, Alexis Courtenay as public relations director and Parker Raybourne as chief of staff. New election codes for the next semester also passed with unanimous consent.

events.title: New senators seated and freshman election results announced
events.body: The senate unanimously voted in four new senate members, two judicial council members and Trib Singh as director of academic and student affairs; Abbey Norvell and Nicole Massarone took the judicial council seats. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch introduced the Legislative Operations Committee and committees on student experience, mental health, sustainability, campus improvement, diversity and student outreach. That night the fall election results named Addison Falkner, Sam Kurtz and Jenna Wells freshman senators and Arivumani Srivastava the Gatton Academy senator.

events.title: 21st Senate passed its first resolution and stripped the speaker of a vote
events.body: At its Oct. 5 meeting SGA passed Resolution 1.21f, addressing the lack of an advisor evaluation system, by 21-2, the first resolution of the 21st Senate. Bill 2.21f, barring the speaker of the senate from voting on legislation to avoid bias, also passed 21-2, and Bills 3.21f and 4.21f, repealing an obsolete 2007 bylaw and outdated staff and faculty senate assignment rules, passed by unanimous consent. Parking director Jennifer Tougas discussed a possible monthly parking tag subscription and campus bookstore operations.

events.title: EF-3 tornado struck Bowling Green, killing 11 in Warren County
events.body: An EF-3 tornado with 150 mph winds slammed into Bowling Green early on Dec. 11, killing 11 people according to the coroner and destroying homes and businesses across Warren County. Gov. Andy Beshear signed a state of emergency and President Biden signed an emergency declaration. The disaster shaped SGA relief efforts the following semester.

events.title: First 2022 meeting funded the tornado-drained food pantry
events.body: At its first meeting of 2022, SGA passed Bill 1.22s by unanimous consent, providing $1,000 to restock the food pantry in the WKU Office of Sustainability, whose food and toiletries the Herald reported had been drained by the tornado recovery effort. Wininger announced an initiative to create a student resource handbook for underclassmen. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch set spring election signups to close April 8, with voting April 18-19.

events.title: Syllabi clause, crosswalk resolutions and Title IX meetings passed
events.body: At its Feb. 15 meeting SGA unanimously passed Resolution 6-22-S adding an SGA clause to course syllabi, listing meeting times, office location and the organization's purpose, which the Herald reported would be the first of its kind in SGA history. Resolutions 3-22-S, 4-22-S and 5-22-S, supporting new crosswalks below the Van Meter green space, in front of 1600 Chestnut St. and near 1566 Normal St., all passed unanimously. Bill 6-22-S required a committee chair or delegate to meet the Counseling Center director and the Title IX coordinator at least once a semester, and the senate also approved a task force for the iWKU app and funding for a financial success workshop.

events.title: Judiciary Council cleared Bornefeld's campaign over student-all email
events.body: After several SGA members complained that presidential candidate Cole Bornefeld's student-wide email about the Swipe Out Hunger initiative violated the election code's ban on self-promotion (section 3.5), the Judiciary Council held a roughly hour-long Zoom hearing on April 13 and voted in favor of his campaign. Speaker Tess Welch argued the signed email constituted self-promotion, and Administrative Vice President Reed Breunig said the email was not cleared by any member of SGA. A statement from President Wininger, read by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, said nothing in the code required executive cabinet or PR approval for a student-all email. Senators said the initiative saw a record number of donations after the email went out.

events.title: End-of-year allocations funded scholarships, organizational aid and planetarium donation
events.body: Hours before the 2022 election results were announced, the senate passed a slate of funding bills: Bill 45-22-S split $15,500 across five scholarship programs unanimously, including summer class, study abroad, ISEC book and Scholar Level scholarships, plus $500 to Black Student Alliance scholarships for the first time; and Bill 42-22-S granted $500 to each organization that applied for fall organizational aid, totaling $8,000. The senate also cut a requested $1,000 Hardin Planetarium donation to $325, a $500 autism walk request to $300, and approved $500 for a student worker appreciation event and $570.02 for an e-waste recycling bin on main campus.

events.title: SGA takes up residence hall mold and DSU food lines
events.body: Executive Vice President Me'Lon Craighead told the senate that SGA was working with Housing and Residence Life on mold accumulation in residence halls and had raised long food lines at DSU, saying part of the problem stemmed from a lack of employment. She said plans were in progress to place an SGA senator on a restaurant group committee. Title IX coordinator Deborah Wilkins opened the meeting describing new Title IX training for Greek life, band and athletics students.

events.title: State Rep. Patti Minter asks SGA to endorse a student borrower bill
events.body: State Rep. Patti Minter, a WKU history professor, asked SGA to endorse legislation she called the "Student Borrower's Bill of Rights," aimed at predatory student loan companies, and clarified it was not a debt cancellation bill. The senate passed Bill 5.21f initiating a Title IX training module for all SGA senators. Four senate nominees were confirmed with unanimous consent and sworn in by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder.

events.title: Bill to buy senator polos draws contention over cost
events.body: Bill 7.21f, allocating funding for polo shirts for senators to wear at meetings, was contested, with some senators arguing the polos would be uncomfortable in winter months. The Herald reported the bill would consume 10% of the discretionary legislative budget if passed. Assistant Provost Molly Kerby spoke on classroom equity work and a rise in WKU's Campus Pride Index score.

events.title: Senate funds job fair scholarships after long debate
events.body: Bill 12.21f, funding three $250 scholarships at an upcoming job fair sponsored by the Advising and Career Development Center, passed after extended debate. Bill 10.21f amending bylaws and Bill 11.21f funding the Chinese club both passed with unanimous consent, as did Resolution 2.21f providing a gift basket for a Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony. Craighead reported progress creating a new university committee for the WKU Restaurant Group.

events.title: Predatory loan resolution stalls on a 17-16 vote
events.body: Resolution 3.21f, on stopping predatory student loans for first year students and stemming from Rep. Patti Minter's visit, did not pass. By a 17-16 vote the senate rescheduled debate to the following meeting. Bill 13.21f, allocating $350 for a finals stress relief tabling event, passed by an overwhelming margin.

events.title: Loan resolution passes on reintroduction; senate backs campus-wide Title IX training
events.body: Resolution 3.21f passed on reintroduction with 17 in favor, 8 against and 4 abstentions after heavy criticism the previous week. Resolution 6.21f, requiring Title IX training for all enrolled students and WKU faculty, passed by an overwhelming margin. Resolution 7.21f, on the teaching of critical race theory, was introduced but its debate and vote were postponed for time.

events.title: SGA approves a meal swipe donation program against food insecurity
events.body: SGA approved a program letting students donate excess meal swipes in the 4th, 8th and 12th weeks of each semester, with the WKU Restaurant Group matching one swipe for every four donated. Students facing food insecurity could request five or 10 meal blocks up to twice per semester, with a pot of up to 1,000 swipes. Senator-at-Large Cole Bornefeld, who pushed the program, said he wanted students to be able to help other students.

events.title: Senate backs LGBTQ+ outreach and training by WKU Police
events.body: The senate voted in favor of Resolution 8-22-S, supporting outreach to the LGBTQ community and training on sexual orientation and gender identity issues by the WKU Police Department. It also unanimously approved Bill 15-22-S allocating $100 for materials for ISEC's Women's History Month tabling. Senators Ataullah Tahiri and Tramaine Hawkins were unanimously confirmed.

events.title: Constitution amended on mental health committee; food insecurity clause added to syllabi
events.body: Bill 22-22-S, amending the SGA constitution to redefine the duties of the Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee, passed unanimously. Resolution 10-22-S, adding a food insecurity clause to course syllabi pointing students to the meal swipe request form and the Office of Sustainability, also passed unanimously. Bill 36-22-S funding an Easter egg hunt benefiting the Kentucky Veterans Brigade was passed with the amount amended upward from $500 to $750.

events.title: SGA put $1,200 and a mechanical bull into Homecoming
events.body: Bill 8-21-F allocated $1,200 from legislative discretionary funds to the Intercultural Student Engagement Center for its Homecoming 2021 events at Centennial Mall on 27 October, free and open to all students from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. The bill records that the attraction was a mechanical bull, intended to get students socialising after the pandemic had made networking difficult for ISEC. It had its first reading on 26 October 2021.

src.label: SGA Bill 8-21-F, Funding for the ISEC Homecoming 2021 events and activities

events.title: Free teeth cleanings through the dental hygiene programme
events.body: Bill 9-22-S allocated $500 from the legislative discretionary budget to the WKU Dental Hygiene programme to start a voucher system giving students free teeth cleanings. The bill said the $500 would cover 20 cleanings and would also help the dental hygiene students, who needed a set number of patients to complete their studies. It had its first reading on 8 February 2022 and the voucher was still part of SGA's programme four years later.

src.label: SGA Bill 9-22-S, Funding for vouchers for free teeth cleanings through the WKU Dental Hygiene Program

events.title: Love The Earth tabled on Valentine's Day
events.body: Bill 8-22-S allocated $100 from legislative discretionary funds for the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee's Love The Earth tabling event at Downing Student Union on 14 February 2022, from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. SGA handed out snacks and flyers, promoted WKU Recycling and sustainability organisations, and collected student input.

src.label: SGA Bill 8-22-S, Funding for a "Love The Earth" Valentine's Day Event

events.title: Fifteen hundred dollars into the Run on Walmart
events.body: Bill 20-22-S proposed allocating $1,500 from the legislative discretionary fund to the Run on Walmart, an event hosted by Alpha Phi Alpha at 9:06 p.m. on 20 March 2022 with Alpha Omicron Pi, Omega Phi Alpha, Walmart and Omicron Nu Lambda. The money bought vouchers so students could buy goods for donation to First Christian Church, which passed the groceries on. The bill was aimed at homelessness, hunger and tornado relief and had its first reading on 8 March 2022.

src.label: SGA Bill 20-22-S, Funding for the "Run on Walmart" event

events.title: Earth Day tie-dye returned after two years without a celebration
events.body: Bill 41-22-S allocated $125 from legislative discretionary funds for the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee's Earth Day tie-dye tabling event at Centennial Mall on 22 April 2022, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The bill noted that COVID-19 had left WKU without a proper Earth Day celebration for two years, and that the year's theme of sustainable fashion made recycled tie-dye a fitting activity.

src.label: SGA Bill 41-22-S, Funding for an Earth Day Tie-Dye Tabling Event

events.title: SGA's first Mental Health Awareness Week
events.body: SGA ran a mental health awareness week from 25 to 29 April 2022, ahead of Mental Health Awareness Month in May, with an event each day. The week opened with tabling at Centennial Mall from 10:30 a.m. to 2 p.m., with raffled gift cards, music and counselling information, and continued with a Zumba class in the Preston Center on 26 April run with GroupX Fitness. Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Alex Cissell said the point was to reduce the stigma around mental illness.

src.label: Herald, 21 Apr 2022 - "SGA to host Mental Health Awareness events across next week"

events.title: Hilltopper Hunt raised money for a veterans' food charity
events.body: Bill 36-22-S allocated $500 from legislative discretionary funds to Hilltopper Hunt: Egging out Hunger, a donation drive and fundraiser for the Kentucky Veterans Brigade, a charity assisting south central Kentucky veterans facing hunger, homelessness and financial strain. The brigade had opened its doors to the whole Bowling Green community after the December 2021 tornado outbreak. The event doubled as the senior capstone project of four WKU public relations majors.

src.label: SGA Bill 36-22-S, Funding for Hilltopper Hunt: Egging out Hunger for Kentucky Veterans Brigade

events.title: Resolution condemning critical race theory bans passed 16-15
events.body: After weeks of debate and several speeches of affirmation and negation, the senate passed Resolution 7.21f, condemning the banning of critical race theory teaching in postsecondary education. The vote was 16 in favor and 15 against, with two abstentions. Sponsors cited an anticipated bill request in the Kentucky General Assembly, and sponsor Olivia Blackmon said the measure was meant to ensure intellectual freedom in the curriculum rather than politicize classrooms.

events.title: Senate confirmed the year's budget in Bill 1.21f
events.body: At the third meeting of the 21st Senate, on 7 September, SGA passed Bill 1.21f, confirming its budget for the year. Dean of Students Martha Sales opened the meeting on leadership, telling senators they had to learn how to lead and pressing them on their purpose as a student body. President Matthew Wininger announced a planned donor drive in partnership with at least four other student organizations, and Chief of Staff Parker Raybourne announced a Hilltopper Hangout event for 24 September.

events.title: Spring voting opened for the senate that would sit in 2021-22
events.body: SGA's spring election for the senate that would sit in 2021-22 opened on TopNet on 12 April 2021 and ran two days. The Herald published the ballot: candidates stood for senator-at-large, the class seats, the first-generation seat, the Gatton Academy seat and the college seats, with Avery Wells and Reed Breunig running for administrative vice president and Wells also standing for a senate seat. Candidate statements promised campus safety work across gender, age, sexual orientation and race, and an expanded SGA scholarship programme worked up with WKU Health Education and Promotion. The page has since been marked with the winners, showing Matthew Waninger elected student body president and Me'Lon Craighead executive vice president.

src.label: Herald, 12 Apr 2021 - "SGA voting opens today: Who is on the ballot"

events.title: A lobbyist and former Tennessee legislator spoke to the senate
events.body: Debra Maggart, a WKU alumna and former Tennessee state representative working as a lobbyist, was the guest speaker at the 1 February 2022 meeting and urged senators to get involved with the issues they cared about. President Matthew Wininger nominated Tyler Hopkins, Lauren Willet, Jack Galloway and Matt Brown as senators and all four were confirmed by unanimous consent. Executive Vice President Me'Lon Craighead announced ten nominations to a newly created Faculty Awards Committee, set up to review professors and help students find ones who would be useful to them. Bills 4.22s and 5.22s, removing the requirement that an author attend Legislative Operations Committee meetings and setting when office hours may be collected, both passed by unanimous consent.

src.label: Herald, 2 Feb 2022 - "SGA welcomes WKU alumna and former state representative, passes pair of bills"

events.title: A constitutional amendment passed 31-0 and was vetoed the same day
events.body: Bill 13-22-S, written by Emily Bunning, a senior senator, and Alex Cissell, chair of the Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee, was first read on 15 February 2022 to redefine that committee's duties around a holistic approach to wellness. It had its second reading on 22 February 2022; the bill sheet records an initial Senate vote of 31 in favor and none against, and a veto the same day. A shorter revision, Bill 22-22-S, was first read on 8 March and passed both the Senate and the Executive Cabinet on 22 March 2022.

events.title: The seventh standing committee is created
events.body: Bill 21-22-S, first read 8 March and given a second reading on 22 March 2022, amended the constitution to establish a Community Relations Committee to advocate for students' needs in Bowling Green, encourage volunteer service and coordinate a yearly voter drive; the bill stated the committee was not meant for pushing a political agenda. Its authors were senators Margaret Glaser, Emily Bunning and Cole Bornefeld, sponsored by the Outreach and Student Experience and Legislative Operations committees. The current constitution still lists the Community Relations Committee last among seven standing committees.

events.title: Council fixed the size of the Organizational Aid Board
events.body: Asked whether section 6.1.1's figure of six members for the Organizational Aid Board was a floor or a ceiling, the council ruled that six was the minimum needed for the board to operate and that the constitution set no maximum. At the same meeting it ruled that the executive vice president could appoint SGA senators to Faculty Senate committees.

events.title: Council ruled the constitution can be amended by ordinary bill
events.body: After debate on whether constitutional change required the special amendment committee, the council ruled that the constitution could be amended through bills, which students could write, and that the special committee was reserved for larger amendments. It also ruled that the constitution definitively placed the president on the Senate Executive Committee of Faculty Senate without a Senate confirmation.

events.title: Council held the constitution supreme over the bylaws on the executive veto
events.body: Ruling on a discrepancy between the constitution and the bylaws over which members of the executive cabinet could vote on a veto, the council held that supremacy went to the constitution and that the bylaws had to be amended to match. It took no action on votes already cast but required proper procedure in future. At the same meeting it set a standard of three unexcused committee-meeting absences for senators, effective the following semester, with no action against senators already over the line.

events.title: Judicial Council gets its first written procedural rules
events.body: Bill 17-22-S, first read 1 March 2022 and given a second reading on 8 March, supported adoption of the General Procedural Rules of the Judicial Council. The bill stated that the council had previously had no formal written established guidelines or procedures pertaining to its functions and duties. The rules that followed rank as equal to the Legislative Bylaws, set out the council's attendance, censure and judicial review procedure, and provide for the Senate to override a Judicial Council veto by two-thirds of those present and voting.

In February 2022 the Senate approved the creation of an iWKU app task force that Craighead had petitioned for, with Craighead to appoint its chair the following week. She was also the named contact officer on Bill 18-22-S, which funded the Diversity and Inclusion scholarship for the Mahurin Honors College membership fee.

executive.name: Zachary Skillman
profile: Zachary Skillman was elected a WKU SGA senator-at-large in September 2021, one of two Skillmans (with fellow business economics junior Jacob Skillman, no relation established in the sources) sworn in on 14 September. A junior majoring in business economics and a Gordon Ford College of Business ambassador, he said Matthew Wininger had encouraged him to run and that he wanted to continue the recycling and sustainability initiatives Wininger had started as head of the sustainability committee, including off-campus recycling, a used-WKU-apparel recycling program and an adopt-a-highway effort.

By 2021-22 Skillman chaired the renamed Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee. In April 2022 he won Senate approval of $570.02 for an e-waste recycling bin on WKU's main campus, saying the project would earn WKU 0.25 credits toward Gold certification from the Association for the Advancement of Sustainability in Higher Education. He also co-authored Resolution 12-22-S, adding benches to South Lawn, and authored Bill 41-22-S, funding an Earth Day tie-dye tabling event.

profile: Tess Welch was Speaker of the Senate in 2021-22, under President Matthew Wininger. At the 14 September 2021 meeting, as the Senate seated new members and confirmed judicial council members and a director of academic and student affairs, she introduced the year's slate of committees covering legislative operations, student experience, mental health, sustainability, campus improvement, diversity and outreach.

At the first meeting of 2022, on 18 January, she announced the spring election dates as the Senate voted $1,000 to restock the Office of Sustainability food pantry that tornado-recovery efforts had drained.

In April 2022 Welch argued before the Judicial Council that presidential candidate Cole Bornefeld's student-wide email about the Swipe Out Hunger initiative was self-promotion barred by the election code; after an hour-long hearing on 13 April the council ruled in favour of his campaign.

officers.name: Elizabeth DeLozier
officers.note: Appointed on Speaker Welch's motion by unanimous consent on 31 August 2021. She co-authored Bill 4-22-S amending the constitution and Resolution 6-21-F, which asked that students be included in mandatory Title IX training.
profile: DeLozier was already a sitting senator when Speaker Tess Welch moved to appoint her Senate secretary at the 31 August 2021 meeting; she spoke to her qualifications and was confirmed by unanimous consent.

In the April 2022 election she won the College of Health and Human Services senate seat for 2022-23, and that September the new Senate installed her as chair of the Legislative Operations Committee, the body that reviews bills and resolutions before they reach the floor.

leaders.name: Cole Bornefeld
leaders.note: Elected April 2022 with 49% of 1,448 votes. In February 2023 the Speaker of the Senate brought a censure case against him over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram; the Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure, and a Title IX report seeking his removal was filed two days later. Last name currently on the plaque.
profile: Cole Bornefeld came to the presidency by an unusually fast route. He transferred to WKU from Volunteer State Community College as a junior, emailed then-President Matthew Wininger during his first week on campus, and was appointed a senator-at-large at their first meeting. He had not planned to run for president, but after senators urged him to, he formed a ticket the week of the filing deadline and won. He campaigned on programs he backed as a senator, including the Share-A-Swipe meal donation program and growing SGA's scholarship budget, which rose by $3,500 during his presidency. Adjusting to the office, he said it felt like "drinking out of a fire hose," and he sought advice from former student body presidents weekly.

Bornefeld opened the 2022-23 year with an executive retreat on Aug. 29 at the Cliff Todd Center, where his team set three priorities: a one-stop resource guide for students, a push to represent WKU's five regional campuses, which he said was "an area that I really don't think SGA has ever touched," and financial assistance for students as the year's underlying goal. He had met with the director of regional campuses the week before to start that work.

His spring semester was dominated by fallout from anti-LGBTQ Instagram posts he had liked. After the judicial council unanimously declined to censure him, the Queer Student Union removed SGA meetings from its list of campus safe spaces and said it would not associate with SGA until a public apology was released. Addressing the senate on Feb. 21, Bornefeld, who also served as student regent, said he "always commits to loving thy neighbor" but could not commit to always agreeing, tying his position to his Christian values and offering to meet any student over coffee or breakfast to discuss disagreements.

events.title: The Speaker takes the President to the Judicial Council
events.body: Speaker of the Senate Yulia 'Julie' Mishchuk requested a censure hearing against President Cole Bornefeld over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram. Members of the Queer Student Union and both vice presidents attended. The Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure.

events.title: Executive retreat set the year's goals
events.body: SGA's executive team held a formal retreat dinner on Aug. 29 at the Cliff Todd Center to set its agenda for the year. President Cole Bornefeld said the group was building a one-stop student resource guide and wanted better representation for WKU's regional campuses in Elizabethtown, Fort Knox, Glasgow, Owensboro and Somerset; he said he had met regional campuses director Derick Strode and called it an area SGA had never touched. Speaker of the Senate Julie Mishchuk said the underlying goal of the year was financial assistance for students.

events.title: First meeting filled senate and cabinet vacancies
events.body: At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 30, the senate approved all of President Bornefeld's nominees, including Juan Thomas, Will Hemenover and Sydney Denney as senators-at-large, Aniya Johnson as director of information technology, Donte' Reed as director of enrollment and student experience, and Isaac Kind and Garrett Baum to the judicial council. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz spoke on the budget and Chief Justice Holden Schroeder swore in the new members.

events.title: Senate approved five nominations and reviewed a shrinking budget
events.body: The senate unanimously confirmed five nominations, including Adan Canizalez as chair of student enrollment and experience and Miles Huff, a track athlete, to the Judicial Council, filling the vacancy left by Holden Schroeder. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz urged senators to sponsor more resolutions, which use university funds, because only about $39,460.76 remained of SGA's $100,000 annual budget for bills, and Speaker Julie Mishchuk floated a constitutional amendment requiring every senator to sponsor at least one bill or resolution. Chief Justice Justin Goins nominated Isaac King as associate chief justice.

events.title: Narcan resolution aimed to put overdose spray in residence halls
events.body: SGA unanimously passed Resolution 2-23-S on Feb. 7, with support from five of seven committees, backing placement of Narcan, an opioid overdose reversal spray, in WKU residence halls. SGA had planned to spend about $1,000 of its own budget, but a University of Kentucky harm reduction specialist helped secure the product through a government grant instead, so the resolution became a statement of support. Housing and Residence Life asked to delay installation to Aug. 1 to allow staff training before putting the spray in AED-style boxes across its 15 dorms, and director of housing operations Lana Kunkel said no overdose incidents had occurred in a WKU residence hall.

events.title: Menstrual product legislation passed as the Queer Student Union protested
events.body: At its Feb. 21 meeting SGA passed a resolution supporting menstrual product dispensers on the first floor of every academic building, a $200 bill to distribute 35 menstrual cups at tabling events, $100 for a community relations survey and funding for Sexual Assault Prevention Month t-shirts. Queer Student Union president Alistar Flowers told the senate QSU had removed SGA meetings from its list of campus safe spaces after the Judicial Council declined to censure President Bornefeld over his Instagram activity, and said QSU would not associate with SGA until a public apology was released; Flowers also questioned the fairness of a Judicial Council whose members are mostly nominated by the president. Bornefeld responded in his officer report that he "always commits to loving thy neighbor" but cannot always agree.

events.title: Senate passed a committee-merger bill and funded Mental Health Awareness Week
events.body: At the April 11 meeting the senate passed Bill 44-23-S, a constitutional amendment merging the Community Relations and Outreach committees starting in 2023-24, which Speaker Mishchuk said would create a stronger committee amid low membership. SGA's own legislation record shows the Executive Cabinet vetoed the bill, and the current constitution still lists Community Relations and Outreach and Public Relations as separate committees, so the merger did not take effect. Senators also unanimously funded a slate of Mental Health Awareness Week events for April 23 through 28, including an Out of the Darkness suicide prevention walk, and passed a $62 terrarium tabling bill. President Bornefeld reported 44 applicants for the upcoming SGA elections.

src2.label: SGA Bill 44-23-S and WKU SGA Legislation Archive

events.title: Committee chairs installed; vice president serves on governor's higher education committee
events.body: Six committee chairs were installed, including Olivia Feck on student mental health and wellbeing, Elizabeth DeLozier on legislative operations and Ahatali Tahiri on diversity, equity and inclusion. Bornefeld commended Executive Vice President Garrison Reed for his work on Gov. Andy Beshear's higher education committee. Provost Bud Fischer briefed senators on the Quality Enhancement Plan tied to WKU's 2025 accreditation reaffirmation submission.

events.title: SGA presses administrators on Big Red Backpack opt-out default
events.body: Assistant Vice President Jennifer Tougas took SGA feedback on the Big Red Backpack course materials program, which SGA discussions had prompted. Asked why the program defaulted to opt-out, Tougas acknowledged that "schools that use the opt-in approach are far more successful" but said WKU chose opt-out to keep the per-credit-hour cost low. Senators also raised missing textbooks in student orders, and President Timothy Caboni appeared to commend SGA for its role in creating the program.

events.title: Senate passes a Bowling Green Pride sponsorship bill and hears a student veteran scholarship announced
events.body: A bill by Senator Meghan Pierce allocating $250 from the Legislative Directory to sponsor Bowling Green Pride passed the Senate that night, naming SGA a Rainbow Sponsor and securing tabling space for diversity, equity and inclusion. SGA's own legislation record shows the bill, filed as Bill 2-22-F, did not clear the Executive Cabinet, so the sponsorship as the Senate passed it did not take effect. Director of Enrollment and Student Experience Donte' Reed announced a scholarship for a student veteran in partnership with the Student Veterans Association. Senators also discussed the new campus e-bikes, with suggestions for a Park Street dock and a safety awareness campaign.

src2.label: SGA Bill 2-22-F and WKU SGA Legislation Archive

events.title: Executives report on a campus listening tour as enrollment chief briefs senate
events.body: Bornefeld said he, Garrison Reed and Sam Kurtz had been holding a listening tour to increase SGA's accessibility to students, citing feedback from the Panhellenic Council. Ethan Logan, vice president of enrollment, told senators WKU's retention rate stood at 76.66% and discussed reaching students who do not speak English as a first language. Senator Salvador León asked whether students could serve as bilingual counselors.

events.title: Appeals court revives part of former SGA president's suit against WKU
events.body: The Sixth Circuit vacated summary judgment on the pre-February 2018 Title IX student-on-student harassment claims of Loandria "Andi" Dahmer, SGA president in 2017-18 and a former student regent, and vacated qualified immunity for SGA faculty adviser Charley Pride. The court upheld dismissal of her remaining claims, including a retaliation claim over President Timothy Caboni declining to write a Rhodes Scholarship recommendation. University spokesperson Jace Lux said WKU would renew its motion for summary judgment on the remaining issue.

events.title: Senate funds a trivia night at the Glasgow regional campus
events.body: Bill 38-23-S, funding a trivia night with pizza and prizes at the WKU Glasgow campus, passed unanimously after being presented over Zoom by Glasgow regional ambassador Peyton Hess. Junior Senator Mallory Hardesty said the event would give satellite campus students a real student experience. Adan Canizalez was voted senator of the month for January.

events.title: WKU dedicated the Commons at Helm Library
events.body: WKU formally dedicated the $35 million Commons at Helm Library, a renovation funded through a partnership with Aramark, and President Timothy Caboni announced early plans for a similar makeover of Cherry Hall. SGA President Cole Bornefeld spoke at the ceremony, saying the building had been full of excitement and community since it opened.

events.title: Afro-Latinidad event funded unanimously
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Bill 40-23-S on 21 March 2023 to fund the Afro-Latinidad event held on 3 April, which featured art displays, presentations, influential Latino figures and culinary displays. Spanish instructor Yertty Vandermolen spoke for the bill, saying people usually picture a tanned Central or Latin American person and forget the African presence in Spanish-speaking countries, and that her students had worked all semester to honour Afro-Latino culture.

events.title: A former state representative told the senate to get on LinkedIn
events.body: WKU alumnus Jim DeCesare, who spent 14 years in the Kentucky House of Representatives and runs the DeCesare Group, spoke as guest at the senate meeting of 11 April 2023 on the value of LinkedIn for building business relationships and finding work. He told senators he would not do a ten million dollar deal by text and that LinkedIn was a way to make the first introduction. He said Warren County had 7,000 jobs going unfilled.

src.label: Herald, 13 Apr 2023 - "WKU SGA discusses Mental Health Awareness week, combining of committees"

events.title: Fall election turnout doubled and vice president Garrison Reed joined the state postsecondary council
events.body: Fall 2022 election results, announced at midnight, seated Rush Robinson, Callison Padgett and Rhett Helland as freshman senators, Neel Patel for the Gatton Academy, Shy'Ante Williams as graduate senator and Salvador Leon Golib as international student senator. President Cole Bornefeld said the vote total rose from 398 the previous fall to 805. SGA also announced that student body vice president Garrison Reed had been appointed student representative on Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education, with a term running through 30 June 2023.

events.title: Title IX complaint against the SGA president sought his removal
events.body: A Title IX report filed with Student Conduct on 19 February 2023 accused President Cole Bornefeld, described in the report as student regent and representative of the student body, of gender-based harassment over four Turning Point USA Instagram posts he liked. The complaint sought his removal, a public statement from WKU and a public apology; the complainant's identity was redacted from the records released to the Herald. Spokesperson Jace Lux said the university does not comment on complaints made to the Office of Student Conduct. Removing an executive who will not resign requires written endorsement from at least 20 percent of the senate, a wait of at least fourteen days and a two-thirds vote of the full senate sitting as a judicial body; the Herald's report of 2 March recorded no outcome.

events.title: Election reform bill failed 19-15; Dance Big Red funding rejected
events.body: Bill 39-23-S, which would have moved the transfer, non-traditional and first-generation senate seats to the fall election and required a two-thirds senate vote before a vacant seat could become an at-large seat, failed 19-15, short of the two-thirds needed. Sponsor Neel Patel, the Gatton Academy senator, called reliance on the president to convert vacancies a dangerous practice for a government organization. Bill 40-23-S, funding an Afro-Latinidad cultural event on 3 April, passed unanimously. Bill 41-23-S, funding Dance Big Red, failed.

events.title: Kurtz ticket elected unopposed
events.body: Sam Kurtz, the outgoing administrative vice president, was elected student body president on a ticket that ran unopposed, with Salvador León as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president. Voting opened on TopNet on 17 April. Fourteen at-large senators were elected, along with the college, class and first-generation seats. Results were read at about 12:30 a.m. in the Downing Student Union senate chambers by Judicial Council Chief Justice Justin Goins.

events.title: Two voucher bills pass unanimously, a poetry night by one vote short of it
events.body: Bill 28-23-S put $500 toward free teeth cleanings at the WKU Dental Health Clinic, amended by committee chair Adan Canizalez to draw on the scholarship programme fund rather than the Legislative Discretionary Fund. Chief of staff Lauren Willett, an author of the bill, said voucher use had risen 660 per cent over the fall semester. Bill 27-23-S allocated $2,000 split 60/30/10 between the ID centre, the Preston Center and the dental hygiene clinic, and both bills passed unanimously. A third bill, $260 for a poetry mic night run with the Talisman, passed on a roll call with senator Ethan Huffaker the only vote against, citing superfluous spending; former SGA president Matthew Wininger had opened the meeting as guest speaker.

events.title: Safety Awareness Week passed 37-0
events.body: Bill 7-22-F allocated $467.68 from legislative discretionary funds for a Safety Awareness Week running 17 to 21 October 2022, and passed 37 votes to nil on 11 October. Monday and Tuesday were tabling days for students to sign up for self-defence classes and to advertise Wednesday's giveaway, with Hope Harbor present to promote its work. Wednesday handed out 72 personal alarms at $227.88 and 40 keychain utility tools at $239.80; Thursday and Friday were self-defence classes led by Officer Bailey. Tabling on the first three days counted towards senators' office hours. The bill records what was planned and funded, not how the week went.

events.body: Bill 8-22-F proposed allocating $500 from the legislative discretionary fund to the Intercultural Student Engagement Center for the 2022 Spook Fest, held in Downing Student Union on 27 October 2022 from 5 to 7 p.m. The bill itemises the spend: $285 on eight to ten Halloween booths including spell jars, cookie and whoopie pie decorating, stuffed plushies, bubbles and a witch's hat toss, and $215 on a pair of Beats headphones as the grand prize for a game called Who Shot Ya. It was authored by ISEC Senator Tramaine Hawkins with senators Juan Tomas and Megan Pierce, sponsored by the Student Enrollment and Outreach Committee, and read a second time on 25 October 2022; the posted form leaves the vote line blank.

events.title: Senate renamed three of its committees 36-1
events.body: Bill 4-22-F, authored by Speaker Julie Mishchuk and Senator Caleb Collins, was read on 4 and 11 October 2022 and carried 36 votes to 1. It cited a lack of clarity in the naming of constitutional committees and struck the abbreviations, making the Committee of Enrollment and Student Experience the Enrollment and Student Experience Committee, the Committee of Outreach and Student Experience the Outreach and Student Engagement Committee, and the Committee for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Committee.

events.title: Council held college seats must be filled from their colleges
events.body: Answering questions from Senator Ethan Huffaker, the council held that college, transfer and class senate seats must be filled by students of that college, status or class, because the requirement is inherent in the name of the seat. It held that only the freshman, graduate, international and Gatton Academy seats become senator-at-large seats when vacant under section 3.8.2, and that all other named seats remain what they are even when unfilled.

events.title: Council ruled a constitutional amendment veto can be overridden by two thirds
events.body: Answering the Secretary of the Senate, the council held that a presidential veto of a constitutional amendment could be overridden by a two-thirds vote under section 3.1.9, that the veto power extended to bylaw amendments, that senators elected in spring take office in the fall and cannot conduct business before then, and that nothing in the governing documents stopped the Senate funding bills from outside the legislative discretionary line. It also granted amnesty on late election expenditure sheets.

officers.note: Continued as chief justice into a second year. He chaired the Judicial Council on 16 September 2022, walking the new justices through the procedural rules he had written, and reported the September election dates to the Senate on 30 August 2022. He was gone by January.
profile: Schroeder was one of four judiciary nominees Student Body President Will Harris brought before the Senate on 24 September 2019, along with Jason Herlick, Derek Collins and Turner Reynolds. He had been chief justice of Kentucky Boys State as a high school junior and was a prosecution attorney on WKU's mock trial B-team; the Senate confirmed him to the Judicial Council unanimously.

By the start of the 2021-22 year he had become chief justice, swearing in senators and executive appointees at the Senate's first fall meeting on 31 August 2021 and bringing that semester's updated election codes to the floor. In April 2022 he read a statement from President Matthew Wininger during a Judicial Council hearing that cleared presidential candidate Cole Bornefeld of a self-promotion complaint over a student-wide email about the Swipe Out Hunger initiative. He wrote the council's General Procedural Rules and was lead author of Bill 17-22-S adopting them.

He continued as chief justice into the 2022-23 year, walking new justices Isaac King and Garrett Baum through those rules at the council's 16 September 2022 meeting and swearing in that year's new senators and cabinet appointees on 30 August 2022. The Senate elected Justin Goins to succeed him as chief justice on 17 January 2023, and had filled his own vacated council seat by the 25th.
