profile: Goins served as an associate justice on the Judicial Council in 2021-22, then moved up to associate chief justice under Chief Justice Holden Schroeder at the start of 2022-23.

After Schroeder left the council, the Senate elected Goins chief justice on 17 January 2023, in a vote Parliamentarian Meghan Pierce moved up the agenda; President Cole Bornefeld swore him in and he then swore in that meeting's new senators. He went on to nominate Isaac King as his associate chief justice.

On 17 February 2023 Goins presided over a Judicial Council hearing on Speaker of the Senate Julie Mishchuk's censure complaint against President Bornefeld, who had liked several Instagram posts Mishchuk said were transphobic; Mishchuk read the council a letter from the Queer Student Union about the visibility given to transgender students and said the group had removed SGA from its list of safe spaces; QSU's president said the same to the Senate four days later. The council heard both sides and voted unanimously against censure, and Goins announced the decision, saying the justices "could not find any basis for discrimination in the current WKU constitution."

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Former administrative vice president. Elected April 2023 on an unopposed ticket with Salvador Leon and Annalise Finch.
profile: Sam Kurtz, then the outgoing administrative vice president, was elected student body president in results announced early on April 19, 2023 in the Downing Student Union senate chambers, after voting opened on TopNet on April 17. His KFL ticket, with Annalise Finch as executive vice president and Salvador León as administrative vice president, ran unopposed, and Chief Justice Justin Goins read the results. In a statement, Kurtz said the ticket would "listen to students' concerns, represent their voices, lead with integrity, and promote transparency."

At the 23rd Senate's first fall meeting on Aug. 29, Kurtz nominated Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the Judicial Council from what he called a record number of applicants, and named seven committee heads, including Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. The Senate's first bill of the year, passed unanimously that September, funded the SGA Pink Walk breast-cancer event. That November the senate backed moving DSU fire drills from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. and funded a Boys and Girls Club toy drive. Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney wrote or co-wrote several of the year's bills, including a resolution capping student parking fees at $50, a $700 fund to help students pay parking fines, and voucher funding for the Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center. In February 2024 Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donté Reed rolled out a 450-voucher Uber giveaway aimed at student safety and outreach, followed in March by a need-based scholarship awarding Uber vouchers and a Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen; that month the senate also planned a Frankfort trip for the Rally for Higher Education.

The year's fight was internal. In February 2024 the Judicial Council voted 6-0 to censure Administrative Vice President Salvador León after a hearing brought by Denney and the executive cabinet, which alleged León had spent SGA funds - including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit for Neurodiversity Acceptance Week - before the Senate passed the funding bill, in violation of the constitution's clause 2.5.3 requiring the administrative vice president to expend funds only as the Senate authorizes. Chief Justice Isaac King said the cabinet, excluding León, had asked for the censure after León spent the funds despite Kurtz's condition that he wait for Bill 22-23-F to pass, and after he pushed PR Director Preston Romanov to promote the week on SGA social media ahead of the vote, effectively forcing the Senate's hand. León countered that text messages showed Kurtz had signed off on the spending in advance; the council found the spending improper but recommended no discipline beyond the censure itself.

In January 2024 Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and enrollment director Donte Reed both resigned, with Reed moving up to chief of staff. That April, Kurtz ran for a second term with Reed as his executive vice president candidate and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president; the ticket again ran unopposed on a ballot of more than 60 legislative candidates, and the three were re-elected as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the night of April 16-17, 2024. Before that, SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for a final Red Wave tailgate on April 9, with a student-DJ contest winner earning a $500 scholarship. The 23rd Senate held its last meeting on April 16 with no legislation on the agenda, and Kurtz thanked senators in his final report for what the group had accomplished that year.

events.title: The 23rd Senate corrects its own governing documents
events.body: Three bills from the Legislative Operations Committee: fix references to a 'University Senate' that had since split into separate Faculty and Staff senates, reconcile bylaws language about expelling senators with a constitution that only provides for impeachment, and update committee names that had drifted.

events.title: Fall election winners sworn in
events.body: SGA announced its fall election results on Sept. 20 over an Instagram livestream, electing Savanna Kurtz, Malick Ibrahim and Chloe Ralston as freshman senators, ShyAntye'e Williams as graduate senator, Sim Guan Zhou as international senator and Livi Ray as Gatton Academy senator. Five of the six were sworn in at the following Tuesday meeting. Sophomore senator Rush Robinson received the year's first Senator of the Month award.

events.title: Midyear resignations reshuffle the executive cabinet
events.body: President Sam Kurtz announced the resignations of Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and of Donte Reed as director of enrollment and student experience at the first meeting of the spring semester. The senate approved Kurtz's nominations of Reed as the new chief of staff and Sarah Vincent as director of enrollment and student experience. Kurtz also filled vacant transfer/non-traditional, sophomore and graduate senate seats with Sawyer Edmonds, Gabe Jerdon and Elizabeth Gannon.

events.title: Judicial council censures Salvador León
events.body: At a Feb. 7 hearing, Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney presented three allegations against Administrative Vice President Salvador León, including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit paid Feb. 1 from the executive project and legislative discretionary budgets before Bill 22-23-S reached the Senate on Feb. 6. León countered with text messages in which Kurtz replied "sweet" and "bet sounds good" to his spending plans, and said he was only paying a fee and doing his job. The judicial council voted 6-0 to censure him, recommended no further disciplinary action, and called the episode a learning experience.

events.title: 23rd Senate holds its final meeting
events.body: The 23rd Senate met for the last time with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on senators' final remarks. Kurtz thanked the senate and said in his final report, "We've done a lot of great things this year." Executive Vice President Annie Finch and Administrative Vice President Salvador León also gave closing reports before the 24th Senate's first meeting on April 23.

events.title: Kurtz re-elected unopposed to a second term
events.body: Running with Chief of Staff Donté Reed for executive vice president and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president, Kurtz was re-elected without opposition as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the same night. More than 60 students had appeared on the ballot for the spring 2024 general election.

events.title: Senate backs a later fire-drill time, funds a toy drive
events.body: At the 23rd Senate's 11th meeting, senators unanimously passed Resolution 6-23-F, backing a change to DSU fire-drill timing from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. after the Mental Health and Wellness Committee argued the earlier hour caused sleep problems and anxiety for students on early schedules or with accommodations. They also unanimously passed Bill 12-23-F, allocating $200 from the legislative discretionary fund for a Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green toy drive, and swore in newly elected ISEC senator Ashlee Potter.

events.title: Spring committee heads sworn in
events.body: At the spring semester's first meeting, Kurtz appointed Madison Parker Payne as Outreach Committee chair and Sophia Bryant as Mental Health and Well-Being Committee chair; both were approved without contested debate. Executive Vice President Annalise Finch appointed Jaden Marshall to chair the Graduate Advisory Council campus committee and Chloe Ralston to chair the Colonnade General Education committee. Kurtz urged senators to spend down the senate's still-large discretionary budget before the semester's end.

events.title: Cabinet requests censure hearing against León
events.body: Kurtz told the senate the Executive Cabinet had filed a formal report seeking a Judicial Council censure hearing against Administrative Vice President Salvador León. Chief Justice Isaac King said the cabinet's complaint was that León spent project funds before President Kurtz or EVP Finch consented, that he had done so after Kurtz conditioned permission on Bill 22-23-S first passing, and that he pushed PR Director Preston Romanov to promote Neurodiversity Week on SGA social media before the funding bill passed, effectively forcing the Senate's hand. León said the matter was not personal and that he would explain more at the hearing. The Executive Cabinet, excluding León, asked for a censure; the hearing was set for Feb. 7.

events.title: Rally trip to Frankfort, new voucher and cleanup plans
events.body: Kurtz previewed a senate trip to Frankfort for the Rally for Higher Education, where SGA planned to meet state Rep. Kevin Jackson and other Kentucky campus governments, and urged senators to seek re-election to preserve institutional knowledge. Chief of Staff Donté Reed introduced a need-based scholarship awarding four Uber vouchers and the Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen. Campus Improvements and Sustainability chair Rush Robinson moved Earth Day from April 22 to April 19 and set a tentative Bowling Green cleanup for March 28.

events.title: SGA closed the year with a Red Wave tailgate
events.body: SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for the school year's last tailgate before a baseball game against Louisville, featuring winners of a "Battle of the DJs" social-media poll; sophomore Wilson Patterson won the $500 top scholarship prize as "DJ WLZN." Kurtz called the crowd to "savor one last tailgate of the 2023-2024 school year," with SGA grilling food for attendees.

events.title: Spring general election opened with over 60 candidates
events.body: Voting for the spring 2024 general election opened on TopNet with more than 60 students on the ballot for legislative seats. Kurtz, Chief of Staff Donté Reed and junior senator Ethan Taylor ran unopposed for student body president, executive vice president and administrative vice president respectively; the legislative council ballot included three senior, three junior and three sophomore senator seats, six college seats, an ISEC senator, a first-generation senator, a transfer/non-traditional senator and 14 senator-at-large seats.

events.title: Senate rejects Shark Tank grant fund, funds Pride table
events.body: Senators voted 3-21 against Bill 2-23-F, which would have taken $750 from the legislative discretionary budget for grants at a Student Activities "Shark Tank" pitch event. The same meeting passed Bill 3-23-F, spending $30 to sponsor an SGA table at Bowling Green Pride on Oct. 21, by 21-0 with three abstentions.

events.title: Caboni takes senator questions on election day access and buildings
events.body: President Timothy Caboni told the ninth meeting of the 23rd Senate that WKU would use the Historic Railpark's BG Trolley to carry students to State Street polling places on a class day. He also outlined plans to replace Hugh Poland, Douglas Keen and Grise halls and to build a fieldhouse and a new Gordon Ford building. Senators questioned him on accessibility ramps, sustainability partnerships and Living Learning Communities.

events.title: Senate spends $10,000 in organizational aid on 20 groups
events.body: Bill 5-23-F, written by Administrative Vice President Salvador Leon, split $10,000 among 20 registered student organizations at $500 each, including Black Women of Western, WKU Mock Trial, HOLAS and Best Buddies. The meeting also passed a constitutional amendment fixing the title of the Intercultural Student Engagement senator, $120 for World Kindness Day tabling and $600 for a Veterans Day 5K at Kereiakes Park. All four measures passed unanimously.

events.title: Resolution asks WKU to move fire drills from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m.
events.body: Resolution 6-23-F, created by the Mental Health and Wellness Committee, put SGA behind changing residence hall fire drill times from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. The committee argued the 5 a.m. time caused sleep problems and anxiety for students with early schedules, accommodations or emotional support animals. Authors were Geoffrey Aberle, Sophia Bryant and Callison Padgett, and the resolution passed unanimously.

events.title: Eight bills create Honors senate seat and set Judicial Council office hours
events.body: The final fall meeting passed all eight measures unanimously, including the bill creating a Mahurin Honors College senator seat, sponsored by the Judicial Council and written by Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson with MHC student Audrey Clark. Another raised the chief justice's required office hours from one to five per week, and a third required Judicial Council members to keep two office hours monthly. Leon reported the Senate had spent $1,347.63 of its $9,750 legislative discretionary budget, about 14.87%. The Herald numbered these bills 14-23-F, 13-23-F and 16-23-F; the versions SGA later posted carry the numbers 13-23-F and 12-23-F for the first two.

events.title: Senate backs a $5 per semester sustainability fee
events.body: Resolution 26-23-S, written by Sophomore Senator Rush Robinson, put SGA behind charging students a $5 sustainability fee each semester with the proceeds going to the Office of Sustainability. Robinson also authored Bill 25-23-S, giving that office $500 from the legislative discretionary budget for the food pantry, scholarships and an Earth Day event. Both passed unanimously.

events.title: Borrow-a-Calculator program created after student survey
events.body: Bill 2923-S set up a program letting students check out TI-84 calculators from the SGA office for a week at a time. Authors Kaison Barton and Donte Reed cited a survey finding 17% of students surveyed owned no calculator and 93% had taken a class requiring one. Assistant Provost Marko Dumancic spoke for the bill and said the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning would fund 10 more calculators, bringing the total to 15. The Senate also passed Resolution 2132-S seeking awnings or benches at Topper Transit stops.

events.title: Student group confronts SGA over silence on Rittenhouse visit
events.body: Avery Wells and members of the student advocacy group "For the People" told the Senate that SGA was the only major organization not to oppose Turning Point USA bringing Kyle Rittenhouse to campus, and called the response they got from the executive board unacceptable. Wells also said 40% of the Senate belonged to Greek life and that SGA had a disconnect with cultural communities on campus. Kurtz replied that as an apolitical organization SGA's role was to ensure all voices could be heard, and said he did not control who chose to run. Senators voted the same night on 13 constitutional amendments, including renaming the executive posts, raising senate and cabinet GPA floors to 2.5 and 2.75, and allowing removal from office after two censures in one year.

events.title: Every executive candidate runs unopposed at spring town hall
events.body: At an Executive Town Hall in the senate chambers, Chief Justice Isaac King questioned the three executive candidates, all of whom were unopposed: Kurtz for student body president, Donte Reed for executive vice president and Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president. Kurtz said the ticket intended to create more voucher programs modeled on the February Uber vouchers and to keep grilling at SGA events for students who were food insecure. Reed said students did not have to be in SGA to write a bill or resolution.

events.title: 24th Senate opens with Vincent as speaker and Henderson as chief justice
events.body: Sarah Vincent defeated Sophia Bryant for Speaker of the Senate at the first meeting of the 24th Senate. Anne-Marie Wright was appointed chief of staff and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed chief justice, all sworn in by outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King. Kurtz announced the Chief Communications Officer post, formerly Director of Public Relations, was open.

events.title: Pink Walk held with Panhellenic and the Interfraternity Council
events.body: SGA, the Panhellenic Society and the Interfraternity Council together held the Pink Walk on 5 October 2023, a guest-speaker event honouring those affected by breast cancer. The first bill passed by the 23rd Senate, on 20 September, had funded it. The walk became an annual SGA fixture, repeated in October 2024.

events.title: Abby Nash Creativity Scholarship opened
events.body: SGA opened the Abby Nash Creativity Scholarship in March 2024, honouring a senior graphic design and marketing major who died on 13 December 2023. It gave two students $500 each, aimed at those in creative departments such as art and design, marketing, English, media and communication, music and theatre and dance, though anyone could apply. Authored by CEBS senator Kayla Distler with Jack McCoun and Mckenna Fleshman, it was non-renewable unless a later senate wrote a bill to change it.

events.title: DEI Week ran a different theme every day
events.body: Bill 34-23-S allocated $150 from the legislative discretionary budget for SGA's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Week from 25 to 28 March 2024, with a themed tabling initiative each day. Mental Health Matters on 25 March brought Humane Society dogs and Talley Family Counseling Center material; Multicultural Day followed on 26 March with a prize wheel on campus demographics; Safe Sexual Health on 27 March was run with Health Education and Promotion and handed out free HIV testing information; and 28 March covered deaf awareness and hearing education.

events.title: Two hundred dollars for a book drive and a raffle basket
events.body: Bill 55-23-S passed unanimously on 11 April 2024, allocating $200 from the legislative discretionary budget for a book drive collecting donations in the SGA office and at tabling events from 15 to 26 April for local schools and programmes. Fifty dollars of that funded a "book lovers" raffle basket of books, pens and snacks to encourage donations, with raffle tickets given for each book donated.

events.title: First bill of the 23rd Senate funded the Pink Walk
events.body: At its fifth meeting the 23rd Senate passed its first piece of legislation, Bill 1-23-F, allocating $500 from SGA's scholarship budget to the SGA Pink Walk, an October breast cancer awareness event for students and the Bowling Green community. The money covered bracelets, ribbons, water and raffle prizes. The bill was written by Donte Reed, Rush Robinson and Anne-Marie Wright and passed unanimously, 28-0.

events.title: SGA launched an Uber voucher program and moved against parking fees
events.body: President Sam Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, given out through weekly social media giveaways, senate meeting attendance, SGA events and need-based scholarships. Resolution 18-23-S, written by Speaker of the Senate Sydney Denney and Reed, put SGA on record supporting a $50 cap on student parking fees, noting citations ranged from $10 to $600. Bill 19-23-S set aside $700 from the legislative discretionary budget to pay citations for financially vulnerable students, excluding tickets for disability, safety zone or fire lane violations. Bill 23-23-S allocated a further $1,045 for Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center vouchers, and all the legislation passed unanimously.

events.title: Kurtz seated a five-member Judicial Council and seven committee heads
events.body: At SGA's first meeting of the fall semester, the senate approved President Sam Kurtz's nominations of Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the 2023-24 Judicial Council. Kurtz said a record number of students had applied and were interviewed over the summer before the field was narrowed to five. He also announced seven committee heads, among them Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. The new appointees took the oath of office at the meeting.

events.title: Four bills fund a month of events, and one of them takes a fight
events.body: At the 23rd Senate's twentieth meeting, on 12 March 2024, four funding bills passed. Bill 34-23-S gave $150 to an SGA Diversity, Equity and Inclusion week of tabling from 25 to 28 March, a different initiative each day: mental health, campus demographics, safe sexual health, and deaf awareness. Bill 35-23-S gave $450 to an SGA Spring Fling on the South Lawn, a cookout with kickball and cornhole tournaments and raffles for Uber vouchers, its proceeds going to the Kids Cancer Alliance; after debate among senators over the amount it passed 28-2, the only bill of the four not carried unanimously. Bill 36-23-S gave $280 to a Hope Harbor Denim Day event on sexual assault awareness and Bill 38-23-S gave $650 to the annual Mental Health Week in April.

src.label: Herald, 13 Mar 2024 - SGA passes 4 bills to fund upcoming events

events.title: The Chief Justice's Verdict Award, a new monthly honour
events.body: At the eighth meeting of the 23rd Senate on 18 October 2023, Chief Justice Isaac King presented the September Chief Justice's Verdict Award to Senator-at-Large Karley Solorzano, who was in her first year as a senator and as head of the diversity, equity and inclusion committee. King had created the award that year, alongside a requirement that senators log office hours and encouragement to attend tabling events, as a way of getting the Judicial Council more involved in the day-to-day life of SGA. He described the council as SGA's supreme court, taking complaints about senators and executives and interpreting the constitution. The August award had gone to Ogden College senator Madison Payne.

src.label: Herald, 19 Oct 2023 - "SGA announces September Chief Justice's Verdict Award"

events.title: A Veterans Day 5K at Kereiakes Park
events.body: Bill 7-23-F allocated $600 from the legislative discretionary fund for a Veterans Day 5K at Kereiakes Park on 15 November 2023 from 5 to 7 p.m., with donations collected through a raffle for veterans and WKU's ROTC programme. The money covered decorations, cookout supplies, Veterans Day merchandise for the runners and a ninth-generation iPad as the raffle prize. Attending counted for two office hours for SGA senators. The bill was read twice on 7 November 2023; the posted form leaves the vote line blank.

events.title: Fourteen constitutional amendments were read together
events.body: On 12 March 2024 the Senate gave a first reading to a fourteen-bill package, Bills 19-24-S through 32-24-S, drafted by a constitutional referendum committee and sponsored by the Legislative Operations Committee and the Judicial Council. At the second reading on 28 March, thirteen of the fourteen passed both the Senate and the Executive Cabinet: they abolished the directorships of information technology and enrollment and student experience, renamed the Executive Vice President and Administrative Vice President as Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, raised the grade point average floors to 2.75 for the executive branch and 2.5 for the legislative and judicial branches, required removal after a second censure in a year, required documented executive spending, and moved committee-head appointments to the Speaker. A fourteenth bill, binding the Legislative Operations Committee to certify bills as nonpartisan, was tabled at that reading; the same language later appears in the current constitution.

events.title: Constitutional Referendum Committee began work
events.body: Chief Justice Isaac King told the council the Constitutional Referendum Committee would start on 14 February 2024 at 7pm. By 13 March the committee had written twelve bills, to be presented after spring break. The package that reached the Senate raised grade point floors, retitled the executive offices, required removal after a second censure in one year, and required a chief justice to be eligible to serve a full academic year.

events.title: Senate lowers the bar for changing its own constitution
events.body: Bill 22-24-S, one of the package given a second reading on 28 March 2024, amended clause 10.1 so that the constitution may be amended by a two-thirds vote of the present senators rather than of the full membership of the Senate. The bill stated that the old rule limited amendment votes to meetings at which at least two-thirds of the full Senate were in attendance. Bill 23-24-S, passed the same night, moved constitutional amendment elections from the end of the fall and spring semesters to the fall and spring senator elections, citing higher turnout in representative elections.

profile: King was appointed to the Judicial Council on 30 August 2022 by unanimous voice vote, one of two new justices seated that night alongside Garrett Baum. Chief Justice Justin Goins had nominated him associate chief justice by late January 2023.

King became chief justice for 2023-24. That November he authored Bill 12-23-F, which raised the chief justice's required weekly office hours from one to five; the bill called the office the constitution's designated interpreter and said a single required hour made it too hard to reach. In February 2024 the Executive Cabinet accused Administrative Vice President Salvador León of spending project funds before a funding bill had passed, despite President Kurtz's having conditioned his permission on waiting for the bill's passage, and of pressuring the public relations director to promote an event ahead of that vote. King explained the complaints to the Senate and announced a censure hearing for 7 February; the Judicial Council censured León 6-0 with no further discipline.
King's term ended on 23 April 2024, when he swore in the new 24th Senate's officers, including his successor as chief justice, Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson.

She was a recurring co-author that spring, alongside Senator at Large Joel Hornback, on the fourteen-bill package rewriting large sections of the constitution that the Senate read together on 12 March 2024; thirteen of the fourteen passed at the second reading on 28 March. She also co-authored the bill funding SGA's spring 2024 Organizational Aid round with Administrative Vice President Salvador Leon Golib and others.

profile: Jaden Marshall served as a senator at large in SGA's 23rd Senate in 2023-24, co-authoring, with Administrative Vice President Salvador Leon and others, the bill funding Neurodiversity Acceptance Week. He returned to the Senate for 2024-25, reappointed to a senator-at-large seat and confirmed by unanimous voice vote on 11 February 2025, and again for 2025-26 as an ISEC senator (Intercultural Student Engagement Center), where he co-authored a bill funding the Go With the Flow menstrual-product program together with a WKU Food Pantry donation drive, a Black History Trivia Night held with Why Knot Us and Black Women of Western, graduation cords for transfer students, and resolutions supporting the installation of drinking-water dispensers, printers and computers in residence halls and an accessible 24-hour space on campus.

In April 2026 Marshall ran for SGA president on a ticket with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude, against Caden Lucas, Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry, taking questions at a town hall in the DSU auditorium. On 13 April 2026 the Judicial Council, acting on its own initiative rather than a complaint, found the Marshall ticket guilty 4-0 of breaching the election code's ban on distributing perishable food within 48 hours of an election, after Red Bull cans were handed out at their campaign table and photographed for their campaign's social media story; the council issued a formal censure but declined to remove the ticket from the ballot. Two days later, on 15 April 2026, the council found the same ticket guilty 5-0 on a separate, unrelated complaint of campaigning in the Commons while voting was open; it censured and disbanded the ticket's campaign team rather than issuing a second censure to the ticket itself. Lucas's ticket won the election, with turnout up 66 percent over the previous year's uncontested race. Marshall was sworn into a new role at the first meeting of the 26th Senate on 28 April 2026, alongside Gabby Pace, Cayden Bailey and Maggie Phelps.

members.name: Geoffrey Aberle
profile: Aberle served as the Transfer/Non-traditional Senator in 2023-24. He co-authored, with Sophia Bryant and Callison Padgett, Resolution 1-23-F, asking the university to move residence-hall fire drills from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. The WKU archive files the measure under that number, but the Herald's report of the 14 November 2023 meeting — describing an identical measure with the same three authors, passed unanimously — calls it Resolution 6-23-F; the numbering discrepancy between the two records is unresolved. He was also one of six co-authors, with David Darnell, Thomas Pabin, Callison Padgett, ShyAnte Williams and Sophia Bryant, of Bill 6-23-F, allocating $120 for a National Kindness Day tabling event on 13 November 2023 offering coffee, hot chocolate and donuts.

members.name: Kaison Barton
profile: Barton served as a Senior Senator in 2023-24 and continued as a Senator at Large in 2024-25. In February 2024 he was one of five co-authors — with Jaden Marshall, Joel Hornback, Kayla Distler and Salvador Leon — of Bill 4-24-S, funding a Neurodiversity Acceptance Week that ran 6 to 9 February. He and co-author Donte Reed then authored Bill 9-24-S, creating the Borrow-a-Calculator program letting students check out TI-84 calculators from the SGA office; they cited a survey finding 17 percent of students owned no calculator while 93 percent had taken a class requiring one, and the bill drew matching university funding for ten more calculators.

In February 2025 he presented, alongside Alexandria Chumbley, the bill funding the Steven "Brent" Chumbley Student-Athlete Impact Scholarship, named for WKU's director of cross country and track and field, who had died weeks earlier; the Senate allocated $500 after Legislative Operations chair Caden Lucas resisted a motion to raise the figure to $1,000, calling it rash given what remained in the discretionary budget.

members.name: Samantha Bodemann
profile: Bodemann served as a Senior Senator in the 23rd Senate, 2023-24. In November 2023 she was one of four co-authors — with Legislative Operations Committee chair Meghan Pierce, Hannah Evans and Joel Hornback — of two of the committee's bills correcting SGA's governing documents: Bill 8-23-F, rewriting the constitution's description of the Executive Vice President's power to make University Senate appointments, and Bill 9-23-F, reconciling the bylaws' language on committee-chair removal and senator expulsion with a constitution that provided only for impeachment.

In March 2024 she was one of seven co-authors — with Ellen Henderson, Garrison Reed, Hannah Evans, Isaac King, Joel Hornback and Meghan Pierce — of the fourteen-bill constitutional amendment package, written after SGA anticipated university budget cuts. Thirteen of the fourteen bills passed the Senate and Executive Cabinet at the 28 March second reading, abolishing the directorships of information technology and enrollment and student experience, renaming the Executive Vice President and Administrative Vice President as Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, raising GPA floors for all three branches, requiring removal after a second censure in a year, and moving committee-head appointments to the Speaker.

leaders.name: Sam Kurtz
leaders.note: Re-elected unopposed. Warned the Senate repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber meant the 2025 election mattered more than usual.
profile: Kurtz opened the 2024-25 year presiding over the 24th Senate, which passed SGA's $100,000 budget at its first meeting on Aug. 27. Sitting down with the Herald editorial board alongside his executive cabinet, he described SGA as "a vessel for good" and a group of 45 to 50 people advocating for students, and credited President Caboni with keeping the budget untouched for several years.

Through the spring he presided over a run of student-welfare legislation, including the Gordon Wilson Hall elevator resolution and a resolution seeking 24/7 library hours during finals week. In February he announced a POLLapalooza push to raise election participation, telling the Senate, "My goal is that 3,000 students vote in our election."

Kurtz closed his term at the 24th Senate's final meeting on April 15, having served as student body president for two years and holding executive branch positions for most of his college career, and prepared to graduate at the end of the semester. He received a standing ovation after his last report, and his parting words to senators were "Please be for the students."

events.title: A mental health survey, and a warning about the election
events.body: The Senate passed Bill 4-25-S funding a DEI Committee tabling event to gather anonymous mental health survey responses. Dean of Students Martha Sales told the Senate 'you cannot isolate and educate at the same time'. Kurtz warned repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber made the spring election matter more than usual.

events.title: Rush Robinson elected on a turnout of 966
events.body: Elected alongside class, college, transfer, first-generation, Intercultural Student Engagement Center and Honors College senators - constituencies the 1966 constitution had no concept of.

events.title: Fall election winners sworn in, school safety bill passed
events.body: Five senators elected in the fall election, three freshman senators plus an international and a Gatton Academy senator, were sworn in at the Oct. 1 meeting. The Senate passed three bills, including Bill 4-24-F to make school safety training mandatory for WKU professors and require posted emergency exits in classrooms, and two bills backing a Spooktober fundraiser for the Potter Children's Home Initiative.

events.title: Three senators removed for excessive absences
events.body: Senators Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty were removed from their seats at a Nov. 6 censure meeting after each accumulated at least six unexcused absences from weekly senate meetings. The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove them under a constitutional provision requiring removal of any senator censured twice, calling the decision a matter of accountability rather than an attack on character.

events.title: Chief justice says the SGA constitution may need a DEI amendment
events.body: Chief Justice Morgan Gammons told the Herald after the weekly meeting that the SGA Constitution's diversity, equity and inclusion provisions might need amending after President Donald Trump's Jan. 20 executive order directing federal agencies to end DEI mandates. Gammons said the Judicial Council would meet to decide whether to send a constitutional referendum to the Senate, noting that WKU receives federal funding as a public university and had to reevaluate. At the same meeting four senators were appointed to new positions and Gavin Grawe was voted associate chief justice.

events.title: Resolution backed Gordon Wilson Hall elevator
events.body: The Senate passed Resolution 2-25-S supporting installation of elevators in Gordon Wilson Hall, prompted by wheelchair user Kiersten Washington, whose dance appreciation class was scheduled on the building's third floor. It also passed Resolution 1-25-S supporting 24/7 hours at The Commons at Helm Library during finals week, and Kurtz announced a POLLapalooza effort with a goal of 3,000 voters in the April election.

events.title: Resolution supported mental health advisory board
events.body: The Senate passed Resolution 4-25-S supporting the formation of a Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Advisory Board to advise upper-level administration on student mental health policy, with Dean of Students Martha Sales planned to oversee its creation. Co-author Emma Harris, the Resident Staff Association president, said Counseling Center staffing shortages had pushed students to rely on resident advisors. The Senate passed eight bills at the same meeting.

events.title: Students ratified the DEI committee amendment with 88% of the vote
events.body: In the spring election the student body approved Bill 21-25-S, the constitutional amendment renaming the DEI Committee the Action and Opportunity Committee, with 88% of votes in favour. Committee chair Megan Farmer said the committee at its core was not changing and that the new name better communicated its actions. Rush Robinson was elected student body president unopposed on a ticket with Savanna Kurtz and Gabriel Jerdon, and results for 31 senate seats were announced the same night.

events.title: The 24th Senate held its final meeting
events.body: The 24th Senate met for the last time on April 15 with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on farewells. Student Experience Officer Savanna Kurtz reported 295 scholarship applications in the spring semester alone, against an average of about 40 in past years. President Sam Kurtz, Vice President Donte Reed and Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor each received a standing ovation after their final reports.

events.title: 24th Senate installed: Vincent elected speaker, Henderson named chief justice
events.body: At the 24th Senate's first meeting, newly elected senators were sworn in and Sarah Vincent, College of Health and Human Services senator, was elected Speaker of the Senate over Sophia Bryant. Senior senator Anne-Marie Wright was appointed Chief of Staff, and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed Chief Justice. Outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King swore in the new officers, officially opening the 2024-25 term.

events.title: Committee chairs and Judicial Council approved at fall opener
events.body: At the 24th Senate's first fall meeting, the Senate unanimously approved Kurtz's nominations of Aziz Umarov, Madison Payne, Neill Kane and Sam Dorris to the 2024-25 Judicial Council, and confirmed six committee chairs: Hannah Evans (Legislative Operations), Savanna Kurtz (Student Experience and Enrollment), Ryan Dilts (Outreach and Public Relations), Megan Farmer (DEI), Sophia Bryant (Student Mental Health and Wellbeing) and Annie Finch (Community Relations). President Timothy Caboni addressed the Senate on campus building renovations, the Mahurin Honors College restructuring and WKU's push for R2 research status.

events.title: Student regent presses administrators over student worker funding
events.body: At the Board of Regents retreat, Student Regent Sam Kurtz said a friend working in the biotechnology center had been told some 2023 funding for student jobs would not return in 2024. Kurtz raised the concern during a budget model presentation as units across WKU were being ordered to cut 7.5% of their approved spending and absorb a 10% overhead charge on self-generated revenue. He asked the room, "Isn't that the point of why we're all here, to look out for the students?" and afterwards told the Herald the answers he got were cookie-cutter.

events.title: 24th Senate approves $100,000 budget and seats first Honors senator
events.body: The Senate unanimously approved Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor's $100,000 budget, which raised legislative discretionary and office worker spending and cut public relations spending. Five senators were appointed, including Caden Lucas as the first Mahurin Honors College senator. Caboni gave the university report and closed on meal plans, saying orange chicken had become a meal swipe.

events.title: Executives break down the SGA budget for the Herald editorial board
events.body: Taylor told the Herald Editorial Board the 2024-25 budget included $20,000 for organizational aid, $23,500 for scholarships and $10,705 in legislative discretionary funding. Kurtz said the total had stayed at $100,000 for several years and credited Caboni with keeping it untouched. Taylor and Vice President Donte Reed both said they meant to spend the whole allocation. Chief Justice Ellen Henderson said the Senate would vote on election codes at its Sept. 3 meeting and stressed the Judicial Council's independence from the Senate and cabinet.

events.title: Senate passes bill declaring SGA nonpartisan
events.body: Bill 50-23-S reaffirmed that SGA represents the student body rather than acting as a political group and stated its duty to put forward only nonpartisan legislation. It passed unanimously. The same meeting named Rush Robinson chair of the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee, swore in Hadley Whipple as Secretary of the Senate and added Hailey Stapleton to the Judicial Council.

events.title: Vice president pushes for an on-campus polling place
events.body: Student Body Vice President Donte Reed told the Senate he was working with a student advocacy group to get a polling center on campus, saying he otherwise had to drive about three hours home to vote. Kurtz said SGA should find ways to calm tensions after the November election and remind students where to get help. Dean of Students Martha Sales spoke on stress and belonging and told senators to check on their strong friends.

events.title: Fall ballot draws 20 freshman candidates and none for graduate seat
events.body: Chief Justice Ellen Henderson reported that 20 students were running for freshman senator, one for Gatton Academy senator, one for international senator and none for graduate senator, with voting set for Sept. 26 and 27 on TopNet. The Senate also passed Resolutions 1-24-F and 2-24-F backing a semester-long fundraising drive to raise $2,000 for Potter Children's Home, beginning with a Jump Air Zone event where 40% of proceeds would go to the fund. Both resolutions were written by sophomore senator Jade Ismail and passed unanimously, committing SGA to four fundraisers, one in September, two in October and one in December, each carrying a QR code pointing students at a GoFundMe. Resolution 2-24-F set out Soarin' in September at Jump Air Zone on Wednesday 25 September from 8 to 10 p.m., a $10 entry covering the two hours and socks, with every participant signing a liability waiver.

events.title: Bill seeks mandatory school safety training for professors
events.body: Bill 4-24-F, authored by Senator Annalise Finch, called for school safety training to be made mandatory for all WKU professors and for emergency exits to be posted in every instructional classroom. Finch noted the training was not then mandatory and that K-12 rules do not transfer directly to college. Professors would be able to opt out for mental health reasons. The bill passed, and five senators elected in the fall race were sworn in.

events.title: Three senators removed from the Senate after second censure
events.body: The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty for excessive unexcused absences, each having accumulated at least six. Section 2.2 of the bylaws allows three unexcused absences a semester, and Section 4.6.12 of the constitution requires removal after a second censure; all three had already been censured once and given extra office hours. The council's minutes said senators cannot represent students they are not present to serve. Petty later told the Herald her absences were due to medical issues.

events.title: Senate funds food pantry and swears in a new chief justice
events.body: Bill 17-24-F gave $500 to the Office of Sustainability to restock its food and resource pantry, with Director of Sustainability Leslie North telling senators the office had given away 16,000 items the previous semester. Bill 16-24-F funded 40 Fresh Food Company meal vouchers for the Dean of Students office, and two more bills funded a finals week tabling event and a Boys and Girls Club toy drive. Chief Justice Ellen Henderson swore in Associate Chief Justice Morgan Gammons as chief justice before graduating.

events.title: Heat press bill revived after failing in the fall
events.body: Bill 19-24-F, allocating $240 for a heat press for the Fashion Merchandising Department, passed unanimously after failing at the last meeting of the fall semester and being carried over. Author Jenna Wells said the department had overspent in the past and lacked excess funds. Kurtz said several senators had resigned over the break and Judicial Council members had graduated, requiring him to make appointments, and he pressed senators to build the coming election.

events.title: Senate backs Gordon Wilson elevator and a 24-hour finals study space
events.body: Resolution 2-25-S, written by wheelchair user and honorary SGA member Kiersten Washington, supported installing an elevator in Gordon Wilson Hall after she was scheduled for a third-floor class in a 1927 building with no elevator. DEI Chair Megan Farmer said students cannot get the full range of an education if they cannot enter the space. Resolution 1-25-S, by senators Jakob Barker and Cayden Bailey, sought 24-hour hours at the Commons at Helm Library during finals week, noting WKU offers no 24-hour student space.

events.title: Faculty Senate endorses two SGA resolutions
events.body: The Faculty Senate voted to endorse SGA Resolution 2-25-S on the Gordon Wilson Hall elevator and Resolution X-22-S on extending Commons at Helm Library hours during finals week. The library resolution recorded Dean of WKU Libraries Joshua Vossler's position that staffing made 24-hour service unworkable and that student use would not justify the cost, so the Faculty Senate endorsed finding an alternative 24-hour space instead. Senate Chair Gordon McKerral said Provost Bud Fischer told them the elevator was already a top priority.

events.title: Whipple elected speaker as the 25th Senate convenes
events.body: Hadley Whipple won the Speaker of the Senate vote over Caden Lucas and Sophia Bryant at the first meeting of the 25th Senate. President Rush Robinson appointed Maggie Yelton chief of staff and Amelia Tucker senator-at-large, and Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins kept his post for a second year. Former Speaker Sarah Vincent swore in the new Senate.

events.title: Gordon Wilson elevator scheduled for construction
events.body: Chief Facilities Officer Bryan Russell told the Herald that Facilities Management and Planning, Design and Construction would jointly install an elevator in Gordon Wilson Hall, with a project goal of starting construction in fiscal 2026. The project followed Washington's February resolution and the Faculty Senate's April endorsement. Russell also said two Cravens Library elevators would be modernized, the first finishing in September and the second in December.

events.title: Robinson reappoints Jenkins chief communications officer
events.body: In one of his first acts after taking office, Robinson reappointed Preston Jenkins as chief communications officer; the Senate later confirmed the pick unanimously.

events.title: Borrow-A-Calculator went live
events.body: Chief of Staff Anne-Marie Wright told the senate on 3 September 2024 that the Borrow-A-Calculator programme had started, run with the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning, the Department of Mathematics and Ogden College. Students could borrow a new TI-84 graphing calculator free for one week and renew it, on presentation of a valid student ID.

src.label: Herald, 3 Sep 2024 - "SGA passes bill, details Borrow-A-Calculator program"

events.title: Hill-O-Ween drew just over a hundred students
events.body: SGA held Hill-O-Ween at Centennial Mall on 29 October 2024, handing out sweets and running activities with the Hilltopper Organization of Latin American Students and the Accessibility Ambassadors. Students painted succulent pots and made candy apples. Junior senator Rush Robinson, who organised it, counted just over 100 people. At the meeting that evening the senate allocated $325 for a Pack the Pantry food drive run with WKU ROTC through November.
events.money: $325 for the Pack the Pantry food drive

src.label: Herald, 29 Oct 2024 - "SGA hosts 'Hill-O-Ween', passes new bills to fund future events"

events.title: First Topper Chef cooking class
events.body: SGA held the first Topper Chef cooking class on 4 November 2024 in Academic Complex room 202, where students cooked pork and vegetable tacos, beans, elotes and guacamole from 4 p.m. and ate together until 7:30. Senior Jenna Wells pitched it from her seat on the Student Mental Health and Well-being Committee, saying students needed to look after themselves outside the classroom and that basic cooking and cooking safety were useful skills. She cited a grease fire in Pearce-Ford Tower the previous year.

src.label: Herald, 5 Nov 2024 - "SGA hosts 'Topper Chef' cooking class"

events.title: Second Veteran's Day 5K raised money for ROTC
events.body: SGA held its second annual Veteran's Day 5K at Kereiakes Park on 8 November 2024, with a $15 entry fee raising money for WKU's ROTC. Every entrant went into a raffle for an iPad, the first ten finishers got medals and hamburgers were grilled at the end. Senior senator and community relations head Annie Finch organised it and said the previous year's race raised about $2,000. ROTC member Rowen Wilkinson finished first.

src.label: Herald, 8 Nov 2024 - "SGA hosts second annual Veteran's Day 5K"

events.title: Giving Thanks November closed a term of Potter Children's Home fundraising
events.body: The senate passed Bill 15-24-F allocating $374 for Giving Thanks November, held in the Downing Student Union lobby from 3 to 6 p.m. on 20 November 2024 with the Zeta Epsilon chapter of Pi Kappa Alpha. SGA laid on cupcakes, lemonade and Panera, and ran raffles for a ninth-generation iPad at $10 a ticket and a Spencer's Coffee basket at $5, or $12 for both. It was the last of the term's fundraisers for the Potter Children's Home Initiative; the earlier one, SGA Spooktober, had been a Halloween film screening whose ticket revenue went to the same cause.

src.label: Herald, 13 Nov 2024 - "SGA passes bill for Potter Children's Home fundraising event"

events.title: Scholarship created in memory of Brent Chumbley
events.body: On 18 February 2025 the senate allocated $500 to the Steven "Brent" Chumbley Student-Athlete Impact Scholarship, named for WKU's director of cross country and track and field, who died on 30 January. Senator Kaison Barton presented the bill alongside Chumbley's daughter Alexandria and said the scholarship would continue his work with students who gave significant time to sport. A motion to raise the figure to $1,000 was resisted by Legislative Operations chair Caden Lucas, who called it rash given what was left in the discretionary budget.

src.label: Herald, 19 Feb 2025 - "SGA allocates funds to scholarship honoring the late Brent Chumbley"

events.title: Gregory McKinney Black History Month scholarship awarded
events.body: Vice President Donte Reed presented the Gregory McKinney Leadership and Involvement Black History Month Scholarship to Summer Doris and Kyanna Edmonds at the meeting of 11 March 2025. The award goes to an African American student showing leadership through campus or community involvement, and carries the name of WKU's first African American student regent. The same meeting amended Bill 6-25-S to grant $350 for a live musical performance at that year's AfroLatinidad event.

src.label: Herald, 12 Mar 2025 - "SGA awards scholarship, passes bills to fund upcoming events"

events.title: Senate backed a Myanmar flag, distributed $10,000 in organizational aid and funded more calculators
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Resolution 5-24-F, authored by Senator Van Zing, supporting a Myanmar flag on the empty pole outside the Mahurin Honors College after students said Burmese and Chin students had no flag representing them. Bill 9-24-F distributed the fall organizational aid budget of $10,000 to registered student organizations graded from 58 applications, with a $500 annual cap per group. Bill 10-24-F added $540 to buy five more calculators for the Borrow-a-Calculator program, which had lent 28 calculators that semester. Kurtz appointed freshman Emaun Riley as ISEC senator and Mahurin Honors College senator Caden Lucas as the senate's parliamentarian.

events.title: Senate renamed the DEI Committee the Action and Opportunity Committee
events.body: Senators unanimously passed Bill 21-25-S, a constitutional amendment restructuring the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee as the Action and Opportunity Committee and retitling Chief Diversity Officers as Chief Engagement and Opportunity Officers, following President Trump's executive order dismantling DEI mandates. Rush Robinson moved to table the bill to the fall, but senators chose to vote; with fewer than the 21 members needed for a two-thirds vote present, absent members were called onto Zoom to reach quorum. Co-author Gammons called the change mostly a formality and said a loss of federal funding had been alluded to as a possible issue. The amendment then went to a student referendum during the 13-15 April election.

events.title: The second Pink Walk drew survivors to South Lawn
events.body: SGA's second annual Pink Walk was held on the evening of 17 October 2024, created and hosted by Vice President Donte Reed with WKU Panhellenic, the Interfraternity Council and the National Pan-Hellenic Council, raising money for the Susan G. Komen Breast Cancer Foundation. Students gathered at the Big Red statue in Downing Student Union and walked along Centennial Mall to South Lawn, where SGA served burgers, snacks and drinks. Breast cancer survivors Michelle Denney and Robbin Taylor spoke, along with Tate Sine, whose mother Tonya had spoken at the previous year's walk after her diagnosis in September 2021.

src.label: Herald, 17 Oct 2024 - "Students walk for breast cancer awareness at SGA Pink Walk"

events.title: A fortnight-long toy drive with Student Activities
events.body: SGA ran a toy drive with Student Activities from 20 November to 3 December 2024 for the Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green, taking donations of toys for children aged 3 to 16 at the SGA and Student Activities desks in Downing Student Union. Bill 20-24-F, passed at the meeting of 19 November, put $200 towards additional toys. Donors earned one service hour per toy up to five. The bill was written by sophomore senator Savanna Kurtz, who had worked on the previous year's drive through the Community Relations Committee.

src.label: Herald, 26 Nov 2024 - "SGA collecting toy donations for Bowling Green Boys & Girls Club"

events.title: SGA Pollooza put a student music festival on South Lawn
events.body: SGA staged Pollooza, an all-day music festival on South Lawn, on Sunday 13 April 2025, with food trucks, tailgating and a bill of performers drawn entirely from current WKU students. The name folded the word polls into it because the spring election opened that night. Students were told to bring blankets, chairs and tents from about 3 p.m., tailgate rules applied so alcohol was allowed in a cup, five acts were billed from 3 p.m. to 8.30 p.m., and SGA said it would try to stream the final round of the Masters. The Herald's photographers covered the day.

src.label: Herald, 10 and 13 Apr 2025 - notice and "Photos: SGA Pollooza brings local music to South Lawn"

events.title: Council ruled a missed office hour counts as an unexcused absence
events.body: Under the heading of interpretation of the constitution and bylaws, the council decided that failure to complete office hours would be treated as an unexcused absence, so that two missed meetings and unfinished office hours amounted to three unexcused absences. Chief Justice Ellen Henderson had reported a large number of unsubmitted office hour forms and unexcused absences at the same meeting, and explained censure proceedings.

events.title: Council heard two candidates and nominated Blake Graham chief justice
events.body: After the spring elections the council heard speeches from two contenders for chief justice, deliberated and voted. Chief Justice Morgan Gammons recorded that the council would nominate Blake Graham for chief justice the following week, for confirmation by the Senate.

executive.name: Donté Reed
profile: Donte Reed was executive vice president of SGA for 2024-25, elected on Sam Kurtz's ticket in the spring 2024 election announced just after midnight on 17 April 2024, alongside administrative vice president Ethan Taylor.
In August 2024 he sat down with the Herald editorial board with the rest of the cabinet, saying SGA tried to use its roughly $100,000 budget in full to help as many students as possible.

executive.name: Ethan Taylor
executive.note: Listed as Administrative Vice President in the spring 2024 election results; called Chief Financial Officer in Herald coverage through the year.
profile: Ethan Taylor co-authored Bill 17-22-F, funding the Midnight on the Hill student organization, as a sophomore senator; the Senate passed it 28-0 on 8 November 2022. He ran for administrative vice president in the spring 2024 general election on a ticket with Sam Kurtz for student body president and Donté Reed for executive vice president, and all three ran unopposed. At an Executive Town Hall on 11 April 2024, Chief Justice Isaac King questioned the unopposed candidates about their plans; Kurtz said the ticket intended to create more voucher programs and keep grilling at SGA events for food-insecure students.

As chief financial officer for 2024-25, Taylor's $100,000 budget was approved unanimously by the 24th Senate at its first meeting on 27 August 2024; it raised legislative discretionary and office-worker spending and cut public relations spending. He, President Kurtz and Vice President Reed each received a standing ovation at the 24th Senate's final meeting on 15 April 2025.

executive.name: Anne-Marie Wright
executive.note: Appointed at the 24th Senate's first meeting, 23 April 2024.
profile: As a junior senator, Anne-Marie Wright co-wrote Bill 1-23-F with Donté Reed and Rush Robinson, funding the SGA Pink Walk breast cancer awareness event; it was the 23rd Senate's first piece of legislation, passing 28-0 on 20 September 2023. She was appointed chief of staff at the 24th Senate's first meeting on 23 April 2024, sworn in by outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King alongside newly elected Speaker Sarah Vincent and Chief Justice Ellen Henderson.

On 3 September 2024 Wright told the Senate the Borrow-a-Calculator programme had started, a partnership with the Center for Innovative Teaching and Learning, the Department of Mathematics and Ogden College letting students borrow a graphing calculator free for a week on presentation of a student ID.

executive.name: Preston Jenkins
executive.note: Appointed over the summer of 2024 on what Chief of Staff Wright described to the Senate as President Kurtz's executive decision, and welcomed at the first meeting of the year on 27 August 2024. He handled the fall election and Uber voucher graphics and the senators' t-shirt orders. He was reappointed in April 2025 and served a second year.

officers.note: Elected over Sophia Bryant at the 24th Senate's first meeting, 23 April 2024.
profile: Sarah Vincent, a College of Health and Human Services senator, was elected Speaker of the Senate over Sophia Bryant at the first meeting of the 24th Senate on 23 April 2024, when the newly elected senators were sworn in and Ellen Henderson was named chief justice.
A year later, at the first meeting of the 25th Senate on 22 April 2025, Vincent, by then the outgoing speaker, swore in the new Senate after Hadley Whipple was elected to succeed her.

officers.name: Ellen Henderson
officers.note: Appointed from Associate Chief Justice at the 24th Senate's first meeting, 23 April 2024; still Chief Justice as of the 27 August 2024 meeting.
profile: Chief Justice Isaac King nominated Henderson associate chief justice at the Senate's 5 September 2023 meeting; she told senators she was honored by the nomination and excited to be more involved in SGA, and was confirmed by unanimous voice vote.

At the 24th Senate's first meeting on 23 April 2024, the outgoing King swore Henderson in as chief justice, alongside newly elected Speaker Sarah Vincent and Chief of Staff Anne-Marie Wright. She continued in the role into the fall, swearing in the winners of the October 2024 senate election at the 1 October meeting, where the Senate also passed a bill requiring school safety training for WKU professors. On 19 November 2024, ahead of her graduation, Henderson swore in Associate Chief Justice Morgan Gammons as her successor.

officers.name: Morgan Gammons
officers.note: Serving as Chief Justice by the Senate's 4 February 2025 meeting; the Herald's coverage does not pin the exact date she succeeded Henderson.
profile: Morgan Gammons was one of five students — with Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson and Garrison Reed — nominated by President Sam Kurtz to the 2023-24 Judicial Council out of what Kurtz called a record field of applicants. She was serving as chief justice by SGA's 4 February 2025 senate meeting, though Herald coverage does not pin the exact date of her succession. That April she co-authored Bill 21-25-S, which restructured SGA's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee into the Action and Opportunity Committee and renamed Chief Diversity Officers to Chief Engagement and Opportunity Officers, telling the Herald the change followed President Trump's February 2025 executive order dismantling federal DEI mandates. She called the renaming "mostly a formality" and declined to say how it would affect WKU students, though she said the possibility of losing federal funding over resistance to the shift had been alluded to. The bill needed a two-thirds senate vote to pass as a constitutional amendment; when that week's meeting fell short of the 21 members required, absent senators were called in over Zoom so the vote could proceed, and it passed unanimously before going to a student referendum.

officers.name: Hadley Whipple
officers.note: The secretaryship was recorded vacant at the first meeting on 27 August 2024, Speaker Vincent asking anyone interested to text her. Whipple, confirmed as Ogden College senator at that same meeting, held the post by March 2025 and was elected Speaker of the 25th Senate the following month.

officers.name: Rush Robinson

profile: Jenna Wells was elected a freshman senator for 2021-22 as a Mahurin Honors College student majoring in strategic marketing. She told the Herald she wanted to represent the freshman class by listening to their concerns and reaching out intentionally to students she was not typically around.

She continued in the Senate as the Gordon Ford College of Business senator for 2022-23, co-sponsoring funding for the Midnight on the Hill organization and a bill amending the SGA constitution. By March 2025 she was chairing the Community Relations Committee, a post Annie Finch had originally been confirmed to on 27 August 2024. That January, as a senator, she authored Bill 19-24-F funding a heat press for the WKU Fashion Merchandising Department, which passed unanimously after being held over from the previous semester while she checked on the department's past spending.

The Herald reported her authoring a bill as Senator Caroline Yates on 11 November 2025, which confirms she held a Senate seat as a continuing member in a later year.
