leaders.name: Rush Robinson
leaders.note: Elected 13-15 April 2025 on a turnout of 966. Told the Faculty Senate to 'take a field trip' to see the state of WKU's residence halls. Handed his successor the red suit jacket on 28 April 2026.

sources.label: WKU News - Board of Regents, 8 Aug 2025

profile: Robinson, a senior from Benton, Kentucky triple-majoring in psychology, philosophy and sociology and a member of Sigma Phi Epsilon and Omicron Delta Kappa, won the SGA presidency in the 13-15 April 2025 general election on a turnout of 966, running with Savanna Kurtz for vice president and Gabriel Jerdon for chief financial officer. He also succeeded Sam Kurtz as WKU's student regent; the Board of Regents administered his oath of office on 8 August 2025, the same meeting at which it named the new Gordon Ford College of Business building Amy and David Chandler Hall and elected Jan West chair, Doris Thomas vice chair and Melissa Dennison secretary for 2025-26.

Robinson ran on turning SGA away from national politics and toward direct student advocacy, saying the organization had sometimes echoed national political talking points and that he wanted it to act as "an advocate and resource for students" who could be pointed to the right contact in the administration. His cabinet - Kurtz as vice president, Jerdon as chief financial officer, Maggie Yelton as chief of staff, and Preston Jenkins, reappointed chief communications officer on 22 April 2025 and confirmed by the Senate - ran a legislative program heavy on small, direct-benefit measures: vouchers for CPR certification, dental cleanings, transcripts and identification cards, equipment to borrow such as umbrellas, calculators and hammocks, and a resolution urging accessible restroom stalls in Grise Hall. Jenkins also organized a student-painted mural for a column in the SGA chambers. In March 2026 SGA drew on its projects fund to host a baseball-game tailgate, a response to Athletics Director Todd Stewart's call for more student engagement. The Senate closed its final meeting on 14 April 2026 having passed 56 bills for the year, the most since 2018-19, with Jenkins also reporting that a new university Artificial Intelligence Committee was weighing bulk AI-product subscriptions for students.

Robinson's most sustained policy push was on student mental health, working with Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Veronica Butler on a year-long program backed by data from social work professor Jay Gabbard, who told SGA that 44 percent of WKU students reported depression symptoms and 10 percent had considered suicide in the past year. SGA co-organized Mental Health Week with the WKU Counseling Center and the campus NAMI chapter, ran a Toppers Talk About It awareness campaign, and had student recommendations - including relocating counseling services from Potter Hall to the Downing Student Union - reviewed by the Counseling Center Review Committee before forwarding them to administrators, though Butler said it was unclear whether they would be enacted. The push closed with an Out of Darkness suicide-remembrance walk on 18 April 2026, and successor Caden Lucas said the focus would continue "in a sustained and meaningful way."

At the Senate's first meeting under his successor, Robinson opened by telling the mostly-new chamber they looked untainted by SGA's usual troubles, then handed president-elect Caden Lucas the red suit jacket passed president to president - the same jacket Sam Kurtz had given him the year before. His term as student regent outlasted his SGA presidency: at the Board of Regents' 5 June 2026 meeting, his last as regent, he cast the lone vote against a $204, 1.69 percent tuition increase, saying the board had "to do whatever we can to not raise the tuition" to preserve affordability. Afterward he planned to remain at WKU for an Ed.S. in school psychology, aiming for a career as a school psychologist in a school district.

events.title: Robinson sworn in as student regent, succeeding Kurtz
events.body: The Board of Regents administered Robinson's oath of office as student regent, succeeding graduating president Sam Kurtz. At the same meeting the board elected Jan West chair, Doris Thomas vice chair and Melissa Dennison secretary for 2025-26.

src.label: WKU News - Board of Regents, 8 Aug 2025

events.title: SGA commissioned a student-painted mural for the chambers
events.body: Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins announced a plan to have four student artists each paint one side of a column in the SGA chambers, incorporating WKU campus elements, with selections due by 19 September.

events.title: WKU Restaurant Group answered senators' questions
events.body: Restaurant Group representatives fielded senator questions on the removal of Steak 'n Shake seasoning, kiosks in Subway and adding spicy chicken sandwiches to Chick-fil-A's meal-swipe menu, and said the service handled about 60,000 meal transactions a week.

events.title: CPR-voucher bill and Grise Hall accessibility resolution passed
events.body: The senate unanimously passed Bill 2-26-S, funding six vouchers for free CPR certification through the Area Health Education Center's WKU CPR Training Center across the Heartsaver and Basic Life Support courses. Senator Amelia Tucker introduced the bill with a countdown timer and said the certifications, which the centre prices at $75 to $100, are required for some students' classes. Resolution 7-25-F, supporting additional handicapped-accessible restroom stalls in Grise Hall after a student's father said the building had only one large stall, also passed, and Chief of Staff Maggie Yelton reported that seven dental, one ID and 13 transcript vouchers remained.

events.title: Senate adopted a fully codified rewrite of its bylaws
events.body: The Senate adopted an official codified version of the SGA Executive and Legislative Bylaws, superseding all prior versions, effective 24 February 2026.

src.label: WKU SGA, Executive and Legislative Bylaws, as amended 24 Feb 2026

events.title: Senate learns the Gilbane housing partnership cleared the legislature
events.body: At its Thursday meeting SGA senators learned that the Kentucky Legislature had approved WKU's public-private partnership with developer Gilbane, which the Board of Regents had provisionally approved 11 December 2025 to design and build a new residence hall replacing Douglas Keen and Hugh Poland Halls. "WKU is now in the clear to start building the new residence halls," said Senator Jakob Barker, who with Senator Ethan Vietze also sponsored Resolution 7-26-S, backing a crosswalk at Alumni Avenue and Kentucky Street for residents of the 1355 Kentucky Street apartments who Barker's resolution said had to "step into oncoming traffic" to reach the Alumni Square parking garage. The same meeting passed legislation funding textbooks, exam supplies and lab goggles and authorizing a student-experience survey.

events.title: SGA funded a tailgate to boost turnout at a baseball game
events.body: SGA used its projects fund to host free hot dogs, giveaways and a scholarship drawing before WKU baseball's home game against Louisville, an effort Robinson said answered Athletics Director Todd Stewart's call for more student engagement at games.

events.title: Weekly meeting funded a senior cookout, transfer cords and spikeball nets
events.body: SGA allocated $602.58 through three bills and one resolution at its weekly meeting: $287.67 for a senior sunset cookout, $239.94 for 240 transfer-student graduation cords and $74.97 for borrowable spikeball nets. The resolution, on signage and navigation in Downing Student Union, drew nothing from the fund. Chief Financial Officer Gabriel Jerdon said $71.17 would remain in the legislative discretionary fund if every bill on the next week's docket passed as written. Speaker Hadley Whipple told senators to stay respectful because they might have to be choosy about what passed.

events.title: 25th Senate closes the year having passed 56 bills, the most since 2018-19
events.body: The 25th Senate's final meeting passed its last three bills of the year - funding an NPHC preview day, the Office of Sustainability's food pantry, and massage-therapy vouchers for finals week, the latter two amended to spend down the year's remaining $71.17 budget - bringing the year's total to 56 pieces of legislation. Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins reported that WKU's new Artificial Intelligence Committee, which he sat on, was in early talks about bulk subscriptions to AI products such as ChatGPT Pro for all students and a possible introductory AI course for freshmen. A representative of Parking and Transportation also spoke; her report is recorded separately.

events.title: Two tickets take questions in the DSU auditorium
events.body: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry against Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated questions submitted by the student body.

events.title: Turnout jumps 66% in a contested race
events.body: 1,601 students voted, 635 more than the year before. Lucas won. The clearest evidence in the whole record that WKU turnout tracks whether there is an actual contest.

events.title: Robinson tells the Faculty Senate to look at the dorms
events.body: Sitting next to Faculty Regent Shane Spiller during a discussion of WKU housing, Robinson told senators to 'take a field trip' and see the state of the residence halls.

events.title: The red suit jacket changes hands
events.body: At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, Robinson handed Lucas the red suit jacket, "the one that Sam (Kurtz) gave me." The same night, Gabby Pace, Cayden Bailey, Maggie Phelps and Jaden Marshall were sworn in to their new roles.

events.title: Year-long mental health push closed with the Out of Darkness Walk
events.body: Robinson and Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Veronica Butler spent the year pressing WKU on student mental health, citing data from social work professor Jay Gabbard that 44 percent of students reported depression symptoms and 10 percent had considered suicide in the past year. SGA co-ran Mental Health Week with the WKU Counseling Center and campus NAMI chapter, launched a Toppers Talk About It campaign, and forwarded student recommendations - including moving counseling services out of Potter Hall - through the Counseling Center Review Committee. The year closed with an Out of Darkness suicide-remembrance walk on April 18; incoming president Caden Lucas said the focus would continue.

events.title: Robinson opens the year with Pearce Ford Tower air conditioning
events.body: At the first meeting of the fall, President Rush Robinson said Executive Director for Housing and Residence Life Catherine LaRoche had assured him the Pearce Ford Tower HVAC system was being repaired and that residents could move temporarily to Hugh Poland Hall. Robinson said 29 of the more than 600 PFT residents had chosen to relocate, and that a chiller unit was also being arranged. Karlee Powell was elected Secretary of the Senate.

events.title: Caboni tells SGA all community bathrooms will be phased out
events.body: President Timothy Caboni told the Senate that WKU intends to eliminate community showers and bathrooms as residence halls are replaced, with two to four people sharing each facility. He said the Student Life Foundation had announced Hilltopper Hall would come down the following summer and that Hilltopper, McCormick and Rodes Harlin halls would all be replaced by fall 2030. He said the university had to reach a point where its offerings created a competitive advantage.

events.title: SGA sets up meal swipe donations through Swipe it Forward
events.body: Chief of Staff Maggie Yelton told the Herald Editorial Board that Swipe it Forward would let students donate up to three meal swipes a semester from traditional meal plans and let students in need request them through a food assistance form. Donated swipes are usable at the Fresh Food Company and the program is sponsored by the WKU Restaurant Group. Robinson said he expected it to appear on the iWKU app within a couple of weeks.

events.title: Senate moves to surface the Hilltoppers concern form
events.body: One of two bills passed replaced the existing Hilltoppers concern form, which author Jakob Barker said was buried behind five links on WKU's homepage, with a pop-up intended to make it easier to find. Barker said the change was about lowering the barrier for student contact. The second bill funded a raffle giveaway to build SGA's social media following, and five senators elected the previous week were sworn in.

events.title: General counsel tells SGA that House Bill 4 binds its spending
events.body: WKU General Counsel Andrea Anderson told the Senate that the WKU Pride Center would become a student-run organization, losing its status as a university-related initiative and its Downing Student Union office, under House Bill 4. Anderson said the statute, passed March 28 and enforced by the Attorney General's office and a committee formed by Provost Bud Fischer, applies to SGA because SGA receives university money for events and bills. She said SGA could still fund organizations and events if they were content neutral, and that HB4 counts social media and digital content as a resource.

events.title: Senate funds 78 organizations and strikes a food pantry bill
events.body: Bill 10-25-F allocated organizational aid to registered student organizations graded on timeliness, allocation quality and financial dependence. Chief Financial Officer Gabriel Jerdon said 78 applications were submitted, that groups could receive up to $500 a year and $250 a semester, and that the lowest-graded organizations would still get a $50 minimum. The Senate voted to strike Bill 8-25-F, which would have funded food pantries.

events.title: Senate amends food pantry bill from $123 to $750 after SNAP cuts
events.body: Senator Amelia Tucker introduced a bill to help the WKU Food Pantry in response to cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, which the article reported has served more than 645,000 people in Kentucky. Tucker handed out 24 slips of paper, six marked with a star, to illustrate that one in four people aged 18 to 26 experience hunger during the year. The bill was introduced at $123 and successive amendments raised it to $750, including $500 drawn from emergency assistance funding.

events.title: Senate waives constitutional requirement for chief justice candidates
events.body: Judicial Council chair Blake Graham told the Senate that neither Sophie Stirling nor Xavier Spiess had completed the year as associate chief justice that the constitution requires of chief justice candidates. The Senate voted an exemption allowing both to run. The same meeting passed a bill extending the Go With the Flow free menstrual product program with a full box expected to last the semester, plus a hygiene donation box, and a bill funding borrowable umbrellas from the SGA office.

events.title: Judicial Council elects Stirling chief justice 3-1
events.body: The Judicial Council voted 3-1 on Nov. 12 to elect Associate Justice Sophie Stirling as chief justice over Associate Justice Xavier Spiess. Stirling told the council a constitution should empower its leaders and said it would under her leadership. She was to be sworn in Nov. 18, when Blake Graham stepped down before graduating.

events.title: Spring budget update shows SGA spent under half its fall funds
events.body: Chief Financial Officer Gabriel Jerdon reported that SGA wrote more bills in the fall than in previous years but did not reach 50% of its semester budget, spending $4,573.73. Remaining balances included $10,100 in organizational aid, $11,500 in scholarships, $6,865 in legislative discretionary spending and $1,300 in vouchers. Jerdon told senators not to be afraid to ask for a large amount if the legislation was worth it.

events.title: Organizational aid split among 33 student groups
events.body: The Senate passed a bill distributing $10,000 in organizational aid as grants of $100 to $500 among 33 registered student organizations, including the Black Student Alliance, Toppers Myanmar Association, Habitat for Humanity and the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition. Author Gabriel Jerdon said applications were graded by about 11 people on a point system, with grades averaged and a dollar amount assigned per point. The Herald later corrected the story to renumber Bill 14-26-S and revise its funding figure to $580.

events.title: SGA announces legislative approval of the Gilbane housing partnership
events.body: Senator Jakob Barker told the Senate that the Kentucky Legislature had approved WKU's public-private partnership with the real estate firm Gilbane, saying WKU was clear to start building the new residence halls. The Board of Regents had approved the pre-development agreement on Dec. 11, 2025, and renderings were unveiled Feb. 20, 2026. The meeting also passed Resolution 7-26-S supporting a crosswalk at Alumni Avenue and Kentucky Street, arguing residents of 1355 Kentucky Street must step into traffic to reach the Alumni Square Garage.

events.title: Parking director tells SGA bus fuel costs have doubled
events.body: The director of Parking and Transportation told the final meeting of the 25th Senate that the monthly diesel bill for WKU buses, normally seven to eight thousand dollars, had reached 14 thousand the previous month. She said service was assured for the rest of the year but transit would have to find money elsewhere if oil prices held, and that permits would be ordered for the lots serving Regents and Normal halls when they open the following spring. The Herald gives her name as "Ginny Griffin"; the official senate minutes give "Jenny Griffith" - unresolved which is correct.

events.title: Outgoing officers close the books on the 25th Senate
events.body: Outgoing Vice President Savanna Kurtz told the first meeting of the 26th Senate that every scholarship offered in 2025-26 had been awarded, and introduced two of the 15 recipients of the Blue Grass Community Foundation Scholarship. Outgoing Chief Financial Officer Gabriel Jerdon reported that $100 of organizational aid remained as a reserve for groups in need and that all other accounts, including office supplies, award plaques and the year-end banquet, had been zeroed out.

events.title: SGA gains a new adviser as Rash becomes interim director
events.body: Andrew Rash, who had served as Associate Director of Student Activities and Greek Life since August 2022 and as SGA's faculty adviser, became interim director of Student Activities on July 1 following the retirement of Charley Pride. Assistant Director of Student Activities and Leadership and Volunteerism Amelia Kolb will advise SGA going forward. Rash said his new duties cover budgeting and Downing Student Union management.

events.title: Chandler Hall opened for the fall semester
events.body: The new Gordon Ford College of Business building, named Amy and David Chandler Hall after a $7.5 million gift and funded largely by a Kentucky General Assembly appropriation, opened to students on the first day of fall classes.

src.label: WKU News - Board of Regents, 8 Aug 2025

events.title: Lucas voices concern over proposed tuition increase
events.body: WKU released a proposed 2026-27 budget that would raise tuition by $210 to $6,246 per semester within a $405.1 million operating plan. Lucas, identified as SGA president and soon-to-be student regent, said he was "generally concerned" by a proposal that would raise the cost of attending WKU. He said students deserved both a high-quality education and an affordable way to achieve it.

events.title: Lucas named ODK Circle Leader of the Year
events.body: WKU's Omicron Delta Kappa circle named President Caden Lucas its Heather Strode Circle Leader of the Year, an award for a student demonstrating leadership and dedication to the campus community across ODK's five core values.

events.title: Meet and greet over sandwiches in the SGA office
events.body: SGA held a meet and greet in its office before the weekly meeting on 9 September 2025, with Jimmy John's sandwiches and sodas, to introduce new students to the organisation. Enrollment and Student Experience Committee chair Jakob Barker organised it, arguing that starting with freshmen meant more students would understand what the body could do and SGA could serve them better. Students then moved into the senate chamber for the meeting, where a bill for a new Big Red Rise event was introduced.

src.label: Herald, 9 Sep 2025 - "SGA hosts meet and greet event for greater student engagement"

events.title: Big Red Rise gave seniors a sunrise breakfast
events.body: SGA held the first Big Red Rise on the morning of 1 October 2025, gathering students on a dark South Lawn to watch the sunrise over doughnuts and coffee before fall break. President Rush Robinson said freshmen were already celebrated with Topper Walk and M.A.S.T.E.R. Plan, and that Big Red Rise was made as a send-off for graduating seniors each semester. He called it a trial run and said SGA hoped to hold another sunrise or sunset event in the spring.

src.label: Herald, 1 Oct 2025 - "SGA celebrates seniors with sunrise breakfast on South Lawn"

events.title: Go With the Flow extended and umbrellas added to the lending shelf
events.body: On 11 November 2025 SGA announced a bill extending Go With the Flow, the programme it created to put free menstrual products in campus bathrooms, by supplying a full box expected to last the rest of the semester and adding a donation box for toothbrushes, toothpaste and soap. Senator Caroline Yates, who wrote it, called menstrual products a basic need. A second bill that passed the same night funded borrowable umbrellas from the SGA office, lent like the calculators.

src.label: Herald, 12 Nov 2025 - "SGA supports Go With the Flow program"

events.title: Senate revived the transcript voucher program with $195 for 15 vouchers
events.body: The senate passed Bill 24-25-F, introduced by Legislative Operations Committee Chair Caden Lucas, allocating $195 from the legislative discretionary fund for 15 transcript vouchers handed out at the SGA office, one per student per semester in exchange for an official transcript from the registrar. Lucas said WKU charges $13 to send a single transcript and that the cost stacks as students send more. The same meeting passed Bill 25-25-F funding a Professor of the Month award and Bill 26-25-F funding replacement ping pong paddles and balls for the DSU recreation area.

events.title: Regents raise tuition over the student regent's lone no vote
events.body: The Board of Regents approved a $204 tuition increase, of 1.69 per cent, taking tuition to $6,240 a semester, the sixth consecutive yearly rise, alongside a 5 per cent housing increase and a 2 per cent meal plan increase within a $405 million operating budget. Every regent voted for it except outgoing SGA president Rush Robinson, who said the board had to do everything it could to preserve affordability. It was his last meeting as student regent before Caden Lucas took the seat. The board also suspended several majors, kinesiology and geological sciences among them, for reworking and mergers.

src.label: Herald, 5 Jun 2026 - WKU Board of Regents approves tuition increase

events.title: Sippin' in September, snowcones and lemonade for Hope Harbor
events.body: The senate passed a bill on 26 August 2025 clearing a fundraiser called Sippin' in September, run with the local businesses Pelican's Snowcones and Tay Tay's Lemonade in aid of Hope Harbor, the Bowling Green organisation that counsels and supports people affected by sexual harm. Pelican's pledged a fifth of everything raised at the event to Hope Harbor. The bill was written by Jade Ismail, chair of SGA's Action and Opportunity Committee.

src.label: Herald, 26 Aug 2025 - "SGA announces 'Sippin' in September' fundraiser to support sexual assault victims"

events.title: A hundred pumpkins on South Lawn for Hope Harbor
events.body: SGA's Action and Opportunity Committee held a campus-wide pumpkin carving contest on South Lawn on Thursday 23 October 2025 from 3 to 5 p.m. as a fundraiser for Hope Harbor. Bill 4-25-F, tabled at its second reading on 9 September before passing at a third reading on 16 September, allocated $320: $250 for a pallet of 100 to 150 pumpkins from Hodge Family Farms, stored in the DSU basement until the day, and a $70 Boo Basket of a heated weighted blanket, candles and donated gifts as the prize. Entry was $10 for up to two carvers, paid straight to the Hope Harbor GoFundMe, and judging was to be done blind by faculty. The Alpha Chi chapter of Alpha Omicron Pi and the Chi Eta chapter of Phi Gamma Delta partnered on the event, covering carving materials and promotion.

src.label: SGA Bill 4-25-F, A Bill to Fund the Pumpkin Carving Contest Fundraiser benefitting Hope Harbor, Inc.

events.title: Toppers Talk About It, a week built around a faculty-student panel
events.body: A bill passed on 28 October 2025 set up a Mental Health Awareness Week for 3 to 7 November, with a different event each day, among them a day of writing positive affirmations in chalk on the pavements and a day of writing positive messages on sticky notes for other students. The week ended with Flipping the Script, a two-part panel at which faculty from the WKU Counseling Center and the Student Accessibility Resource Center answered questions submitted by students, and then turned the format round so the faculty questioned a group of selected student leaders. The bill was written by Veronica Butler, who told the Herald she wanted the week to raise awareness, reduce stigma and create a supportive campus culture.

src.label: Herald, 28 Oct 2025 - "SGA focuses on mental health awareness"

events.title: Judicial Council heard a censure case against a committee chair and dismissed it 7-0
events.body: The Judicial Council heard a censure case against Senator Jade Ismail, chair of the Action and Opportunity Committee, on 12 November 2025. The complaints included one from members of Alpha Omicron Pi alleging she had treated them poorly when they volunteered at the 23 October pumpkin carving fundraiser she ran, an allegation that she had underspent the sums bills had allocated, which Chief Justice Blake Graham described as undercutting senators' ability to use legislative discretionary funds, and an allegation that she had emailed registered student organisations about a bill before it passed. The council voted 7-0 not to censure, treating most of it as poor communication, and Associate Justice Hannah Hash urged her to keep writing bills.

src.label: Herald, 19 Nov 2025 - "SGA votes to exempt parking tickets for food donations"

events.title: Food for Fines let students pay off a parking ticket in tinned goods
events.body: The senate passed a bill on 18 November 2025 allowing students to donate food in exchange for exemption from a parking citation, a scheme called Food for Fines run jointly with the WKU Food Pantry and WKU Parking and Transportation Services. Its author, Caden Lucas, chair of the Legislative Operations Committee, argued it would pull far more students into the university food drive at a time when many needed it. At the same meeting a bill from Jade Ismail proposing a raffle in Downing Student Union for Hope Harbor was the only one to fail, senators taking the view that the money should be spent on students on campus.

src.label: Herald, 19 Nov 2025 - "SGA votes to exempt parking tickets for food donations"

events.title: Happy Holidays from the Hill: cards and blankets for a care home
events.body: Bill 22-25-F allocated $218.61 from the legislative discretionary fund to buy 72 Christmas cards and 60 blankets for residents of Chandler Park Assisted Living. SGA tabled in Downing Student Union on 2 and 3 December 2025 so students could sign the cards, and delivered them with the blankets on 4 December. Students who helped deliver could claim up to three service hours, and senators up to three office hours for attending or tabling. The bill passed its second reading on 18 November 2025.

src.label: SGA Bill 22-25-F, Funding for Happy Holiday's from the Hill

events.title: Senators in Christmas pyjamas voted for an open house
events.body: At the last meeting of the autumn semester on 2 December 2025, senators wearing Christmas pyjamas and Santa hats passed a bill allocating $50.10 to an SGA Winter Welcome on 3 February 2026, an open house at the SGA office meant to raise student attendance at senate meetings. The author, Senator-at-Large Amelia Tucker, told the Herald the house was always open but an open house might bring more people in. The meeting lasted thirty minutes and senators left for the SGA Christmas party at the Cliff Todd Center.

src.label: Herald, 2 Dec 2025 - "SGA passes bill at festive final meeting"

events.title: Black History Trivia Night with Why Knot Us and Black Women of Western
events.body: Bill 1-26-S allocated $65 from the legislative discretionary fund towards a Black History Trivia Night held with Why Knot Us and Black Women of Western on 18 February 2026, from 6 to 8 p.m. in DSU room 2123. SGA's share paid for crisps, drinks and the room hire, while the two partner organisations split the cost of eight gift cards between them. The bill describes the evening as an interactive way to mark black history, culture and achievement, and passed at its second reading on 3 February 2026.

src.label: SGA Bill 1-26-S, Funding for the Black History Trivia Night

events.title: A 200-player Uno tournament to fund student research
events.body: Bill 3-26-S allocated $209.96 for an Uno tournament fundraiser run with STEMPOWERMENT, passing at its second reading on 24 February 2026. The money hired DSU rooms 3023, 3024 and 3025, merged into one space for three hours at $20 per room per hour, a total of $180, with $29.96 buying four Uno decks. The tournament was capped at 200 players with a $2 entry and paid re-entries at $2 a time, the proceeds supporting student research.

src.label: SGA Bill 3-26-S, Funding for the STEMPOWERMENT and SGA Uno Tournament Fundraiser

events.title: F1rstGen staff briefed the senate as it passed a bike rack resolution
events.body: Cierra Waller and April McCauley of WKU's F1rstGen initiative were guest speakers at the 3 March 2026 meeting, describing the mentorship programme, the first-generation living learning community and the Make It Count service, which gives $250 grants to first-generation students who attend F1rstGen events regularly. Waller said such students were not short of ability but often needed help with unfamiliar university machinery, giving the renaming of the Bursar's Office as the Office of Student Billing and Account Services as an example of the confusion F1rstGen had pushed to clear up. The senate then passed Resolution 3-26-S, which allocates no money but commits SGA to work with Parking and Transportation Services on siting new bike racks and revising the campus bike rack map, prompted by bikes and scooters being locked to railings and stairways.

src.label: Herald, 3 Mar 2026 - "SGA discusses resources for first-generation students, passes resolution for new bike racks"

events.title: Four more Adirondack chairs for the green spaces
events.body: Bill 11-26-S allocated $398.98 from the legislative discretionary fund to expand the Adirondack Chair Project, buying two pairs of red Westin Trends chairs at $199.49 a pair. The project had begun in spring 2025, placing chairs at popular spots around campus so students could use the green spaces, and the bill records that students had found the first batch popular and useful enough to justify more. It passed its second reading on 26 March 2026.

src.label: SGA Bill 11-26-S, Funding for the Expansion of the Adirondack Chair Project

events.title: A campus safety committee appears outside the constitution's seven
events.body: Resolution 1-26-S, read on 3 and 10 February 2026, designated 30 March to 3 April 2026 as WKU Campus Safety and Security Week in response to violence at other universities. It was sponsored by a Campus Safety and Security Committee alongside the Legislative Operations Committee. That committee is not one of the seven named in the constitution; the Senate minutes of 14 April 2026 record its work reported jointly with the Student Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee under chair Veronica Butler.

src.label: SGA Resolution 1-26-S and Senate minutes, 14 Apr 2026

events.title: Council set its own attendance standard
events.body: Chief Justice Blake Graham recorded that senator attendance would now be judged on three criteria, timeliness, thoroughness and validity of the excuse, and that the council itself would meet permanently on Wednesdays at 6pm with a maximum of two unexcused absences, voting on each other's attendance with the justice in question recused. The council also set out a strategy for revising the constitution and said it aimed to join the appeals process for parking and transportation citations.

events.title: Council granted a unanimous eligibility exemption and lost a justice
events.body: Under section 2.2.5 a student who had not served a full year in SGA asked to run for executive office; the exemption required a unanimous vote, and the council granted it 6-0 after hearing the applicant. At the same meeting it ruled that family members could help campaign and that outside organisations could endorse tickets, provided no incentives were offered for showing votes. Associate Justice Kaden Blankenship resigned from the council effective 2 April 2026 and stood on a presidential ticket.

events.title: Council censured a presidential ticket during the election
events.body: Acting on its own initiative rather than a complaint, the council found the Marshall, Blankenship and VanRude ticket guilty 4-0 of breaching section 3.11 of the election codes, which barred distribution of perishable food within 48 hours of an election, after Red Bull cans were handed out at their table and a photograph was reposted to their campaign story. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling and Associate Chief Justice Hannah Hash held that the legal test for perishability was not open to debate and that ticket members were responsible for educating their campaign team. The council issued a formal censure but declined to remove the ticket from the ballot.

events.title: Council disbanded a campaign team and narrowed its own precedent
events.body: On an anonymous complaint of campaigning in the Commons while voting was open, backed by video the chief justice and associate chief justice obtained themselves, the council found the same ticket guilty 5-0 of breaching election codes 3.13 and 3.13.1 on polling places and not guilty on 3.6.8 on posters. It held that its precedent in Lee, Rosenbaum, Willmes v. Cook of fall 2025, which made a candidate wholly responsible for campaign materials, was too broad for acts by a team member, and narrowed it. It censured and disbanded the MBV campaign team rather than issuing the ticket a second censure, ruled that future breaches by designated team members would be attributable to the ticket, and required all tickets to file campaign team rosters before elections.

executive.name: Savanna Kurtz
profile: Savanna Kurtz was elected a freshman senator in SGA's fall 2023 election, announced 20 September over an Instagram livestream and sworn in the following Tuesday. The Senate confirmed her as chair of the Student Experience and Enrollment Committee at the 24th Senate's fall opening meeting on 27 August 2024. That November she wrote Bill 20-24-F, funding a two-week toy drive with Student Activities for the Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green with an extra $200 for toys, building on committee work she had done on the same drive the previous year.

Kurtz was elected student body vice president unopposed on Rush Robinson's ticket with Chief Financial Officer Gabriel Jerdon in the spring 2025 general election, the same election in which 88% of students voted to rename the DEI Committee the Action and Opportunity Committee. As vice president she authored Bill 9-25-F, funding the 2025-26 SGA Pink Walk, which the Senate passed on 9 October 2025. At the 26th Senate's first meeting on 28 April 2026, as outgoing vice president, she reported that every scholarship offered in 2025-26 had been awarded and introduced two of the fifteen recipients of the Blue Grass Community Foundation Scholarship.

executive.name: Gabriel Jerdon
profile: Gabriel Jerdon was elected chief financial officer on Rush Robinson's ticket, unopposed, alongside Vice President Savanna Kurtz, in the spring 2025 general election. As CFO he authored the Senate's fall organizational-aid appropriations bill, 10-25-F, which passed 16 October 2025; he told the Senate 78 organizations had applied, that groups could receive up to $500 a year and $250 a semester, and that the lowest-graded organizations would still get a $50 minimum, and the same meeting struck a separate bill that would have funded food pantries.

In a February 2026 budget update, Jerdon reported SGA had written more bills that fall than in previous years but had not reached half its semester budget, spending $4,573.73, and told senators not to be afraid to ask for a large amount if the legislation was worth it. In March 2026 he reported organizational aid split among 33 registered student organizations; the Herald later corrected the story to renumber the bill and revise the funding figure to $580. In April 2026, as the discretionary fund neared zero, he said $71.17 would remain if the final week's bills passed as written. At the 26th Senate's first meeting on 28 April 2026, as outgoing chief financial officer, he reported $100 of organizational aid held in reserve and every other account, including office supplies, plaques and the year-end banquet, zeroed out.

executive.name: Maggie Yelton
profile: President Rush Robinson appointed Maggie Yelton chief of staff at the 25th Senate's first meeting on 23 April 2025, alongside senator-at-large Amelia Tucker; former Speaker Sarah Vincent swore in the new Senate.

Yelton told the Herald's editorial board on 11 September 2025 that a new Swipe It Forward programme, sponsored by the WKU Restaurant Group, would let students donate up to three meal swipes a semester from their meal plans, redeemable at the Fresh Food Company by students who requested them through a food-assistance form; President Robinson said he expected it to appear on the iWKU app within a couple of weeks. At the Senate's 17 February 2026 meeting, which passed a bill funding CPR-certification vouchers, Yelton reported seven dental, one ID and thirteen transcript vouchers still available in the voucher program.

executive.name: Preston Jenkins
executive.note: Reappointed 22 April 2025; confirmed by the Senate.
profile: Preston Jenkins was appointed chief communications officer over the summer of 2024, an appointment Chief of Staff Anne-Marie Wright described to the Senate as President Sam Kurtz's decision; he was welcomed at the year's first meeting on 27 August 2024, where he reported he was planning graphics for the fall election. President Rush Robinson reappointed him to the post on 22 April 2025, one of his first acts in office, and the Senate confirmed the reappointment unanimously; Jenkins kept the post through the 25th Senate's opening on 23 April 2025.

In August 2025 Jenkins announced a plan to have four student artists each paint one side of a column in the SGA chambers, incorporating WKU campus elements, with entries due by 19 September. At the 25th Senate's final meeting on 14 April 2026, he reported that WKU's new Artificial Intelligence Committee, on which he sat, was in early talks about bulk subscriptions to AI products for students and a possible introductory AI course for freshmen; the Senate closed the year having passed 56 bills, the most since 2018-19.

officers.name: Hadley Whipple
profile: Hadley Whipple was confirmed as the senate's Ogden College senator at SGA's first meeting of 2024-25 on 27 August 2024, the same meeting at which the secretary's post was announced vacant. She held the secretaryship by March 2025, and the following month the 25th Senate elected her Speaker over fellow nominees Caden Lucas and Sophia Bryant. "Since the day I came in, I knew I wanted to run for speaker," she said, adding that being the voice of the senate mattered to her and that she wanted to be approachable. As speaker into spring 2026 she chaired the senate's final meetings of the term, at one point urging senators running low on discretionary funds to be choosy and respectful about what they passed as bills competed for the last dollars. A graduating senior, she was succeeded as speaker after the senate's 28 April 2026 meeting, when it elected Veronica Butler to follow her.

officers.name: Karlee Powell
officers.note: A graduating senior; missed the 26th Senate's first meeting to present her capstone project.
profile: Karlee Powell, a Gordon Ford College of Business ambassador, was elected Secretary of the Senate at the 25th Senate's first meeting on Aug. 19, 2025. She told the Herald she had joined SGA because friends were already members, and that she would have regretted leaving WKU without joining. She said she hoped to bring "fresh ideas and a new perspective" and to represent every student in the room.

As secretary Powell also continued to author legislation from the floor: Bill 11-25-F, passed to fund $76.89 in chalk and fidget toys for the Senate's "Toppers Talk About It" Mental Health Awareness Week tabling in November 2025, and Bill 5-26-S, passed to fund $492.98 for an SGA International Women's Day tabling event in March 2026. At the Feb. 17, 2026 meeting she was one of three senators who spoke in favor of a bill creating CPR-certification vouchers for students, which passed unanimously.

src.label: WKU SGA, Executive Cabinet minutes, 12 Aug 2025

profile: Blake Graham served as chief justice of the Judicial Council for the 2025-26 Student Government Association, one of seven officers on President Rush Robinson's executive board when it met on 12 August 2025. At that meeting he reported five pending appointments to the Judicial Council to be sworn in at the Senate's first or second meeting, set 2 and 3 September as the dates for that fall's election code meetings with candidate packets due by 9 p.m. on the 3rd, and said the minimum GPA required of an SGA candidate had been lowered to 2.0.

He did not finish the year in the office. The Judicial Council met on 12 November 2025 to choose a successor and elected Associate Justice Sophie Stirling 3-1 over Associate Justice Xavier Spiess; the Herald reported that Stirling would be sworn in at the SGA meeting of 18 November, the same meeting at which Graham stepped down.

officers.name: Sophie Stirling
officers.note: An associate justice under Graham in October 2025 and chief justice by 26 January 2026, when she wrote the council's minutes herself; a chief justice election had been scheduled for 12 November 2025. She set the April 2026 election dates and drafted the election codes. The minutes she wrote spell the name Stirling, which supports that spelling against the Herald's single "Sterling".

src.label: WKU SGA, Judicial Council minutes, 26 Jan 2026

profile: Sophie Stirling was an associate justice on the Judicial Council under Chief Justice Blake Graham in the fall of 2025. The Senate waived the constitutional requirement that a chief justice candidate have served a full year as associate chief justice, allowing her and Associate Justice Xavier Spiess to stand, and the council elected her 3-1 over Spiess on 12 November 2025; she was to be sworn in on 18 November, when Graham stepped down.

She wrote the council's minutes of 26 January 2026 herself. At that meeting she welcomed Kaden Blankenship, whom President Rush Robinson had appointed to the council, and appointed Hannah Hash as associate chief justice, both pending the Senate's approval the following week. She told the council she would begin drafting that year's election codes, with elections on TopNet tentatively set for 15 to 17 April 2026 and a reveal party for the new Senate planned in the SGA chambers on the 17th.

leaders.name: Caden Lucas
leaders.note: From Harned. Beat Jaden Marshall in a contested race on a turnout of 1,601 - up 66% on the previous year. WKU Spiritmaster, chair of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, works for the City of Bowling Green's Downtown Development Division. Sworn in 28 April 2026 at the first meeting of the 26th Senate.

sources.label: WKU News - ODK Circle Leader of the Year

profile: Lucas entered SGA in September 2024 as its inaugural student senator for the Mahurin Honors College, a seat created as the college began a program revision; he was also an Honors Teaching Fellow for HON 251, working with first-year Honors students on civic engagement. A junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster, chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition and an employee of Bowling Green's Downtown Development Division, he won the SGA presidential election on April 15, 2026, with running mates Jakob Barker for vice president and Will Derryberry for chief financial officer. Running under the motto "Lead, build, deliver," his campaign centered on increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body, and he defeated Jaden Marshall, who had sought to become the first Black male student body president. After the results were announced Lucas said he felt "electric" and that the "work starts tomorrow," beginning with thank-you cards to supporters.

Lucas took office at the first meeting of the 26th Senate on April 28, 2026, where outgoing president Rush Robinson presented him with the traditional red suit jacket passed from president to president. Lucas thanked the new cabinet, nominated his defeated campaign opponent Jaden Marshall as an at-large senator, calling his campus work "phenomenal," and saw Gabi Pace and Cayden Bailey sworn in as chief of staff and chief communications officer. The meeting's speaker election deadlocked 9-9 between Amelia Tucker and Veronica Butler, a situation the governing documents did not address, and Butler won the seat in a re-vote.

Days after taking office, Lucas was named a 2026 Truman Scholar, WKU's second in the award's history and Kentucky's only recipient that year, chosen from 781 candidates nationally; the scholarship funds $30,000 toward graduate or professional study for students committed to public service. A political science, legal studies and strategic communications major, he had spent that summer establishing the Civic Engagement Resource Center, a joint Mahurin Honors College, SGA and Housing and Residence Life initiative that opened 30 October 2024 with a lending collection on civic life, saying his goal was to get students "talking about what it means to be a good citizen." In May, WKU's Omicron Delta Kappa circle named him its Heather Strode Circle Leader of the Year, an award recognizing collaboration, inclusivity, integrity, scholarship and service.

Before he was sworn in as student regent, Lucas told the Herald he was "generally concerned" by a proposed $210 tuition increase; the Board of Regents approved a $204 increase days later, with outgoing regent Rush Robinson casting the only dissenting vote before handing the seat to Lucas.

Caden Lucas, a junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster, chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition and an employee of Bowling Green's Downtown Development Division, won the SGA presidential election on April 15, 2026, with running mates Jakob Barker for vice president and Will Derryberry for chief financial officer. Running under the motto "Lead, build, deliver," his campaign centered on increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body, and he defeated Jaden Marshall, who had sought to become the first Black male student body president. After the results were announced Lucas said he felt "electric" and that the "work starts tomorrow," beginning with thank-you cards to supporters.

events.title: Caden Lucas wins SGA presidential election
events.body: Caden Lucas and his ticket of Vice President-elect Jakob Barker and Chief Financial Officer-elect Will Derryberry won the spring election to serve during the 2026-27 academic year, defeating Jaden Marshall's ticket. Lucas, a junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster and chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, ran on the motto "Lead, build, deliver" and a promise to make SGA operations more visible to students. The Herald did not publish vote totals or turnout figures; the story also listed the full slate of senators elected to the incoming 26th Senate.

events.title: 26th Senate seated; tie vote for speaker resolved in Butler's favor
events.body: At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, outgoing president Rush Robinson passed the traditional red suit jacket to Caden Lucas, and the body swore in Gabi Pace as chief of staff, Cayden Bailey as chief communications officer, Maggie Phelps to the judicial council and defeated presidential candidate Jaden Marshall as an at-large senator. The race for speaker of the senate ended in a 9-9 tie between Amelia Tucker and Veronica Butler, and Chief Justice Sophie Sterling confirmed that neither the constitution nor the bylaws addressed a tie. Outgoing speaker Hadley Whipple ordered a re-vote, which elected Butler as speaker.

events.title: Executive candidates face off at SGA town hall
events.body: SGA held a town hall in the Downing Student Union Auditorium for the two executive tickets: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry, and Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated as the candidates answered 27 questions submitted by students. Both tickets made increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body their central campaign promise.

events.title: Herald and Revolution Radio hosted a presidential debate
events.body: College Heights Herald Editor-in-Chief Jake McMahon and Assistant News Editor Kane Smith sat down with presidential candidates Caden Lucas and Jaden Marshall for a debate co-hosted with campus station Revolution Radio, ahead of voting opening the following Monday on TopNet.

events.title: Lucas named a 2026 Truman Scholar
events.body: Days after taking SGA's top office, President Caden Lucas was named a 2026 Truman Scholar, WKU's second in the scholarship's history and Kentucky's only recipient that year. The award, chosen from 781 candidates at 305 colleges nationally, provides $30,000 toward graduate or professional study and recognizes commitment to public service.

executive.name: Caden Lucas
executive.note: Also student regent on the WKU Board of Regents.

executive.name: Jakob Barker
profile: Jakob Barker served as a WKU SGA senator, first as a freshman and then as a sophomore, and chaired the Student Experience Committee, where he reworked its scholarship grading process and expanded the Bluegrass Leadership Scholarship to applicants from Tennessee. As a sophomore senator for 2025-26 he sponsored funding for an SGA "Meet n Greet" and resolutions on campus safety and a student experience survey.

In April 2026 Barker ran for student body vice president on Caden Lucas's presidential ticket, with Will Derryberry for chief financial officer. At an executive-candidates town hall that month he said he planned to move scholarship applications from paper to digital and, as WKU transitioned from the Student Life Foundation to a public-private housing partnership, argued students still needed representation in decisions about it. The Lucas ticket won the election announced 15 April 2026, and Barker succeeded outgoing vice president Savanna Kurtz.

At the new Senate's first meeting on 28 April 2026, Barker reflected on rising from a freshman senator to the vice presidency in two years; two years earlier, he said, he "didn't really know what was in store for me."

executive.name: Will Derryberry
profile: Will Derryberry, a sophomore senator, ran as chief financial officer on Caden Lucas's "Lead, build, deliver" ticket, which won the SGA presidential election on 15 April 2026 against a ticket headed by Jaden Marshall. He said he had never expected to hold the position when he first came to WKU, and that he did not plan to lower the executive branch's stipends. He took office after the senate's swearing-in of the new administration on 28 April 2026.

profile: Gabi Pace was elected the Potter College of Arts and Letters senator in SGA's April 2026 election. At the senate's first meeting of the new term on 28 April 2026, she was sworn in as chief of staff to President Caden Lucas; the Herald's report of that meeting rendered her name as "Gabby Pace" in that instance, a spelling discrepancy unresolved in this record.

executive.name: Cayden Bailey
profile: Cayden Bailey was elected a junior senator in SGA's April 2026 election. He was sworn in as chief communications officer at the senate's first meeting of the new term on 28 April 2026, succeeding outgoing Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins.

officers.name: Veronica Butler
officers.note: Won a re-vote after a 9-9 tie with Amelia Tucker; the governing documents had no tie-break procedure.
profile: Veronica Butler was elected a junior senator in SGA's April 2026 election and chaired the senate's Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee. Working with outgoing President Rush Robinson, she helped build a year-long slate of mental health programming, including SGA-sponsored Mental Health Week events, and told the Herald that knowing when to seek help had been one of her own biggest struggles, and that much of it came down to whether students felt able to use the resources available and found them accessible. At the senate's first meeting of 2026-27 on 28 April 2026, she was one of four senators — with Amelia Tucker, Molly Ricky and Jaden Marshall — who ran for Speaker of the Senate to succeed the graduating Hadley Whipple. The first vote tied 9-9 between Butler and Tucker; with neither the constitution nor the bylaws providing a tie-break procedure, outgoing Speaker Whipple called a re-vote between the two, which Butler won.

senate.note: Maggie Phelps was sworn to the Judicial Council and defeated presidential candidate Jaden Marshall was seated as an at-large senator, both at the 26th Senate's first meeting, 28 April 2026. The chief justice's name appears as both 'Sophie Sterling' (Herald, 28 Apr 2026) and 'Sophie Stirling' (Herald, 8 Apr 2026 and Herald, 5 Apr 2026, the latter quoting her 2 Apr 2026 weekly report to the 25th Senate) in Herald reporting; the official 25th Senate minutes of 14 Apr 2026 (in 2025-26's documents) twice give 'Sophie Stirling'. That is now three Herald mentions and the official minutes agreeing on 'Stirling' against one 'Sterling', which favors that spelling but does not fully settle it, since the 28 Apr Herald report post-dates all of them and could reflect a correction rather than an error. No committee chairs had been reported as of this update - the 26th Senate's first fall meeting had not yet occurred.
